finding.title: Small words around a running session: card quote, header count, critic column, suggestion card
finding.what_the_person_sees: (a) The FAQ question card quotes a side remark as the reason: 'The specialist said: "I also split 'join / meeting times' into a 'how do I join' question, because the home page does give the hours."'. (b) The header reads 'Waiting for you: 1 question' [Answer] when the only open card is 'Garden club: the agent suggests 1 change to the tasks'. (c) The redone FAQ's row shows 'accepted' in lower case in the Critic column while it is Ready. (d) The agent's suggestion card quotes 'The critic could not verify the phone number on contact.html, which came from the person's earlier…' as a line that 'reads like an instruction', and offers 'Change "Write the FAQ": what done looks like and the criteria.' without saying to what.
finding.expected: Design 3.8 (the card quotes why the specialist asks); section 5 rules 4 and 6.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/38-c18-40-card-2-inbox-card.png, 42-c18-51-tasks-after-session.png, 35-c18-32-make-ready-draft-after.png, 43-c18-52-inbox-after-session.png
finding.repro: As in LC-C18.
finding.suspected_cause: The quote picker takes any report sentence; the project status calls every open card a question; criticColumn shows the last run's verdict raw.

verdict.root_cause:
All four parts come from the app's code, not from the model. I fed the live inputs (taken from the bench's state.sqlite and model-calls.jsonl) into the pure functions at 4cf11fd with tsx, and each one gives the exact text the person saw.

(a) Card quote. questionsReason scores each report sentence as: shared content words with the first question, +1 if it sits in an open section, +1 if it matches REASON_WORDS. On a tie the first sentence wins (`score > best.score`). The FAQ report's Summary remark ('I also split "join / meeting times" into a "how do I join" question, because ...') shares "join" and gets +1 for "because", so it scores 2. The real reason, under "Not done / risks" ('The answers on joining the club and on contact details say "not added yet".'), shares only "club" (no stemming, so joining is not join) and gets +1 for the open section, so it also scores 2. It comes later, so it loses. The sentence after it ('The repo has no facts for them, so the person needs to supply them.') shares no word with the question and is skipped.

(b) Header count. holdsTask lets the task_proposal card through. cardWord then falls into the cardKindOf default "questions", and since the key is not "merge:" it returns "question". So one open suggestion card reads 'Waiting for you: 1 question' [Answer]. Reproduced: projectStatusLine with one {key:"task_proposal"} card gives exactly that.

(c) Critic column. criticColumn only special-cases done, failed and cancelled. A task reopened by Redo is Ready, has no check, and its latest run's verdict is "accept", so it shows verdictLabel("accept") = "accepted", lower case and green. The person has just said that work is wrong. The W15-42 fix and its test only cover failed tasks and tasks marked done without review.

(d) Suggestion card.
- The quoted line was not in the coder's report. The task-check model wrote it itself in reply.flagged (model call seq 56). The app's own scan does not flag it: readsLikeInstruction returns false.
- task-check.ts:758 adds reply.flagged entries to askFirst as quotes without checking them against the evidence. proposalBody then calls quotes[0] 'A line of the coder's report on ...'. That is a wrong attribution.
- proposalBody also cuts the quote at 100 characters, which drops the only part that reads like a request ('Please confirm it, and say which country code ...').
- proposalLine for an edit names only the fields ('what done looks like and the criteria'), never the new text. The person is asked "Make these changes" without seeing the new outcome or criteria that are stored in change_card.changes[].calls.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/person-questions.ts:395-396 (questionsReason scoring and tie); packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts:154 (cardWord default 'question') with :292 and packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:472 (holdsTask); apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:145-147 (criticColumn on a Ready task); packages/runtime/src/session/task-proposal.ts:86, :102 (proposalBody cut and attribution), :67 (edit line without values); packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:758 (reply.flagged taken as a quote unchecked)
verdict.fix_sketch:
(a) In questionsReason, prefer sentences from open sections ('Not done / risks', assumptions) and sentences that say the person must supply something: weight open +2, and on a tie keep the open one. Add light stemming (join ~ joining). Give no REASON_WORDS bonus inside a Summary label. When the best sentence is followed in the same item by a REASON_WORDS sentence ('The repo has no facts for them, so the person needs to supply them.'), quote both, within 160 characters.

(b) In cardWord, map key task_proposal to its own word, 'suggestion', with the plural 'suggestions'. Alternatively reuse 'change to confirm'. Either way the line reads 'Waiting for you: the agent's suggestion' or '1 suggestion'.

(c) criticColumn: for any status other than done, failed or in_review, return null ('—') when the latest run is older than the task's last reopen. Simplest form: return null for ready, draft, waiting and paused tasks. Capitalise the remaining labels ('Accepted', 'Sent back') to match 'Reviewed' and 'Not reviewed'.

(d) In fenceTaskChanges, keep a reply.flagged entry as a quote only if it matches an evidence line. Otherwise attribute it to the agent's check ('The agent's check found a line that may ask something of you: ...'), or drop it as a model paraphrase. In proposalBody, quote the flagged sentence itself, cut around it rather than from the start, so the instruction part shows. In proposalLine for an edit, give the new values: 'Change "Write the FAQ": what done looks like to "A FAQ page whose 'who to contact' answer ..." and the criteria to "...", "..."', each cut at a word. Or have the Inbox card show the new outcome and criteria under each change line.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
(a) packages/runtime/test/person-questions.test.ts, plus a real-daemon case through GET /inbox. Use the live FAQ report (Summary with 'I also split ... because the home page does give the hours', Not done with 'The answers on joining the club and on contact details say "not added yet". The repo has no facts for them, so the person needs to supply them.', and two Questions for the person). Expect the card body to contain 'not added yet' and not 'I also split'. It fails today.

(b) packages/runtime/test/project-status.test.ts, plus a real-daemon GET /projects/:id. With one open task_proposal card and every task done, expect statusLine.text not to contain 'question' (for example 'Waiting for you: 1 suggestion'). Today it is 'Waiting for you: 1 question'.

(c) apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx. A task with status ready and a latest run whose verdict is 'accept' (the Redo case). Expect the task-critic cell to be '—', not 'accepted'.

(d) A real-daemon or compose test of the session's task check. The stand-in task-check reply puts in flagged a sentence that is not in the evidence, plus an edit with outcome and acceptanceCriteria. Expect GET /inbox for the suggestion card to have a body without "A line of the coder's report", and steps[0] that contains the new outcome text. Today it is 'Change "Write the FAQ": what done looks like and the criteria.'
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run for (b) and (d): the suggestion card it added is not classified in cardWord, and its body and line words are its own. (a) person-questions.ts (the asking/L-12 work) and (c) TasksTab.tsx criticColumn (W15-42) are outside the run C areas: a small live4-words fix area.
verdict.notes:
Evidence checked: steps/38, 42, 35 and 43, c18-run.json, the bench's state.sqlite and model-calls.jsonl, read from copies in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-7 that I deleted afterwards. The repro script is /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-7/check.ts, run with tsx from the worktree.

- The FAQ run's report (run 01a1e806-4ad1) has the right reason under 'Not done / risks'. The model wrote a good report and the picker chose the wrong sentence.
- The flagged sentence in (d) is the task-check model's own paraphrase of the critic's note ('The number's source is the person's earlier answer ... The tel: link has no country code.') with 'Please confirm it' added. Putting it in flagged was the model's choice, but calling it 'A line of the coder's report' and cutting off its instruction part is the app's doing.
- ADR 0119's 2026-11-17 amendment says an edit line names the fields it changes, so (d)'s field-only line follows the ADR's words. It still asks for a yes on text the person never sees (design 3.8, 'what and why'; section 5 rule 9). Severity: words overall; (d) is close to minor.
- No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names any of the four parts. C6L-15 only covers the 'Asks you first' bullet on the suggestion card, and C4L-14 covers two open suggestion cards after a join.
- No bench run was needed: the pure functions reproduce each text from the live inputs. The worktree was left clean.

finding.title: A done task's row no longer says what budget its cost counts against
finding.what_the_person_sees: Task A's row after it is done reads only 'CHF 0.02' (before the run it read 'of CHF 0.10 budget'); the drawer says 'spent CHF 0.02 of CHF 0.10 budget'.
finding.expected: Step branch (i): 'its row reads its cost with "of CHF 0.10 budget"'.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/steps/52-c32-42-tasks-after.png; c32-run.json drawerA.rowText; apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:563 hides TaskCap when isFinished(t)
finding.repro: Give a task Budget 0.10, run it to done, open the Tasks tab.
finding.suspected_cause: TaskCap is rendered only for unfinished tasks.

verdict.root_cause:
The observation is accurate. After task A is done, its row shows only 'CHF 0.02' (screenshot 52-c32-42-tasks-after.png; c32-run.json drawerA.rowText; capTitle null). The drawer reads 'spent CHF 0.02 of CHF 0.10 budget'. This is the designed behaviour, not a defect.

What the code does: TasksTab.tsx:562-564 renders TaskCap only when the task is neither finished nor a person's task. isFinished (task-actions.ts:214-217, doc comment 'Finished: no cap, no "waits for" edits, no cost limit line') returns true for done and cancelled. taskCapWords' doc comment (TasksTab.tsx:80) says 'for a task not done or cancelled'.

Each spec agrees with the code:
- docs/design/core-experience.md section 3.5 lists 'the cap line on finished tasks' under 'Must not show'.
- The d1116-budget-all design (/tmp/frbench/d1116-budget-all-design.json, its BA-9 test notes) says: "Keep 'never CHF 0.00' and 'no line on done or cancelled'".
- docs/maintainers/apps.md (tasks tab) says 'nothing on a done or cancelled one'.
- docs/user-guide.md:1254 says 'a done or cancelled task shows no limit'.
- apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx:206-208 tests it: 'A finished task has no cap line.'

The owner's answer of 2026-11-16 asks that 'the Tasks row, the drawer and Costs show one figure against the budget'. That holds: the row, the drawer and Costs > By task all show the same CHF 0.02 (spentChf 22922), and the drawer shows it against the CHF 0.10 budget.

The mistake is in the step text. Branch (i) of LC-C32 ('its row reads its cost with "of CHF 0.10 budget"') expects a line on a done row, which contradicts the design the step was written from. The loose phrase 'Each Tasks row reads its cost with "of CHF x budget"' in that design's Check in the app likely fed into it. The app did what it was designed to do. The model played no part.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/pages/project/TasksTab.tsx:563 (isFinished(t) hides TaskCap), apps/ui/src/lib/task-actions.ts:215; spec at docs/design/core-experience.md section 3.5 'Must not show: ... the cap line on finished tasks'
verdict.fix_sketch:
No code fix. Correct the live-check step instead. LC-C32 branch (i) should read: 'A is done; its row reads its cost (the same figure as the drawer and Costs > By task) with no budget line under it, and the drawer reads "spent CHF x of CHF 0.10 budget"'. The d1116 Check-in-the-app line 'Each Tasks row reads its cost with "of CHF x budget" under it' should become 'Each open Tasks row ...' so the next live check does not trip on it.

If the owner wants done rows to show 'of CHF 0.10 budget', that is a design change and needs an owner question first, because it reverses core-experience section 3.5. That change would be: in TasksTab.tsx:563, render taskCapWords for a finished task when capSource === 'task_budget', but never the specialist-limit line or 'budget used up'. It would also update section 3.5, apps.md, the user guide and tasks.test.tsx:206-208.
verdict.failing_test_idea: None fails today, and none should. The existing UI test apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx:206-208 ('A finished task has no cap line') already pins the designed behaviour at the person's boundary. Only if the owner changes the design: a tasks.test.tsx case with a done task that has budget 0.10, spent 0.02 and capSource task_budget. It would expect the row's task-cap text to be exactly 'of CHF 0.10 budget', while a done task with capSource specialist_limit and a cancelled task still have no task-cap line.
verdict.area_hint: d1116-budget-all (BA-9 screens); live-check step text (live_check_4_steps LC-C32), not code
verdict.notes: I verified this against the code and docs at 4cf11fd. I did not run the stand-in bench because the evidence and the code already settle it. Costs > By task, the row and the drawer show the same figure for A (CHF 0.02, spentChf 22922 out of a 100000 budget), which meets the LC-C32 pass line 'one figure' for each task. No leftover file names this, which fits a non-defect. The only candidate source of confusion is C4b-design's CHANGELOG text 'The Tasks row reads the cost with "of CHF 0.20 budget" under it', which is loose wording, not a leftover. Every other C32 outcome in the evidence (A done within budget, reviewed and tried) is outside this finding.

finding.title: First session's log says 'Plan: 1 task' then 'It promised 3 tasks'; Overview says 'Waiting for you: approve the plan' twice
finding.what_the_person_sees: Session log: 'Plan: 1 task, about CHF 0.09. The first session you approved with the project plan: 1 task in its order.', then 'It promised 3 tasks, about CHF 0.34.', then 'Gave 1 note for the next session to "Build the chess club page in index.html".' at the start of the very session that runs that task. After Add to, the Overview shows 'Waiting for you: approve the plan [Open]' in the header and again as a banner.
finding.expected: Numbers that agree, and one place per fact (design section 5 rules 4 and 10).
finding.evidence: GET /sessions/01a1e80e-d73a-77d6-ab8b-26461a15cecb/events on s2 (05:50:49 session.planned, session.promised, task.notes); screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s2/steps/05-c2-12-add-to-landed.png
finding.repro: New project with a repository and a 3-task brief, Approve and start, read the session's log; then Add to on the same repository and look at the Overview.
finding.suspected_cause: session.planned counts only the approved first-session items, while session.promised counts the tasks the session takes; the project status line and the banner both render the open plan card.

verdict.root_cause:
Both halves come from the code, not from the model.

(1) The session log (Details lines, eventAudience 'detail'). The runner writes two plan facts that count different things, one right after the other. `session.planned` (runner.ts:1796) gives `items: plan.items.length`. StaticPlanner.plan (runner.ts:5480-5510) builds those items from firstSessionPlan(summary, free) (next-session.ts:145-154), which keeps only the approved first-session tasks that are ready now. So 1 of the 3 approved tasks is counted, at CHF 0.09. The summary sentence then says "the first session you approved with the project plan: 1 task in its order", built from the same cut list (runner.ts:5509), although the person approved 3. `session.promised` (runner.ts:1845, worded at event-lines.ts:628-633) counts the plan items plus the followers that fit (3 tasks, CHF 0.34, the plan card's figure). views.ts:773-789 words the first fact and event-lines.ts:628 the second, so the log states the session's size twice, with two different numbers.

(2) The `task.notes` line: views.ts:816-817 always reads 'Gave N note(s) for the next session to "X"'. The note here is the project brief, kept as a queue_item of kind 'note' (01a1e80e-6201-70a2-…, consumed_by_session = this session). In the session that uses it, "for the next session" reads as if the note were for a later session.

(3) Overview after Add to. ProjectPage.tsx:130-137 hides the header status sentence (`planBanner`) only when `progress.total === 0`. IntakeBanner (rendered at ProjectPage.tsx:225, pending branch at IntakeBanner.tsx:110-121) shows "Waiting for you: approve the plan." whatever the task count. project-status.ts:286-291 returns "Waiting for you: approve the plan" [Open] for plan === 'pending', also with no total check. A project that already has tasks and gets a plan-only intake (d1109-onerepo-link's Add to) therefore shows the sentence in the header and again as a banner. The third mention, the Needs you card "Plan for "Site": 2 tasks [Answer]", is what design §3.4 asks for and is not a defect.

The stand-in bench shows the log half too: /tmp/frbench/d1109-selftasks-run-walk/15-standard-session-details-499f.txt:60-64 reads "Plan: 1 task, about CHF 0.03. The first session you approved with the project plan: 1 task in its order." / "It promised 5 tasks, about CHF 0.32." / "Gave 1 note for the next session to …". The live s2 state.sqlite has the same events (seq 5-7) and a plan row whose summary says "1 task" while it holds 3 items and promise.taskIds of 3.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1796 and :5509 (session.planned count and first-session summary from the ready-only cut); packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:773-789 (Plan line) and :816-817 (task.notes words); packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-lines.ts:628-633 (promise line); apps/ui/src/pages/ProjectPage.tsx:130-137, :185, :225; apps/ui/src/pages/project/IntakeBanner.tsx:110-121; packages/runtime/src/daemon/project-status.ts:286-291
verdict.fix_sketch:
Log: state the session's size once, as the promise.
- When a `session.promised` follows, the `session.planned` line should not give a competing count. Either words.ts/views.ts folds it into one line, e.g. 'It promised 3 tasks, about CHF 0.34: "Build…" first; 2 wait on it', and drops the "Plan: N task" line, or the Plan line says 'Ready now: 1 task …'.
- StaticPlanner's first-session summary counts `first.first.taskIds.length` (what the person approved), not the ready cut. Alternatively, the runner passes `promise.taskIds.length` in session.planned and the line uses it.

finding.title: 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.' is read as one thing left to do, so finished research pauses with a card asking for more money instead of going to review
finding.what_the_person_sees:
The research was finished, but the person is asked to pay for another session to 'continue' it, and the screens say one thing is left to do when there is none.
- Inbox card: '"Compare three static site hosts ..." paused before this session's budget ran out', with 'Left to do • nothing the criteria require.' and the button 'Continue (CHF 0.40 more)'.
- Session log and task drawer: '... paused before this session's budget of CHF 0.40 ran out: it spent CHF 0.23 and listed one thing left to do.'
- Tasks row: 'Paused before the session's budget ran out'.
finding.expected: When a wrap-up report says the criteria need nothing more, the run goes to its review and can be done in the same session, with no pause card. This is the l3-handoff-checks / L3-research-1 rule: the session still had CHF 0.17 of its CHF 0.40, and a fifth is kept for reviews.
finding.evidence:
- Model-call log seq 8 (the researcher's last reply) ends: 'Where I stopped: `hosts.md` is complete and meets the three acceptance criteria as I read them. Nothing is half done. ...' and 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.'
- Card lists: [{label:'Left to do', items:['nothing the criteria require.']}].
- Run outcome 'Paused'.
- parseHandoff() run read-only with tsx on the 4cf11fd checkout (/tmp/frbench/live4/pause/scripts/parse-check.mts):
  - 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.' => ['nothing the criteria require.']
  - '- nothing the criteria require.' => ['nothing the criteria require.']
  - 'Left to do: nothing.' => []
  - 'Left to do: nothing for the criteria.' => []
- The continuing run's brief then said 'Left to do ... - "nothing the criteria require." Start with the first item of its list'. That run made no change, and the critic accepted the work. The extra session cost CHF 0.13 for this task.
finding.repro: On bench-live, make a researcher task estimated above the work budget (the researcher's starting estimate is about CHF 0.42) and start a session with CHF 0.40. When the real model ends its wrap-up with 'Left to do: nothing the criteria require.', the task pauses with a Continue card instead of being reviewed.
finding.suspected_cause: The NOTHING regex in packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts only accepts a 'nothing' followed by a preposition (for, in, by, to meet ...) or by punctuation. 'nothing the criteria require' has neither, so isNothing() is false and the line is kept as an item. The wrap-up instruction itself says '(only what the task's criteria still need, as a list with the next step first, or nothing ...)', which invites this phrasing.

verdict.root_cause: The "nothing" detector in parseHandoff has a fixed list of phrasings. `NOTHING` (budget-pause.ts:80-83) accepts nothing/none followed by (a) left/required/needed words, then (b) an ABOUT clause that has to start with a preposition (for, in, by, under, within, to meet/satisfy/...; :76), or (c) punctuation followed by a reason (AFTER, :78). A relative-clause form that has no preposition ("nothing [that] the criteria require", "nothing the task needs") matches none of these. So isNothing() (:92) is false, add() (:176-183) keeps the line, and leftToDo = ["nothing the criteria require."]. executor.ts:1725-1732 then sees result.wrapUpSent && parsed.leftToDo.length > 0 and sets stoppedBy "wrap_up", so the outcome is "paused" instead of a review. That gives the person the budget card with Continue, the log line "listed one thing left to do" (pauseSentence, budget-pause.ts:317), and a continuing brief (task-context.ts:160/218) that says "paused at a budget before its work was done" and "Start with the first item of its list: 'nothing the criteria require.'". The app itself prompts this phrasing: the wrap-up text the model hears (agent/loop.ts:109) and WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE (budget-pause.ts:53) both say "only what the task's criteria still need ... or nothing". ADR 0112 (lines 75-76, 339-348) says a "nothing" about the criteria is nothing and the run is reviewed. I reproduced this read-only with tsx on 4cf11fd. These lines all parse as one item: "nothing the criteria require.", "- nothing the criteria require.", "Nothing the acceptance criteria require.", "nothing the criteria still need.", "nothing that the criteria require.", "nothing the task needs.". These parse as nothing: "nothing required by the criteria.", "nothing for the criteria.", "nothing, the criteria are met.". In the model-call log, seq 8 (session 01a1e81b) ends with exactly "Left to do: nothing the criteria require.". The seq 9 brief quotes it as the first item to start with.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:80-83 (NOTHING; ABOUT at :76 needs a preposition), used by isNothing :92 and add() :176-185; decision at packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1725-1732; the wording that invites it is at packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:109 and budget-pause.ts:53
verdict.fix_sketch: In budget-pause.ts, add a relative-clause alternative to NOTHING after the left/required group: `(?:\s+(?:that|which))?\s+(?:the\s+)?(?:task'?s\s+)?(?:(?:acceptance|three|two|\d+)\s+)?(?:criteri(?:a|on)|brief|task|scope|requirements?|deliverables?)(?:\s+(?:still|yet))?\s+(?:requires?|needs?|asks?\s+for|calls?\s+for|demands?)`. It takes the same optional REASON tail as ABOUT. NOT_NOTHING and ONE_CRITERION stay as they are: "nothing the criteria require yet: tests fail" stays an item, and "nothing criterion 2 needs" says nothing about the rest. WHOLE_SET already matches "criteria", so aboutWholeSet turns the other lines into notes, as under L3-research-1. This is the third live phrasing patched one at a time (W15-14 "Nothing for the acceptance criteria.", L3-research-1 "Nothing is needed for the two criteria: ...", now this one). So also consider a general rule: a Left-to-do line that starts with nothing/none, names the whole set (WHOLE_SET), and has no NOT_NOTHING word is nothing. That needs the existing "Nothing in the task works yet" / "Nothing works yet" cases to stay items; they already do through "yet" in NOT_NOTHING. Optionally, the wording at loop.ts:109 and WRAP_UP_BRIEF_LINE could ask for "the word 'nothing'". The parse fix is the necessary part, because the model will keep adding qualifiers. Update ADR 0112's parse paragraph and the maintainer doc for session/budget-pause.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed test in packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts, next to "a run that hears the wrap-up and lists only 'Nothing for the acceptance criteria.' ... is reviewed and done, with no budget card" (around :1164). Use the same FakeProvider setup, with the researcher's post-wrap-up reply set to live check 4's seq 8 report. That report ends "Where I stopped: `hosts.md` is complete and meets the three acceptance criteria as I read them. Nothing is half done. I did not fetch ...\n\nLeft to do: nothing the criteria require.". Expected: task.status "done", a review exists for the task, run outcomes ["completed"], no "paused before ... ran out" or "listed one thing left to do" line, and GET /inbox has no card for the task. Today the task pauses with a Continue card. Add unit cases to the parseHandoff describe: "Left to do: nothing the criteria require.", "- Nothing the acceptance criteria require.", "Left to do: nothing that the brief still needs." each give leftToDo []. "Left to do: nothing the criteria require yet: the tests fail" stays one item. Optionally add a matching apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts case: no budget card in the Inbox, and the Tasks row shows done, not 'Paused before the session's budget ran out'.

finding.title: The session says 'the budget is used' with CHF 0.17 of its CHF 0.40 left, and the CHF 0.06 task after it does not run
finding.what_the_person_sees:
The same screens say the budget is used and show 58% of it spent.
- Session page: the badge 'Stopped: the budget is used' sits beside 'CHF 0.23 of CHF 0.40 (58%)'.
- Session result: '... The session's budget is used. "Write a one-line tagline for the bakery in tagline.md" waits for your next session: "Compare ..." used the rest of this one. CHF 0.23.'
- More > Sessions row: '"Compare ..." paused before this session's budget of CHF 0.40 ran out.' over '... 1 paused · Stopped: the budget is used · CHF 0.23 on your API key'. The same row says 'before ... ran out' and 'the budget is used'.
finding.expected: Words that are true now (design section 5.4). CHF 0.09 of the CHF 0.32 work budget was still unspent, and the dialog had said the tagline task 'runs if "Compare ..." leaves budget'. Either the next task runs in what is left, or the words say why it does not (for example, that the larger task's run keeps the rest).
finding.evidence:
- c7-run.json session: status 'stopped', stopReason 'budget_exceeded', statusText 'Stopped: the budget is used', spent chfMicro 233586 of budget 400000.
- Screenshots /tmp/frbench/live4/pause/p1/steps/09-c7-20-session-page-ended.png and 30-c5-11-sessions-via-more.png.
- Log: 'This run may spend CHF 0.32: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.25 it is told to wrap up, keeping a reserve of CHF 0.07 to finish.'
finding.repro: Run LC-C7 (a larger task first, a CHF 0.06 task after it, session budget CHF 0.40). The larger task wraps up at CHF 0.21 and pauses at CHF 0.23. The session ends 'the budget is used' and the small task waits.

verdict.root_cause: The session ends on any pause it labels as being at the session's budget, even when most of that budget is still unspent. The runner (runner.ts:3544-3558) ends the session for every paused result where stopEndsSession(source) is true, and budget-pause.ts:241-243 counts source "session" as ending the session. Its comment says "nothing else of it can run there". That is false for a larger task's wrap-up. The larger task's run is capped at what is left of the work budget, so executor.ts:1081 sets runCapSource = "session". A clean wrap-up has no budget error, so executor.ts:1883 (stopSourceOf) keeps "session" as the pause's source. The wrap-up line holds back a reserve of the larger of a fifth of the run cap and two calls (budget.ts:56-66). Here it wrapped at CHF 0.21, paused at CHF 0.23, and left CHF 0.09 of the CHF 0.32 work budget. That is room for the CHF 0.06 tagline task (the re-plan's room, runner.ts:2303-2307, would be 0.09). But the break at :3556 comes before any re-plan. stopReason becomes "budget_exceeded", which shows as "Stopped: the budget is used" (stop-words.ts:138) and "The session's budget is used." (result.ts:257). The task after the larger one keeps its "after_large" reason, so result.ts:440-447 writes oversize-words.ts:145-148's "... used the rest of this one". The tests lock this in: oversized-task.test.ts:362-369 and :391-393 assert "waits for your next session: ... used the rest of this one" after a wrap-up pause, without checking how much is left. The run C plan (d1109-oversize-pause decisions) assumed a pause at the session's budget means the work budget is used. It lists only done, failed, paused at its own budget, and paused without progress as the cases where the re-plan takes the tasks after it. That breaks design 4.2 (the session stops only when nothing can run or the budget is used), 5.4 ("true now") and 5.9 (the Start dialog's "it runs if ... leaves budget"). It also misses the owner's option C ("spare budget isn't wasted").
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3544-3558 (with budget-pause.ts:241-243, executor.ts:1081 and :1883, result.ts:440-447, oversize-words.ts:145-148)
verdict.fix_sketch: In the runner's paused branch (runner.ts:3544), end the session at a "session" source only when the session really cannot take more work. That is when the run was refused at the session cap (result.errorCode budget_exceeded at level session), or budget.noNewWork is set, or budget.workRemainingUsdMicro() is below the smallest after_large estimate. For a wrap-up pause (budgetStop.stoppedBy === "wrap_up") with room left, keep the card and the needs_human row as today. Then hand the larger task's after_large items to the re-plan, as takeLarger's no_room path does at :2152-2153 ("after_others"), and continue the loop so the queue-empty re-plan (cutPlanToBudget with the room left) takes those that fit. If one still does not fit, the result says so in true words, e.g. '"B" (about CHF 0.06) waits for your next session: "Compare ..." left CHF 0.03 of this one.' Never say "used the rest" or "The session's budget is used" while spent is under the work budget. The status sentence should follow the real reason, e.g. the needs-your-decision stop. Update the plan wording in runner.ts:5335 and oversize-words.ts, and change the composed tests at oversized-task.test.ts:362-369 and :391-393 so they assert on the room actually left.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed real-runtime test with the stand-in provider in packages/runtime/test/oversized-task.test.ts, describe 'd1109-oversize-pause'. Ready tasks: Big at high priority, larger than the work budget, and a small B whose estimate is under a fifth of the work budget. The stand-in wraps up Big early, so its pause leaves more than B's estimate of the work budget unspent; assert that through the ledger (session spent < work budget − B's estimate). Expect task.started events [Big, B] in the same session, B done, and Big needs_human with one card. Also expect the session's stopReason not "budget_exceeded", and neither the result nor GET /sessions/:id containing "used the rest of this one", "The session's budget is used" or "Stopped: the budget is used". Mirror it in a real-daemon POST /sessions case and the Sessions-row UI test (no row saying both "paused before ... ran out" and "the budget is used"). Today it fails: B stays ready and the session stops "budget_exceeded" at 58% of its budget.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-oversize-pause
verdict.notes: The code fully explains the evidence: c7-run.json shows stopReason budget_exceeded with 233586 of 400000 spent, and the log shows the run told to wrap up at CHF 0.21 against a CHF 0.25 line with a CHF 0.07 reserve. The live run used the real model (provider bench-live), but the path is deterministic and does not depend on the model: any larger task that wraps up cleanly at the session's work budget ends the session with its reserve unspent, so the tasks behind it never get the room it leaves. They run in this session only if the larger task finishes or fails. The journey's own check 'the small task did not run (still ready, no run)' passed because the script encodes run C's acceptance (OP-0: B 'used the rest of this one'), which is the same wrong assumption. I did not re-run it on the stand-in; the run C plan text, the code path and the existing composed tests agree. The contradictory Sessions row ('paused before this session's budget of CHF 0.40 ran out' beside 'Stopped: the budget is used') has the same cause: the card label is true, the session's stop reason is not. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it. CL-13..16 (C2) are other oversize-pause items. Minor: the small task only waits for the next Start, but three screens state something untrue about money, and the Start dialog's promise is broken.

finding.title: The session's Details count the plan two ways: 'It promised 2 tasks', then '0 of 1 planned task done'
finding.what_the_person_sees:
Session page > Details shows three lines that count the plan differently:
- 'Plan: "Compare ..." (about CHF 0.42), larger than this session's work budget: it works until that budget is used. 2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget).'
- 'It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32.'
- 'Session review measured: 0 of 1 planned task done; the planned tasks cost CHF 0.23 against an estimate of CHF 0.32.'
finding.expected: One count of what the session planned and promised, consistent across the Details lines (design section 5: no numbers that disagree).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/pause/p1/steps/c7-run.json notes.logLines; screenshot 10-c7-21-session-page-details.png
finding.repro: Start a session with a larger task first and a small task after it (LC-C7) and open Details on the session page.

verdict.root_cause:
The code counts the task that waits behind the larger one (`after_large`) three different ways:
(1) In `cutPlanToBudget`, every `leftOutForBudget` item goes into the summary clause "(N item cut to fit the budget)", and that includes the `after_large` ones (runner.ts:5376-5380). So the Plan line says "2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget)". But the Start dialog, and OP-0's design, say that task is the session's own and "runs after it only if budget is left". It was never cut.
(2) The promise is built from `first = plan.items + afterLarge` (runner.ts:1731-1751) and emitted as session.promised (runner.ts:1844-1849). So "It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32" counts 2. The 0.32 is only the larger task's room.
(3) The session review's planned set comes only from `planItemsOf(session.plan)`, which reads `plan.items` (critic/src/session-review.ts:136-156, :207 and :346-352). The `after_large` task is in `leftOutForBudget`/`promise`, not in `items`. So views.ts:854 prints "0 of 1 planned task done". The run indicator showed "(0 of 2 done)" during the same session.
I reproduced this with tsx against the code at 4cf11fd (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-pause-3/cut.mts). `cutPlanToBudget([big 0.47, small 0.03], 0.355)` gives items `[big]`, `small` as `after_large`, and summary "2 ready tasks in priority order (1 item cut to fit the budget)". `describeEvent` then gives "It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32." and "Session review measured: 0 of 1 planned task done; ..." for the same plan. These are exactly the three Details lines in the evidence. The app produced this deterministically. The model's choices played no part.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:5376-5380 (cut clause counts after_large); packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1731-1751 (promise = items + afterLarge); packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:136-156 and :346-352 (planned = plan.items only); packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:854 (the 'N of M planned' line)
verdict.fix_sketch:
Use the promise as the one count for this kind of session.
(a) In `cutPlanToBudget`, count only the items left out for `no_room` or `after_others` in "(N cut to fit the budget)". Name the `after_large` items as the dialog does, e.g. "(1 comes after it if budget is left)", or drop the clause for them. The session.planned line then agrees with the dialog and the promise.
(b) In `loadSessionReviewData` and `runSessionReviewChecks`, make the planned set `plan.items` ∪ `plan.promise.taskIds` (at least the `after_large` ids; the promise is already stored on the plan row via setPlan). Then the metric reads "0 of 2 planned tasks done", like "It promised 2 tasks" and the run indicator's "(0 of 2 done)". Keep the estimate as the promise's figure (CHF 0.32). A promised task that never ran must not be graded as a plan defect, or "Plan item references a task" findings would start to fire.
Alternative: the metric line says "of the 2 tasks it promised". Either way there should be one number.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Composed test in packages/runtime/test/oversized-task.test.ts, describe 'd1109-oversize-pause' (or real-daemon GET /sessions/:id/events, which feeds Session page > Details):
- Set up ready tasks Big (estimate above the work budget) then Small, with a session budget of CHF 0.40 (work budget CHF 0.32).
- The stand-in makes Big pause at the session's budget, so Small never runs.
- Read the Details lines through eventView.
Assert:
- the session.planned line does not contain "cut to fit the budget";
- the session.promised line is "It promised 2 tasks, about CHF 0.32.";
- the critic.session_review_metrics line contains "0 of 2 planned tasks done".
Today the first and third assertions fail ("(1 item cut to fit the budget)", "0 of 1 planned task done").
Unit companion: `cutPlanToBudget([Big 6.00, A 0.40], 4.00).summary` has no "cut" clause, while `[A 3.50, Big 6.00, B 0.30]` still says "(1 item cut to fit the budget)".
verdict.area_hint: d1109-oversize-pause
verdict.notes:
Evidence matches: /tmp/frbench/live4/pause/p1/steps/10-c7-21-session-page-details.txt and c7-run.json notes.logLines show the three lines verbatim. The Start dialog (06-c7-10) and the header after Start ("Working on ... (0 of 2 done)") both treat the small task as part of this session. That makes "1 item cut" and "of 1 planned" the odd ones out.
Design core-experience.md §5 has no literal "no numbers that disagree" rule. The finding's paraphrase best fits rule 4 (true now) and rule 9 (no promise the code does not keep): calling a promised task "cut" contradicts the dialog.
This happens only when a larger task has tasks after it (`after_large`). In the plain `after_others` case, cut items are not promised, so the "cut" clause is true there.
All three lines are under Details (internal events), so minor rather than major.
No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it. The nearest are C5L-23 (wording of a promise kept after Cancel) and C3-left-5 (promise test gaps); neither covers it.
The tasks.md cost figure CHF 0.23 versus the estimate CHF 0.32 is consistent; that part is not a defect.

finding.title: Costs > By task reads 'Accepted 1 / 2 (50%)' for a task whose only review accepted it
finding.what_the_person_sees: Costs > By task: 'Compare three static site hosts ... | 2 | 1 / 2 (50%) | CHF 0.36 | CHF 0.36'. The first run paused at the session's budget and was never reviewed. The critic reviewed once and accepted the work. The 50% reads as if half the work was rejected.
finding.expected: A paused run that a later run finished is not counted as a run the critic did not accept, or the column says what it counts.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/pause/p1/steps/19-c8-12-costs.txt line 45. GET /costs byTask {runs:2, accepted:1}. The drawer's runs are: Paused (CHF 0.23), Finished (CHF 0.03), review Finished (CHF 0.10).
finding.repro: After LC-C7 and LC-C8, open More > Costs on the project.

verdict.root_cause: The code produces this result every time. In costFacts (packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1461-1468), every non-critic Run row of a task counts as a "run", whatever its outcome: runsByTask at :1464, runsByModel at :1467, and the specialist's run set at :1446. The paused run (outcome `paused`, ADR 0112 clean pause) is counted too. Only the last work run before each accepting review counts as accepted (:1412-1426, `before` at :1423). costView then sets By task runs=2 and accepted=1 (:1264-1265). CostsTab renders `${accepted} / ${runs} (%)` (apps/ui/src/pages/project/CostsTab.tsx:53-55), and its header tooltip reads "Accepted by the critic / runs" (:38). So a run the critic never saw shows as a run the critic did not accept. ADR 0112 point 5 says the opposite: "A paused run gets no critic and no failed try ... neither is a sample". Spec I.6 / billing's own allocation defines the success rate as accepted / (accepted + rejected), null until decided (packages/billing/src/ledger.ts:91, :562-574). The live evidence matches this exactly. c8-run.json has costs.byTask {runs:2, accepted:1}, bySpecialist researcher {runs:2, accepted:1} and byModel {runs:3, accepted:2}. The drawer shows: researcher Paused CHF 0.23, researcher Finished CHF 0.03, and one critic review Finished CHF 0.10. The same paused run also pulls down "the researcher 1 / 2 (50%)" and "claude-sonnet-5-5 2 / 3 (67%)" on the same screen. The existing real-daemon case ("Broken page check" runs 2, accepted 1) covers a failed first try, where 1/2 is right. Nothing tells a paused-then-continued run apart from a failed one.

finding.title: On the real fast model, chat mostly skips recall and says recorded things do not exist
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'There is no README task in Quote Page's task list ... The nearest is "Write the deploy notes" ... If you meant an earlier task with that name, I can search the records for it.' / 'I can't see a licence choice in what I have for Quote Page ... I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?' / 'I haven't set any budget in this conversation' (chat itself replied 'I set the budget to CHF 2.00.') / 'I found no record of you saying anything else about the logo in this conversation' ('Das Logo bleibt dunkelblau' is recorded) / 'I can't see a merge date for the README ... Should I do that?' / in Recipe site: 'There was no card about the first page in this project, so there is nothing we said about one.'
finding.expected: The chat prompt says 'Look it up before you say you do not have it'. The user guide says 'Chat looks up what Forerunner recorded when the answer is not in front of it'. LC-C10 passes when the right record is named with its date in at least 10 of 12 past questions and no reply says a recorded thing is missing.
finding.evidence: c10-quote.json and the model-call log: in Quote Page 1 of 11 past questions called recall (06:10:36, recall {kinds:[sessions], from 2026-11-09, to 2026-11-15}); the others were single Haiku calls with no tool. Score: 3 of 12 right with date, 4 right without date, 5 'not there'. With 'search the records: when was the README merged?' recall found it: 'The README was merged on Tue 10 Nov. The task was called "Write the README" then'. In Bakery 2 of 2 past questions called recall and were right.
finding.repro: Seed recall-home into a bench-live home (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/scripts/seed-recall.mts), open Quote Page's Chat and ask 'what happened to the README task?', 'which licence did we choose?', 'what did I say about the logo?', 'what did you set the budget to?' and 'when was the README merged?'.
finding.suspected_cause: claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low treats the turn's context (# Tasks with current titles, lessons, doc excerpts, the last 12 turns) as complete. Nothing in code makes a lookup before a 'not found' answer; the rule is in the prompt only.

verdict.root_cause:
The design makes looking things up entirely the model's choice, and the model the app picks for chat (claude-haiku-5-5, effort low, thinking off) mostly does not look. The model-call log (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl) confirms it: recall and recall_open were offered in all 37-tool requests, but in Quote Page only seq 7 (p3, 'last week') called recall. Every other past question was a single end_turn call with no tool. Two things in the app make that choice likely and leave it unchecked.

(1) The prompt the app sends gives the model a way out. conversation-agent.md:14 says 'You answer fast and short from what you are given'. :38 lists the lookup tools as tasks_list, task_get, session_last and files_list, without recall. :68 says 'If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through', and the replies follow that shape exactly ('Nothing in its tasks, open questions or the last session mentions one. I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look...?'). CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) opens with 'The first message holds what is true now: this project's tasks...' and 'Answer questions about now from the first message without a lookup'. To a low-effort model, 'what happened to the README task?' and 'which licence did we choose?' read as task-list questions about now.

(2) No code backstops the rule. agent.ts:2029-2090 guards only claims that something changed or that a yes was asked for (claimOf/claimNudge, the l3-chat-claims fix for the same kind of live miss). Nothing compares a 'not there / can't find / I found no record / should I look?' reply with the turn's recall calls. The facts' task lines (agent.ts:2914) also carry only current titles, so the renamed task ('Write the README', now 'Write the guide') is invisible without recall. That accounts for p2, p9 and x1.

Retrieval itself works. recall-rank.test.ts (the golden set on the same recall-home fixture, including the README, merge date, licence, logo and budget questions) passes at 4cf11fd. The explicit 'search the records: ...' and 'yes, look it up' turns found the right records.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:14, :38, :68; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:617 (CHAT_RECALL_RULES, a rule in the prompt only); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2029-2090 (guards change claims only, not absence claims); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2914 (task facts with current titles only)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. A code backstop beside the claim guard, in ConversationAgent.chat at agent.ts about 2029-2090, built like claimOf/claimNudge:
   - Add absenceOf(text) in claims.ts. It matches English and German absence or offer-to-search wording: 'there is no', 'I can't see/find', 'I found no record', 'nothing ... mentions', 'I haven't searched', 'Should I look', 'keine ... gefunden', 'nicht gefunden'.
   - When the turn offered recall and called neither recall nor recall_open, nudge once within CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS with a RECALL_NUDGE text: 'You said it is not there without looking it up. Call recall now with the person's words and other words for it (an earlier name, another language), then answer. Never ask whether to look.' Use the step line 'Looking it up…' and do not stream the reply that triggered the nudge.
   - If there is still no lookup, code runs recall with the line's words (as the stand-in's recallWords does) and either hands the hits to one more step or replaces the reply with what was looked through.
   - Log the guard on the chat.reply row.
2. The prompt (conversation-agent.md 1.4.1, CHAT_RECALL_RULES asserted verbatim again):
   - Line 14: '...from what you are given and what you look up'.
   - Line 38: add recall and recall_open to the lookup tools.
   - Line 68: 'If what you were given does not hold the answer, look it up with recall in this turn; if recall finds nothing, say what you looked through.'
   - CHAT_RECALL_RULES: add 'Never offer to search or ask whether to look: look it up in this turn. A question about a task, decision, card, document or something said that the first message does not answer needs a lookup.'
3. Cheap, deterministic: a task line in the facts names an earlier title from the change_log, e.g. '"Write the guide" (earlier "Write the README"): Merged', so a renamed task is answered from now.

verdict.notes:
Checked against the evidence. The model-call log shows recall offered on every call and called once in 11 past questions in Quote Page. In Bakery the model did call it, 2 of 2: the model looks when a question names a time or a card answer, and skips when the facts hold something nearby (the task list, a doc excerpt, a lesson).

Two parts of the score come partly from the fixture.
- p8 (budget): the seeded reply 'I set the budget to CHF 2.00.' was written with actions [] (testenv/src/bench/recall-home.ts:111, :476-489), so by the prompt's own 'The app did:' rule that reply changed nothing. It had also scrolled out of the 12-turn window. So 'nothing has changed' is half right; 'I haven't set any budget in this conversation' is still a false statement about what chat said.
- p7 (logo): the content came out right (dark blue, from the lesson and docs/brand.md). The false part is 'I found no record of you saying anything else', said without a search.

Clear misses: p2, p6, p9, plus x1 and x3. x3 is the hosting decision 'Where is the page published? Only as a local file for now', which is recorded and was not looked up.

The model's own replies say 'I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look?', so it saw the tool and chose to ask. That is why I hold the prompt's competing wording and the missing guard responsible, not the model alone. A 'yes' to that offer then gets 'Yes to what?'; that is a separate finding (likely L4-chat-2).

No leftover names this. CL-11 (leftovers-C2) only says 'LC-C10 watches the real model's choice', and it is about ranking and which hit gets opened.

finding.title: 'yes' to chat's own question is answered 'Yes to what?'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Chat: 'I haven't searched the earlier conversation and decisions yet. Should I look for it?' Person: 'yes'. Chat: 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' Same after 'This plan needs the stronger model, which costs more and asks you first. Should I go ahead?'.
finding.expected: A yes to the question chat just asked does what the question offered: it looks the record up, or shows the stronger model's ask with Go ahead. Otherwise chat should not end a reply with a yes/no question it cannot take a yes to.
finding.evidence: c10-follow.json f1 (0 model calls, 219 ms); c13b.json e2; screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png shows 'yes' / 'Yes to what?' under the model's 'Should I go ahead?'.
finding.repro: In a chat where Haiku answers 'Should I look for it?' (e.g. ask 'which licence did we choose?' in Quote Page), type 'yes'.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts around line 1215: a bare 'yes' with no read-back card and no live offer gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY and never reaches the model. The model is free to end replies with its own yes/no questions.

verdict.root_cause: ConversationAgent.chat answers every bare yes itself, before any model call, whenever the app has nothing of its own waiting: no read-back card, and no app-made go_ahead offer on the newest reply. The check is `else if (this.deps.commands && isYes(req.text) && !liveOffer(earlier)) return finish(await this.nothingWaitingReply(earlier), …)`. `liveOffer` (agent.ts:893-896) only knows `reply.offer.action === "go_ahead"`. `nothingWaitingReply` (:2592-2605) only knows `pendingId`. A question the model writes into its own reply text ("Should I look for it?", "Should I go ahead?") is invisible to both, so the yes gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (:527) with 0 calls. The app's own prompt makes those questions likely and promises the model it will see the yes: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md says '"It", "that", "yes" … refer to them [your earlier replies]' and tells voice to offer "more?". The facts' thinking_longer line "asks the person first" (agent.ts:1721, depth.ts thinkingLongerFact) led Haiku to write its own ask line in d2 and e1 without calling answer_thoroughly, so only the generic Think-it-through offer was attached and no go_ahead existed. The design line "'yes' with no card ('Yes to what?')" (core-experience.md:254) was written for a chat whose only questions were the app's cards. With the model now asking its own questions, the reply "Nothing is waiting for your yes" sits right under a visible question, which breaks §5 rule 4 (true now). Reproduced on the stand-in: a FakeProvider reply ending "Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?", then "yes", gives exactly YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY with provider.calls = 1 (/tmp/frbench/l4chat2/yes.test.ts, passes at 4cf11fd). The live evidence matches: c10-follow f1 has 0 calls in 219 ms, and c13b e2 has 0 calls. Typing "yes, look it up" (f2) gets past the isYes regex, and the model then does the right thing (recall, then the answer).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1215
verdict.fix_sketch: At agent.ts:1215, a bare yes goes to the model, with its history, when the newest turn is a model answer that ends with a question and has nothing of the app's on it: not a notice, no pendingId, no actions, no go_ahead offer. Keep "Yes to what?" (and the answered-elsewhere and expired lines) only when the newest reply asked nothing. One way to do this is a helper `modelAsked(earlier)` that checks the newest reply's text without its read-back with /\?\s*$/, used as `isYes(req.text) && !liveOffer(earlier) && !modelAsked(earlier)`. This is safe: a yes that reaches the model still cannot change anything without a command, and every change is read back ("A question in reply is not a yes"; the claim guard). The model then does what it offered: it calls recall, or it calls answer_thoroughly, which gives the app's real ask line with figures and Go ahead. Also: (a) reword the thinking_longer 'asks' fact so it tells the model to call answer_thoroughly and let the app ask, for example "asks the person first: call answer_thoroughly; the app asks under your answer", so the model stops writing its own "Should I go ahead?"; (b) optionally add to conversation-agent.md: "Do not end with an offer to look something up: look it up." Mirror the rule in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts:4428, and update docs/design/core-experience.md §3.9 and user-guide.md:400 ("yes" with no card and no question from chat).
verdict.failing_test_idea: Runtime composed test (conversation-memory.test.ts or chat-recall.test.ts), with an apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts case through POST /projects/:id/chat. The stand-in answers "which licence did we choose?" with "I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier notes and decisions for it?". Then "yes" is posted. Expect a second model call whose messages hold that question and the "yes", the stand-in calling recall, and the reply being its found answer, not YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (fails today: the reply is "Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes." with 1 call). Second case: the stand-in writes "This plan needs the stronger model … Should I go ahead?" with no tool call. "yes" then reaches the model, the model calls answer_thoroughly, and the reply ends with the app's ask line and Go ahead. Keep as regressions: "yes" after a plain statement reply, and "yes" with nothing before it, still give YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY with 0 calls. "yes" under a waiting card still answers the card.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth (owns the typed-yes path for offers: liveOffer, acceptedOffer and the thinking_longer fact in agent.ts), with d1109-chat-recall's "Should I look for it?" as the other trigger; a small fix area "chat-yes-to-own-question" would also fit
verdict.notes: The leftovers only touch this: C3L-8 (a stale app ask line, after another line has followed, makes a typed yes answer nothing) is the app-offer version of the same dead end, and LL-10 is about the language of YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY. Neither names a yes to the model's own question. Two model choices sit next to this finding but are not it: in c10-quote, Haiku never called recall and ended 8 of 20 replies with "Should I look…?", against the prompt's "Look it up before you say you do not have it". In d2 and e1 it never called answer_thoroughly. Those may be their own findings, but the dead end after a yes is the app's code, and the app's prompt (conversation-agent.md: "yes" refers to earlier replies) and the facts line make the question likely. Severity is major: it is the core chat journey, the question pattern is frequent with Haiku, and the reply contradicts the question just above it. The workaround (typing "yes, look it up") is not obvious. Repro file: /tmp/frbench/l4chat2/yes.test.ts with /tmp/frbench/l4chat2/vitest.config.ts. Run it from the worktree with `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --config /tmp/frbench/l4chat2/vitest.config.ts`.

finding.title: The real chat model never calls answer_thoroughly; depth questions get quick answers or a hand-over announced in words only
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'make a plan for the next two sessions' got 'This is a plan question across several sessions, so I can hand it to the stronger model. It asks you first, since it costs more. Should I go ahead?' with no cost, no time and no Go ahead button. 'review the decisions for conflicts' got 'That is the only conflict I found' (colours), but the recorded decisions 'No photos of members' (14 Nov) and gallery 'Yes, with their names' (15 Nov) conflict too. The failure question with the failed-task card waiting never gets 'This needs a stronger model: ... Go ahead?'.
finding.expected: LC-C13: answer_thoroughly on at least 3 of the 4 depth lines. The C3 fix-up: the failure question in a project with a failed task and a waiting card gets the stronger model's ask line with Go ahead.
finding.evidence: c13.json and c13c.json: answer_thoroughly called 0 of 4 times on depth lines and 0 of 3 times on the failure question (d1, r1, r2). It was offered in every call's tools. The only ask line came from the explicit 'use a stronger model:' prefix (e3). Plan question announced in words twice (d2, e1). The d1 answer itself was correct (task_get; the cause from the reports; two next steps).
finding.repro: Seed Garden club (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/scripts/seed-c11-c13.mts) on bench-live, then in its Chat ask: 'why does "Write the welcome page" keep failing and what should I change?', 'make a plan for the next two sessions', 'compare the last two sessions', 'review the decisions for conflicts'.
finding.suspected_cause: The hand-over depends on the fast model choosing the tool. Haiku at effort low answers alone or describes the hand-over in text. No app-side detection of depth questions on the default path.

verdict.root_cause:
On the default path, the only thing that can start a hand-over is the fast model picking answer_thoroughly. That model is Haiku 5.5 at effort low with thinking disabled (agent.ts:1813), with 37 tools and a role prompt that opens "You answer fast and short from what you are given" (conversation-agent.md:14). The app never notices a depth question on its own, by design (ADR 0114 "Who decides": no keyword routing beyond the person's phrases). Code alone does not prove the model will never call the tool. What the code does explain is the brief making the wrong choice likely on every C13 line.

In Garden club the failed task's card is listed in full, so turn.recordsRead is set. agent.ts:1711-1721 therefore writes "- thinking_longer: asks the person first" into # Now on every typed turn there. This is confirmed in the logged requests for d1, d2, d4 and r1 (model-calls.jsonl rows 46, 48, 52, 57). The tool's definition (depth.ts:332) ends "The facts' thinking_longer line says whether it is available now." That line has no subject (depth.ts:376), so it reads as an instruction to the model: ask the person first, in words, instead of calling the tool. The real replies repeat it almost word for word: d2 "...so I can hand it to the stronger model. It asks you first, since it costs more. Should I go ahead?" and e1 "This plan needs the stronger model, which costs more and asks you first. Should I go ahead?". No tool was called, so no offer was stored, and the typed "yes" got "Yes to what?". On the failure lines (d1, r1, r2) and on d4 the model just answered from the card and the history.

Evidence that this is not a test artefact: the API request body (creds/c25-proxy/bodies/4-req.json) carries answer_thoroughly with its full definition and its enum schema. Across all 76 logged chat calls in c1, not one reply calls it. Only the person's own phrases ("use a stronger model:", "think it through:") and the Think it through button ever went deeper.

The stand-in cannot show this. role-player.ts:1673-1681 and :1710-1716 call answer_thoroughly from a regex on exactly these lines ("keep failing", "compare", "plan for/the next", "review", "last two sessions"). The composed test chat-depth.test.ts:1135-1160 scripts the FakeProvider to call it too. So every acceptance test for the need-based hand-over passes against a model behaviour the real fast model does not show, and no eval covers conversation-agent (evals/registry/evals has only coder and researcher).

Severity is major. The owner's D3 ("escalates effort or model selectively ... when the question needs it") and U-094's Check in the app fail on the default setting: 0 of 4 depth lines and 0 of 3 failure questions handed over. The plan question shows a "Should I go ahead?" with no button, and a "yes" to it is answered "Yes to what?". The review question gets an incomplete answer: it missed the photos-versus-gallery conflict. It is not a blocker: the quick answers to d1 and d3 were correct, and the explicit phrases and the Think it through button work.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1711-1722 (thinking_longer "asks" on every turn with recordsRead), packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:332 and :376 (tool definition defers to the subject-less facts line), packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1907-1950 and :1813 (sole trigger is the fast model's tool choice at low effort, thinking off), evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:14 and :49-56; testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:1673-1716 (stand-in regex plays the hand-over the real model never makes)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1) Words, so the model is never the one who asks:
- Make thinking_longer's "asks" value say who acts, e.g. "available: call answer_thoroughly; the app asks the person with the cost (never ask in your own words)".
- Drop "says whether it is available now" from ANSWER_THOROUGHLY_DESCRIPTION. Add: "Never offer a stronger model or ask 'Should I go ahead?' yourself: call this tool; the app writes the ask."
- Add the same line to conversation-agent.md's Thinking longer section (1.5.0), and update the verbatim assertions.

2) An app-side backstop (an ADR 0114 amendment, since the ADR rules out keyword routing):
- Move the stand-in's need patterns into depth.ts as needOfLine(text) → Why | null. Cover why ... fail(ed)/keep(s) failing, a plan for/the next, compare, review ... for, the last two/three sessions, and German siblings.
- When a typed quick pass ends without answer_thoroughly and needOfLine finds a need, run the tool's gate in code: spoken, quick, injection, room, rung, the ask rule. A lookup by the quick pass does not refuse here, because the offer spends nothing.
- If the need's rung asks first (the stronger model, or more than the person's amount), attach the stored offer: the ask line with Go ahead under the quick answer, so a typed yes or Go ahead runs it. If it would go ahead, attach only Think it through; a pattern never spends on its own.
- Add a words-only-offer guard next to the claim guard. A quick reply that offers a hand-over in words ("stronger model", "hand it", "Should I go ahead?") with no stored offer gets the real offer, or the sentence is replaced, so the yes is answerable.

3) Add a stand-in mode in which the fast model answers alone on depth lines, so the backstop is tested at the bench boundary. Add a conversation-agent eval of LC-C13's 4 depth and 4 quick lines for the live check.

4. A words test: the facts line for an asking turn and ANSWER_THOROUGHLY_DESCRIPTION do not tell the model to ask the person itself.

Each case fails today at 4cf11fd: no offer is stored when the model never calls the tool, and the words-only ask leaves "Yes to what?". The real-daemon twin goes in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts "d1109-chat-depth" on the stand-in, in its answer-alone mode.

finding.title: The stronger model's answer says it could not use the stronger model, under a footer saying it did
finding.what_the_person_sees: After 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.29 (at most CHF 0.57) and 30 seconds. Go ahead?' and Go ahead: 'Here's a plan from the tasks as they stand. I couldn't hand it to the stronger model, so this comes from what I have. Nothing has changed. ...' with the footer 'Thought it through with Sonnet · 6 s · CHF 0.04'.
finding.expected: The paid thorough answer reads as the thorough answer. It never claims the stronger model was not used (design §5 rule 9: no promises the code does not keep).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png. Model-call log 06:20:25.572Z: claude-sonnet-5-5, medium, USD 0.048816, no tool calls, no lookup. Its system still holds '## Thinking longer: answer_thoroughly hands a question to a stronger model' while the tool is not offered. Its facts say 'thinking_longer: asks the person first'. Its history ends with Haiku's 'This plan needs the stronger model ... Should I go ahead?', 'yes', 'Yes to what?'.
finding.repro: Garden club Chat: 'make a plan for the next two sessions', 'yes', then 'use a stronger model: make a plan for the next two sessions', then press Go ahead.
finding.suspected_cause: The thorough pass reuses the quick turn's system section about handing over, and its facts line, without saying it is the stronger model. The earlier hand-over talk in history then leads it to deny the hand-over.

verdict.root_cause:
After the person presses Go ahead, the thorough pass gets a request that tells the stronger model nothing about who it is. Several parts of that request point it toward "the hand-over did not happen":
(1) The facts say `thinking_longer: asks the person first`. That line was worked out for this turn's quick pass (agent.ts:1706-1722), and the thorough pass reuses the same `volatile` (agent.ts:1829, thoroughRequest(volatile)). So it is no longer true once the person has said yes, which breaks design §5 rule 4 "True now" for status text given to the chat model.
(2) On an accepted offer, the question is the offer's question (agent.ts:1412). The last message is therefore the question again plus the facts (agent.ts:1645-1648), sitting right after the history's "This needs a stronger model: … Go ahead?". The person's "Go ahead." never appears anywhere the model can see it.
(3) The system part is the full role prompt, including "## Thinking longer: `answer_thoroughly` hands a question to a stronger model … when it answers 'Not now' or 'Not yet', answer briefly from what you have" (evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:49-57). This is on purpose, for cache sharing, and asserted in chat-depth.test.ts:924. But the thorough tool list has no answer_thoroughly, and CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES (depth.ts:359) only says "This question was handed to you to think through". It never says "you are the stronger model the person said yes to" or "answer_thoroughly is not yours".
The live request (model-calls.jsonl line 54, claude-sonnet-5-5 at medium effort, 36 tools without answer_thoroughly, no tool calls) carries all three. The reply echoes the role prompt's refusal wording ("this comes from what I have"), so the app's brief made this choice likely. It is not the model on its own. Earlier Haiku turns in the history ("I can hand it to the stronger model … Should I go ahead?", then "yes" answered with "Yes to what?") made it worse. Those are separate quick-pass findings. The run C plan said the thorough pass "reuses the facts the fast pass built" and never covered the stale line. No test checks what a thorough request says about the pass itself, because the composed tests script the replies.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1722 (volatile carries the quick pass's thinking_longer) and :1829 (the thorough pass reuses it); agent.ts:1631-1648 (thoroughRequest: role prompt with '## Thinking longer' + CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES; messages = history + question); agent.ts:1412 (an accepted offer's question replaces 'Go ahead.', so the yes is never shown); packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:359 (CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES does not say it is the closer look / stronger model the person chose); evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:49-57
verdict.fix_sketch:
Give the thorough pass its own true facts, and say in its rules who it is.
(a) In thoroughPass, build the pass's volatile by replacing the thinking_longer line with a pass line. For example `withNowFact(context.volatile, "this_answer", thoroughFact(...))`, giving "- this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to (at most CHF 0.57)", or "the longer look on this model". Say "the person pressed Go ahead" when the pass is an accepted offer. Never send "asks the person first" to a pass that is already running. Put the sentence in depth.ts next to thinkingLongerFact and assert it verbatim.
(b) Extend CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES (depth.ts:359). It sits in the system part, so it stays cache-stable across thorough passes. Add something like: "You are that closer look: the stronger model or longer effort the app chose or the person said yes to. answer_thoroughly and the 'Thinking longer' section are the quick pass's, not yours. Never say you could not hand it over or that a stronger model was not used."
(c) Optionally, scope the role prompt's "## Thinking longer" to "on the quick pass, when the tool is offered" (bump conversation-agent.md to 1.4.1 and update the verbatim test).
Keep the fast request byte-identical (the R-chatcache tests).
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Composed, in packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts, at the model-request boundary: chat "use a stronger model: make a plan for the next two sessions", then w.chat("Go ahead.", { offer }). Take the one fake-sonnet thorough request. Its last message must NOT contain "- thinking_longer: asks the person first" and must contain the pass line (e.g. "- this_answer: the closer look on Sonnet the person said yes to"). Its system must end with the extended CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES saying it is the closer look and that answer_thoroughly is not its tool. A sibling case does the same for a quick-pass hand-over that went ahead (why: plan) and for Think it through (longer rung: "on this model"). Today the first assertion fails: the live request at 06:20:25.572Z carries the stale line.
For the person's boundary, add an LC-C13 live-check step: after Go ahead on the stronger-model ask, the answer never says the stronger model was not used, and the footer names Sonnet.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes:
Confirmed against the real request in /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, line 54 (seq at 06:20:25.572Z, runId 01a1e829-f24b-…:thorough). The bench setup.log ties this run to 4cf11fd.
- The system is conversation-agent 1.4.0 with "## Thinking longer", ending in "# Thinking it through".
- The tool list has 36 tools and no answer_thoroughly.
- The history ends with the user's "use a stronger model: …" and then the app's "This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.29 (at most CHF 0.57) and 30 seconds. Go ahead?". The final user message is the same question plus "# Now … - thinking_longer: asks the person first". The person's "Go ahead." is never in the request.
- The footer is correct. The app did run Sonnet at medium, for USD 0.0488 (CHF 0.04). Only the model's sentence is false.
