finding.title: Recall's card hit leaves out what the card asked, so chat says the record does not say it
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'It is not clearly about a first page, and it is no longer open. No card about the first page was found, and nothing in the records says what the writer asked there.' The card asked 'Which recipes go on the first page?'.
finding.expected: A card's hit line carries its question (as recall_open's 'It asked: ...' does), so a recall-only answer can say what was asked.
finding.evidence: Model-call log, the tool result for recall {words:'card first page', kinds:[cards, conversation]}: 'r6 [card, Mon 16 Nov, Recipe site, weak] "Write the index page" needs your answers: You answered "your answers". Answer: The three soups. (you)'. recall_open of the same card shows 'It asked: The writer asks: Which recipes go on the first page? ...'.
finding.repro: Recipe site Chat (seed-c11-c13.mts): 'look it up: what did the writer ask on the card about the first page, and what did we say about that card?'
finding.suspected_cause: The cards kind of recall builds the hit from the card's title and outcome, not its question.

verdict.root_cause: cardHits builds a card hit's visible line from the Inbox title plus `detail`, and `detail` holds only the Answered outcome and the answer (recall.ts:707-720). The search line prints the title and then a snippet of `r.detail ?? r.body` (recall.ts:1528). Because `detail` is set, the body is never shown. That body holds r.why and r.steps, which are the words the hit matched on. For a questions card (person_questions:*), the title is '"X" needs your answers' or '"X": the specialist asks you' (request-words.ts:559), so the title never names the question either. cardAnswerWords drops the question when the card has one question: `if (pairs.length === 1) return pairs[0]?.chosen` (recall.ts:347). With several questions it does print "Q A; Q A". So the search can find a one-question card by its question, but the hit line never shows the question. Only recall_open shows it ('It asked: ...', recall.ts:736). The base pins this behaviour: chat-recall.test.ts:963 expects the Bakery hit '"Ask for the opening hours" needs your answers: Answers saved ...; Answer: Mon to Fri 9 to 18.' with no 'What are the opening hours?'. I ran that test at 4cf11fd and it passes. In the live turn (model-call seq 7) the hit was r6, weak, and nothing in its line said "first page". The model judged it 'not clearly about a first page' and did not open it.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/recall.ts:720 (detail without the question; title at :703, single-answer words at :347, hit line from detail at :1528)
verdict.fix_sketch: In cardHits, when the card's title does not carry its question (questions cards, whose title is '"X" needs your answers' or '"X": the specialist asks you'), start `detail` with the question(s). Use the same words as recall_open: `It asked: ${r.steps.map(withoutNoActionGiven).map(oneLine).join(" | ")}`, cut to about 120 characters. Then put the outcome and 'Answer: ...' after it. snippetOf then centres on the matched words ("first page"). Keep the generic card unchanged: its title already is the question ('Where is the page published?'). Optionally have the hit print the pair as 'Q → A' for a one-question card instead of only A. Recheck the 1,500-token search budget with 8 card hits, and confirm the result's injection scan and envelope still wrap it (the question can carry planted words, as here). Update chat-recall.test.ts:963 and the maintainer doc's cards sentence (runtime.md recall paragraph).
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed test in packages/runtime/test/chat-recall.test.ts, at the model boundary: the tool_result text the model receives. Seed an answered person_questions card on task "Write the index page" with steps ['Which recipes go on the first page?'], answered {answers:[{question, answer:'The three soups'}]}. Run recall {words:'card first page', kinds:['cards']}. Assert the r1 line contains 'Which recipes go on the first page?' and 'Answer: The three soups.'. Today it fails: the line is '"Write the index page" needs your answers: ... Answer: The three soups.'. Also change the CR-3 Bakery expectation (line 963) so it holds 'What are the opening hours?'. For the chat boundary, a scripted-provider turn that plays recall only (no recall_open) for 'what did the writer ask on the card about the first page?' should find the question in the tool_result it is handed.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-recall
verdict.notes:
The evidence matches the model-call log (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, seq 7 and 9-10). seq 7 is the recall result with r6 weak and no question. In seq 9-10, recall_open of the same card shows 'It asked: The writer asks: Which recipes go on the first page? ...'. The model did part of this: CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) say to open the hit you need with recall_open and never present a weak hit as fact. Haiku did neither, and it claimed 'nothing in the records says what the writer asked' without opening the hit. Still, the app's hit line hid the only words that tied the hit to the question, so this is not the model alone.

Two things in the evidence are seed artefacts, not this finding. The outcome text 'You answered "your answers"' comes from the daemon setting the seeded card's change_card.outcome to 'unrecognized_answer' at 06:16:07 (state.sqlite row 01a1e584...). That makes questionsOutcome return null and the fallback answerWords returns the literal 'your answers' (request-words.ts:392). That fallback is a separate small wording issue. The title '... needs your answers' also comes from the seed: there is no go_ahead/context on the card, so it reads as the person's own task.

The weak rank, below the person's own question lines, is the ranking issue already named in CL-11 (leftovers-C2.json). CL-11 also covers card hits with several questions being cut at 160 characters, and snippetOf centring on the first term. It is related, but it does not name the missing question of a one-question card, so I left known_leftover empty.

I did not start the bench. The composed unit test at the base already shows the hit line, and the live log confirms it.

finding.title: No 'From:' line on recalled answers when the model answers from recall's hit lines
finding.what_the_person_sees: Answers from recall ('Last week there were two sessions on Quote Page: Monday 9 Nov ...', 'The Bakery work cost CHF 0.21 last week', 'On Sun 1 Nov you answered ... Mon to Fri 9 to 18') show no From line. The From line appeared only after recall_open (Garden club session comparison, the opened card).
finding.expected: A reply that rests on recorded records names them in its From line (d1109-chat-recall and chat-depth).
finding.evidence: In 5 of 7 recall turns the real model called recall and answered without recall_open. The turn records have no sources. agent.ts line 2322: namedSources(reply, recallScope.opened, ...) uses opened records only.
finding.repro: Bakery Chat: 'what did I answer about the opening hours?'
finding.suspected_cause: Sources come only from recall_open. The real model rarely opens a hit when the hit line already answers.

verdict.root_cause: A reply's sources come only from records that recall_open opened in the turn. agent.ts:2322 calls namedSources(reply, recallScope.opened, ...). namedSources (recall.ts:1616-1643) loops over `opened` only. `opened` is filled only inside recall_open's execute (recall.ts:1596). recall's own hits go into scope.refs, which is replaced on every recall call (recall.ts:1525) and never reaches namedSources. The hit lines recall returns already carry what the answer needs: kind, local date, title and a snippet ("Answer: Mon to Fri 9 to 18", "It cost CHF 0.32", "What it cost: CHF 0.21 from 9 to 15 Nov"). CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) say only "open the hit you need with recall_open". So the real model reasonably answers from the hit line, and the turn gets no sources.records and no From line. The design wrote this narrowing in: ADR 0114 "Sources" and the runC-plan say "among those it opened". It was never caught because the bench stand-in always plays recall and then recall_open of the first strong hit (testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:1657-1658). Every sources test scripts recall_open before the answer (chat-recall.test.ts:1424-1500, the real-daemon test at apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:18635). Checked in the live store (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/data/state.sqlite, chat.reply rows) against model-calls.jsonl. 11 turns called recall and only 2 also called recall_open: the Recipe-site card and the Garden club session comparison. Only those 2 rows have sources.records. The other 9 (last week's sessions, README merged, Bakery spending, opening hours twice, the card search, the colours, and two thorough passes) have none. The finding said 5 of 7; the real count is worse. CR-12's own acceptance line, 'what did I answer about the opening hours?' → sources [{kind:'card'}], gets no source on the real model (seq 29-30).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2322 (namedSources over recallScope.opened); packages/runtime/src/conversation/recall.ts:1616-1643 (namedSources), recall.ts:1596 (opened filled only by recall_open), recall.ts:1525 (scope.refs replaced on each recall; hits not kept); testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:1657 (the stand-in always opens)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1. In RecallScope (recall.ts:173), keep `seen: {record, strong}[]`, added to on every recall call of the turn (next to the refs assignment at recall.ts:1525). 2. In namedSources, go through the opened records first, as today. Then go through the seen hits that were not opened. A hit counts as named when the reply carries its title or an earlier title. It counts by date alone only when it was a strong hit. Without that rule, the weak "session of Wed 4 Nov" hit would be named for "finished on Wed 4 Nov" in seq 30. Keep the cap of three and drop duplicates by record. 3. Pass recallScope as a whole from agent.ts:2322. Update the ChatSources doc comment (agent.ts:349), the "Sources" bullet of ADR 0114 (dated amendment: a record the reply names among this turn's hits, opened or not) and docs/maintainers/runtime.md. 4. Give the bench stand-in a path that answers from the hit line without recall_open (for example, when the top strong hit's snippet holds an "Answer:" or a CHF figure), so the bench and the real-daemon case exercise this path. No change to the model-facing text is needed.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real daemon, in describe 'd1109-chat-recall, run C' (apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts), next to the case at :18635. The answered "Ask for the opening hours" card is seeded, and the stand-in plays recall and then answers from the hit line with no recall_open ("On Sun 1 Nov you answered: Mon to Fri 9 to 18."). POST /chat/stream 'what did I answer about the opening hours?' should return reply.sources.records [{kind:'card', date:'1 Nov', link:'/inbox?answered=…'}], and GET /projects/:id/conversation should keep it after a restart. Today both have no records. Composed twin in packages/runtime/test/chat-recall.test.ts: w.reply([toolReply('recall',{kinds:['sessions'],from:'2026-11-12',to:'2026-11-12'}), textReply('The session of Thu 12 Nov at 15:30 checked the images.')]) should give res.sources.records equal to [session 'The session of Thu 12 Nov at 15:30']. Today it is undefined. Add a negative: a weak hit that shares only the date is not named. UI: Conversation shows 'From: …' under that reply.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-recall
verdict.notes: The app works exactly as the C2 spec says ("among those it opened"), so this is a design gap, not a coding slip. That design relied on a model behaviour the app's own hit lines discourage, and the stand-in hid it. That is why model_only is false: the recall result the app sends makes skipping recall_open the natural choice, and the fix belongs in code. No leftover names it. CL-11 (leftovers-C2) says LC-C10 watches which hit the real model opens, but it is about ranking, not sources. C3L-9 is about From-line links that open nothing. Severity stays minor: the answers were correct and dated, and only the one-click From line was missing. Separate issue seen in the same evidence, outside this finding: recall's card hit title reads '"the task" needs your answers: You answered "your answers"' (seq 24 and 30), a wording bug in the card hit title. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl and /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/data/state.sqlite (read-only). I did not run tests: the code path is unambiguous, and the stand-in cannot reproduce it because it always opens.

finding.title: Questions about something never recorded get no lookup and a guess
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'I can't find anything about a pizza oven in Quote Page's tasks, the last session or the files I have. The pizza oven is probably in the Bakery project, which has two open cards. I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look through the earlier conversation and notes for it?'
finding.expected: Chat looks it up, then says what it looked through ('Looked through: ...'), and guesses nothing.
finding.evidence: c10-quote.json c1 and c2: one call each, no tool; the C2 'what I looked through' wording never came from a real lookup.
finding.repro: Quote Page Chat: 'what did I say about the pizza oven?', 'when did we decide on the newsletter?'
finding.suspected_cause: Same as L4-chat-1.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding matches the model-call log (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl seq 17 and 18). Both control turns ran on claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low with thinking off. recall and recall_open were among the tools sent, yet each turn made one call with no tool call and ended normally (end_turn). The app did as designed: recall was offered, and CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:617) plus conversation-agent.md:46 say to look it up before saying you do not have it. The model chose not to. The app's own text still made that choice likely, and no code catches it:
(1) conversation-agent.md:68 says "If nothing you were given or looked up holds the answer, say what you looked through". That gives the model a sanctioned way out without any lookup, and its replies use exactly that form ("in Quote Page's tasks, the last session or the files I have"). Line 14 adds "You answer fast and short from what you are given."
(2) The 12-turn history (transcript.ts:267 HISTORY_TURNS) replays the model's own earlier offers. Those offers began at p2 ("I can search the records for it") and p6 ("I haven't searched the records yet. Should I look...?"). By c1 the history held 3 such replies and by x4 it held 6. Every miss after p6 copies the wording almost word for word. The base tendency is still the model's own: p2 skipped the lookup with no such history, and Recipe site seq 3 did the same. Bakery, with an empty history, called recall 2 of 2 times.
(3) Nothing in code checks for this. The claim guard (agent.ts:2028-2095, claimOf in claims.ts:139) catches only false change or ask claims. A reply that says it lacks something, or asks "Should I look?", without a recall call in the turn goes to the person unchanged.
The "guess" happened in c1 only ("probably in the Bakery project, which has two open cards"). It is a hedged guess built on the facts line "+2 cards in Bakery", and it is the model's own doing. The step expects Bakery to be named only after looking there. c2 guessed nothing and neither reply invented a record. This does not reproduce on the stand-in bench: role-player.ts:1645-1662 always calls recall for a PAST_RE line and returns "Looked through:". Same cause as L4-chat-1.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:68 (and :14); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2028 (claim guard only, no lookup check); agent.ts:617 (CHAT_RECALL_RULES); packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:267
verdict.fix_sketch:
1) Prompt (conversation-agent.md 1.4.x and CHAT_RECALL_RULES, both asserted verbatim):
- Replace line 68 with: "When the first message does not hold what the person asks about, call recall before you answer; if it finds nothing, say what it looked through."
- Add: "A lookup reads only and needs no yes: never offer to look something up or ask whether to, just look." and "Never say where something probably is (another project) without looking; use recall with project 'all'."
2) Code guard next to the claim guard (agent.ts ~2028): add missOf(text) in claims.ts. It matches lacks-or-offers wording ("can't find|don't have|haven't searched|no record|Should I (look|search)|I can search"). The guard fires when the turn's runs made no recall call, recall is in the tools, the run completed and calls are left (CHAT_MAX_MODEL_CALLS 6). It then sends one nudge step, without streaming its text: "You have not looked this up. Call recall with the person's words and other words for it, then answer from what it returns." As the claim guard does, it resets the live bubble with CHECKING_STEP and the "Looking through everything recorded…" step line. With no call left, the reply stays. The nudge runs inside the turn's call room and budget, and the claim guard runs after it.
3) That breaks the history loop: once each miss runs a lookup, the history stops filling with "Should I look?" offers, so the history itself needs no change.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-recall (model-facing recall text and conversation-agent.md); the miss guard sits beside l3-chat-claims' claim guard in agent.ts
verdict.notes: Agree minor. Both replies are honest: they say they have not searched and invent no record. The person needs one more line, and a plain "yes" to the model's offer gets "Yes to what?", which belongs to a separate finding. The finding's "a guess" applies to c1 only. CL-11 mentions that LC-C10 watches the real model's choice, but it is about recall ranking, not about whether the model calls recall, so no leftover names this. Evidence checked: model-calls.jsonl seq 17 and 18 (tools list includes recall and recall_open; toolCalls []), and the history trace by turn (p2 was the first miss with no offers in history; Bakery seq 27 and 29 looked up with an empty history; Recipe site seq 3 missed with an empty history). I did not run the stand-in bench: its role-player always calls recall for these lines, so it cannot reproduce a model-choice miss. No files changed.

finding.title: Chat bubble glues a paragraph onto the next list and a heading onto the previous bullet
finding.what_the_person_sees: '... Nothing has changed. Session 1:' on one line, and '- In the same session, run "Add the photo gallery" and "Write the FAQ". Both are ready and don't depend on anything. Session 2:' with 'Session 2:' inside the bullet.
finding.expected: Blank lines in the reply keep paragraphs and list headings apart.
finding.evidence:
48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png. The reply text in the model-call log has '

Session 1:
- First ...' and '

Session 2:
- Run ...'.
finding.repro: Any reply with 'Heading:' on its own line followed by '- ' items (e.g. the Sonnet plan above).
finding.suspected_cause: RichText in apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx does not end a list at a blank line followed by plain text.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is real, but its suspected cause is wrong. RichText handles blank lines correctly. A blank line is a text line, and a text line ends a list. The fault is earlier in the chain: a settled chat reply is shown as `<RichText text={inAppText(text)} />` (apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:560), and inAppText ends with `out.replace(/\s{2,}/g, " ").trim()` (apps/ui/src/lib/plain-words.ts:27). U-074 (c88b660) added that collapse for one-line read-backs. It also turns every "

" in a model reply into a single space, while single "
" breaks survive. So "Nothing has changed.

Session 1:" becomes "Nothing has changed. Session 1:". "...anything.

Session 2:
- Run" becomes "...anything. Session 2:
- Run", and RichText then correctly puts that line into the previous bullet. The trailing paragraphs ("If the members file..." and "Which fix...") are glued into the last bullet the same way. The stored reply is intact: the chat.reply event payload in state.sqlite and the model-call log line 54 both have "

Session 1:
- ..." and "

Session 2:
- ...". The live streaming bubble (Conversation.tsx:342) skips inAppText, so the reply first looks right and reflows into the glued form when the turn settles. There is a worse second instance in the same run. The 'compare the last two sessions' reply was stored as "The two most recent sessions:

- **Sun 15 Nov...**". It showed as "The two most recent sessions: - Sun 15 Nov...": the first item lost its bullet and a raw "- " marker is visible, which design §5 rule 6 forbids (no raw markdown). This happens whenever a reply puts a blank line before a list, in both the Chat tab and Talk (both use Conversation).
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/lib/plain-words.ts:27 (inAppText collapses /\s{2,}/ including "\n\n"), applied to model replies at apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:560
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Add to apps/ui/test/rich-text.test.tsx, through the Chat tab with the fake daemon. Set harness.daemon.state.nextChatReply = "Nothing has changed.

Session 1:
- First fix the blocker.
- Run the FAQ.

Session 2:
- Run the link check.

Which fix do you want?". Send a line and wait for chat-agent data-streaming=false. Expect two lists. The first list's items should equal ["First fix the blocker.", "Run the FAQ."]; today the second item is "Run the FAQ. Session 2:". The second list's items should equal ["Run the link check."]; today the item is "Run the link check. Which fix do you want?". The text content should not contain "changed. Session 1:". In a second case, the reply "The two most recent sessions:

- **Sun:** done.
- **Mon:** failed." should give one list of 2 items, and the agent text should not match /sessions: -/. A unit assertion that inAppText("a

b") === "a

b" pins the helper. All of these fail at 4cf11fd. I reproduced this with tsx and renderToStaticMarkup (/tmp/frbench/l4chat10/render.ts): RichText alone gives the correct lists, and RichText(inAppText(...)) gives the glued bullets.
verdict.area_hint: Small fix area for chat-reply rendering in the UI (apps/ui/src/lib/plain-words.ts inAppText, U-074; and Conversation.tsx:560). The nearest run C owner of Conversation.tsx is d1109-chat-depth.
verdict.notes: I checked the evidence: the screenshot 48-c13b-03-e3-go-ahead.png and its .txt match the glued text, and the model reply plus the stored chat.reply event both keep the blank lines. So this is not the model's choice and not a test artefact. The finding's suspected cause (RichText not ending a list at a blank line) is wrong. RichText ends the list correctly, and inAppText removed the blank line before RichText ever saw it. No leftover file (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) mentions inAppText, blank lines or paragraph gluing. The repro scripts are in /tmp/frbench/l4chat10/ (collapse.mjs, render.ts). I did not edit the worktree. I kept severity at minor: no information is lost and nothing wrong is said. It is frequent, though: every multi-paragraph chat reply is affected, and an intro line followed by a blank line and a list shows a raw "- ".

finding.title: Change read back twice: once in chat's own words, once on the card
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Pausing "Write the FAQ" needs your yes. Press Yes on the read-back to put it on hold; nothing changes until then.' then 'Pause "Write the FAQ"? No session runs it until you press Resume. [Yes] [No]'
finding.expected: Design §3.9: a change is read back once in one line.
finding.evidence: c13.json q2 reply and readback.
finding.repro: Garden club Chat: 'put the FAQ on hold for now'.
finding.suspected_cause: The model is not told that the read-back card carries the question, so it adds its own.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is real. The person sees the change twice, and the prompt the app sends is what asks for the extra line. On the model path, the chat reply is the model's own text followed by the card's read-back: agent.ts:2204-2206 builds it as `${replaced}${reply ? `${reply} ` : ""}${pendingCard.readback}`. server.ts:2840-2843 then removes only the read-back from the reply text and keeps the model's line above the yellow card.

The model is told to write that line. The tool result hands it the question word for word (packages/commands/src/registry.ts:203-209: "Needs confirmation. The person is asked: Pause \"Write the FAQ\"? ..."). The system prompt evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:84-86 (v1.4.0) says "do not repeat the read-back. When a tool answers \"Needs confirmation\", say so in a few words and stop". The built-in DEFAULT_PROMPT at agent.ts:576-578 says the same ("say so and stop"). Haiku did what it was told: it said so, in its own words.

The finding's suspected cause is partly wrong. The model is told that the runtime reads the change back. The cause is the instruction to "say so", together with the code always showing the model's text above the card. On the parser path (replyForResult, agent.ts:2666-2669) the reply is the read-back alone, so only changes made through model tools show the change twice.

The evidence agrees. Both read-backs made through model tools in live check 4 have the extra line:
- c13 q2: "Pausing \"Write the FAQ\" needs your yes. Press Yes on the read-back to put it on hold; nothing changes until then."
- c16d ch1: "Pausing \"Write the README\" needs your confirmation. Press Yes to put it on hold."

In c13 the second model call (end_turn, after the task_pause tool_result) wrote that line, and screenshot 37-c13-02-q2.png shows it above the card. The same screen's hint line says "a change to a task is read back once", and design §3.9 says "Changes are read back once in one line"; §5 gives the read-back's "After, once" form. "Press Yes on the read-back" also uses the internal word "read-back".
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:84-86 (the "say so in a few words" rule); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2204-2206 (model text + read-back joined), agent.ts:576-578 (DEFAULT_PROMPT "say so and stop"); packages/commands/src/registry.ts:203-209 (the tool result that carries the question to the model)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Prompt (conversation-agent.md 1.5.0, rule 2, and DEFAULT_PROMPT at agent.ts:576): "A change that needs a yes is shown under your reply as one question with Yes and No. When a tool answers \"Needs confirmation\", write nothing about that change: do not restate it, do not say it needs a yes, do not say press Yes. Answer only what else the person asked; with nothing else, write nothing." Keep the claim-guard sentences (lines 86-89).

2. Tool result for the chat binding: say that the app shows this question under the reply and it must not be repeated. Keep the specialist path's "Needs confirmation. The person is asked:" prefix, which specialist-propose-tool.test.ts asserts. One way is a suffix, or a chat-only variant chosen in loop/commands.ts commandToolSpecs.

3. Code backstop in agent.ts at 2204: when the turn has a pendingCard, drop the sentences of the model's text that only speak about this card. Examples: a "needs your yes/confirmation/approval" sentence, a "Press/Tap Yes" sentence, "nothing changes until …", or a sentence that names the card's task title together with the same verb. Reuse the sentence splitter and the style of claims.ts. If nothing is left, the reply is the read-back alone, as on the parser path. Keep sentences that answer another part of the line. Check that needs_device cards already carry the device instruction in their read-back before dropping "Confirm it on your paired device" (conversation.test.ts:516-520 relies on that line today).
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Tested at the conversation the Chat tab reads. In apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, or a composed case in packages/runtime/test/conversation.test.ts:
- Script the model: call task_pause {task: "Write the FAQ"}, then, after "Needs confirmation", reply "Pausing \"Write the FAQ\" needs your yes. Press Yes on the read-back to put it on hold; nothing changes until then."
- Send "put the FAQ on hold for now".
- GET /projects/:id/conversation: the last turn's reply.readback is "Pause \"Write the FAQ\"? No session runs it until you press Resume." and reply.text is "". No sentence other than the card names "Write the FAQ" or says yes/confirm.
- The ChatTab render shows "Write the FAQ" exactly once, in the card with Yes and No.
- A second case, "how is it going and put the FAQ on hold", keeps the status answer and drops only the confirmation sentence.

This fails today: reply.text holds the model's line, and the card is shown under it. Also assert word for word, as conversation-memory.test.ts:1189 does, that the system part and the tool result the model receives say not to restate the change. Today they say "say so in a few words".
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat (the chat's read-back on the model path: the results loop and composed read-back at agent.ts:2164-2206, the rule "one question per line, never a second"); the prompt file conversation-agent.md was last versioned by d1109-chat-depth (1.4.0)
verdict.notes: I verified this from the code and the live evidence and did not start the stand-in bench. The bench's stand-in chat echoes every tool result ("The command tool task_pause answered: Needs confirmation. The person is asked: …", testenv/src/bench/role-player.ts:1729-1737), so it would show the same double display, but only as the stand-in's artefact. The evidence that the real model follows the app's prompt is the live log: 2 of 2 read-backs made through model tools in live check 4 had the extra line (c13.json q2 and c16d.json ch1 under /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/), and screenshot 37-c13-02-q2.png shows it above the card. Changes made through the parser path read back once. Voice has the same issue: the model's line is spoken, then the read-back. None of leftovers-{L3,C2,C3,C4,C4b-design,C4b,C5,C6}.json names it; C6L-6 is a different duplicate (the one-off press repeating the person's line). The owner's decisions of 2026-11-09 do not change design §3.9's "read back once in one line".

finding.title: Inbox Answered entries read 'You answered "your answers".'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Inbox, Answered: '"Write the index page" needs your answers · Recipe site / You answered "your answers".'
finding.expected: The answer given (e.g. 'The three soups'), or 'Answered.'
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/35-c11-inbox-answered.txt. request-words.ts answerWords returns 'your answers' for an answer of {answers:[...]}, and the Answered line wraps it in quotes. Seen on seeded questions cards; the answer shape is the fixture's copy of the app's.
finding.repro: Answer a questions card (person_questions) on a task that is not done yet, then open Inbox, Answered.
finding.suspected_cause: The answerWords fallback is meant as a phrase, not as a quoted answer.

verdict.root_cause: This is a test artefact: the fixture's card is not the shape the app writes. In the bench DB copy, all three seeded questions cards (Recipe site 'Write the index page' and the two Bakery ones) end with change_card {key:'person_questions:<question text>', outcome:'unrecognized_answer', applied_at:...}. They have no task_id, no task_title and no questions. The cause is scripts/seed-c11-c13.mts at lines 261-275, which inserts change_card {key:`person_questions:${why}`, outcome:'answered'}. It sets no task_id and no applied_at, and keys the card by the question text instead of by the task id. Because applied_at is missing, the app's own sync (applyAnswers, run on every answer and poll) picks the row up. personQuestionsCardOf returns null when there is no task_id (person-questions.ts:454), so markAnswer writes over outcome with 'unrecognized_answer' (person-questions.ts:1046-1047). questionsOutcome (request-words.ts:569-592) returns null for that outcome. requestWords then falls back to answerWords, which returns the placeholder 'your answers' for an {answers:[...]} answer (request-words.ts:392), and wraps it in quotes (request-words.ts:1862). The same missing task_id is why the title reads '"the task" needs your answers'. In the real app it does not happen. Cards the app files carry task_id and key person_questions:<taskId> (person-questions.ts:527-528). POST /requests/:id/answer awaits rt.syncApprovals() before it returns the view (server.ts:2515). markAnswer sets outcome 'answered' or 'task_moved_on'. The person sees 'Answers sent: "Write the index page" goes on with them; …' or 'Answers saved in the decision record; … is done', which real-daemon.test.ts:3524/3608 already checks. A tsx run of requestWords on the real card shape gives exactly that. The repro as written ('answer a questions card on a task not yet done') therefore does not produce the reported line.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:1862 (quoted fallback) and :392 (answerWords placeholder); reached only via questionsOutcome returning null (request-words.ts:569-592). The evidence comes from the fixture /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/scripts/seed-c11-c13.mts:261-275 (card without task_id or applied_at), which person-questions.ts:1046-1047 marks 'unrecognized_answer'.
verdict.fix_sketch: Fixture first: the seed should insert a card the app itself would write, with key person_questions:<taskId>, task_id, task_title, questions:[why], source:'specialist' and on_answer:'ready'. Then either let the app's sync apply the answer, or also set applied_at so the seeded outcome 'answered' is kept. Optional polish for the remaining fallback, which shows for an answered but not-yet-applied card: an answer from the phone or web on shared state before the approvals poll, or a step of syncApprovalsOnce that threw before syncPersonQuestions. Keep the placeholder out of quotes. In the person_questions branch of requestWords, when questionsOutcome is null and the card is not marked yet, say 'Answers received: they are used when "<task>" goes on.' (or quote the first answer, e.g. 'You answered "The three soups".'). Make answerWords return null for {answers:[...]} so no caller can quote 'your answers'. Do the same for InboxPage.tsx:889 answerText, which returns 'your answers' the same way.
verdict.failing_test_idea: For the latent fallback only; the reported repro passes today. Add a unit test in packages/runtime/test (request-words): an answered person_questions card built the way person-questions.ts:527 builds it, with no applied_at or outcome yet and answer {answers:[{question, answer:'The three soups'}]}. Assert requestWords(...).outcome does not contain '"your answers"' and names the answer or the task. At the boundary: in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, file a specialist's questions card, write the answer straight into the shared store (as a phone answer would, with no route call), then GET /requests and open the Answered list before the poll. The line must not read 'You answered "your answers".'
verdict.area_hint: small words fix area (Inbox request words, request-words.ts); no run C area owns it. The main fix is in the live-check bench seed (scripts/seed-c11-c13.mts).
verdict.notes: Checked in a read-only copy of /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/home/data/state.sqlite (copied to /tmp/frbench/l4c6): all three person_questions rows have outcome 'unrecognized_answer' and no task_id in the card. One of them also has task_id null on the row. The seed had set outcome 'answered', so the app's sync overwrote it. A tsx run of requestWords (script at /tmp/frbench/l4c6/words.mts) gives: real card applied 'answered' -> 'Answers sent: "Write the index page" goes on with them.'; real card not yet applied -> 'You answered "your answers".'; card marked unrecognized -> same; seed card -> same. The route path cannot leave a real card unrecognized, because assertAnswerAccepted refuses answers personQuestionsAnswerFor cannot read (U-034). So the placeholder shows in real use only in the narrow not-yet-applied window: an answer from another device on shared state before the poll, or a sync step that threw. That is worth a 'words' polish at most, not this finding. No bench was started; no files in the checkout were changed. None of the L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 leftovers names it.

finding.title: The ask card's 'about CHF' is far below what Use API key then spends, and below the dialog's and plan card's figures for the same work
finding.what_the_person_sees: Card: 'Your API key can do the waiting work now: about CHF 0.10.' After Use API key the session spends CHF 0.65: CHF 0.24 on the two tasks that waited, the rest on two tasks the agent added under the same yes. For the same waiting work the Start dialog said 'about CHF 0.15' and the plan card 'About CHF 0.37 for the 2 tasks'. Second stop: card CHF 0.05, plan card CHF 0.15, dialog CHF 0.10.
finding.expected: The card's figure is within a factor of two of the real spend after Use API key, and the card, the dialog and the plan card give one figure for the same waiting work (C6L-3).
finding.evidence: Inbox API body 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 08:26. Your API key can do the waiting work now: about CHF 0.10.'; start-session-run-out 'Runs now on your API key until 08:26, about CHF 0.15; nothing passes this session's budget.'; ledger after the press: 60 rows, USD 0.818311 (task 16874e 0.212904, task 5d66a1 0.088728, added 07a838 0.395557, added 0ce1e8 0.108554). Files: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24b.json, c24c.json.
finding.repro: Save both credentials, choose 'Subscription first, ask before API key', and have the subscription at its limit. Draft a 2-task plan and press Approve and start. Read the card, the Start dialog and the plan card. Press Use API key. Compare with Costs.
finding.suspected_cause: The card's estimate (credential-ask's estimate_usd_micro, priced with the Start check) seems to count only part of the waiting work. It has no margin for reviews and rework, and none for tasks the agent adds while the yes stands.

verdict.root_cause:
The ask card's figure is the closure in compose.ts that RouterTaskBilling's `ask` calls. For each waiting project it adds two things: `check.runnable` (ready tasks, priced by the planner), and the claimed or in_progress tasks at their raw stored figure, `(t.est_cost_usd_micro || t.budget_usd_micro || 500_000) - actual`. That second part was added in CS-8. Two gaps follow.
(1) The task that hit the stop is claimed when the card is filed, so it is priced at the plan's raw work-only guess. That guess has no review part. The Start dialog and the plan card price the same task with planEstimateUsdMicro / estimates.of, which add the review part (d1116-budget-all). This goes against the owner's binding answer of 2026-11-16 ("its estimate includes the reviews and fixes").
(2) It ignores `check.later`: the follower tasks that wait on the claimed task. A "Use API key" yes runs them in the same session (ADR 0120 §3: the waiting session goes on as the person's start, and promiseOf counts runnable + later).
The bench DB confirms this exactly. The first card's change_card.estimate_usd_micro = 126000, which equals the coder task's est_cost_usd_micro (126000); the tester task (est 207000) is not counted. The second card's 66000 equals the Bird walk coder's est_cost_usd_micro (66000); its tester (90000) is not counted.
The other two figures differ as well. The Start dialog's Use API key line (server.ts credentialAtStart) sums only `r.runnable`, so CHF 0.15 is the coder alone with its review part. The plan card prices every task with its review part: 0.15 + 0.22 = CHF 0.37. The result is three figures for one piece of waiting work. Real spend on the two waiting tasks was CHF 0.24 (0.212904 + 0.088728 USD), 2.4x the card's CHF 0.10. With the fix, the card would read about the plan card's 0.37, within a factor of two of 0.24 and also of the total 0.65.
The other CHF 0.41 went to two tasks the agent added during the run (D7, allowed by the owner). No up-front estimate can foresee them. That part is by design: the session budget still bounds it, and the explain line honestly says "for what waits now".
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:1811-1827 (ask closure: inFlight priced at raw est_cost_usd_micro at :1820; sum of check.runnable + inFlight only, no check.later, at :1826); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1567-1572 (Start dialog's Use API key figure: r.runnable only); packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:142-160 (promiseOf, the figure both should use)
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add a composed case to packages/runtime/test/credential-ask-figure.test.ts using credWorld with no injected provider. The project has two tasks, B depending on A, with planner estimates whose review part is non-zero. Set policy subscription_then_ask, limit the subscription, start a session and call settleSessions. Then read three things at the person's boundary: the "Use your API key until 15:00?" card body from GET /inbox, the start-check's Use API key line from GET /projects/:id/start-check, and the plan card's per-task figures for the same tasks. Assert that the card's "about CHF N" equals the dialog's figure, and that both equal the A+B promise priced with the review part. Assert that it is more than A's raw est_cost_usd_micro alone. Today the card gives A's raw estimate only (as with 126000 vs the plan's 0.37) and the dialog gives A only.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-screens
verdict.notes:
C6L-3 (rated words) already names the three figures (card, runnable-only dialog, plan card per task) and asks for one figure per thing. This finding shows the root cause is more than words. The card leaves out the follower tasks the yes will run, and it prices the claimed task without its review part, so the money consent understates the waiting work by more than 2x on the real run. That is why I keep major; minor is also defensible, since the amounts are small and the session budget still caps everything.
The expectation that the card match spend that includes the agent-added tasks is too strong. That part is model and design (D7), not code.
Evidence checked in the read-only DB /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs/home/data/state.sqlite: the human_request change_card estimate_usd_micro values 126000 and 66000 match the task rows' est_cost_usd_micro exactly.
Also seen in c24b, not part of this finding: the request_blocking notification title says "until 07:26" while the card says "until 08:26", which looks like a UTC vs local time mix-up in the notification words.

finding.title: The ask card's notification gives the reset time in UTC, an hour off the card
finding.what_the_person_sees: Urgent notification: 'Use your API key until 07:26?' / 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 07:26. ...' The Inbox card, rows, bar and Settings all say 08:26 (the person's zone is Europe/Zurich). Same for the second stop: 07:01 against 08:01. The credential_switch notification in LC-C23 used the person's clock (08:28).
finding.expected: Every sentence uses the person's clock, never UTC (C5 CE-4).
finding.evidence: GET /notifications/recent: request_blocking at 06:47:11.532Z, title 'Use your API key until 07:26?'. Inbox card title 'Use your API key until 08:26?'. restingUntil 2026-11-17T07:26:44Z; config timezone Europe/Zurich. File: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24b.json.
finding.repro: Set a person's zone other than UTC and choose ask. With the subscription at its limit, press Approve and start on a plan. Read the desktop notification (GET /notifications/recent).
finding.suspected_cause: The notification text for the ask card is built without the person's timezone (formatted in the daemon's process zone, UTC on the bench). The card's own words are built with the timezone.

verdict.root_cause: The finding is real. The suspected cause is slightly off: the time is not formatted in the daemon's process zone, it is hard-coded to UTC. The ask card's row stores only a placeholder `why`. Its title and body are computed when the card is shown, by askCard() in request-words.ts, from ctx.credentialAsk.timezone. The Inbox fills that context: views.ts:1059-1060 calls credentialAskFor(), which reads human.timezone at views.ts:1088. The notification path does not. compose.ts:3451 calls notifications.requestOpened(row, human.id, names), and producers.ts:187-190 calls requestWords(req, { projectName, taskTitle }) with no credentialAsk. So askCard (request-words.ts:1385-1394) passes no timezone, and askCardWords then calls stopWordsOf, then clockTime(), then validZone(undefined), which returns "UTC" (credential-wait.ts:231). The urgent request_blocking notification therefore always gives the reset in UTC, for any person whose zone is not UTC, on a real PC as well as on the bench. The credential_switch notification is right because compose.ts:3554 formats `until` with human.timezone itself. A smaller related point: askCard falls back to Date.now() for nowMs (request-words.ts:1394) instead of the clock, so near midnight the same-day check ("07:26" or "Tue 18 Nov, 07:26") can also differ from the card.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/notifications/producers.ts:187 (requestWords without credentialAsk); packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3451 (caller passes no zone); packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:1393-1394 (timezone omitted, nowMs falls back to Date.now()); packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:231 (no zone means "UTC")
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Let requestOpened(req, humanId, names, ctx?) take the same RequestWordsContext pieces the Inbox uses, and pass them to requestWords.
2. In compose's humanRequest.insert hook (compose.ts ~3436-3451), when the row's change_card.key is CREDENTIAL_ASK_KEY, build the context the way the Inbox does. Either export views.ts credentialAskFor (or a small shared helper in request-words / views) and call it, or at least pass { timezone: human.timezone, nowMs: Date.parse(card.filed_at) }. The notification then says what the card says, including the sessionWaits and goesOnAt words.
3. Close the trap: askCardWords/stopWordsOf should not fall back silently to UTC for a person-facing sentence. Either make timezone required on AskCardInput, or have askCard take nowMs from card.filed_at instead of Date.now().
4. Grep the siblings that render request words outside the Inbox: requestOpened, the email/Telegram channels (which reuse the same Notification), and any summary or chat path that calls requestWords for a credential:ask row. Give each the same context.
5. Update docs/maintainers notifications and credential docs as the module rule requires.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Real-daemon route case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, in the 'd1109-cred-engine' describe:
1. Set the person's timezone to Europe/Zurich and the policy to subscription_then_ask.
2. Put the subscription stand-in at its limit with a reset at 07:26Z.
3. Approve and start a plan, then read GET /notifications/recent and GET /inbox.
4. Assert that the request_blocking notification's title equals the ask card's requestView title, "Use your API key until 08:26?", and that its body contains "until 08:26" and not "07:26".

Today this fails: the notification reads 07:26. Add a unit twin in packages/runtime/test/notifications-wiring.test.ts that drives the composed insert hook with a credential:ask row and a Europe/Zurich human, and asserts the notifier received 08:26. Run both with TZ unset and with TZ=Europe/Zurich: the fallback is hard-coded UTC, so it fails either way.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (CE-7 ask card; the notification wiring in compose/producers)
verdict.notes: I reproduced it at 4cf11fd with a tsx script, /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-5/repro.ts, run with TZ=Europe/Zurich (process zone Europe/Zurich). requestOpened(askRow) gives "Use your API key until 07:26?" / "...at its limit until 07:26...". requestWords with credentialAsk.timezone=Europe/Zurich gives "08:26". So the daemon's process zone does not matter: any person outside UTC gets the wrong hour in the urgent notification, and the same Notification goes to the desktop tray, email and Telegram. The evidence matches for both stops: c24b/c24c show 07:26 against card 08:26, and c24d/c24e show 07:01 against 08:01. No known leftover names this. C5L-7 is about credentialHold reading the timezone once at compose time, which is a different issue. I agree with major: it is an urgent prompt for a money decision, and in Zurich at 07:47 local, "until 07:26" reads as a reset that has already passed.

finding.title: Sessions tab leaves out the session that ended to wait, while Last result and the continuation point to it
finding.what_the_person_sees: While the session waits, the Overview shows 'Last result ... Open the session' but the Sessions tab says 'No sessions yet.' Afterwards the Sessions tab shows '1 session ... goes on with your session of 07:24', a session the list never shows.
finding.expected: The list shows every session other screens name (D2), or rows do not name a hidden one.
finding.evidence: GET /projects/:id/sessions returned {count:0, rows:[]} while session 01a1e82d... existed (status stopped). Files: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c21/steps/10-c21-waiting-sessions-tab.txt, 18-c21-sessions-tab-after-work.txt.
finding.repro: With only the refused key, start a session on a ready task. Open Sessions. Save a new key and open Sessions again.
finding.suspected_cause: listedCountForProject / pageForProject leave out sessions that ended with nothing done.

verdict.root_cause: The rule for which sessions get listed leaves out any session that ended with no run row and no cost-ledger row. SessionRepo.listedWhere (packages/state/src/repos/session.ts:158-170) keeps a row only when its status is planned, running or paused, or EXISTS a run, or EXISTS a ledger row, or plan.intake is set. Both pageForProject (:176) and listedCountForProject (:193) use this rule, so the session list (session-list.ts:669 count, :684 ended page) leaves the session out. Its working query (session-list.ts:672-682) only covers planned, running and paused, so it misses the session there too. The Overview's sessionCount (views.ts:507) also comes from this rule. In this journey the person pressed Start (plan.startedBy.by='person', trigger 'manual'), and the credential pick refused before any run was written. The session went straight to status 'stopped' with handoff.stop_reason 'credential_wait', 0 steps and no ledger row (checked read-only in /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c21/home/data/state.sqlite). Applying the listed SQL to that database gives only the continuation 01a1e83a. 01a1e82d is left out, although summary_cache.last_session pointed to it during the wait (Overview 'Last result ... Open the session') and the continuation's plan.startedBy.continues names it (row: 'goes on with your session of 07:24'). ADR 0116 rule 5 says the exclusion is there because 'an automatic start that found nothing is not news (design §4.8)'. A person's Start that stopped to wait is not that case, and owner decision D2 says every project lists its sessions. The plan expected a row for this case: d1109-sessions SL-11 says 'a session that ended at a credential wait reads ... on its page's badge and its row'. But the SL-11 real-daemon case seeds a run row into every session (apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:16130), so the real path never got tested: in that path the wait comes before any run.
verdict.where: packages/state/src/repos/session.ts:158 (listedWhere; used by pageForProject :176 and listedCountForProject :193); consumers packages/runtime/src/daemon/session-list.ts:669,672-688 and packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:507; test gap apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:16130
verdict.fix_sketch: In listedWhere, also list (1) a session the person started, (2) a session that ended to wait, and (3) a session another row continues. For (1), json_extract(s."plan",'$.startedBy.by') IN ('person','continuation'), plus the Postgres form. For (2), json_extract(s."handoff",'$.stop_reason') IN ('credential_wait','plan_awaiting_approval'). For (3), EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM session c WHERE json_extract(c."plan",'$.startedBy.continues') = s."id"). Automatic starts (hands_off, schedule) that found nothing stay out, as ADR 0116 intends. The count, the page and the Overview's sessionCount follow, because they share the rule. Amend ADR 0116 point 5 and the runtime.md listed-rule paragraph (around :7431) to match. Extend the state suite: a person's start that stopped at a credential wait with no run is in pageForProject(ended) and in the count, and an automatic one is not. A narrower alternative: the session list skips the stored rule for the session that summary_cache.last_session names and for any session a listed row continues. That is less clean.
verdict.failing_test_idea: A real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts through the client. Use the stand-in provider and the w15-run credential helpers with only a refused API key. Make a project with one ready task and client.startSession, which stops at once with 'Stopped to wait for a Claude credential: nothing done'. Then client.projectSessions(project.id) should give count 1 and a row with the waiting session's id, endedWords 'Stopped to wait for a Claude credential' and the 'Waits for a new API key' gist (today: count 0, rows []). client.projectSummary(...).sessionCount should be 1. Save a working key so the continuation runs to done. Then the list should hold 2 rows, and the continuation row's startedBy 'goes on with your session of HH:MM' should name a session id in the same list. Also compose a second time on the same home and read again. On the UI side, the Sessions tab while the session waits should show that row, not 'No sessions yet.'
verdict.area_hint: d1109-sessions
verdict.notes: Evidence is consistent. c21-evidence/c21-api-start.txt shows SESSIONS {count:0, rows:[]} while RUNNING has sessionId 01a1e82d in state 'waiting'. The database shows 01a1e82d with status stopped, trigger manual, startedBy person, stop_reason credential_wait, no run and no ledger rows. Continuation 01a1e83a has startedBy {by:'continuation', continues:'01a1e82d...', continuesAt:'07:24'}, 2 runs and 8 api ledger rows. C6L-2 (cred-screens, 'Start on 1 Dec') is related but not the same: it is about a start that should have been kept, and it assumes such a session would show in the list. finding.title: 'Waits for your answer ... The card is in the Inbox.' stays after the card is answered
finding.what_the_person_sees: After Wait (and also after Use API key), these still read 'Waits for your answer: use your API key? The card is in the Inbox. 1 task waits on other tasks. CHF 0.00.': the session page result, the Overview's Last result, the Inbox Updates and the session_ended notification. Meanwhile the Inbox says 'Nothing needs you.' The rows are right.
finding.expected: That sentence shows only while the card is open (C5 leftovers).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/cs-evidence/c24d.json (sessionB, overviewB, inboxAfterWait); c24c.json (overviewRunning).
finding.repro: Do the same as L4-creds-4, then press Wait on the card. Open the session page and the Overview.
finding.suspected_cause: The stored session summary and the Update are written when the session ends, while the card is still open, and are not reworded after the answer.

verdict.root_cause: The session result is stored when the session ends, while the ask card is still open. So it carries the ask form 'Waits for your answer: use your API key? The card is in the Inbox.': credential-wait.ts:291-292, reached through askShown in executor.ts:1842 / 2131, stored by runner.ts:3906-3914 (outcome.credentialWait = waitSentence(...)). Three places re-read that stored text: the session page (server.ts:2139), the Overview's Last result and Read aloud (views.ts:426), and the Inbox Update (server.ts:2475). All three go through resultAfterWait (run-indicator.ts:60-67). That function returns the text unchanged unless it contains '; then your session goes on.' (line 66), so nothing re-checks the ask sentence after the card is answered (askCardOpen false). The C5 fix-up (FX-CE B1) applied askShown only to sentences written after the answer, never to results already stored. Its test (credential-ask-words.test.ts, 'after Wait...') checks only the second session. Reproduced on the composed stand-in: after Wait, with no open ask card, GET /sessions/:first, GET /projects/:id/summary lastSession.summary and the GET /inbox Update all still say 'The card is in the Inbox'. verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/run-indicator.ts:66 (resultAfterWait handles only the goes-on clause); stored at packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3906; read at packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:2139, server.ts:2475, views.ts:426; sentence at packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:292

At session end, also store the structured wait (sourceId, stopKey, kind, until) on the session's handoff or outcome, or find the stop's ask card (CREDENTIAL_ASK_KEY with that stop_key). In resultAfterWait, or a storedResultNow wrapper all readers use: if the text has the ask form and askCardOpen(store, sourceId, stopKey) is false, swap it for what is true now. After Wait: waitSentence of the plain wait (askShown's plain form), which then passes through the existing goes-on rule ('Waits until 08:01 (your subscription's limit); then your session goes on.'). After Use API key: a line saying the work went on with your API key, or the plain stop sentence. Keep the 3-line result rule. Route chat's project facts (conversation/project-facts.ts) and the typed 'summary' command through the same rule (the port C5L-15 already asks for). verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/credential-ask-words.test.ts, extend 'after Wait, a session started before the stop ends says the plain wait': after answering Wait on the card (before the second Start), read GET /sessions/:first.sessionId .summary, GET /projects/:id/summary .lastSession.summary and the GET /inbox messages[].body. Expect none to contain 'The card is in the Inbox'. Expect the session page and Last result to contain 'Waits until 15:00 (your subscription's limit); then your session goes on.'.
