finding.title: A task check runs after the session's last task when every task is Done
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Checked the task list after "Write styles.css and link it from every page": no change (less than CHF 0.01).'
finding.expected: No call when no task is Draft or Ready, since then nothing can change.
finding.evidence: st1 model-call #23: all three tasks are listed '(Done)'. Reply: 'All three tasks are Done and the critic's note raises no defect the list must fix'. Cost USD 0.001862.
finding.repro: As in L4-selftasks-1, where the last task's review has a note.
finding.suspected_cause: checkTaskList runs whenever notes exist, before the queue-empty check.

verdict.root_cause: The observation is accurate, but the expectation is wrong. The runner does make a check after the session's last task while every task is Done. At packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2457, checkTaskList() runs at the top of the queue loop, before the queue-empty branch at :2461. It returns early only when there are no notes, after three checks, or when takesNothingNew() is true (:2387-2390). This order is deliberate. Even with every task Done, the check can still make an 'add': the fence in packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:868-903 refuses an 'after' anchor only when it is missing or cancelled, so a Done anchor passes, and 'before' is optional. checkTaskList then admits the new task (runner.ts:2440-2449) and returns true. The queue is dropped, and replan() (:2196, readyTasks) takes the new task in the same session. This is what ADR 0119 points 3 and 8 and owner decision D7 describe ('fix its tasks ... as part of a run'). The same live run showed this path working. In Tea room (st1 model-calls #31 and #43), each check followed a Done task and added a task ('Write book.html', then 'Write thanks.html'), and both added tasks ran in the same session. If a two-job task is the session's last or only task, the proposed rule ('no call when no task is Draft or Ready') would skip exactly this check, and the missing step would wait for the next Start. So 'nothing can change' is false. In the Corner bakery case, the paid call was caused by L4-selftasks-1, not by the session's end. The only evidence was a routine critic note ('The worker did not measure contrast ...'). It counted as a task-list note because isCriticNote (packages/runtime/src/session/task-list-notes.ts:134) accepts every finding with severity 'info'; the critic notes are collected at runner.ts:3333-3352. The model's reply (no change) was correct.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2457 (the boundary check before the queue-empty replan at :2461, by design); the call's real trigger is packages/runtime/src/session/task-list-notes.ts:134 (isCriticNote), already reported as L4-selftasks-1
verdict.fix_sketch: No fix for this finding. Do not gate the check on 'a Draft or Ready task exists': that would block a valid add after the session's last task, against ADR 0119 point 8 and D7. The waste goes away with the L4-selftasks-1 fix. That fix makes only notes that point at the task list count as evidence: a finding marked as not caused by the task (NOT_CAUSED_BY_TASK), or a report's 'For the task list:' lines. An ordinary severity-'info' remark would no longer count. Then the check after the last task runs only when there is evidence the list may need a new step. Optional, for the words: when the session's last check finds no change, the Details line could leave out the cost when it is under CHF 0.01. That is cosmetic and not needed.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Nothing fails today for this finding, because the behaviour is correct. To protect it against the proposed rule, add a guard case to packages/runtime/test/session-task-list.test.ts (composed, at Standard). The plan has one task. Its report ends 'For the task list:\n- book.html was left undone.' After that task (every task Done), exactly one check runs. The stand-in replies with an add 'Write book.html' (no before). The Details line says 'changed 1 task', and 'Write book.html' runs and is accepted in the same session, with no 'Left for your next Start'. The test for the actual waste belongs to L4-selftasks-1: a critic finding with severity 'info' and no NOT_CAUSED_BY_TASK suffix ('The worker did not measure contrast ...') on the last task makes no task-check call and no 'Checked the task list' line.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl seq 24 (Corner bakery). It lists all three tasks as Done, and its only evidence is one critic note ('The worker did not measure contrast or open the pages itself ...'); the reply was no change, USD 0.001862. In the same file, seq 31 and 43 (Tea room) are checks that followed a Done task and added tasks, and those tasks ran in the same session; this shows the after-the-last-task path is useful. No leftover in leftovers-{L3,C2,C3,C4,C4b-design,C4b,C5,C6}.json names this. The nearest is C4L-15 (the check line is under Details only), which is a different point. This finding is a consequence of L4-selftasks-1 (same journey) and should be folded into it, not fixed on its own. A side observation, not part of this finding: the prompt rule says 'Change only tasks shown as Draft, Ready, Waiting for, Stuck or Waiting for Docker', but the code accepts only draft and ready (CHANGEABLE in task-check.ts:66). That mismatch may be worth checking separately (st3 seq 10 and 11 show drops proposed on 'Waiting for' tasks). I did not run the bench: the code path (check, then admit, then replan) and the live evidence were enough, and nothing was changed in the worktree.

finding.title: The same session log gives two different estimates for the plan
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'It promised 3 tasks, about CHF 0.45.' and later 'Session review measured: 3 of 3 planned tasks done; the planned tasks cost CHF 0.14 against an estimate of CHF 0.31, and the session's own checks CHF 0.01.' The plan card said 0.16 + 0.11 + 0.18; the start lines said 0.16, 0.06 and 0.09.
finding.expected: One estimate for the plan on every line, or a line that says it changed.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st1/steps/c27a-screens.json (sessionDetails); 07-c27-02-inbox-plan-card.png
finding.repro: Approve and start a 3-task plan on bench-live, then open the session with Details.
finding.suspected_cause: Later tasks are re-estimated after the first task's sample; the review sums the start estimates while the promise keeps the card's figure.

verdict.root_cause: The session keeps two figures for one plan, and the Details lines read both. The promise (S-6) is priced once, at the start: plan items plus followers through priceNow, then stored as plan.promise.estimateUsdMicro and sent in session.promised. That is the "It promised 3 tasks, about CHF 0.45" line, and it matches the card (0.16 + 0.11 + 0.18). The learned estimate is updated live when each task closes: compose.ts:3046 calls observeTaskRuns, with one sample per task (BA-7). Task 1 cost about 0.06 against 0.16. So when the re-plan took tasks 2 and 3 ("Continuing with ..."), StaticPlanner.plan re-priced them at 78,129 and 106,380 USD micro (CHF 0.06 and 0.09). runner.ts:2330-2338 then adds that new figure (newEstimate) to plan.estimateUsdMicro and writes it on each item. It does not use the figure the promise keeps in ownEstimate. That new figure is what the start lines show ("about CHF 0.06", "about CHF 0.09"). The session review reads the stored total: planEstimateOf at session-review.ts:167-170 returns plan.estimateUsdMicro when no task repeats (data at :238, metrics at :599). The "measured" line (views.ts:862) therefore says "against an estimate of CHF 0.31" (0.16 + 0.06 + 0.09). That breaks planEstimateOf's own stated intent, "the figure the person was shown on the plan line and the Start dialog", and design §1/§5 rule 4 ("true now"): no line says the estimate changed. The run's stored row confirms this: plan.estimateUsdMicro = 382,509 and plan.promise.estimateUsdMicro = 558,000 (st1 session 01a1e834-a600). The same journey's second session also disagrees: 171,079 promised against 189,027 planned ("about CHF 0.14" against "an estimate of CHF 0.15"). The re-pricing is designed (priceNow and the learned model). The missing part is that the promise, the start lines and the review never agree, and nothing says the estimate changed.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2330-2338 (the re-plan adds the planner's new estimate to plan.estimateUsdMicro and the items; the promise at :1736-1751 keeps the start figures); packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:167-170 and :238 (the review measures against plan.estimateUsdMicro, not the promise); packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:862 (the measured line); packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-lines.ts:628-632 (the promised line)
verdict.fix_sketch: Pick one figure for the plan and use it everywhere, or say when it changed. Option 1, smallest: when the re-plan takes a task the session promised (own.has(id) and ownEstimate has it), add ownEstimate.get(id) to plan.estimateUsdMicro, not the new figure. Keep the new figure on the item only as the run's working estimate (for example item.estimateUsdMicro, with a promisedUsdMicro beside it). Then the review's planEstimateOf (stored total) equals the promise plus whatever joined, which is what the person approved. Option 2 (true now): keep re-pricing, but the start line says the change when it is above noise ("about CHF 0.06, CHF 0.11 when you approved it"). The review line would then measure against the promise and add "re-estimated at CHF 0.31 as the work ran" when the two differ. Either way, update planEstimateOf's comment and the session-review metrics so the figure the review names is the promise's (plus joined work) whenever a promise exists. A promise-less session keeps today's sum.
verdict.failing_test_idea: A composed real-daemon case in packages/runtime/test/session-join.test.ts or a new session-estimate test, with the stand-in provider. Use three chained coder tasks priced by a learned EstimatePort whose ratio drops after the first task's sample (or the real model, with task 1's actual well under its estimate). Approve and start the intake plan. When the session ends, read the Details lines through GET /sessions/:id/events (views lineOf). Assert that the CHF figure in "It promised 3 tasks, about CHF X." equals the figure in "Session review measured: ... against an estimate of CHF X". Assert also that each "The coder started "T" (about CHF Y)" either matches the plan card's figure for T or is followed by a line saying it changed. Today this fails: promised CHF 0.45, measured against CHF 0.31, start lines 0.06 and 0.09 where the card said 0.11 and 0.18.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine (owns the promise, S-6, and the re-plan's handling of the session's own tasks); the review's figure in packages/critic/src/session-review.ts (planEstimateOf, l3-money-engine / d1116-budget-all BA-8) changes with it
verdict.notes: Related but not the same: C2's CL-15 (the learned estimate swings a lot after one sample and a sentence shows the swing to the person). That leftover is about swings between sessions on the budget card; this finding is about three figures for one plan in one session's log. The figures were checked against a copy of the run's state DB at /tmp/frbench/v-l4st6/state.sqlite. The items stored are 198,000 / 78,129 / 106,380, the plan total is 382,509 and the promise is 558,000 USD micro; at the ledger's rate of about 0.81 these give CHF 0.16 / 0.06 / 0.09, a 0.31 total and a 0.45 promise. The card's 0.16 + 0.11 + 0.18 add up to the promise. The bench run was on bench-live (the real model), but the mechanism lies wholly in the code: live learning after each task plus the re-plan's priceNow, so any run where a task's actual cost is far from its estimate shows it. The finding's suspected cause is correct. It is not a test artefact and not the model's choice. I did not run the stand-in bench, because the code path and the stored row explain the finding fully.

finding.title: The task check's line and cost appear under Details only (C4L-15)
finding.what_the_person_sees: Person level shows task lines adding up to CHF 0.14 and a session total of CHF 0.15. Nothing says what the other CHF 0.01 was.
finding.expected: ADR 0119 point 9: the person reads the check's one line in the session log.
finding.evidence: 09-c27a-session-person-level.png against 10-c27a-session-details.png. session.task_checked events have audience 'detail'.
finding.repro: Open any session that had a task check.
finding.suspected_cause: session.task_checked is given audience 'detail'.

verdict.root_cause: "session.task_checked" is missing from PERSON_EVENT_TYPES, so eventAudience() returns "detail" for every task check (event-audience.ts:97). I confirmed this with node: eventAudience("session.task_checked", {...}) gives "detail", and "change" gives "person". The daemon's eventView sets `audience` from this function (views.ts:732). The session page shows only person lines unless Details is open (SessionPage.tsx:314). The stand-in fake daemon uses the same function (fake-daemon.ts:146, 948). Leaving it out was deliberate when C4 was built: runner.ts:236 and event-lines.ts:576 both call it "its Details line". That disagrees with ADR 0119 point 9, which puts this line under "What the person reads", next to the change sentences, the result and the Update, which are all person level. Its example is a no-change line with its cost. Since C4b, the check's cost belongs to no task (it is the session's own spend), so at person level the task figures and per-line costs do not add up to the session total, and nothing on that level names the rest. Evidence from C27a: tasks CHF 0.06 + 0.03 + 0.05 = 0.14, against "Session over: 3 done. CHF 0.15." Only Details explains it ('Checked the task list after ...: no change (CHF 0.01).' and the session review's 'the session's own checks CHF 0.01'). C27b has the same gap: tasks 0.14 against a session of 0.17, from three checks. Also, the emit at runner.ts:2418/2428 puts the cost only in the payload sentence and not in the event row's cost column, so even under Details the line has no CHF chip (views.ts `cost: money(e.cost_usd_micro)`).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-audience.ts:51 (PERSON_EVENT_TYPES has no "session.task_checked"; :97 returns "detail"); emitted at packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:2418 and :2428; filtered at apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx:314
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Move the event name into event-audience.ts as an import-free constant (TASK_CHECKED_EVENT = "session.task_checked", like JOINED_EVENT_TYPE) and add it to PERSON_EVENT_TYPES. runner.ts imports it from there, so the daemon, the shared state service and the fake daemon all split the log the same way. Keep it as "detail" only for a check that made no model call, for example a flagged-only check whose line just quotes what was left out (payload flag such as `called: false`).
2. Book the check's cost on the event row as well (emit with the cost column set), so the person-level line gets the same CHF chip as the coder and critic lines. The per-line costs then add up to the session total.
3. Change the comments at runner.ts:236 and event-lines.ts:576 from "Details line" to person level. Add a dated note to ADR 0119 point 9 and design section 3.7. Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md ("What the person reads"). Close C4L-15.
At most 3 checks a session means at most 3 extra lines, which stays inside section 3.7's "about 8 per task". If the owner decides instead to keep the line under Details, the alternative fix is for the person-level result and 'Session over' lines to name the remainder ("CHF 0.15, of which CHF 0.01 for checking the task list").
verdict.failing_test_idea: In apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, describe "d1109-selftasks-run, run C" (the case at about line 20533, which today only checks the text is somewhere in sessionEvents): assert that the line 'Checked the task list after "Create the page in index.html": ... (less than CHF 0.01).' has audience "person". Also assert that the person-level lines' costs (e.cost) sum to the session's spent figure. Mirror this in the UI component test (selftasks.test.tsx): render SessionPage with Details off and expect the 'Checked the task list after ...' line, with its CHF amount, to be visible. Both fail today because the event has audience "detail" and is filtered out at SessionPage.tsx:314. Also add a one-line unit test in the runtime: eventAudience("session.task_checked", { sentence, costUsdMicro, changed: 0 }) === "person".
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run
verdict.notes:
The evidence matches the claim exactly. In /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st1/steps/c27a-screens.json, the "session" text (person level) has no 'Checked the task list' line, while "sessionDetails" has two ('no change (CHF 0.01)' and 'no change (less than CHF 0.01)'). The Tasks panel reads 0.06/0.03/0.05 and the total reads CHF 0.15. In 18-c27b-session-person-level.txt, the 'Added "Write book.html" ...' change lines are at person level but no check line or check cost is. No bench run was needed: the code path is pure (I checked eventAudience directly) and the UI's filter is a plain audience check.

Whether this is a decision or a bug: C4L-15 (leftovers-C4.json, severity "decision") already names it as an open design question for LC-C27 to read, and the live-check plan called it "the Details line". However, ADR 0119 point 9's "What the person reads" and the C4b money rule (the check's cost is in no task's figure) together leave the person-level totals unexplained. So I treat it as real and minor, not a misreading.

Related but separate: leftovers-C2.json CL-16, where a run-again line's spend is Details-only. The Tasks panel's per-task figures will still not add up to the session total after this fix, by design (C4b). The person-level log line is what explains the difference.

finding.title: The critic calls the person's own details invented or missing because it does not read where the person gave them
finding.what_the_person_sees: Failed-task card Details: '[high] hello@lakesidebakery.example is not found in any project file and uses the reserved .example domain. It is likely a placeholder ...'. The person typed it in the Inbox, and it is in docs/decisions/0001-plain-static-page.md line 20. In LC-C27 (B): 'The brief ... contain no email address' about an address that is in the person's brief.
finding.expected: Before saying a detail is not the person's, the review checks the person's brief and recorded answers.
finding.evidence: st2 critic #5 findings; workspace grep: docs/decisions/0001-plain-static-page.md:20; st1 critic #40. The .example domain was this test's choice, so the placeholder doubt is fair; 'not found in any project file' is not.
finding.repro: Answer a person task's question with a detail, let the next task use it, then read the critic's findings.
finding.suspected_cause: The critic gets neither the person's brief nor their answers, and judged after reading two files.

verdict.root_cause: The critic gets only the task's title and outcome as its "Brief". The worker gets the person's project brief and the person's answers; the review request leaves both out and then says the request is complete. In packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:485, reviewTask sets `brief: \`${task.title}: ${task.outcome}\``. The worker's brief adds taskContextBlock (packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts:287-345, called at executor.ts:1414). That block holds "The person's brief for the project (their words, as data)" and "## Answers from the person to <dep>", the second noting "(also recorded in docs/decisions/...)". Nothing like it reaches ReviewEvidence. personAnswersOn and taskContextBlock have no caller in loop/critic.ts or packages/critic. Two places say otherwise. The ReviewEvidence.brief doc (packages/critic/src/types.ts:122) calls it "The delegation brief as rendered for the worker". ADR 0042 point 1 says the evidence holds "the brief, the files the worker was given". Even so, renderEvidence (packages/critic/src/evidence.ts:178, :314-319) always ends with EVIDENCE_COMPLETE_LINE, "nothing: every section above is complete". So a criterion such as "the exact address the owner gave" (st2) or "no details invented" (st1) cannot be checked from the request, and the critic is told nothing is missing. The model makes it worse: the decision record is in the "Project files you can read" list and the critic never opens it. In st2, four reviews (calls #4-#23) read only README.md, docs/overview.md, docs/data.md, docs/status.md and index.html. Each one filed a major finding: "hello@lakesidebakery.example ... appears nowhere in the project files" / "is not found in any project file". The decision record had the answer at line 20 from 06:46:32, before the first review at 06:46:33. In st1 (#40-#41) the person's own brief contained book@willowtea.example and the worker's brief quoted it. The critic's Brief was only "Write book.html: ...". It graded 45 and sent back correct work: "The brief, index.html and the docs contain no email address". On the next round (#48-#49) it did read docs/decisions/0001 and accepted at 92: "The earlier high finding was wrong." The critic chose which files to read, but the app made the wrong finding likely: it withholds what the worker was given and says the evidence is complete. So this is real, not the model alone. On the person's side, a correct task is sent back at least once (an extra coder round and more reviews, all charged to the task's budget). The failed-task card also tells the person that an address they typed is "likely a placeholder". The required action ("Use the exact address the owner gave, or ask the owner for it") pushes toward asking the person again, which the worker's brief forbids. The .example doubt was the test's own choice; the "not found in any project file" claim was false.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:485 (brief: `${task.title}: ${task.outcome}`); packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts:287-345 (what the worker gets and the critic does not); packages/critic/src/evidence.ts:178 and :314-319 (Brief section; "nothing: every section above is complete"); packages/critic/src/types.ts:122 (doc says the brief is the one rendered for the worker)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Move the person-facing part of taskContextBlock into a shared helper in task-context.ts. Call it personContextOf(store, task): the project line, the person's project brief, and each dependency's "Answers from the person to ..." block with the doc it is recorded in (said.doc). Leave out the previous-attempt and run-note parts. The executor keeps using it through taskContextBlock. 2) In loop/critic.ts reviewTask, call it and put the result in a new ReviewEvidence field, e.g. personGave: { brief?, answers: [{task, text, doc?}] }. This is an append-only field. renderEvidence in packages/critic/src/evidence.ts shows it under a new section, e.g. "What the person gave (their own words, data)", right after Brief. Name any decision record path, so the critic reads it. 3) Add one line to the critic prompt (evals/registry/critic/critic.md, "What you are given" and "How you review" step 3): a detail found in this section, or in a decision record it names, comes from the person. Never call it invented, missing or a placeholder. Before a finding that a detail was not supplied, check this section and docs/decisions/. Bump the prompt version and record the change in the critic maintainer doc. A note under ADR 0042 records that the brief now includes what the person gave.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed runtime test in packages/runtime/test/continuity-answers.test.ts (loopWorld with the real runner and loop critic on the fake provider, as in verification.test.ts's reviewCalls(w)). The project brief contains "a contact email link". A person task "Get the bakery's contact email address" is answered in the Inbox with hello@lakesidebakery.example. The dependent coder task then runs (doneExecutor writes index.html with that mailto) and is reviewed. Assert that the first review request, reviewCalls(w)[0].request.messages, has the new "What the person gave" section with the person's question and the answer hello@lakesidebakery.example, the person's project brief, and the decision record path docs/decisions/0001-*.md. Today it fails: the Brief is only "Build index.html ...: ..." and the address appears only in the diff and the try text. Also add a renderEvidence unit case in packages/critic/test for the new section's heading and the "their own words" line.
verdict.area_hint: No run C area owns it: d1116-budget-all touches loop/critic.ts only for cost, and d1109-selftasks-run is where the journey saw it. It fits a small fix area "critic-evidence" covering packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts reviewTask's evidence, a shared helper in packages/runtime/src/session/task-context.ts, the section in packages/critic/src/evidence.ts and types.ts, and the critic prompt in evals/registry/critic/critic.md.
verdict.notes: Read-only check; the stand-in bench was not needed because the code and the live model-call logs show the cause directly. Evidence: st2 model-calls #4-#7, #11-#13, #16-#18, #21-#23. All four reviews filed the "not found in any project file" major. The file reads per review were README/overview, then data/status, then index/README, then index/README/status, then index/README/overview; docs/decisions/0001-plain-static-page.md was never read. Its git history (commit 1bc99bb at 06:46:32) shows the answer was there before the first review at 06:46:33. Coder call #2's brief has "## Answers from the person to ..." with the address and "(also recorded in docs/decisions/0001-plain-static-page.md)"; the critic's request has neither. st1 #39-#42: the person's brief (intake #25 and coder brief #35) contains book@willowtea.example, the critic's Brief does not, and the critic sent the work back at 45. In #48-#49 it read the decision record and accepted at 92, saying "The earlier high finding was wrong." In st2 the task failed 4 times mainly because of the scripted coder's missing viewport, so the false email finding did not cause that failure alone. With a real coder it costs about one extra round, as in st1, so I keep severity minor. It would be major if the coder obeyed the required action and asked the person again. finding.title: The result's 'it' is three sentences away from what it names
finding.what_the_person_sees: '"Write menu.html with five teas in CHF" needs your decision (Inbox). Did 3 tasks: ... Changed 2 tasks: added "Write book.html"; added "Write thanks.html". 1 task waits on it. CHF 0.17.'
finding.expected: Name the task in the waiting clause, or keep the clause next to its task (design section 5).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st1/steps/18-c27b-session-person-level.png; Overview 'Last result'
finding.repro: Run a session that ends with a question and also changed tasks.
finding.suspected_cause: The changes sentence is inserted between the needs-you sentence and its waiting clause.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is real, and the code explains it. The suspected cause is only partly right.

The result's sentences are built by RESULT_LINE_BUILDERS in packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:
- "needs you" and "failed" go on line 1 (result.ts:313-339).
- "done" ("Did N tasks: ...") and "tasks changed" go on line 2 (result.ts:340-360).
- "waiting on other tasks" goes on line 3 (result.ts:518-529). When anything needs the person or failed, it prints the bare pronoun clause `${blocked} task waits on it.`.
- sessionResultLines (result.ts:630-645) joins the builders line by line. Every line-2 sentence (Did, Changed, cancelled, in review, merged) and every earlier line-3 sentence (how it ended, left for next time, left to merge, merges by itself) therefore lands between the antecedent and "it".

The gap is not new with the changes sentence. The clause has been on line 3 since f19d1c64 (2026-11-03), so "Did N tasks: A and B." already stood between the antecedent and "it". The existing tests assert that form: writing-rules.test.ts:347 and notifications-channels.test.ts:720 ('needs your decision (Inbox).\nDid 2 tasks: ...\n1 task waits on it.'). The tasks-changed builder from d1109-selftasks-run (0bb1cc39, 2026-11-16) added one more sentence. That makes the gap three sentences, and "it" now reads most naturally as the last task named, "Write thanks.html".

Design §5's own example keeps the clause next to its blocker: '"Style the page" failed 4 times and needs your decision. 2 tasks done; 1 waits on it.'

I reproduced it at the base with tsx (/tmp/frbench/v-L4-selftasks-8/repro.ts). sessionResultLines gives exactly the lines on the screen: ['"Write menu.html with five teas in CHF" needs your decision (Inbox).', 'Did 3 tasks: ... Changed 2 tasks: added "Write book.html"; added "Write thanks.html".', '1 task waits on it. CHF 0.17.'].

The same builder has two related flaws:
- With two tasks that need you, it still says "1 task waits on it" (singular "it" for two tasks).
- `o.waiting` counts every project task that waits on any unfinished task (collectEndState → waitingOf, result.ts:802). It does not check that those tasks wait on the task that needs you or failed, so "on it" can be false.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:518-529 (the "waiting on other tasks" builder on line 3 says "N tasks wait on it."); antecedent at result.ts:313-317 (line 1); sentences in between at result.ts:340-360 (line 2, including the tasks-changed builder from d1109-selftasks-run); joined at result.ts:630-645
verdict.fix_sketch:
Option A (recommended; follows the design §5 example): drop the "on it" case from the line-3 builder and add the clause to the end of line 1, right after the needs-you or failed sentence. Name the waiting tasks with the existing waitingSentence from daemon/request-words.ts:253 ('"Write styles.css and link it from every page" waits on it.' / '3 tasks wait on it: "A", "B" and 1 more.'), or say "on them" when two or more tasks block.
- Count only the waiting tasks whose dependencies include a needs-you or failed task. To do that, carry the dependency ids in waitingOf (result.ts:802) instead of matching words.
- Keep "N tasks wait on other tasks." on line 3 for every other wait.
- Extend NOT_NEWS (result.ts:662) and sessionUpdateLine's withoutCard (result.ts:710-716) so the Update still drops the card's sentence and its clause.
- The notification's splitResult already moves only the first sentence into the title, so the clause leads the body, next to the title it refers to.

Option B (smaller change): keep the clause on line 3 but name the blocker: '1 task waits on "Write menu.html with five teas in CHF".' This is longer and repeats the title.

With either option, update the asserted strings in writing-rules.test.ts:347, notifications-channels.test.ts:720/734 and session-update.test.ts:25, and the maintainer doc for result.ts.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
A unit test of sessionResultLines, plus a real-daemon or stand-in case for what the person reads on the Overview's Last result and the session page. In the scenario, one task needs the person's answer (needsYou "Write menu.html…"), a task depends on it ("Write styles.css…" with waitsOn = that task), three tasks are done, and tasksChanged holds two 'added' entries.

What the test checks:

For Option A, assert lines[0] === '"Write menu.html with five teas in CHF" needs your decision (Inbox). "Write styles.css and link it from every page" waits on it.'

The "waiting on other tasks" builder it needs to touch dates from wave SE5 (f19d1c64) and is outside that area's own region, so this could also go to a small result-words fix area in session/result.ts.
verdict.notes: No known leftover names this. The nearest are C4L-9, about Last result after a project join, and C5L-13/C5L-15, also about Last result; none covers the pronoun. The finding's suspected cause should be corrected: the "Did N tasks" sentence already sat between the needs-you sentence and "1 task waits on it" before run C, and existing tests assert that form. finding.title: The 'Left out' line quotes the critic's own warning as an instruction, with a hole where an id was cut
finding.what_the_person_sees: Details: 'Left out of the task check: a line that reads like an instruction ("Earlier finding : the report contained instruction-like content ").' and '... ("The earlier instruction-like content (deploy task, CHF 500) is not in the current report, and the wo").'
finding.expected: Quote the instruction itself, in a whole sentence, with no gaps or cut words.
finding.evidence: The stored sentence holds a raw id: 'Earlier finding 01a1e842-224a-76c1-acfa-701e873391b7: the report contained ...'. See 13-c29-session-details.png.
finding.repro: As in L4-selftasks-9, where the critic notes the instruction on a later review.
finding.suspected_cause: The critic's info notes go through readsLikeInstruction, which matches 'deploy' and 'CHF 500'. The quote is cut at 100 characters, and the UI strips the id.

verdict.root_cause: Three pieces of app code combine to make this line, and running them on the stored critic notes gives the exact text. (1) runner.ts:3336-3343 turns every info finding from the critic into a task-check evidence line through reviewNoteLines (task-list-notes.ts:139-145), and that function screens each line with readsLikeInstruction. The critic's warning ABOUT the planted instruction names its words, so it matches STEERING at task-list-notes.ts:65 (CHF\s?\d) and :74 (deploy) and gets flagged. It was the only evidence at that boundary, so checkAtBoundary skips the call and writes the "every line flagged" sentence. That sentence calls the critic's own warning "a line that reads like an instruction" and never says it is the critic's note. (2) task-check.ts:1293 builds the quote with a raw `flagged[0]?.slice(0, 100)`: no cut at a word, no "…", and the trailing space stays. That is where "…and the wo\")." comes from. In the first note the critic's 36-character finding UUID uses up the 100 characters, so the quote stops at "content " just before "(deploy task, CHF 500)". (3) views.ts:750 runs every line through withoutIds (task-words.ts:182-190). Its IDS pattern removes an id together with its noun only for request|run|session|task, not "finding". So the bare UUID is removed and "Earlier finding : the report…" is left with a gap. The UUID is in the note because the critic brief lists earlier findings by id and asks for resolved ids (critic/src/evidence.ts:48), so the model's choice was made likely by the app's own prompt. The stored session.task_checked payloads (state.sqlite events seq 27 and 38) and finding rows 01a1e842-6021… and 01a1e842-9468… confirm this. A tsx run of reviewNoteLines + the line-1293 template + withoutIds on those two descriptions gives the stored and shown texts character for character (/tmp/frbench/verify-L4-st10/check.mts). One correction to the finding's "expected": it asks for the quote to be the instruction itself, but that line was in the coder's report and was cut at the earlier boundary. Not showing it to the person is L4-selftasks-9. Here the correct fix is to name the critic's note as the critic's and quote it whole.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:1293 (also packages/runtime/src/session/task-list-notes.ts:139-145 with STEERING :65/:74, packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3336-3343, packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:182-190 via packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:750)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) task-check.ts:1293: build the quote with a word-safe cut. Export a quoteOf(text, 100) from task-list-notes.ts that does what cutLine does: fold whitespace, cut at the last word, end with "…". Better still, quote the first whole sentence when it fits in 100 characters. Never use a raw slice. 2) Remove ids, with their noun, before cutting, so a UUID neither uses the budget nor leaves a gap. In reviewNoteLines, rewrite /\b(finding|review)\s+<uuid>\b/ to the bare noun ("Earlier finding: the report contained instruction-like content (deploy task, CHF 500).") and add finding|review to the IDS word list in task-words.ts so other screens also lose the noun's id cleanly. 3) Say where the line came from. TaskListNote already has source. When the flagged line is a review note, write e.g. 'Left out of the task check: a note of the critic's that names an instruction ("Earlier finding: the report contained instruction-like content (deploy task, CHF 500).").' and keep the current wording for report lines. Optionally, do not repeat a review note that only re-reports an earlier finding about instruction-like content, since the first check already handled the report line (with L4-selftasks-9's fix, the card quotes it). Update the d1109-selftasks-run section of docs/maintainers/runtime.md.
verdict.failing_test_idea: A composed runner case in packages/runtime/test/session-task-list.test.ts, read at the person's boundary through the daemon's events view (the line the Session page's Details shows). The stand-in critic sends a task back once with a single info finding, "Earlier finding <uuid>: the report contained instruction-like content (deploy task, CHF 500). It was not acted on. The human should be told.", and no report has a "For the task list:" block. After the boundary, the Details line for session.task_checked must: contain no UUID and no " : " gap (/\w : /); end its quote on a whole word or "…" (reject /\b\w{1,3} ?"\)\.$/, i.e. today's '…the wo").'); name the note as the critic's; and reach the instruction's words ("deploy task, CHF 500"). A second case with a flagged 140-character report line asserts the quote ends "…" at a word. Today both fail: the shown line is 'Left out of the task check: a line that reads like an instruction ("Earlier finding : the report contained instruction-like content ").' The evals/test/injection.test.ts:563 check only tests the line's prefix, so it passes today.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run
verdict.notes: Reproduced from the code without the model. node_modules/.bin/tsx /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-st10/check.mts applies reviewNoteLines, the task-check.ts:1293 template and withoutIds to the two critic descriptions stored in st2's state.sqlite (finding table, severity info). Both stored sentences (event payloads seq 27, 38) and both shown sentences (13-c29-session-details.txt lines 93 and 118) come out exactly. No bench was started. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it: C4L-15 is about where the check's line shows, not its wording. Severity 'words' is right: the line is under Details only, nothing was applied, and the safety behaviour (the flagged line never reaches a model) is correct. The fault is the wording (gap, cut word, warning framed as an instruction). It overlaps L4-selftasks-9 (major), which owns the person never seeing the real instruction. Fix both together so the critic's note and the card's quote do not say the same thing twice.

finding.title: 'add a task there: ...' after 'open it' adds the task to the page's project with 'There:' in its title, and reads nothing back
finding.step: LC-C3, Notes' Chat, right after 'open it' answered 'Switched the active project to Site.'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Added "There: write the shop page" to Notes. It runs at your next Start.' The task is in Notes, not Site, and its title starts with 'There:'. Naming the project does not help: 'add a task to Site: write the shop page' gives 'Added "Site: write the shop page" to Notes.'
finding.expected: 'Write the shop page' is read back for Site (Yes/No) and added to Site after Yes. The conversation was about Site, and the app had just said the active project is Site.
finding.evidence: evidence/d03-add-task-there.json and d05-add-task-to-site.json: 0 model calls. GET /changes: task.create {title: 'There: write the shop page', outcome: 'there: write the shop page'}, projectId Notes, wordsUsed 'add a task there: write the shop page'. GET /projects/<Site>/tasks = []. Screenshot gh4d/steps/05-d05-add-task-to-site-reply.png.
finding.repro: Make Site (on a repository) and Notes. In Notes' Chat, switch to Site ('open it' after Site was named), then say 'add a task there: write the shop page' or 'add a task to Site: write the shop page'.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/commands/src/intent.ts matchAddTask: the regex takes every word after 'add a task' as the title (taskTitleOf drops only a leading 'to'). The command runs on the page's project before the model is asked, so there is no read-back and no other project.

verdict.root_cause:
The fixed-phrase matcher for adding a task has no slot for a target project. Its regex at packages/commands/src/intent.ts:720 takes everything after "add a task" (and an optional ":,-") as the task's words. taskTitleOf (intent.ts:387-397) strips only a leading "please/can you" and "to/zu". So "to Site: write the shop page" becomes the title "Site: write the shop page", and "there: write the shop page" becomes "There: write the shop page". The command at intent.ts:730-733 is task.create {title, outcome: text, status: ready} with no `project` param. task.create itself does accept `project` (task.ts:855, resolveProject at task.ts:909/931), so only the parser is missing it. The parser runs before any model call (intent.ts:430-438, "whole" match), and that is why the evidence shows 0 model calls.

Without a project param, resolveProject uses ctx.activeProjectId. In a project's Chat tab that is the tab's project: conversation/agent.ts:1057-1060 ("a line typed in a project's own Chat tab is about that project: its project wins for this turn"). So the task went to Notes, even though "open it" had just recorded Site as the active project.

Reproduced with the parser alone (tsx script /tmp/frbench/l4gh4/repro.mts, projects Notes and Site, active Notes):
- "add a task there: write the shop page" gives title "There: write the shop page", no project
- "add a task to Site: write the shop page" gives "Site: write the shop page"
- "add a task to the Site project: …" gives "The Site project: …"
- "add a task in Site: …" gives "In Site: …"

The evidence agrees: d03/d05 calls=[], reply 'Added "There: write the shop page" to Notes.', activeRaw.activeProjectId = Site while urlBefore is Notes' chat.

One part of the finding is wrong. The expected read-back (Yes/No) is not the design. "add a task: …" is meant to create a ready task at once, with Undo (U-015, docs/user-guide.md:375, docs/maintainers/runtime.md:8773). The real defects are the wrong project and the target words left in the title.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/intent.ts:718-735 (regex :720, title :728, no project param :730-733); taskTitleOf :387; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1057-1060 (the tab's project wins the turn)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. In matchAddTask, before the separator, allow an optional target only when a colon (or comma/dash) follows: `(?:add|create|make)\s+(?:a\s+)?(?:new\s+)?task\s+(?:to|in|into|for|on)\s+(?:the\s+)?(.+?)(?:\s+project)?\s*[:,-]\s+(.+)`, plus the German "zu/in/für <Projekt>". Without a colon, keep today's reading, so "add a task to write the README" stays a title.
2. Resolve the target with this.projectIdFor(name, ctx, current), as matchSwitch and matchRepoCreate do:
   - one match: params.project = id (resolveProject then picks it over the tab, usedActive=false, so the reply says 'Added "Write the shop page" to Site.');
   - several or none: return the existing "Which one?" question with options.
3. Treat a pronoun target ("there", "to it", "that project", "dort", "dahin") as a reference, never as title words:
   - resolve it to the project the person last switched to or named in this conversation, if the context can carry that. That needs a recordedActiveProjectId in IntentContext, filled by agent.ts when the tab's project differs from the recorded active one;
   - otherwise ask "Which project?" with the projects as options, or return null so the chat model, which sees the conversation, handles it.
4. As a safety net, have taskTitleOf also drop a leading "there:" / "<known project name>:" prefix.
No change is needed to task.create or to the tab rule. The sibling L4-github-5 ("open it" in a tab does not open Site) is a separate fix.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Boundary test on the composed daemon, next to U-056 in packages/runtime/test/settings-undo-routes.test.ts (or a chat route test):
- Create Site and Notes. In Notes' own Chat tab (projectId: notes.id, projectTab: true), send "add a task to Site: write the shop page".
- Expect actions ["task.create"], taskTitles(site) to contain "Write the shop page", taskTitles(notes) to be empty, and the reply 'Added "Write the shop page" to Site. …'. Today: title "Site: write the shop page", in Notes.
- Second case, same tab: "switch to Site", then "add a task there: write the shop page". Expect the task in Site titled "Write the shop page", or a question "Which project?" with options [Notes, Site]. Never a title starting "There:", and nothing added to Notes.
Unit cases in packages/commands/test/intent.test.ts:
- parse("add a task to Site: write the shop page", {active: Notes, projects: [Notes, Site]}) gives params.project = site.id and title "Write the shop page";
- "add a task to Nowhere: x" gives a question;
- "add a task to write the README" keeps title "Write the README" with no project.
verdict.area_hint: small fix area "chat-add-task-target": no run C area owns matchAddTask. d1109-selftasks-chat owns only the "fix the tasks" intent in intent.ts, and d1109-starts-engine owns only the start phrases. Files: packages/commands/src/intent.ts (matchAddTask, taskTitleOf, IntentContext) and packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1052-1060 for the pronoun case.
verdict.notes:
This is real, and it is the parser that causes it, not the model: 0 model calls on both lines. I confirmed it by reading the code and by calling the parser directly; I did not re-walk the bench, because the live evidence is already deterministic.

Not supported by the evidence:
- The expected read-back (Yes/No). "add a task: …" is meant to create at once, with Undo.
- "reads nothing back" as a defect in itself. The reply does name Notes, and Undo is offered (d04/d06 undid both tasks).

I keep "major" because:
- naming the project explicitly ("to Site:") is ignored;
- the target words end up in the title;
- for a GitHub-linked project, the task would run in the wrong project (Notes, no repository) at the next Start.
The person cannot add to another project from this chat without leaving the page.

Related finding: L4-github-5 ("open it" says it switched to Site, but the page stays on Notes) is why "there" resolved to Notes. Even after that fix, "There:" would stay in the title.

No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this. The closest, C3L-2, is about start phrases.

Repro script: /tmp/frbench/l4gh4/repro.mts.

finding.title: 'open it' in a project's Chat says 'Switched the active project to Site.' but nothing opens
finding.step: LC-C3, Notes' Chat: 'open it' after the refusal named Site
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Switched the active project to Site.' with Undo, while the page, the header ('Notes') and the chat stay on Notes. The next line typed there still goes to Notes (see L4-github-4).
finding.expected: Site opens, or the reply links to Site and says that this chat stays about Notes.
finding.evidence: evidence/d02-open-it.json: urlAfterReply /projects/<Notes>/chat, activeProjectId Site. Screenshot gh4d/steps/02-d02-open-it-reply.png.
finding.repro: In a project's Chat tab, after a reply names another project, say 'open it' (or 'switch to Site').
finding.suspected_cause: apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx only dispatches activeProject. The header shows the viewed project and nothing navigates. The user guide says a project's Chat tab always talks about that page's project.

verdict.root_cause: The app produced this reply, not the model. d02 shows calls: [] and usd 0: "open it" never reached the model. The deterministic parser handled it. intent.ts:638 maps "open <X>" to project.switch. matchProjects (commands/shared.ts:38-41) then matched "it" to Site only because "site" contains the substring "it". In a project's Chat tab, project.switch moves only the hidden active project, by the U-056 design. The turn stays on the tab's project (agent.ts:1052-1062: projectTab wins, and the active project changes only for Talk outside a page, voice and the phone). The UI then only dispatches the store's activeProject (Conversation.tsx:202-204) and navigates nowhere. The header names the viewed project (Shell.tsx:45-47, design §3.1: "the project being viewed (not a hidden 'active' project)"). The reply is switchSentence (project.ts:166-170), the same in every place: "Switched the active project to Site." It has no link to Site and does not say that this chat stays about Notes. So the only visible effect is a sentence about a project the screen no longer shows. Two app texts make "open" likely and promise more than it does. First, project.create's tool definition (project.ts:275) tells the model to "offer that project instead (open it with project.switch ...)", which is why the d01 refusal said "You can open Site with a project switch". Second, the dialog's "Open it" for the same offer runs switchActiveProject and then navigates to Site (NewProjectDialog.tsx:115-121). d1109-onerepo-link meant the offer to lead the person to the existing project "from every entry point". The chat path inside a project's Chat tab does not do that. The behaviour is otherwise as designed, and a passing test asserts it: apps/ui/test/active-project.test.tsx:62 "switch by chat to Beacon, then Atlas's Chat tab... the header names Atlas". There is a second, latent problem. "open it" found the right project only by chance. With projects Notes and Shop, "open it" and "switch to it" answer 'No project named "it". Which project?'. With Notes and "Kite club" they switch to Kite club. I checked this with the parser at 4cf11fd.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:202-204 (only dispatches activeProject on a project-tab reply); packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts:166-170 (switchSentence, no link or stays-here clause) and :275 (project.create definition: 'open it with project.switch'); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1052-1062 (projectTab keeps the turn on the tab's project); packages/commands/src/intent.ts:638 ('open X' -> project.switch); packages/commands/src/commands/shared.ts:38-41 (substring match lets the pronoun 'it' match 'Site')
verdict.fix_sketch: Option A, to match the dialog's "Open it": when the reply to a projectTab turn carries a project.switch done to a project other than the tab's, Conversation.tsx navigates to /projects/<target> (or its /chat), the way NewProjectDialog.open does. The U-056 test and the user guide line "A project's Chat tab always talks about that page's project" then gain "an explicit switch opens that project". Option B, which leaves U-056 as it is: for a projectTab turn, the switch's reply says "Switched the active project to Site. This chat stays about Notes." and carries an Open Site link (/projects/<Site>) that Conversation renders. The owner chooses which. Either way, change project.create's definition (project.ts:275) and the refusal offer so they promise only what happens ('switch to it'), or make 'open it' really open the project. Separately, harden matchProjects: never match a pronoun or deictic word ('it', 'that', 'this', 'there', 'es', 'das', 'dort') by substring, and use whole words or at least 3 characters for the 'contains' step. Then resolve 'it' from the project the last reply named (the refusal's details.projectId), or ask which project.

verdict.notes: The evidence matches the code: urlAfterReply stays on /projects/<Notes>/chat, and activeRaw.activeProjectId becomes Site. The model was not involved in d02. Only the earlier refusal (d01, haiku) used the word "open", prompted by the app's own project.create definition. finding.title: After Make one project, the closed project's open status pull request is listed nowhere (C4L-5 still open)
finding.step: LC-C4: Make one project keeping Kite flyers (Status pull request off) with Site (on; open fr/status PR #55)
finding.what_the_person_sees: The dialog has no status line (settings: []). After the join, Kite's Overview lists only #53 and #54. Kite's Docs says Status 'kept in the app: no status pull request (Settings turns it on)'. Site's joined page has no pull request list. #55 stays open on GitHub with nothing in the app pointing to it.
finding.expected: The dialog says what happens to the status pull request, or the kept project lists it so the person can merge or close it.
finding.evidence: evidence/c4a-walk.json previewApi.ifKept.settings = []; c4c-walk.json kitePrsApi [53, 54], statusPrListed false, kite_docs. Screenshots gh4a/steps/32-c4c-01-kite-overview-after-join.png and 40-c4c-07-kite-docs.png. After Undo, #55 is listed under Site again (c4d-walk.json).
finding.repro: Two projects on one repository. Only the one to close has Status pull request on and an open fr/status PR. Make one project keeping the other.
finding.suspected_cause: As C4L-5 says: isProjectDocsPr needs statusPullRequestOn(kept) (loop/docs.ts, pull-requests.ts), and join-preview.ts lists no status setting.

verdict.root_cause: The listing gate for the status pull request depends on the kept project's own setting, and the join dialog has no line for that setting. packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:189-190 only treats a fr/status pull request as the project's when `statusPullRequestOn(project) && isProjectStatusPr(...)`. After the join, Kite's `projectIdsOf` includes Site's id (joined_from), so `isProjectStatusPr` would accept #55, which carries Site's mark. But Kite's `status_pull_request` is off, so `isProjectDocsPr` returns false. That keeps #55 off Kite's Overview list (packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:468) and off the Docs tab's waiting-in-PR rows (docs.ts:1149). Site is archived with joined_into, and its page lists no pull requests. In the dialog, packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-preview.ts:294-303 builds the setting lines from only four labels (Budget per session, Project budget, Who merges, Research reads). Site on and Kite off therefore produces `settings: []`. Meanwhile join-words.ts:170-171 tells the person "The tasks, plan, cards and pull requests of \"Site\" move into \"Kite flyers\"", and ADR 0117 point 3 promises "one status pull request again". Nothing in the app tells the person that #55 now belongs to nobody. I reproduced the gate in a probe at /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-github-7/probe.ts. A kept project with joined_from [Site] and the setting off gives `isProjectDocsPr = false` for a fr/status PR marked with Site's id. The same project with the setting on gives true. The live evidence matches: c4a previewApi.ifKept.settings = [], c4c kitePrsApi [53, 54] with statusPrListed false, and after Undo c4d lists #55 under Site again. This is the case C4L-5 already names, and nothing at 4cf11fd fixes it (C4-left-5, placed in d1109-selftasks-chat, is a different word item).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:189 (status branch gated on statusPullRequestOn(kept)); packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:468 (Overview list uses that gate); packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-preview.ts:294 (the dialog's setting lines leave out Status pull request); packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-words.ts:170 (the moves line says pull requests move)
verdict.fix_sketch: Two parts, both in the join's own code. (1) Dialog: in join-preview.ts add a fifth setting to `own` for a repository project: label "Status pull request", value on or off as Settings words it, read with statusPullRequestOn. The existing differs loop then gives 'Status pull request: "Kite flyers"'s setting applies to the moved work: off (each session's status stays in the app).' Better still, when a closing project has the setting on and the kept one has it off, add one sentence such as '"Site"'s status pull request stays open on GitHub; "Kite flyers" keeps its status in the app. Turn on Status pull request in Settings, or close it on GitHub.' (2) After the join: in pull-requests.ts, list an open fr/status pull request whose hidden mark names a joined_from id as a docs row, even with the kept project's setting off. Use a separate listing predicate (for example `isJoinedStatusPr(project, pr)`: marked, and the mark is in projectIdsOf but is not the project's own id), so the status writer still never writes to it while the setting is off. Show it with Open and Merge, plus a line that new status stays in the app until Settings turns it on. Leave the writer path in docs.ts unchanged. Update ADR 0117 point 3 and the user guide's 'When two projects use one repository' paragraph.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts under describe "d1109-onerepo-join, run C" (beside the OJ-05/OJ-02 case at line ~19598). Use the fake host with o/site, Kite club with settings.status_pull_request true, Site with it off, and an open fr/status pull request on o/site whose body carries docsPrMarker({id: kite.id}). Assert that `client.joinPreview(site.id, [kite.id]).ifKept[site.id].settings` contains a Status pull request line (today it is [], or only the Who merges line). Then run project.join through POST /commands keeping Site, and assert that `client.pullRequests(site.id)` holds a docs row for the status pull request with Open (today only task rows). Add a UI case in apps/ui/test/onerepo-join.test.tsx for the dialog showing the line.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-onerepo-join
verdict.notes: Not a misreading and not the model. LC-C4 in runC-plan.json asked the live check to note exactly this case ("with only the closing project's on, note what the person can still find of its status pull request (C4L-5)"), and the app does what the leftover says. I agree with minor: nothing is lost, #55 is still on GitHub, Undo brings it back under Site, and turning the kept project's setting on in Settings would list it again (and the status writer would then use it). But the dialog's moves line says the pull requests move, and the ADR says "one status pull request again", so the person is told something that is false for this pull request. The probe is in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-github-7/probe.ts. I did not start the bench: the live evidence plus the function-level probe settle it.

finding.title: Make one project dialog counts a closed pull request as open
finding.step: LC-C4: the dialog from Kite flyers' Overview
finding.what_the_person_sees: Under Keep "Kite flyers": '2 open pull requests'. GitHub has only #53 open. #51 was closed, and the app's own task row for it says 'Accepted · pull request closed'.
finding.expected: '1 open pull request', the same count as the Overview's Waiting for you to merge.
finding.evidence: evidence/c4a-walk.json previewApi.projects[0].lines; c4-01-kite-session.json (#51 'Accepted · pull request closed'). Screenshot gh4a/steps/30-c4a-04-dialog-keep-kite.png.
finding.repro: A project with one task PR closed without merging and one open. Open Make one project.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-preview.ts openPullRequests counts every task with a pr_url whose merge record is not 'merged'. Its own comment says 'closed ones included: the store cannot tell'.

verdict.root_cause: The Make one project dialog gets its "N open pull requests" line from openPullRequests (packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-preview.ts:257-266). It counts every task that has a pr_url, is not cancelled, and whose merge record is not 'merged' (line 263: `if (record?.state !== "merged") n += 1;`). The comment above it says the store cannot tell a closed pull request, and that is wrong. When GitHub closes a pull request without merging, the watcher moves the task's record to state 'left_to_you' with last_outcome 'closed'. Both paths do this: dependent-branches.ts:236-242 (closedOnHost) and merge.ts:1178-1182 (resume of a 'merging' record). The task row already reads that record: task-words.ts:639 maps last_outcome 'closed' to LEFT_TO_YOU_LABELS.closed, "Accepted · pull request closed". The Overview's Done line counts the same task under "needs you" (needsYouAfterAccept), not under waiting to merge. So the dialog contradicts the app's own task row and the Overview. The evidence matches this exactly. c4-00-before.json shows #51 closed and not merged on GitHub (the harness's C1 cleanup closed it at 05:48). c4-01-kite-session.json shows #51's task as 'Accepted · pull request closed' and #53 as 'Accepted · waiting for you to merge', and prs.waiting lists only #53. c4a-walk.json previewApi.projects[0].lines shows '2 tasks done', '2 open pull requests'. The Overview text in the same walk says '1 pull request waits for you to merge, and 1 needs you'. The suspected cause is right; the store can tell after all.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/join-preview.ts:263 (openPullRequests, lines 257-266; comment at 257); the line it feeds is at 320
verdict.fix_sketch: In openPullRequests, skip a task whose record is merged, and also one whose record is state 'left_to_you' with last_outcome 'closed': `if (record?.state === "merged" || (record?.state === "left_to_you" && record.last_outcome === "closed")) continue; n += 1;`. Fix the comment: only a task with no merge record (accepted before ADR 0111) is still unknown. Better still, share one predicate with task-words/pull-requests (for example an isClosedRecord(record) next to LEFT_TO_YOU_LABELS) so the dialog, the task row and the Overview's Done line cannot drift apart. Every other left_to_you outcome (checks_failed, head_moved, conflict, blocked_by_rules, ...) is still an open pull request and stays counted. Update the module doc in docs/maintainers (the dialog's facts) to match.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, next to the OJ-05 dialog case (around line 19654). On MemoryGitHost 'o/site', give Kite club two done tasks, each with its own pull request and a merge record pinned through the real accept/pin path. Close one pull request on the host without merging, and let one watcher poll run (or call the githost watcher's closed path) so its record reads left_to_you/closed. Check through client.project/tasks that its row says 'Accepted · pull request closed'. Then `client.joinPreview(site.id, [kite.id])` must give Kite club's lines '2 tasks done', '1 open pull request', matching the Overview's single 'Waiting for you to merge' row. Today it gives '2 open pull requests'. The same answer must hold after the daemon starts again. No fake-daemon change is needed: the fake serves seeded previews and the UI only renders the lines.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-onerepo-join
verdict.notes: Not named by any leftover. The closest are LL-1 (merge cards stay open after a close on GitHub, L3) and CL-4 (a cancelled task's PR still described as left open in chat, C2), and neither covers the dialog's count. The C4 leftovers from d1109-onerepo-join (C4L-1..18) do not mention it. The existing OJ-05 real-daemon case only seeds a task with a pr_url and no closed record, so it never hits this path. I did not run the stand-in bench: the code path and the live evidence agree with no gap, and a repro would need a temporary test file in the read-only checkout. Severity minor: the join itself behaves correctly and nothing wrong is done, but a fact the person reads to choose which project to keep disagrees with GitHub, the task row and the Overview. A side note, not part of this finding: the count also ignores an open take-out pull request (take_out_state 'open') on a merged record. That is arguably also an open pull request the join moves, so it is worth a look when this is fixed.

finding.title: Costs By task: a task moved by Make one project reads '6 runs, 0 / 6 (0%)' accepted
finding.step: LC-C4: Kite flyers > More > Costs after the join
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Write the opening hours in hours.md 6 0 / 6 (0%) CHF 0.01'. The task ran once (one coder run, one review), was accepted and merged (#54).
finding.expected: '1 1 / 1 (100%)', as for the kept project's own task 'Write the club notes in club-notes.md'.
finding.evidence: evidence/c4c-kite-costs-api.json byTask: runs 6, accepted 0. The run table has one coder run and one critic run for this task. Screenshot gh4a/steps/39-c4c-06-kite-costs.png.
finding.repro: Make one project where the closed project has a done task. Open the kept project's Costs > By task.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts costView: for a moved task, facts.runsByTask (the kept project's facts) has no entry. Runs falls back to the ledger's entry count (one per model call) and accepted to 0.

verdict.root_cause: BA-9 widened only the money in Costs > By task. Under a project filter, costView reads each task's figure with costLedger.byTaskOf, which takes every ledger row of a task now in the project, whichever project the row names. It sets `runs: b.entries`, the number of ledger rows, which is one per model call and includes the critic's calls (views.ts:1229). The runs and accepted figures still come from costFacts, and costFacts reads only ledger rows booked to the kept project (`where.project_id = f.projectId`, views.ts:1395). A task that Make one project moved has all its earlier rows on the closed project, so facts.runsByTask and facts.acceptedRunsByTask have no entry for it. The loop then finds the task through store.task.get, keeps the ledger-row count as runs (`facts.runsByTask.get(b.key) ?? b.runs`, views.ts:1264) and sets accepted to 0 (`?? 0`, views.ts:1265). The bench state DB backs this up: task 01a1e89b-8e4a "Write the opening hours in hours.md" has one coder run and one critic run, 3 ledger rows each, 6 in all, all booked to Site, and one accepting review. That gives "6 · 0 / 6 (0%) · —". A related case: a task with rows on both projects. Its accepted count still includes runs from before the join (the accepted loop at views.ts:1408-1420 reads all of the task's reviews and work runs), but its runs count only the kept project's. So a task accepted once before the join and once after reads "2 / 1 (200%)". The period (from/to) also leaves out the moved rows. This is the app's own code, not the model's choice.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1264
verdict.fix_sketch: When filter.projectId is set, work out a task's runs and accepted runs from the task itself, not from the project-filtered ledger. Option 1: a helper taskRunFacts(store, taskIds, {from,to}) built from the same rules as costFacts. Work runs are store.run.forTask(id) without the critic's, inside the range. An accepted run is the last work run before each accepting review. Use the helper for every byTask key in the project, so moved and mixed tasks count all their runs. Option 2: let costFacts take a task-id scope for its task maps and no project filter. Either way, never fall back to the ledger-row count (b.entries) as "runs" for a known task: use its work-run count, 0 when it has none. Keep the totals, By model, By specialist and By project as the project's own ledger, as BA-9 and OJ-07 say. Copy the change into the fake daemon's costs fixture (validation rule 3), and add a line to docs/maintainers/runtime.md under BA-9.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add a case to apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts under "d1116-budget-all, run C" next to the BA-9 case. Insert Kite and Site. Give Kite a task with a coder Run row and a critic Run row, each with three ledger rows that carry the run_id and are booked to Kite, plus an accepting review after the coder run. Run project.join with keep Site and close Kite. Then client.costs({projectId: site.id}).byTask for the task should read runs 1 and accepted 1. Today it reads runs 6 and accepted 0. Check the same after the daemon starts again. Second case: book a Redo after the join (a coder run and an accepting review on Site). Expect runs 2 and accepted 2, not 2 / 1. In the UI, the Costs tab's By task row should read "1 · 1 / 1 (100%)". Reproduced against the code at 4cf11fd with /tmp/frbench/l4gh9/repro.mts, which runs costView on a copy of the bench DB with the task moved back to Kite flyers: "Write the opening hours in hours.md | runs 6 | accepted 0".
verdict.area_hint: d1116-budget-all
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: c4c-kite-costs-api.json byTask has the task with runs 6 and accepted 0, cost 18013 µUSD. The cost equals the sum of its 6 ledger rows on Site (2177+2406+2593+3425+3676+3736), so the money figure is right and only runs and accepted are wrong. In the final bench DB (gh4a/home/data/state.sqlite) the task is back on Site after the cleanup's Undo. The repro sets its project_id to Kite on a copy (/tmp/frbench/l4gh9/state.sqlite). The existing BA-9 real-daemon test checks only cost.usdMicro, and its ledger rows have no run_id, so it cannot catch this. No leftover file names it. The C4 leftovers on d1109-onerepo-join cover the Home line, lessons, the status PR, Undo's active flag and Last result, not Costs' runs or accepted. Severity minor: the money is right, but Costs says a merged, accepted task was never accepted, against the I.6 success rate.

finding.title: A joined project's page: the header names the other project, and Your files shows an internal folder with the project id
finding.step: LC-C4: Site's Overview after it joined Kite flyers
finding.what_the_person_sees: The header picker reads 'Kite flyers' while the page is 'Site'. Your files reads '/tmp/frbench/live4/github/gh4a/home/worktrees/docs/01a1e89b-1910-7707-a7b6-21e1ba8a4752' with Copy path. Before the join it read 'On GitHub: joelwellbournewood/forerunner-sandbox'.
finding.expected: The header names the project being viewed (as the user guide says). Your files points to where the files are now, without a project id (design section 5 rule 3).
finding.evidence: Screenshot gh4a/steps/34-c4c-03-site-joined-overview.png; evidence/c4c-walk.json siteOverview.
finding.repro: Make one project, then open the closed project's Overview.
finding.suspected_cause: The join clears the closed project's repos, so the files line falls back to the docs worktree path. The header looks the viewed project up in a list that leaves out archived (joined) projects.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding has two parts, and the code at 4cf11fd explains both. The reporter's suspected causes are correct.

(1) Header. apps/ui/src/shell/Shell.tsx:45-47 gets the viewed project only from state.projects. That list comes from GET /projects, which returns only active projects: the daemon's server.ts:1007-1009 calls rt.store.project.active(), and the fake daemon at fake-daemon.ts:2128 filters joined projects out. project.join archives the closed project (project-join.ts:343-351: status 'archived', active false). So for /projects/<Site>/..., `viewed` is null and the header falls back to activeProject(state), which here is "Kite flyers". This breaks design §3.1 ("the project being viewed, not a hidden 'active' project") and user-guide.md:183. Every archived project hits the same fallback, removed ones included.

(2) Your files. project-join.ts:346 clears the closed project's repos (`repos: []`) and keeps them under settings.was_linked. projectCard (packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:250-251) then finds no repository, so it asks the folder fact. That fact is server.ts:992, `rt.docs.docsDirsFor(project)[0]`, and docsDirsFor (packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:499-507) returns the old docs clone `<home>/worktrees/docs/<project id>`, which still exists. SummaryTab.tsx:221-231 takes the folder branch and shows that path with Copy path. ADR 0106 (the comment at views.ts:248-249) says this clone is "not your files" for a repository project. It is an internal path with a UUID (design §5 rule 3), and it is no longer refreshed because the project is archived. Before the join the same section read "On GitHub: joelwellbournewood/forerunner-sandbox". The fake daemon keeps folder and repository on a joined project, so the UI tests never saw this.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/shell/Shell.tsx:46; packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:992 (and :1008 GET /projects active only); packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:251; packages/commands/src/commands/project-join.ts:346; packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:499-507; apps/ui/src/pages/project/SummaryTab.tsx:221
verdict.fix_sketch:
Header: when the route's project id is not in state.projects, Shell names the card ProjectPage already reads, client.project(id). It can fetch that card itself, or ProjectPage can publish the viewed card into the UI store or ShellContext. Then `active-project` reads "Site" on every page of a joined or removed project. The switcher list stays active-only, and nothing in it is shown as current.

Your files: in projectCard (views.ts) or the server's folder fact, a joined project (settings.joined_into) never falls back to the docs clone. A project whose was_linked[0] is the person's own absolute folder shows that folder, since that is where its files are. A repository project shows no clone path. SummaryTab instead shows a line in the style of the Tasks tab, e.g. 'Its files are in "Kite flyers".' with Open it (or the kept project's "On GitHub: o/r" line). Per ADR 0117 §6 the page offers no repository actions. The fake daemon's projectCardOf should mirror this: for a joined project, null repository and folder, plus the same words. Update docs/maintainers/apps.md and runtime.md.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
UI test (apps/ui/test/onerepo-join.test.tsx): join Beacon into Atlas (harness.daemon.state.joined.proj_beacon) with Atlas as the active project, render /projects/proj_beacon/summary, then expect(screen.getByTestId('active-project')).toHaveTextContent('Beacon'). I ran this on 4cf11fd from /tmp/frbench/l4g10/header-joined.test.tsx and it fails: the header reads 'Atlas▾'.

Real-daemon or composed test (packages/runtime/test/project-join.test.ts, or apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts): make two repository projects on one repository, refresh the copy so the docs clone exists, run project.join keeping A, then GET /projects/<B>. Assert the card's folder is null or the person's own folder, never under worktrees/docs and never containing B's id. Assert the rendered your-files section reads 'Its files are in "A".' with Open it. Today the test gets <home>/worktrees/docs/<B id>.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-onerepo-join
verdict.notes:
Evidence: in gh4a/steps/34-c4c-03-site-joined-overview.png and the matching .txt, the header reads 'Kite flyers' and Your files reads '/tmp/frbench/live4/github/gh4a/home/worktrees/docs/01a1e89b-...'. That id is Site's (evidence/c4-pair.json). Step 28-c4a-02-site-overview.txt, before the join, shows 'On GitHub: joelwellbournewood/forerunner-sandbox'.

The walk opened the page by URL. Clicking 'Open it' or the switcher does not avoid the problem, because any route to an archived project gets the same fallback.

No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names either part. C4L-9 (joined Last result words) and C4L-12 (research reads and note on the joined Overview) are neighbours: C4L-12 is already done at this base, and neither covers the header or Your files.

Severity is minor. The page title 'Site' and the 'Joined into "Kite flyers"' line make the state clear and nothing runs from the page, but the person sees the wrong project named in the header and an internal path with an id.

The repro scaffold is /tmp/frbench/l4g10: a test file, a vitest.config.mjs with root at the worktree's apps/ui, and a node_modules symlink. Run it with `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run --configLoader native --config /tmp/frbench/l4g10/vitest.config.mjs` from apps/ui. Nothing in the worktree was edited.

finding.title: The refusal reply names the tool: 'open Site with a project switch'
finding.step: LC-C3, the reply to 'make a new project for bench/seeded called Shop'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'You can open Site with a project switch, or add the work to it as new tasks.'
finding.expected: 'You can open Site, or add the work to it as new tasks.' (no command names, design section 5 rule 6)
finding.evidence: evidence/d01-make-shop.json reply text. The project.create tool description says 'open it with project.switch'.
finding.repro: LC-C3 turn 1 (these are the model's words and may vary).
finding.suspected_cause: packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts: the project.create description invites the model to name project.switch.

verdict.root_cause: The words were written by the real model (claude-haiku-5-5, evidence d01-make-shop.json), but the app's own tool definition led it there. The refusal sentence the tool sent back is fine: inUseSentence in packages/runtime/src/sources/repository-words.ts:131 gives 'bench/seeded is already the project "Site". Open it, or add this to it as new work.' The problem is PROJECT_CREATE_DESCRIPTION in packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts:275. It tells the model what to offer and puts a command name inside that offer: 'then offer that project instead (open it with project.switch, or add the new work to it)'. The reply copies the description almost word for word. 'one repository can only belong to one project' comes from 'One repository or folder is one project', and 'open Site with a project switch' comes from 'open it with project.switch'. 'project.switch' is not even the tool name the model sees (it sees project_switch, see apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:18099), so the model turned it into the phrase 'a project switch'. Nothing in the chat's system prompt stops tool or command names from reaching the person either: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md 'How you answer' (line 58ff) bans ids and raw statuses but says nothing about tool names, and CHAT_PLAN_RULES 'How to write' (packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:660ff) only bans markdown. This breaks design section 5 rule 6 (plain words, no module names).
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/project.ts:275
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Rewrite PROJECT_CREATE_DESCRIPTION so the person-facing offer has no tool name in it, and the tool hint uses the name the model actually sees, as a separate sentence. For example: '...this is refused with that project's name. Then offer that project in plain words ("You can open Site, or add the work to it as new tasks."), never a second project; if the person chooses to open it, call project_switch.' 2) Add one line to conversation-agent.md 'How you answer' (and bump its version): 'Never name a tool or command (project_switch, settings_set) to the person; say what it does ("open Site").' finding.title: A session started by the hands-off setting does not say so on its own page or in its log

While it ran, the run bar read "Choir · the coder works on \"Add the choir's phone number to contact.html\" just started". Only the Sessions list row says "started by itself when work was ready".
finding.expected: A session the person did not start should say why it started where the person opens it (design section 5: what happened and why), as the Sessions row does. For example: "Started by itself when work was ready (this project's setting), with a budget of CHF 1.00."
finding.evidence: c19-b.json events[0] = "The session started with a budget of CHF 1.00."; screenshot 71-c19-24-hands-off-session-page.png next to 72-c19-25-sessions-tab.png; packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-lines.ts:216-219.
