finding.repro: As in LC-C19: turn the setting on, answer a question card, then open the session that starts.
finding.suspected_cause: personLine('session.started') checks only trigger === 'manual' and never reads plan.startedBy. A hands_off start therefore gets the generic line used for any non-manual start.

verdict.root_cause: The runner records who asked for the session on the session.started event itself: runner.ts:1210-1212 writes `by: startedBy.by`, and the captured event's payload is {trigger:"message", by:"hands_off", ...}. The person-level line ignores that field. event-lines.ts:216-219 (personLine 'session.started') looks only at `trigger === "manual"`. Every other start gets the same generic line, "The session started with a budget of CHF X.": hands_off, schedule, and a person's start that uses trigger "message" (Approve and start, Continue, the prepared person start). Only startedByWords in session-list.ts:377-390, which reads plan.startedBy, puts the hands-off reason into words, and only the Sessions list row (session-list.ts:649) uses it. SessionPage.tsx:376-399 builds its header from the project name, start time, status and agent, with no reason. One correction to the suspected cause: personLine does not need plan.startedBy, because the event payload already carries `by`. For continuation, S-10 added its own first log line, and the hands-off start never got one. I reproduced it at the unit level with tsx on the base: personLine('session.started', {trigger:'message', by:'hands_off', budgetCapUsdMicro:1250000}, 0.8) gives "The session started with a budget of CHF 1.00.", and by 'schedule' and by 'person' with trigger 'message' give the same line. Only trigger 'manual' gives "You started the session...".
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/event-lines.ts:216-219 (reads p.trigger only; p.by is written at packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:1210-1212; the only reader of the reason is packages/runtime/src/daemon/session-list.ts:377-390 startedByWords, used at session-list.ts:649 for the Sessions row)
verdict.fix_sketch:
In personLine 'session.started', choose the line from `p.by`, and fall back to startByOf({trigger}) for rows written before `by` existed:
- person: "You started the session with a budget of CHF X." This also covers trigger 'message' starts the person made (Approve and start, Continue, a prepared person start).
- hands_off: "Started by itself when work was ready (this project's setting), with a budget of CHF X." This is under 100 characters and is the same fact as the Sessions row's "started by itself when work was ready".
- schedule: "Started on its schedule, with a budget of CHF X."
- continuation: keep the generic budget line, because CONTINUES_EVENT already comes first.
- unknown: the generic line.
To keep one wording per fact (design section 5 rule 10), share the phrase with startedByWords in session-list.ts, or move both into one map. The S-12 rule ("by itself" only where the setting makes it true) holds, because this line is used only when by === 'hands_off'. No change is needed to the run bar or the header: the log's first line is where the session page says what happened.

finding.title: The Sessions row of a session that ended on questions shows two different counts
finding.what_the_person_sees: After the phone card was answered and that task was done, the row reads "\"Add the choir's phone number to…\" and \"Add the choir's rehearsal address to…\" needed your answer." over "08:19 · under a minute · 2 needed you · Ended: 1 task needs you · CHF 0.02 on your API key".
finding.expected: One count, or two counts clearly told apart (what the session ended with and what still waits now), so the row does not say 2 and 1 about the same thing.
finding.evidence: screenshot 72-c19-25-sessions-tab.png; c19-b.json sessionsTab
finding.repro: End a session with two question cards open, answer one, open the project's Sessions tab.
finding.suspected_cause: The 'Ended: N task needs you' status seems to come from the tasks' current states, while '2 needed you' is the count at the session's end.

verdict.root_cause: One Sessions row reads two different moments. The gist and the task counts come from the record written when the session ended: handoff.outcome.needsYou held both tasks, so the row says "2 needed you" and '"…phone…" and "…rehearsal…" needed your answer.' The ended words come from what still waits now. The daemon passes blockedNow = stillBlocked (server.ts:1796), which drops the phone task because it is now done, and endedStatusText then prints "Ended: 1 task needs you". This was built on purpose: d1109-sessions decided "'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now" (L-21 rule, ADR 0116 rule 10, the same map as the session page's badge). Nobody thought about what happens when the row's past-tense counts sit next to it. The "Ended:" prefix makes the current count read as the count at the session's end, so the person sees 2 and 1 for the same thing. The live evidence matches the code. c19-b.json "after" shows the phone task done and the rehearsal task still needs_human. The second session's handoff has the phone task done. The row text in 72-c19-25-sessions-tab.txt is exactly countsWords + endedWords joined by SessionsTab.sessionRowLine.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/session-list.ts:632-643 (waits = ctx.blockedNow(row.handoff) gives endedWords, while counts/countsWords at :623 and :642 and the "needed you" words at :200 come from the end record); packages/runtime/src/session/stop-words.ts:221 ("Ended: N task(s) need(s) you"); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1796 (blockedNow: stillBlocked); apps/ui/src/pages/project/SessionsTab.tsx:37 (joins countsWords and endedWords on one line)
verdict.fix_sketch: Leave the session page's badge as it is. On the list row, word the current-state part so it reads as now and not as the end, and keep the past-tense counts. In sessionRowView: when the session completed, its record has needsYou/failed/paused tasks, and waits (stillBlocked) is above zero, set endedWords to a "still" phrase such as "1 still needs you" (or "1 still needs you, 1 still paused"), not "Ended: 1 task needs you". When waits is zero after the person answered everything, keep "Done" (the row then reads "2 needed you · Done", which is already coherent). The row would read "08:19 · under a minute · 2 needed you · 1 still needs you · CHF 0.02 on your API key". When nothing changed since the end (waits equal to the end counts), the plain "Ended: 2 tasks need you" can stay, or the "still" form can be used everywhere for consistency. Put the phrase builder next to endedStatusText in stop-words.ts so there is still one map, and update the fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts around :9348) and the d1109-sessions maintainer doc and ADR 0116 rule 10 to say how the list tells the end and now apart.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, next to the L-21 case at :11914. Have the bench stand-in ask on two tasks so one session ends with two open question cards. Answer one card so its task moves on (Cancel task, or Go ahead without followed by a session that finishes it). Read client.projectSessions(projectId) and take the first session's row. Assert sessionRowLine(row) contains "2 needed you" and "1 still needs you" and does not contain "Ended: 1 task needs you". Also assert client.session(id).statusText still follows L-21. Today it fails: the row reads "2 needed you · Ended: 1 task needs you". Add a unit case in packages/runtime/test/session-list.test.ts for the words with waits {needYou:1} against a record with needsYou of 2.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-sessions
verdict.notes: The code fully explains this, so I did not run the stand-in bench. Both parts of the row are each correct: the counts are past tense and true about the end, and the ended words follow design §5 rule 4 "true now". The problem is only how they are told apart on one line, so I rate it words, not minor. The header bar and the Inbox show the right current state ("Waiting for you: rehearsal address"). The d1109-sessions acceptance text says "'Ended: 1 task needs you' stays true now" and "one map for the badge and the row", so this follows the area's own decision; the gap is that the decision never looked at the counts next to it. None of leftovers-L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this. The closest are C6L-2 (Sessions list, a different issue) and the round-2026-11-01 L-21 item, which built the current-state badge.

finding.title: The Answered line reads 'is done; a session started for it'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Inbox > Answered: "Answers saved in the decision record; \"Add the choir's phone number to contact.html\" is done; a session started for it (this project starts by itself when work is ready)."
finding.expected: Events in the order they happened: your answers started a session for it and it is now done (design section 5). Related: L4-session-6, where the Answered line kept a stale 'is running'.
finding.evidence: c19-c.json inboxAfter; screenshot 82-c19-35-inbox-answered-after-hands-off-off.png
finding.repro: With the setting on, answer a question card, let the session finish, then open Answered.
finding.suspected_cause: The answered line puts the task's current state in front of the outcome that was kept when the card was answered.

verdict.root_cause: questionsOutcome builds the Answered line from the task's status now (ctx.taskStatus, which views.ts:1043 reads from the task when the list is shown) plus the start clause the card stored when it was answered. When the task is done, it writes `<task> is done` first and then adds the stored clause. Only prepared outcomes get rewritten to "what waits on it ..." (lines 578-581, isPreparedOutcome). The hands-off start is stored as start "started" with start_by "hands_off", which isPreparedOutcome does not cover. So startWords -> preparedClause gives "a session started for it (this project starts by itself when work is ready)", a clause about the task itself, and it lands after "is done". The line then puts the later event (done) before the earlier one (a session started for it), against design section 5 rule 2. The bench state confirms the stored card for the phone task is {outcome: answered, start: started, start_by: hands_off} with the task done. A tsx probe of requestWords with that card and taskStatus done prints the live line word for word.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:569-591 (questionsOutcome; the done branch at :587-588 and `after` at :578-581); the clause comes from startWords :404-406 -> preparedClause in packages/runtime/src/session/prepared-work.ts:211-214,230-239
verdict.fix_sketch:
In questionsOutcome, when ctx.taskStatus === "done" and the stored start is a start rather than a prepared outcome ("started"/"queued", with or without start_by hands_off), write the events in the order they happened:
- On a specialist's card (the answer sent the task back to work), for example: `Answers sent: a session started for "X" by itself (this project starts by itself when work is ready); it is done.`
- On the person's own task (card.on_answer === "done", where the answer closed the task and the session ran what waits on it): `Answers saved in the decision record; "X" is done; a session started for what waits on it (this project starts by itself when work is ready).`
Apply the same rule to the "without" branch (:582-584), which gives "is done without your answers; a session started for it". Do it in one helper, e.g. doneThenStarted(card, ctx), used by every Done line that adds startWords after "is done". Also fix retryOutcome's accept branch (:494-499): with hands_off it currently produces the broken sentence `"T" is done; what comes after it a session started for it (...)`, because `.replace(/^it /, "")` assumes a clause that starts with "it ". Keep each line at 160 characters or fewer.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine (owns startWords and the Done lines in request-words.ts, S-2/S-12)
verdict.notes:
The finding is real at 4cf11fd. I confirmed it with a read-only query of /tmp/frbench/live4/session/s1/home/data/state.sqlite (card 01a1e896-55db...: answered/started/hands_off, task done). A probe, /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-13/probe.ts, reproduces the exact Inbox text. While the task is running or ready, the same card reads correctly ("Answers sent: ... goes on with them; a session started for it ..."). The order only flips once the task is done.

Same-root siblings the fix should cover:
(1) A person's own task (on_answer done) under hands-off would read "is done; a session started for it". There "it" names the wrong thing: the session ran what waits on it.
(2) The "without" branch.
(3) retryOutcome accept with hands_off, where the probe /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-session-13/probe2.ts prints the ungrammatical '"T" is done; what comes after it a session started for it (...)'.

Related but different: L4-session-6. The Garden club lines in the same screenshot ('is done; what waits on it joins the session that is running') are a stale prepared clause, not an order problem.

No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this. C3L-4 is about the hands-off setting's effect line, not the Answered line. I agree with severity "words": nothing is wrong in what happened, only the order of the words.

finding.title: The crash Update has no Continue button, and the interrupted log line carries the restart's time
finding.what_the_person_sees: Inbox > Updates shows 'Your last session was interrupted when Forerunner closed. "Write a two-sentence welcome note for the bakery in welcome.md" is ready again.' with only 'Mark read'. The session page's last log line reads '08:36 Interrupted: Forerunner closed: nothing done. CHF 0.01.' Forerunner closed at 08:34; 08:36 is when it started again.
finding.expected: Design section 5 (Stop, crash 'after' example): '... is ready again. [Continue]'. The user guide only promises 'one line in the Inbox', and Start session in the header works. A log line's time should be when the thing happened, or the line should say Forerunner started again then.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/pause/p2/steps/08-c6-14-inbox-after-restart.png; 07-c6-13-session-page-details.txt; kill 08:34:53.6 (c6-run.json notes.killedAt), restart 08:36:54 (/tmp/frbench/live4/pause/c6-restart-at.txt)
finding.repro: Start a session on one small task. Kill the daemon's process group during the task's first model call. Start Forerunner two minutes later. Open the Inbox and the session page.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/session/recovery.ts posts the Update without a Continue action. The interrupted event is written at recovery time.

verdict.root_cause:
Both halves come from the code at 4cf11fd, not from the model.

(1) No Continue. recoverInterruptedSessions posts the crash news as a plain message: store.message.send with type "info" and a body only (recovery.ts:309-323). A message cannot carry an action at all. MessageRow (packages/state/src/types.ts:354-368) has no action, link or session field. The Inbox's Updates list (apps/ui/src/pages/InboxPage.tsx:700-723) renders MessageBody, the badges, the sender and time, and Mark read. Its only link is "Undo in Changes", for change sentences (InboxPage.tsx:861-881). The person-start Continue that does exist (POST /sessions with continues, ADR 0118) is wired only to the session page's credential-wait block (SessionPage.tsx:805-870), not to an interrupted session. So the design's "[Continue]" (core-experience.md:367-370, §5 Stop, crash "after") was never built. Run C's d1109-starts-engine decision (runC-plan areas/6/decisions/0) even lists "the recovery Update's Continue" as a person start, but nothing creates one. The user guide (user-guide.md:910-913) promises only "one line in the Inbox; the next Start works at once", which is why the gap went unnoticed.

(2) The end line's time. endDeadSession appends the session.ended event at recovery time (recovery.ts:181-188). EventRepo.append stamps it with the clock's now, and AppendEventOptions (packages/state/src/repos/event.ts:8-12) has no createdAt. On this project there was no plan to approve: the bench DB shows it was made by POST /projects (name and goal only, no intake) and has one coder task made in New task. That suits the singular "report" branch but not the plural "notes" branch. The stored card row confirms the text: human_request 01a1e8aa-6404 has why "The critic's notes on ... says: ..." and steps ["Add \"Document npm test in docs/testing.md\".", "Asks you first: the plan you approved has no task for the writer-marketing."]. finding.title: Go ahead under 'This needs a stronger model' only asks again: the stronger model never runs
finding.what_the_person_sees: The person asks 'use a stronger model: why did "Build the contact form" fail and what should I change?' and gets 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?'. Each press of Go ahead (and a typed 'yes') adds 'Go ahead.' and the identical line again with a new Go ahead button. Nothing else happens, however often they press.
finding.expected: Go ahead runs the stronger model once on the question, within the 'at most' it showed, and the answer ends with 'Thought it through with Sonnet · … s · CHF …'.
finding.evidence: c14.json turn y1 plus c14b-goahead1/2.json and c14c.json: 0 model calls, replies in 95-376 ms. Screenshot 60-c14c-01-y2yes.png shows four identical ask lines. The stored offers' atMostUsdMicro grow each turn: 206,334 -> 208,455 -> 208,905 -> 209,205 -> 209,505, with estimateUsdMicro 48,816 (the median of the one earlier Sonnet pass, LC-C13 e3). With 'Chat asks first' at CHF 0 the longer rung's Go ahead did run, because its 'at most' (twice the estimate) is above the floor. So did the best rung's ('at most CHF 1.13').
finding.repro: On the c1 home (one cheap Sonnet answer, USD 0.0488, already in the conversation), in any project's Chat: type 'use a stronger model: why did "<a failed task>" fail and what should I change?' and press Go ahead under the ask. The same ask line comes back. Press again or type 'yes': same.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1872. personsPass re-asks when yes.atMostUsdMicro < f.floorUsdMicro. The floor is PASS_FLOOR_CALLS (3) x the first call's worst case on the current context (line 1666), and that context now includes the ask turn itself, so it is a little larger each time. 'at most' = max(2 x estimate, floor) (atMostOf). Once a recent stronger pass cost less than half the floor, 'at most' equals the old floor exactly, and every later floor is bigger. Because the estimate is the median of recent passes across the one conversation session that all projects share, every stronger-model Go ahead on the install loops until 200 newer chat replies push that pass out of recentPasses.

verdict.root_cause: The re-ask check compares the yes against an internal number that is always a little lower than the new floor. Go ahead is never handled as a yes. atMostOf (packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:166-173) returns max(twice the estimate rounded up to the centime, floor), and when the floor is larger it returns the floor in micro-USD without rounding. That happens whenever the estimate (recentPasses' median, agent.ts:1667-1669) is less than half the floor, which is PASS_FLOOR_CALLS x the first call's worst case (agent.ts:1666). The offer stores that unrounded value (offerOf, agent.ts:1700-1708). On the Go ahead turn, personsPass (agent.ts:1864-1872) works out the floor again with figuresOf on thoroughRequest. Its history now holds the offered turn itself (the question and the ask line), so the floor is a few hundred micro-USD larger. yes.atMostUsdMicro < f.floorUsdMicro is then always true, and a fresh offer with the same line is stored. That offer's 'at most' is the new floor, which the next turn's floor exceeds again, and so on without end. The re-ask has no reason to fire. The person was shown chfUp(atMost) = CHF 0.17 (USD 0.2125 at 0.8), and every later floor (208,455 to 209,505) still fits inside that figure. So running would not spend past anything the person was shown; the check compares against the unrounded internal value, not the shown one. It persists across the install: conversationSession is keyed by the agent only (agent.ts:2734-2735), so every project shares one session, and recentPasses reads the newest 200 chat.reply rows (event.ts:88-101, newest first). A single cheap stronger pass therefore makes every later stronger Go ahead loop, since no new stronger pass can run to move the median. Confirmed from the c1 store: offers on the same question with estimate 48,816 and atMost 205,890 -> 206,334 -> 208,455 -> 208,905 -> 209,205 -> 209,505, none followed by a Sonnet pass. Reproduced at 4cf11fd with the composed chat (real LoopAgentDriver, CommandLoop, FakeProvider, flatPricing; test at /tmp/frbench/v-l4chat12/t/repro.test.ts). With no seed, or a seeded fake-sonnet pass of 100,000, Go ahead runs fake-sonnet. With a seeded pass of 1,000, three Go aheads give the identical line 'about CHF 0.01 (at most CHF 0.04)' and zero model calls, with stored atMost 39,339 -> 39,519 -> 39,639 -> 39,759. The longer rung's Go ahead in c14d ran only because twice its estimate (12,500) was above its floor.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1872 (the re-ask); causes at packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:172 (atMostOf returns the floor unrounded) and agent.ts:1666-1674 (the floor is measured on a context that the offer turn has grown); the same comparison again at agent.ts:1889
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Make the stored 'at most' the figure the person reads: atMostOf rounds the max up to the centime, i.e. chfToUsdMicroAt(centimesUp(max(2*estimate, floor), chf)/100, chf), so the budget a yes carries equals the CHF on the line. 2) In personsPass, judge a yes against what was shown: re-ask only when the model changed or centimesUp(f.floorUsdMicro) > centimesUp(yes.atMostUsdMicro). The pass then runs with budget = yes.atMostUsdMicro, capped by the room as today. Apply the same change to the duplicate check at agent.ts:1889. 3) Optional: measure an accepted offer's floor without the offered turn's own ask line in the history, so the figures on the accept turn match the ones that turn offered. A re-ask after a real price change or model change (the documented restart case) stays as it is, and the new figure is shown.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts (composed chat, fake-haiku fast pass, fake-sonnet stronger): seed one chat.reply row with a stronger pass {depth: 'stronger', model: 'fake-sonnet', costUsdMicro: 1_000}, in another project of the same agent. Send 'use a stronger model: <QUESTION>' and expect the ask line and no model call. Send 'Go ahead.' with offer: r.transcriptId and expect exactly one fake-sonnet request. Its reply's footer should match /^Thought it through with Sonnet · \d+ s · /, its cost should be at most the CHF 'at most' on the line, and no second ask row should be written. Today it fails: zero requests and the same ask line, with the row's atMostUsdMicro growing on each press. Do the same through the daemon's chat route with the stand-in, and on the UI's Go ahead button: the conversation shows one answer under Go ahead, not a second ask.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes: The evidence supports every part of the claim. The c14 step files show 0 calls on each Go ahead and on the typed 'yes' (95-376 ms). The copied c1 store (/tmp/frbench/v-l4chat12/state.sqlite) holds the offers and their figures as the finding says; the first ask had atMost 205,890 and the Go ahead under it stored 206,334. The cheap pass is the LC-C13 Sonnet pass (48,816). The earlier 'make a plan' Go ahead ran because there was no median yet (estimate = 5 x worst). The best rung ran because no Opus pass had been recorded yet; one cheap Opus pass would make it loop too. The model's own hand-over (answer_thoroughly -> ask) goes through the same accept path, so its Go ahead loops in the same way. Nothing is spent and nothing goes wrong beyond the loop, so I keep major rather than blocker. Still, after the first cheap stronger answer, the stronger and best rungs that the owner's decision D3.2 promises cannot be used anywhere on the install. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this (C3L-8 is about stale ask lines and C3L-13 about the turn floor; neither is this). I wrote no files in the worktree: the repro test and its vitest config are in /tmp/frbench/v-l4chat12/t/, run once under flock. No bench was started.

finding.title: After Answer now, the answer offers 'This needs a stronger model … Go ahead?'
finding.what_the_person_sees: The person presses Answer now during a 'think it through' answer. Under the answer they get 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?' with Go ahead, although they chose to have it answer now. That Go ahead loops (L4-chat-12).
finding.expected: Answer now gives the answer with what was found and offers nothing more. A next-rung offer belongs only to an answer the budget cut off.
finding.evidence:
c16b.json reply: '... which conflicts with these records.

This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?

Thought it through more carefully · 5 s · under CHF 0.01'. Screenshot 76-c16c-after-restart.png.
finding.repro: In Chat type 'think it through: compare every session of Photo club: what each did, what failed in each, why, and what each cost' and press Answer now after about 1.5 s.
finding.suspected_cause: agent.ts:2253 adds the next rung's offer whenever result.wrapUpSent is true. It does not tell the person's Answer now (entry.answerNow -> budget.wrapUpNow, line 1776) apart from a budget wrap-up.

verdict.root_cause: The app cannot tell the person's Answer now apart from the budget's wrap-up. Answer now is wired as `entry.answerNow = () => budget.wrapUpNow(o.runId)` (agent.ts:1776). `SessionBudget.wrapUpNow` (enforcement/budget.ts:283) adds the run to `wrapNow`. `precheck` then sets `wrap = ... (runSpent + lineEstimate > line.lineUsdMicro || this.wrapNow.has(runId))` (budget.ts:266-270): both causes end in the same `line.wrapped` and the same `wrap_up` decision. The loop sets `wrapUpSent = true` either way (agent/loop.ts:712). After the answer, agent.ts:2253 adds the next rung's ask line on `deep && !stopped && result?.wrapUpSent && !offer` alone, so an answer the person cut short gets 'This needs a stronger model … Go ahead?'. ADR 0114 ("their yes under a stronger answer that ran out of room"), runtime.md:4436 and the runC plan say this offer belongs only under an answer whose budget ran out. In the evidence the budget was not the cause: the pass's first call cost USD 0.001046 against a budget of about USD 0.125 (CHF 0.10), far below the 85% line, so the wrap-up came only from the press (the c16b stopRequests show POST /chat/turns/…/answer-now at 08:52:46.445).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2253 (the offer's condition); wiring at agent.ts:1776; packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:266-270 and :283 (wrap-up by spend and by wrapUpNow are merged)
verdict.fix_sketch: Record why the wrap-up came. Exact option: in SessionBudget.precheck, store the reason when it decides to wrap (`line.wrappedBy = runSpent + lineEstimate > line.lineUsdMicro ? "line" : "now"`) and expose `wrapReasonOf(runId)`. The loop or the agent then reads it, and agent.ts:2253 becomes `deep && !stopped && result?.wrapUpSent && budget.wrapReasonOf(runId) === "line" && !offer`. Smaller option, agent-only: in runOf, `entry.answerNow = () => { const ok = budget.wrapUpNow(o.runId); if (ok) answeredNow = true; return ok; }` and add `!answeredNow` to the condition. A press after the budget already wrapped returns false and keeps the offer, which is correct. With either option, the Answer-now reply carries no offer and stores none on the chat.reply row. Update runtime.md's rung paragraph ("reached its wrap-up" means its budget line, never Answer now) and the ADR 0114 amendment.
verdict.failing_test_idea: packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts, the existing case 'Answer now during a longer pass: its next call carries the wrap-up…': add `expect(r.offer).toBeNull()` and `expect((await w.lastRow()).offer ?? null).toBeNull()`. Add a control case: a longer pass whose second call crosses its budget's wrap-up line (no press) still gets 'This needs a stronger model: …'. I ran this probe on the stand-in: a copy of the existing case with only `expect(r.offer).toBeNull()` added (/tmp/frbench/l4c18/pkg/test/l4c18.test.ts, config /tmp/frbench/l4c18/vitest.config.ts; the worktree is unchanged). It fails today with offer {"line":"This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.06 (at most CHF 0.11) and 30 seconds. Go ahead?","action":"go_ahead"}, wrapUpSent true and a pass budget of 125,000 micro-USD that the first call came nowhere near. Outermost boundary: a case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts where client.answerNow(turnId) during a 'think it through' turn leaves the reply and the conversation view with no offer and no Go ahead.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes: Reproduced on the stand-in: the composed FakeProvider with the real LoopAgentDriver and the hooks. The live evidence (c16b.json) agrees: reply, then the offer line 'This needs a stronger model: about CHF 0.04 (at most CHF 0.17) and 10 seconds. Go ahead?' with Go ahead, then the footer 'Thought it through more carefully · 5 s · under CHF 0.01'. The calls were Haiku medium (1,046 micro-USD) and then the WRAP-UP call (645). The model did nothing wrong here: it answered from what it had and said what it could not check, as the wrap-up asked. The offer is added by code. Minor rather than major: the offer is only an ask and nothing is spent without the person's yes. It still goes against the person's choice and the documented rule. Its Go ahead looping is L4-chat-12, a separate finding. The same path would offer the best rung after Answer now on a stronger pass on a project whose highest model is above Sonnet. Leftover C3L-10 (leftovers-C3.json) says only that 'Answer now has no test that fails without it'. That is test coverage of the wrap-up, not this offer, so no known leftover names this finding. The existing Answer now test never checks r.offer, which is why this passed CI. The probe files are in /tmp/frbench/l4c18; its node_modules entries are symlinks into the worktree.

finding.title: Thorough answers take back correct earlier statements without looking them up
finding.what_the_person_sees: After Go ahead on a closer look: 'My earlier answer also gave a date and a file name (map.html, Sunday 15 November). I can't confirm those from the records I have now, so rely on the empty places file as the cause.' (0 lookups). In Garden club: 'I need to correct my earlier answers. I said the Sunday session wrote a placeholder list that the critic rejected, and that the welcome page failed on Friday too. The records I just read don't show that, so I can't confirm it.' All of these statements were true in the run reports and session records.
finding.expected: A thorough pass looks up what it doubts (recall_open of the session or report) before calling an earlier answer wrong, as CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES asks ('Look up what the answer rests on').
finding.evidence: c14d-goahead.json: 1 Haiku call, text only. c15.json k3: recall + session_last only, no recall_open. Seeded report of 15 Nov: 'I wrote a placeholder list, but the critic sent it back'. Session of 13 Nov: 'Write the welcome page' failed.
finding.repro: Photo club: 'think it through: why did "Add the meeting map" fail ...' then, with Chat asks first at CHF 0, ask it again and press Go ahead. Garden club: after earlier failure answers, 'think it through: what did the last two sessions do?'.
finding.suspected_cause: Model behaviour, helped by L4-chat-15 (recall's session record leaves out the failure). In Garden club, session_last also said 'no session yet' because the seed did not write the project's last-session summary (a seed artifact, not reported).

verdict.root_cause:
The two cases have different causes.

C15 (Garden club, k3): the code explains it. The model did look things up (recall kinds=sessions, then session_last). The records it got back were incomplete in a way that read as complete. sessionGist (session-list.ts:215-219) returns only "Did N tasks: <done titles>." when any task was done, so the failed task drops out. The recall hit also shows `detail` (gist + "How it ended" + cost, recall.ts:427-444 and 1528), never the session row's own summary. That summary did say '"Write the welcome page" failed' and '"Write the welcome page" failed again'. The tool result in model-calls.jsonl line 67 reads 'Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Done.' for Fri 13 Nov, and the same pattern for Sun 15 Nov. The model then "corrected" two earlier statements that were true. session_last saying "has had no session yet" is a seed artifact: seed-c11-c13.mts:57 left summary_cache {}, and lastSessionBlock (project-facts.ts:173-177) reads that cache, which a real session end writes. This is the root cause of the sibling finding L4-chat-15. recall_open (sessionText, recall.ts:452-470) and task_get would have shown the failures, but nothing in the hit hinted they were missing.

C14d (Photo club, Go ahead at CHF 0): the model alone. The Go ahead pass had the same system prompt and the same 36 tools as the first thorough pass x1, which called task_get (I compared lines 60 and 64 of model-calls.jsonl: system and tools are identical). The only difference was the history, which held its own earlier answer to the same question. finding.title: Recall's session record drops a task that failed when the same session finished another
finding.what_the_person_sees: Chat says a session did not have a failure it had, and 'corrects' a correct answer (see L4-chat-13). Recall gives the model 'The session of Fri 13 Nov: Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Done.' for a session in which 'Write the welcome page' also failed. A session whose only task failed reads '"Write the welcome page" failed. How it ended: Done.', which the model called contradictory ('why the latest session ... says it ended "Done" when its task failed').
finding.expected: A session's record names its failures as well (e.g. '1 done, 1 failed', as the Sessions list's countsWords says).
finding.evidence: Tool result in the k3 call (model-call log 08:47:57): 'r2 [session, Fri 13 Nov, Garden club, strong] The session of Fri 13 Nov: Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Done. It cost CHF 0.28.' The c16b reply quotes the 'Done' contradiction.

verdict.root_cause: Recall's search hit line for a session uses `detail` = `${view.gist}${ended} It cost ${view.spentWords}.` (recall.ts:427-428; the hit line prints `r.detail ?? r.body` at recall.ts:1528). It never adds `view.countsWords`. `sessionGist` (session-list.ts:213-218) names only the done tasks when there are any, so the failed task disappears from the line. The Sessions list row and recall_open's `sessionText` (recall.ts:462, "Tasks: 1 done, 1 failed.") do say it. The area spec asked for "gist, how it ended and CHF" and left the counts out, although it also says "worded as the screens word them". I reproduced it on the worktree code by calling the real recall tool, with both handoff shapes. Seed shape (no blocked): 'Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Done.' Runner shape (blocked: [failed]): 'Did 1 task: "Make the events calendar". How it ended: Ended: 1 task needs you.' Neither says the welcome page failed. recall_open says 'Tasks: 1 done, 1 failed.' in both. The second half of the finding ('"X" failed. How it ended: Done.', the contradiction c16b quotes) comes from the seed, not the app. The runner always writes `blocked: [...needsHuman, ...failed]` (runner.ts:4072), and recall then reads 'Ended: 1 task needs you' through blockedOfHandoff. seed-c11-c13.mts wrote handoff.outcome without `blocked`, and the unit-test fixture in chat-recall.test.ts:231-262 does the same, so the assertion at chat-recall.test.ts:740 locks in the same unrealistic 'failed. How it ended: Done.' Another gap: recall calls sessionRowView without `blockedNow` (the Sessions list passes stillBlocked, server.ts:1796). finding.title: Once a conversation passes 12 turns, each chat turn writes its history to the cache again
finding.what_the_person_sees: Nothing on screen. Each quick turn pays the cache-write price on the whole history (about 1,900-2,000 tokens per turn on Haiku here; more on Sonnet thorough passes).
finding.expected: cache_read_input_tokens covers tools, system and history on quick turns 2 and 4 (spec of LC-C15).
finding.evidence: c15.json: k2 read 16,128, wrote 1,915; k4 read 16,128, wrote 2,028; k1 wrote 17,988. Every quick request carries 25 messages, and the first person line differs on each turn ('what did we decide about the colours?', 'why did "Write the welcome page" fail three times...', 'compare the last two sessions'), with 0 identical leading messages between k1 and k2.
finding.repro: In a project whose chat has more than 12 turns, send two quick lines within 5 minutes and compare reply.usage in the model-call log.
finding.suspected_cause: The history window is the last 12 turns and slides by one each turn, so the prefix after the system part never matches the previous request's cache breakpoint. A window that moves in steps (or a breakpoint before the newest turns) would keep it.

verdict.root_cause:
The chat's history is a window over the newest turns, and it moves by one turn every turn. historyMessages keeps `turns.slice(-HISTORY_TURNS)` (12 turns). If those turns are over the token budget, it drops the oldest turns one at a time until they fit (`build(from)`). So once a conversation has more than 12 turns, or its history is over the budget, every request starts with a different first message. The prompt cache matches by prefix, so the request matches the previous one only through tools and system. Each turn then writes the whole history to the cache again.

The model-call log shows this: k1, k2 and k4 each carry 25 messages, and no leading message is the same between k1 and k2 or between k3 and k4. k2 and k4 each read 16,128 tokens (tools + system only) and wrote 1,915 and 2,028.

The adapter's breakpoints are right. cacheHistory marks the last message's stable start, and the earlier line of wave 7 (R-chatcache, the now-facts kept out of the line) works. A read-only repro with testenv's PromptCacheSim and the real historyMessages, in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-chat-16/repro.mts, confirms both cases:
- 4 to 5 prior turns: turn B reads 2,720 tokens (tools + system + history) and writes 59.
- 13 to 14 and 20 to 21 prior turns: turn B reads only 2,462 (tools + system) and writes 741 and 755.

The thorough pass builds its history the same way (THOROUGH_HISTORY_TOKENS 8,000), so it has the same slide.

Existing tests miss this because they only use short conversations: conversation.test.ts:1312-1345 and chat-depth.test.ts:887-917.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:379 (const recent = turns.slice(-HISTORY_TURNS)), with :396-400 (the token-cap loop drops the oldest turns one by one) and HISTORY_TURNS at :267; called from packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1605-1607 (quick pass) and :1630 (thorough pass)
verdict.fix_sketch:
Make the start of the window stable and move it in steps, not by one turn each turn. Work out the first turn from facts that do not depend on which turn is asking, for example the turn's index from the start of the conversation (seq or a count, not the position inside the 100-turn read), rounded down to a step of K turns (K = 6):
- start = max(0, floor((n - HISTORY_TURNS) / K) * K)
- The window then holds 12 to 12+K-1 turns and moves forward only every K turns.

Treat the token cap the same way. When the turns are over the budget, drop the oldest turns in blocks anchored to the same start (or keep the start until the budget plus a margin is passed), never one turn per call. The result must stay a pure function of the stored rows, so it is also the same after a restart.

The finding's other idea, a breakpoint before the newest turns, would not help: the change is at message 0, and a prefix cache cannot read anything after the first difference. Carrying up to K more turns is cheap, because they are read at 0.1x the input price instead of written at 1.25x. Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md ('History') to describe the stepped window.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
In packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts ('d1109-chat-depth, run C: caching'), or beside conversation.test.ts's 'chat turns read their history from the prompt cache': use the composed chat agent with FakeProvider({ promptCache: { minTokens: 1 } }). Seed a conversation of 13 turns, or chat 13 lines. Then send two quick lines within 5 minutes on the simulated clock. Check the two requests in the model-call log:
- The second request's messages[0] equals the first request's messages[0].
- The second request's cache_read_input_tokens is greater than what tools + system alone are worth (billed as in conversation.test.ts:1331-1337), and covers the first request's history.

Add a second case under 12 turns whose replies are long enough that the token cap (DEFAULT_CHAT_HISTORY_TOKENS) drops turns. Both cases fail today: the read equals tools + system exactly.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes:
Severity minor, as reported: the person sees nothing on screen. On claude-haiku-5-5 the extra cost is about 1,900-2,000 tokens a quick turn written at USD 0.125/MTok instead of read at 0.01/MTok. That is about USD 0.00022 a turn, roughly 40% of a quick turn's bill (USD 0.000524 for k2). The maximum is the history budget: 3,000 counted tokens on a quick turn, 8,000 on a thorough pass. It costs more on Sonnet and Opus.

LC-C15's thorough part passes: its second call read the first call's 17,786-token prefix. The tools and system read on quick turns 2 and 4 also passes. No leftover file names this (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6 checked). R-chatcache, from the wave 7 leftovers, was a different cause (the now-facts in front of the line), and it is fixed at 4cf11fd.

The runC-plan's d1109-chat-depth acceptance (12) asked that the history be read from the cache, but its test uses only 3 turns. The repro script is at /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-chat-16/repro.mts. It ran with the worktree's tsx and changed nothing in the worktree. No bench or unit suite was started.

Two tasks are done: ...' (the closing paragraph inside the bullet). The same happens with 'Photo club has three recorded sessions, costing CHF 0.87 in total: - Fri 13 Nov: ...'.
finding.expected: The intro paragraph, a three-item list and the closing paragraph, as the model wrote them (blank lines in the stored text).
finding.evidence:
Screenshots 64-c15-01-k1.png, 66-c15-03-k3.png, 76-c16c-after-restart.png. The stored and API text is right: 'Four tasks are left in Garden club, plus one decision for you.

- "Write the welcome page" ...

verdict.root_cause:
inAppText ends with `.replace(/\s{2,}/g, " ")` (apps/ui/src/lib/plain-words.ts:27). It was written for one-line card and read-back texts, to tidy the double spaces left after a voice or email hint is removed (U-074). Commit 5b2798a later wrapped the stored chat reply in it before RichText (Conversation.tsx:560: `<RichText text={inAppText(text)} />`). Every "

" is two whitespace characters, so it becomes one space before RichText splits lines at RichText.tsx:72. The blank line before a list glues the first item onto the intro ("for you. - "Write the welcome page" ...") as a text line that BULLET (RichText.tsx:34) does not match. The blank line after the list glues the closing paragraph onto the last item. Single "
" between items survives, which is why two bullets still render. I reproduced it with node at /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-chat-17/repro.mjs: inAppText on the stored text returns "...for you. - "Write..." failed.
- ...
- ... resolved. Two tasks are done: ...". That is exactly the 64-c15-01-k1 capture: TEXT, BULLET, BULLET with the closing sentence inside. The stored text in c1/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl has the "

" breaks, so this is not the model's doing. Other effects of the same cause: any plain "P1

P2" reply shows as one paragraph, and an indented sub-item ("
  - x") is glued to the line above. The streaming bubble (Conversation.tsx:342) does not call inAppText, so a reply shows its list correctly while it streams and reflows into the glued form when the stored turn replaces it. The bug hits the Chat tab and Talk, both of which use Conversation. The existing tests (rich-text.test.tsx REPLY, plain-words.test.tsx) only use single "
" or one-line texts, so none of them catches it.

finding.title: After a pause, 'Your note goes into its next brief.' for a note the person never wrote
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'put "Write the README" on hold for now' gets the read-back 'Pause "Write the README"? No session runs it until you press Resume.' (no note). After Yes: 'Paused "Write the README": no session runs it until you press Resume. Your note goes into its next brief.'
finding.expected: No 'your note' when the person gave none. If the model adds a note, the read-back shows it and the sentence does not say it is the person's.
finding.evidence: c16d.json: task_pause input {"task":"Write the README","project":"Photo club","note":"Put on hold by the person."}; answered text as quoted.
finding.repro: In Chat: 'put "<a task>" on hold for now', then Yes.
finding.suspected_cause: The task_pause sentence says 'Your note goes into its next brief' whenever the note parameter is present, and the model fills it in by itself.

verdict.root_cause:
The app treats any `note` on a task command as the person's own note, whoever wrote it, and the chat read-back never shows it. In chat the tool caller is the agent (packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:323 sets the actor to kind "agent"). The `note` parameter has no description telling the model to pass only the person's words (task.ts:112 `z.string().trim().max(2000).optional()`, sent as-is to the model by registry.ts:189), and the task.pause description (task.ts:1409) does not mention it either. So Haiku made up "Put on hold by the person.".

From there:
- moveCard builds the read-back with `moveAsk(task, from, to)`, which never includes the note (task.ts:1647). The person's Yes covers text they never saw.
- The card sentence sets `noted: !!params.note` (task.ts:1642), and the run sentence sets `noted: noteId !== null` (task.ts:706). moveSentence then always says " Your note goes into its next brief." (task.ts:601).
- queueNote saves the model's text as a queued note with author_human set to the person even when the actor is the agent (task.ts:326). It reaches the specialist's next brief as 'About "Write the README": Put on hold by the person.'

The design says chat changes are read back in one line and "Nothing is silently forwarded to whatever specialist runs next" (core-experience.md, chat section). It defines the note as the person's own ("Note for the agent (optional)", from the dialog). Here the model's text went into the brief unseen and was labelled as the person's. The model chose to fill the field, but the app invites that (no description), hides the note, and gives it the wrong author.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:1642 and :1647 (moveCard: the sentence says "noted" from params.note, the ask leaves the note out); :596-601 (moveSentence "Your note goes into its next brief."); :706 (run sentence); :112 (noteParam, no description); :326 (queueNote: author_human set for an agent's note). Same "Your note" wording: :1857 (task.update), :2011 (task.dependencies).
verdict.fix_sketch:
1) Give the note parameter a description: `noteParam.describe("Only words the person gave for the specialist, quoted as they said them; leave it out when they gave none. Never a summary of the move.")`, and add one line to CHAT_TASK_RULES with the same point.
2) When the call comes from chat (ctx.actor.kind === "agent") and has a note, moveCard's ask (and the asks of task.update, task.dependencies and task.transition) appends the note, for example `Pause "X"? No session runs it until you press Resume. Note for its next brief: "…"`, so the Yes covers it.
3) moveSentence and the update/dependencies sentences take who wrote the note. "Your note goes into its next brief." only for the person's own note (the person is the actor: drawer dialog or API). An agent's note reads "The note goes into its next brief." The cancelled variant changes the same way.
4) queueNote records author_agent (not author_human) for an agent's note.
5) Sibling: the redirect guards in task.transition (:1257) and task.resume (:1454) skip the card answer whenever a note is present. A note the model made up therefore also turns a card answer into a separate move, so judge 'has the person's note' there the same way. Update the fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-tasks.ts:277, fake-daemon.ts:2880/3188) and docs/maintainers/commands.md "Task sentences and notes".
verdict.failing_test_idea: Commands executor test (packages/commands/test), at the chat boundary: source "chat", actor { kind: "agent" }. Execute task.pause { task: "Write the README", note: "Put on hold by the person." } on a ready task. Expect the pending readback to contain 'Note for its next brief: "Put on hold by the person."', and after confirmByText "yes" expect the sentence not to contain "Your note" (it reads "The note goes into its next brief."). The queued note has author_agent set and no author_human. Today readback is 'Pause "Write the README"? No session runs it until you press Resume.' and the sentence ends 'Your note goes into its next brief.' (reproduced at 4cf11fd with /tmp/frbench/l4chat20/repro.mts). Pair it with a case for the person's own move (actor human, source ui, a typed note) that still says "Your note goes into its next brief.". Also add a composed conversation test (scripted FakeProvider calls task_pause with a note) asserting the chat reply's readback, and a real-daemon/UI case that the drawer's Pause with a typed note keeps "Your note".
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat (the chat's read-back of task changes and their sentences; task.ts sentences). Or a small fix area 'chat-change-notes' touching packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts, CHAT_TASK_RULES and the fake daemon.
verdict.notes:
The evidence supports the claim. In /tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/c16d.json the model's task_pause input carries note "Put on hold by the person.", the read-back has no note, and the reply after Yes is 'Paused "Write the README": no session runs it until you press Resume. Your note goes into its next brief.'

I reproduced it without the model, through the commands executor at 4cf11fd (tsx script /tmp/frbench/l4chat20/repro.mts, using packages/commands/test/helpers.ts world()):

Still, the read-back is where the person approves a change, and the note's content is invisible there. A less harmless made-up note (for example "skip the tests") would reach the specialist with the person's name on it.

None of the leftovers files (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) names this. Nothing in the owner decisions of 2026-11-09 covers notes.

finding.title: Changes row for 'Chat asks first' reads 'from CHF 0.00, so chat asks before every longer answer to CHF 0.10'
finding.what_the_person_sees: On Changes: 'Set the amount above which chat asks first from CHF 0.00, so chat asks before every longer answer to CHF 0.10.'
finding.expected: 'Set the amount above which chat asks first from CHF 0.00 to CHF 0.10.' (the explanation belongs to the new value, or is left out for the old one).
finding.evidence: Changes page text (step c14-changes); POST /commands/execute settings.set chat_ask_above 0.1 returned the same sentence.
finding.repro: Settings, Basics, Chat asks first: set 0, then set 0.10 (Yes); open More, Changes.
finding.suspected_cause: settings.ts sentenceOf uses showFor(old value), which carries the zero value's clause ('so chat asks before every longer answer'), in the 'from' slot.

verdict.root_cause: The "from" and "to" slots of a settings.set sentence both use showFor, which calls the key's `display`. For chat_ask_above, `display` is chatAskAboveWords, and at 0 it returns the value plus what it means: "CHF 0.00, so chat asks before every longer answer". So when the old value is 0, the meaning clause lands in the middle of the sentence: "Set the amount above which chat asks first from CHF 0.00, so chat asks before every longer answer to CHF 0.10. Undo." The change log stores this sentence and the Changes page shows it word for word. The app captured exactly this text in the live run (/tmp/frbench/live4/chat/c1/steps/63-c14-changes.txt:28). The opposite change, 0.10 to 0, reads correctly (line 35), because there the clause follows the new value at the end. The model plays no part: this is the deterministic command sentence. The UI's fake daemon builds the same sentence the same way (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts:6929-6948), so the UI suite would show it too. The card's oldValue carries the same clause (settings.ts:1162).
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:1042 (sentenceOf: ` from ${showFor(t.spec, t.current)}`), with packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:760 (chatAskAboveWords adds the zero clause) and :719 (display: chatAskAboveWords)
verdict.fix_sketch: Keep the value and what it means apart. Option A (cleaner): chatAskAboveWords returns only `CHF ${chf.toFixed(2)}`, and the chat_ask_above spec gets `effect: (v) => (typeof v === "number" && v <= 0 ? "chat asks before every longer answer" : undefined)`. The Changes row then reads "Set ... from CHF 0.10 to CHF 0.00: chat asks before every longer answer. Undo.", the read-back reads "Set ... to CHF 0.00? Chat asks before every longer answer.", and the card's old and new values are plain amounts. Option B (smaller): add an optional `displayValue` (the value only) to SettingSpec, used for the "from" slot in sentenceOf and for the card's oldValue, while the "to" slot keeps `display`. Either way, mirror the change in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts (chat_ask_above branch, around 6929-6948), update commands.test.ts:1739 if Option A changes the to-zero sentence, and touch the maintainer doc for settings.
verdict.failing_test_idea: packages/commands/test/commands.test.ts, the chat_ask_above case near line 1739. After setting 0, run settings.set chat_ask_above 0.1 (it comes back pending because it widens), approve it, then expect the result sentence and the change-log row to be exactly "Set the amount above which chat asks first from CHF 0.00 to CHF 0.10. Undo." and not to contain ", so chat asks". At the person's boundary: a real-daemon case runs POST /commands/execute settings.set chat_ask_above 0, then 0.1 with the yes, then reads GET /changes (the Changes view) and checks the row text. A UI-suite Changes page test on the fake daemon checks the same row text after the same two changes. Both fail today.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth
verdict.notes: I checked the code at 4cf11fd and the live evidence. Changes page text step 63 (c14-changes) shows the row exactly as reported. I did not run the bench: the sentence comes straight from the code, the captured page text matches it, and the fake daemon repeats the same code. git blame shows the "from" slot came from eb395fc (CS-1). The zero clause came from 2e0701e (fixup-d1109-chat-depth), which moved "asks first above" out of the words but put the clause into the shared display. The existing test only covers the change to 0, which reads correctly, never the change away from 0. No leftover names it. C3's leftovers only mention depth.ts's dead askAboveWords export and missing chat-depth acceptance cases. The other display functions return plain value words, so only chat_ask_above has a clause that breaks the "from" slot.

finding.title: Chat reply names an internal tool: 'The session_last lookup also reported no session'
finding.what_the_person_sees: '... The session_last lookup also reported no session for Photo club, which conflicts with these records.'
finding.expected: No tool or module names in replies (design §5 rule 6).
finding.evidence: c16b.json reply; screenshot 76-c16c-after-restart.png. (The 'no session' itself is a seed artifact: the seed wrote no last-session summary.)
finding.repro: A thorough answer whose session_last result disagrees with recall.
finding.suspected_cause: Model wording; the chat rules do not stop tool names in replies, and no filter removes them.

verdict.root_cause:
The words came from the model, but the prompts the app sends make them likely, and nothing removes them afterwards. Four points:

(1) The role prompt names the read tools as bare identifiers (`tasks_list`, `task_get`, `session_last`, `files_list` at evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:39). Its "How you answer" section (line 58 on) forbids ids, raw statuses and tiers, but not tool names.

(2) The shared "# How to write" rule (packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:659-661, CHAT_PLAN_RULES) covers only markdown, although its own comment cites design §5 rule 6.

(3) The thorough-pass rules (depth.ts:359, CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES: "Say what the answer rests on ... and say what you could not check") and the wrap-up line (depth.ts:363, CHAT_WRAP_UP: "say in one sentence what you could not check") push the model to report its sources. CHAT_RECALL_RULES (agent.ts:616) also says "say what you looked through". With the tool identifiers as the only names it was given for those sources, the Haiku wrap-up call wrote "The session_last lookup also reported no session".

(4) No code scrubs tool names from the reply: agent.ts and sentences.ts only cut unfinished sentences. The UI shows the text as written (76-c16c-after-restart.txt line 72).

The evidence matches. In c16b.json the second call was flagged WRAP-UP, and the first call (recall + session_last) had returned "Photo club has had no session yet." (read-tools.ts:335, lastSessionBlock is empty). The finding is right that the "no session" part is a seed artefact: none of the seed scripts write the project's lastSession. That conflict is what led the model to name its source here, so the bug shows up rarely with real data, but nothing in the app prevents it.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:659 (How to write: markdown only, no tool-name rule); evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:39 and :58 (tools named as identifiers; How you answer has no rule against tool names); packages/runtime/src/conversation/depth.ts:359 and :363 (thorough and wrap-up rules ask it to say what it rests on and what it could not check); packages/runtime/src/conversation/read-tools.ts:335 (the "no session yet" result, a seed artefact here)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Prompt rule. Add one sentence to "# How to write" in CHAT_PLAN_RULES (agent.ts:659), which is in both the quick and the thorough system parts: "Never name a tool or a lookup (recall, recall_open, session_last, task_get, tasks_list, files_list, answer_thoroughly, memory_record, settings_set, fix_tasks or any other name with an underscore): say what you read in the person's words ('the last session', 'the runs of "X"', 'the records of 15 Nov')."
2. Same rule in the role prompt. Add the same line to "How you answer" in conversation-agent.md and bump the version to 1.5.0.
3. Wrap-up words. Add "in plain words" to CHAT_WRAP_UP and to CHAT_THOROUGH_RULES' "say what you could not check".
4. Optional code guard. When a turn's reply ends, look for any name from that turn's tool registry (tools.names()) in the reply text. On a match, either send one nudge on the claim-guard path, or replace a fixed map of tool names with person words (session_last -> "the last session", task_get -> "the task's record", tasks_list -> "the task list", files_list -> "the file list"). Keep only the prompt fix if the map rewrite reads awkwardly.
5. Docs and logs. Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md (chat prompt rules) and the U-entry words.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Three tests:

1. Prompt rule, in packages/runtime/test/chat-depth.test.ts next to the "'think it through: …' makes no fast call" case at line 293. Assert that the thorough request's system part, and the quick request's, contain the new no-tool-name sentence verbatim (prompts are asserted verbatim there). This fails today.

2. Code guard (if added). Use a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, or a chat-depth case with the FakeProvider:
- A thorough turn whose first call uses recall + session_last and whose wrap-up call answers "The session_last lookup also reported no session for Photo club."
- Assert that the reply the person gets from the chat turn route (and the stored conversation line) contains no name from READ_TOOL_NAMES, recall_open or answer_thoroughly, and no /\b[a-z]+_[a-z_]+\b/ token.

3. Wording, in evals. An evals chat case with the real model, run by the owner and not on the stand-in: the seeded conflict (sessions recorded, no lastSession) with "think it through: compare every session"; the reply must name no tool.

The stand-in bench cannot reproduce the model's wording (role-player.ts:1692 writes scripted lines), so the boundary test is the request system part plus the reply route.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-chat-depth (the thorough pass and wrap-up wrote it). The fix lives in the shared "# How to write" rule (agent.ts CHAT_PLAN_RULES) and the conversation-agent role prompt, so a small chat-words fix area also fits.
verdict.notes:
The reply in the evidence matches the finding: c16b.json, and line 72 of 76-c16c-after-restart.txt shows it on screen.

Severity "words" is right. The rest of the answer was correct and useful, and the trigger here was a conflict caused by the seed: seed-recall.mts / seed-c11-c13.mts / seed-c14.mts write sessions but no project lastSession, so session_last said "Photo club has had no session yet." That conflict is not a product bug in normal use, because a real session end writes lastSession. With real data the model has less reason to name its source, so this will be rare.

model_only is false. No prompt the app sends forbids tool names; the role prompt presents them as identifiers; and the thorough and wrap-up rules ask the model to name its sources and what it could not check. That fits the "a prompt the app sends made the choice likely" exception.

No leftover in leftovers-L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names tool names in chat replies. The closest are LL-10 (chat correction lines) and C6L-12 (fix_tasks wording); both are different issues.

Design §5's scope line lists the "status texts given to the chat model" rather than chat replies. However, the code (agent.ts:648-661 comment) already applies §5 rule 6 to replies, and rules 3 and 6 forbid event-type and module names.

No bench run was needed or useful, since the stand-in's replies are scripted.

finding.title: Claude Code's refused sign-in is filed as a failed task, not as a refusal: no refused card, the subscription stays 'Works now', and chat asks it again
finding.what_the_person_sees: After Start with an expired or invalid subscription token, the Inbox shows '"Write notes/pond.md" failed' / 'What failed: The run failed: Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid.' with Try again / Mark done anyway / Cancel task. There is an urgent notification '... failed', and the task is Failed. Settings still says 'Claude subscription · Does the work · Works now'. Chat answers 'I could not answer (model call failed).' with 'Think it through ... at most CHF 0.03'. Nothing tells the person the sign-in was refused or that a new one must be saved.
finding.expected: Claude Code's authentication_failed is read as a refusal (CE-8, LC-C22). The person gets one card 'The sign-in has expired or was signed out. Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits.' The task waits for a new sign-in instead of failing. The subscription row reads refused, chat gives its hold reply, and no further request goes to the subscription.
finding.evidence: daemon.log: 'ERROR [agent-sdk] sdk run failed {error: "Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."}'. limits.subscription = {planShareCap, planUsdMicro}, with no refusedAt. Proxy ids 3-6: chat's 4 x 'POST /v1/messages?beta=true 401 authentication_error OAuth access token is invalid.' after the run's refusal. SDK probe output: '{type:"system",subtype:"api_retry",error:"authentication_failed"}' x2, '{type:"assistant",error:"authentication_failed",text:"Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."}', '{type:"result",subtype:"success",is_error:true}', 'ITERATOR THREW after 2650 ms: Claude Code returned an error result: ...'. Screenshots /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22/steps/09-c22-inbox-after-refusal.png, 11-c22-settings-after-refusal.png, 12-c22-chat-question.png.
finding.repro: Save both credentials, with the subscription token invalid or expired (the bench's --subscription token reaching the real API through scripts/proxy-fwd.mjs --forward-subscription; bench started with scripts/start-clean.sh). Choose 'Subscription first, then wait'. Create a project with one ready task and press Start. Read the Inbox, Settings and the request log, then ask chat a question.
finding.suspected_cause: Agent SDK 0.3.304 replaces Claude Code's exit error with a thrown 'Claude Code returned an error result: <text>' after it has yielded the assistant error and the error result. packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts (the refusal mapping after the for-loop, around lines 586-604; catch around 606) and packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts (mapping around lines 182-186; catch at 195) only map authentication_failed and the 401 result text when the loop ends normally. Their catch blocks make the throw 'internal' or 'provider_error'. The tests' fake query ends the stream normally. The same throw probably hides Claude Code's billing_error/rate_limit (the subscription's usage limit, CE-5) on the real SDK.

verdict.root_cause:
Agent SDK 0.3.304's Query.readMessages queues every message first: the assistant error (error:"authentication_failed") and the result (is_error:true, result "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 ..."). When Claude Code then exits non-zero, it fails the input stream with `Error("Claude Code returned an error result: <result text>")`. In the bundled sdk.mjs, `lastErrorResultText` is set for any is_error result, so this replaces the exit error, and iterator.next() rejects after the last message. Forerunner's two consumers only read a refusal correctly when the loop ends normally.
(1) SDK driver, packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts. handle() does read the result as provider_auth (lines 482-490, since isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, said) matches "API Error: 401"). The for-loop at 572-581 then throws, so the post-loop sdkError mapping (usage limit, then authentication_failed, 583-605) never runs. The catch at 606-632 overwrites `error` with code "internal" (the thrown Error is not a ForerunnerError) and logs "sdk run failed". That is exactly the daemon.log line.
(2) Chat provider, packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts. The post-loop errorFromSdk mapping (182-186) is skipped. The catch at 195-207 yields provider_error "Claude Code could not answer: Claude Code returned an error result: ...".
Downstream, executor.ts:1755-1759 treats only provider_auth as credentialStop "refused", so the run and task read Failed and a failed-task card is filed. routed.ts:287 refuses a source only on provider_auth, so limits.subscription never gets refusedAt: no refused card, Settings still says "Works now", and every chat call still goes to the subscription.
The tests' fakes all end the stream normally: cred-world.ts refusedReply, subscription-path.test.ts:520-535 and claude-code-provider.test.ts:156-163. So the gap never showed.
Reproduced at 4cf11fd without the real API. I ran the real SDK 0.3.304 and Claude Code against a local fake server that answers 401 authentication_error. It yielded init, api_retry x2, the assistant error and the is_error result, then threw. SdkAgentDriver.run with that real query returned {outcome:"error", error:{code:"internal", message:"Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."}}. The same messages with no throw at the end return provider_auth. ClaudeCodeProvider.stream returned {code:"provider_error", message:"Claude Code could not answer: Claude Code returned an error result: ..."}.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:606 (catch overwrites the provider_auth set at 487-489 and skips the mapping at 583-605); packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:195 (catch yields provider_error and skips errorFromSdk at 182-186)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Put the stream's verdict in one place, per consumer, and apply it whether the stream ends normally or throws.
2. In sdk.ts, wrap the iterator.next() race in its own try. If it rejects after the stream already reported a failure (sdkError set, or an is_error result seen), mark exited=true and fall through to the existing mapping (usage limit, then refusal) instead of the outer catch. Keep the error handle() set from the result: today provider_auth, and budget_exceeded for error_max_budget_usd, which the catch also turns into a plain error.
3. As a fallback for a throw with no such message, classify the thrown text: strip the "Claude Code returned an error result: " prefix and test it with isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, text) and the usage-limit text check. A bare 401 in a run's own output must still not count (the REFUSED_TEXT rule stands).
4. In claude-code.ts, catch the iterator error in the same way. If sdkError or failure is already set, yield errorFromSdk(sdkError.kind, sdkError.text, rejected) or failure. Otherwise map the thrown text the same way before falling back to provider_error. Never put the token in the text.
5. Change the test fakes (cred-world refusedReply, subscription-path, claude-code-provider and the usage-limit fakes) to throw after the result, as SDK 0.3.304 does. Add one contract test that runs the real SDK against a local 401 stand-in, so the next SDK bump cannot bring this back.
6. Check the siblings the same throw likely hides: Claude Code's billing_error and rate_limit at the plan limit (CE-5, ADR 0100: rest, not Failed) and error_max_budget_usd (a budget stop, not Failed).
verdict.failing_test_idea:
A composed cred-world test at the person's boundary:
- Setup: both credentials saved, policy "Subscription first, then wait", one ready task.
- Claude Code fake: yields init, then {type:"assistant", error:"authentication_failed", text "Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."}, then {type:"result", subtype:"success", is_error:true, result: same}. Then it throws Error("Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."), as SDK 0.3.304 does.
- Press Start. Expect exactly one Inbox card reading "The sign-in has expired or was signed out. Save a new one in Settings; until then the work waits." Expect no failed-task card and no "... failed" notification. The task waits (not Failed). The Run row is credential_refused, limits.subscription.refusedAt is set, and the policy row for the subscription reads refused, not "Works now".
- Then ask chat a question. Expect the hold reply and no new Claude Code call (the call count is unchanged).
- Today, with the throw, the card is the failed-task card, the task is Failed, the row reads "Works now" and chat calls Claude Code again.
A unit sibling in claude-code-provider.test.ts: the same throwing fake must yield provider_auth, not provider_error.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (CE-8 refusal handling; the SDK driver and the Claude Code provider)
verdict.notes:
I checked the evidence against what the person saw:
- The Inbox text dump (09-...txt) shows the failed-task card with "Claude Code returned an error result: ...".
- c22.json and the Settings dump show the subscription row "Does the work / Works now".
- Proxy log ids 3-6 (09:01:41-42) are chat's calls: two Claude Code queries of two calls each, all 401. Ids 8-11 are the hand probe.

Side observation, not this finding: the task run's own Claude Code calls are missing from the bench proxy log. config.anthropicApiBase reaches only ClaudeCodeProvider and AnthropicMessagesProvider (compose.ts:1869/1882), never the SDK driver's req.baseURL. So on the bench, task runs go straight to api.anthropic.com. A person on the default base is not affected, but bench request logs leave out task runs.

Severity is major, not blocker. Nothing is lost and a 401 costs nothing. But on the real SDK every expired or revoked subscription sign-in gives a Failed task with the wrong card, no refused state, and chat keeps calling the refused subscription. Under "then API key" it also does not move on to the key. This defeats CE-8 and owner decision c) for the subscription.

The usage-limit and max-budget siblings are inferred from the SDK code: lastErrorResultText is set for any is_error result. They were not reproduced here.

Scratch files are in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-10: fake401.mjs, probe.mjs, provider-probe.mts, runner-probe.mts. The local 401 stand-in on port 49091 is stopped.

finding.title: Chat's one-off 'Use API key' keeps the question twice in the conversation (C6L-6)
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'What should I do next here?', then 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 10:59, so I have not answered. I can still add, move and start tasks.', then 'What should I do next here?' again, then the answer. The question is still there twice after a reload.
finding.expected: One press answers the held question in place, so the question shows once (C6L-6).
finding.evidence: c25.json b.questionShown = 2 and b.questionShownAfterReload = 2. c25-proxy/bodies/5-req.json: the one-off request's messages hold the question twice, with the hold reply between as the assistant turn. Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c25/steps/12-c25-b-chat-after-reload.png.
finding.repro: Save both credentials, choose 'Subscription first, then wait', with the subscription at its limit. Ask chat a question, press Use API key under the hold reply, then reload the Chat tab.
finding.suspected_cause: Conversation.tsx onOneOff calls send(t.said, {oneOff: true}), which stores the question again as a new person line. The C6 fix-up called it a display duplicate, but it is stored and sent to the model.

verdict.root_cause: The one-off press is a brand-new chat turn carrying the same text, not an answer to the held turn. (1) apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:311 handles the press as `send(t.said, { oneOff: true })`, which also draws a second person bubble. (2) packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1082-1088 reads `earlier`, which already holds the held turn, then writes a new `chat.human` for every request; oneOffSwitch does not change this, so the transcript and conversation view hold the question twice, also after a reload. (3) The held turn was stored as an ordinary turn whose reply is the hold reply (agent.ts:1349-1373, notice:true with oneOff). (4) historyMessages (packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:374-401, replyInHistory at 354) does not skip notice or hold replies, and agent.ts:1605-1607 passes `earlier` in whole. So the model gets: user question, assistant "so I have not answered", user question again. The proxy body /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c25-proxy/bodies/5-req.json shows exactly this. C6L-6's description as "a display duplicate" is wrong: the extra line is stored and sent to the model. The answer was correct and booked once on the key, so the harm is a visible duplicate that survives a reload plus a few tokens of misleading model context. That makes it minor, not major.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:311; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1082-1088 (chat.human written for the one-off too), agent.ts:1349-1373 (held turn stored), agent.ts:1605-1607 + packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:374-401 (hold reply goes into the model history)
verdict.fix_sketch: Let the press answer the held turn in place. (1) Screen: Conversation.tsx onOneOff sends the held turn's id, e.g. `send(t.said, { oneOff: true, heldTurn: t.id })`. The live answer renders under that turn with no second person bubble. (2) Daemon: add `heldTurn` to the chat request (api-types.ts, server.ts:2684/2713, agent.ts). When the newest turn in `earlier` is that held turn and its reply is a hold reply with the one-off: write no new chat.human; write the answer as a chat.reply for the held turn's transcriptId, so readTranscript keeps it in place of the hold reply; build the model history from `earlier` without that held turn, so the question goes to the model once. (3) Separately, historyMessages skips hold replies (a notice with oneOff), since the model never wrote them. (4) The fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts) does the same.
verdict.failing_test_idea: UI, apps/ui/test/credential-chat.test.tsx (Chat tab and Talk): after pressing Use API key and getting the answer, the question text appears exactly once in the thread; after remounting the screen (the reload) it still appears once, and the hold reply line is gone. Real daemon, apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts CS-8 at the stand-in model: after `client.chat({ text: "what is next?", oneOff: true })`, the turns from `client.conversation(null)` contain "what is next?" exactly once; the stand-in's last POST /v1/messages body has "what is next?" in exactly one user message; that body has no assistant message containing "so I have not answered". Both fail today: the existing tests check only that two requests are sent (credential-chat.test.tsx:62) and that the key is used once.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-screens (C6; built the press as CS-8, where C6L-6 comes from). The daemon half is in d1109-cred-engine's chat hold (CE-9, agent.ts).
verdict.notes: Reproduced from the code plus the live evidence; no stand-in run was needed because the path is deterministic. Evidence: c25.json shows questionShown = 2 and questionShownAfterReload = 2. The screenshot 12-c25-b-chat-after-reload.png shows the question, the hold reply, the question again, then the answer. Proxy body 5-req.json shows the question twice in the model's messages with the hold reply between as the assistant turn. C6L-6 already names the display duplicate, but its severity should go from words to minor and its "display duplicate" note be corrected, since the line is stored and sent to the model. finding.title: Costs shows 'By credential: Your API key: CHF 0.00' beside 'Total spend: less than CHF 0.01' for the same calls
