verdict.root_cause: The daemon writes the "By credential" sentence from formatChf alone and never applies the app's money rule (W14-6, moneyWords). That rule says an amount above zero never reads "CHF 0.00". In GET /costs, views.ts builds each byCredential row's `words` as costByCredentialWords(kind, formatChf(cost.chfMicro), share), and the "Not tied to a credential" line uses `${formatChf(cost.chfMicro)}`. formatChf(2035 micro) is "CHF 0.00". The UI's CostsTab.tsx:162 prints `c.words` exactly as sent. Total spend and the By model, By specialist and By task cells all go through the UI's <Money>, i.e. formatMoney -> chfWords, which reads "less than CHF 0.01". So one screen shows the same 2035 micro CHF two ways. The joinedSpend line just above in the same function (views.ts:1309) already wraps its amount in moneyWords; the byCredential lines were left out. I reproduced it on the base code: costByCredentialWords("api_key", formatChf(1665+181+189), null) gives "Your API key: CHF 0.00", and moneyWords on the same amount gives "less than CHF 0.01". The live evidence agrees: the steps 09 and 13 text captures show both strings on one Costs screen, and the ledger has three api rows at 1665, 181 and 189 chf_micro. The tests encode the bug instead of catching it. packages/runtime/test/credential-switch.test.ts:166 expects `Your API key: ${formatChf(...)}`. apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:22599 checks /^Your API key: CHF \d+\.\d\d$/, which "CHF 0.00" passes, and its only case books CHF 1.20. It is one sentence breaking a wording rule: the figure is right after rounding, nothing is charged or routed wrongly, and it shows only while a credential's spend is under a centime. finding.title: A no-op edit in the check's set makes the person's Yes change nothing, and the reply hides it
finding.step: LC-C28, first 'fix the tasks' at Assisted
finding.what_the_person_sees: Read-back 'Make these 3 changes ... change "Write the home page index.html": the criteria; ...' -> Yes -> 'Nothing to change on "Write the home page index.html".' None of the 3 changes is made: the duplicate stays, there is no prices task and no Changes row, and the Inbox card is closed as answered.
finding.expected: An edit equal to the task is dropped before the read-back. Yes makes the drop and the add as one row with one Undo. If part of a set fails, the reply says what was and was not made.
finding.evidence: model-call #1 reply edit {acceptanceCriteria: the same 5 criteria, why 'No change needed to the criteria; ...'}; request steps '2. the task "Write the home page index.html": as it is to unchanged.', part sentence 'Changed "Write the home page index.html": nothing.', answer {verdict: confirmed, kind: yes}; /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/13-c28-10-fix1-reply.png, 15-c28-11-yes1-chat-after-yes.png, 16-c28-11-yes1-changes.png
finding.repro: bench-live; a project with a duplicate and a missing step at Assisted; chat 'fix the tasks' until the planning model sends an edit that repeats a task's criteria (Sonnet did on the first try); press Yes.
finding.suspected_cause: The edit case of fenceTaskChanges (packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts ~806) never compares fields with the task. proposalLine names 'the criteria' whenever the key is present. task.update.run throws 'Nothing to change on ...' and the composed perform is all-or-nothing, so the drop and the add roll back.

verdict.root_cause:
The code at 4cf11fd explains the finding, and it reproduces with the stand-in provider.

The chain:
- **The model sent a no-op edit.** In the live run Sonnet's task-check reply (st3/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, call #1) had an edit of "Write the home page index.html". Its acceptanceCriteria were exactly the 5 criteria the check was sent. Its why was 'No change needed to the criteria'.
- **The fence lets it through.** The edit case of fenceTaskChanges (packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:806-826) checks only that the task can be changed, whether a criterion is removed, and who wrote the task. It never compares title, outcome, criteria or priority with the task, so the no-op passes.
- **The read-back promises a change.** proposalLine (packages/runtime/src/session/task-proposal.ts:68) adds 'the criteria' whenever the key is present. So the read-back says 'change "Write the home page index.html": the criteria'.
- **task.update.plan does not refuse.** The plan step (packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:1803) builds a card with newValue 'unchanged' and the sentence 'Changed ...: nothing.' The composed read-back is offered with Yes and No.
- **On Yes the whole set rolls back.** task.update.run throws 'Nothing to change on "X".' (task.ts:1818-1821). The composed perform (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:673-690) is all-or-nothing, so it undoes the drop that already ran and never reaches the add.
- **The reply hides it.** Chat's reply is the bare refusal: agent.ts:1211, sentenceOf(r, "Confirmed"). It never says that the drop and the add were not made either. The pending card is still marked answered.

**Repro.** /tmp/frbench/l4-12/repro.mts runs the composed chat as chat-fix-tasks.test.ts builds it: the real CommandLoop, LoopAgentDriver and ConversationAgent, with a FakeProvider. The project is at Assisted and the set is drop + an edit equal to the task + add.
- Read-back: 'Make these 3 changes ... change "Style the page": the criteria; ...'
- Yes: 'Nothing to change on "Style the page".'
- After Yes: 0 change-log rows, the duplicate still ready, no new task, and the card status 'answered'.

**Same flaw on the session path.** syncTaskProposals' check uses planCompose, which does not refuse an empty edit (compose.ts:5239). Its composed apply then fails the whole set, and the card is marked not_applied with the left-out line 'Nothing to change on ...'.

**At Standard and up** applyTaskChanges runs each change on its own. Only the edit is refused there, so that case is minor.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:806
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. **Fence (the main fix).** In fenceTaskChanges' edit case, compare each field with the task:
   - title against t.title, trimmed;
   - outcome against t.outcome;
   - acceptanceCriteria, trimmed with empty lines dropped, against t.acceptance_criteria;
   - priority through PRIORITY_VALUES against t.priority.
   Drop the fields that are unchanged from the change. Push the narrowed change into FencedChange.change, so proposalLine and callsOf only ever see real changes. If no field is left, drop the change quietly: no read-back line, no call, and not in the refused list shown to the person.

2. **Belt and braces.** The composed path should never offer a step that changes nothing. Either:
   - have task.update.plan throw a validation error 'nothing to change' when the patch is empty and no note is given, so compose refuses before the read-back; or
   - have callsOf skip an edit whose patch would be empty.
   syncTaskProposals' check should then report a no-op the same way.

3. **Words (chat).** When a Yes to a composed fix set comes back refused, chat's reply should say what was and was not made, e.g. 'None of the 3 changes was made: nothing to change on "X". Say "fix the tasks" to check again.' This follows design section 5, rules 8 and 9. Use fixLeftOut and the pending card's line count rather than the bare refusal text.

Area for parts 1 and 2: d1109-selftasks-run (the fence, proposalLine, syncTaskProposals). Part 3 belongs to d1109-selftasks-chat.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run
verdict.notes:
**Reproduced at the person's boundary.** Repro script: /tmp/frbench/l4-12/repro.mts, run with the worktree's tsx under the heavy lock. The worktree has no changes (git status is clean).

**The evidence matches the screenshots.** 15-c28-11-yes1-chat-after-yes shows 'Nothing to change on "Write the home page index.html".' 16-c28-11-yes1-changes has no new row. 17-c28-11-yes1-tasks still shows 'Build the contact page in contact.html' and no prices task. 20-c28-11-yes1-inbox shows Answered going from 2 to 3. On the second 'fix the tasks' the model sent no edit, and Yes made the drop and the add (25-c28-13-yes2-changes), which confirms that the no-op edit alone sank the first set.

**Not model-only.** The model went against its own rule ('Change only what the evidence shows is wrong'). But the fence is the app's guard on what the model returns, and it promised a change it could not make.

**No known leftover names it.** I searched all eight leftovers files. C6L-11 (the read-back expires) and C6L-14 (recompose loses planFix) are nearby but different.

**Severity: I agree with major.** The Yes silently does nothing, the reply misleads (rules 8 and 9), and the card closes. Nothing is lost: saying 'fix the tasks' again costs about CHF 0.01 and worked on the second try.

finding.title: The chat model writes 'The app did: Updated ...' with no command; the claim guard misses it and the task keeps the old phone number
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'The app did: Updated the outcome of "Write the contact page contact.html" to use the new number, 044 765 43 21.' The task still says 044 123 45 67, Changes has nothing, and the false line stays in the conversation.
finding.expected: No claim of a change that no command made (design section 5 rule 9, l3-chat-claims). Either the guard nudges once and then says nothing changed, or the model calls task_update and the change is read back.
finding.evidence: model-call #5 claude-haiku-5-5: toolCalls [], text 'The app did: Updated the outcome of ...'; the task's outcome and criteria via GET /projects/01a1e8bf-7e88-71f4-b1ca-ce8fe6fa1577/tasks still say 044 123 45 67; /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/58-c28-25-keepopen-after-yes.png
finding.repro: Assisted project, chat 'Our phone number changed: it is now 044 765 43 21. Please update the contact page task so it uses the new number.', then 'Go ahead and update the contact page task to the new number.'
finding.suspected_cause: The CHANGED patterns in claims.ts need a first-person verb ('I've updated'). The model copied the app's own history prefix 'The app did: ...', so claimOf returns null.

verdict.root_cause:
The claim guard only recognises first-person claims. In claims.ts:108-112, every English CHANGED pattern requires "I've/I have <verb>". The German pattern requires "habe ... <participle>". Nothing matches the app's own history marker "The app did: …" (HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD, transcript.ts:280), and nothing matches an agentless change-log sentence ("Updated the outcome of …", "Changed "X": …"). So claimOf (claims.ts:139-148) returns null, falseClaim/claimed (agent.ts:2045-2058) never fires, there is no nudge, and the forged line reaches the person as the reply.

I confirmed this three ways:
- I ran claimOf with tsx at 4cf11fd on the exact reply text. It returns null. "I've updated …" returns {kind:"changed"}.
- In model-calls.jsonl, seq 6 (claude-haiku-5-5, 09:11:42) has toolCalls [] and its run has no nudge call. The next call (seq 7) belongs to the later "Think it through" run.
- The chat.reply row in state.sqlite has actions [] and no claimGuard field.

The app also made this phrasing likely:
- The history shows earlier changes as assistant lines "The app did: <sentence>" (actionLines, transcript.ts:340-346). The seq 5/6 history held "The app did: Dropped …".
- The rules tell the model that this line means a change (agent.ts:595-608; evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:22). Nothing tells it never to write the line itself.
- replyInHistory (transcript.ts:354-365) passes a reply's own text into later history unchanged. So the forged "The app did: Updated …" became an assistant line in the next turn's history (seen in seq 7). That breaks the rule "a reply without one changed nothing".
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:108-112 (CHANGED patterns: first person only) and :139-148 (claimOf); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2045-2058 (falseClaim/claimed); packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:280 (HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD) and :354-365 (replyInHistory keeps a forged marker)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. claims.ts: add a CHANGED pattern for a sentence that starts with the app's marker (/^The app did:/i, built from HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD). The model must never write this line; the app adds it from actions. Also add an agentless pattern: a sentence-initial change-log verb (Updated|Changed|Added|Dropped|Paused|Resumed|Cancelled|Reopened|Set|Moved|Renamed) followed by a quoted title or "the". Keep the EARLIER and NEGATION filters, so "Earlier, the app updated …" stays history.
2. agent.ts: after the guard, a model-written HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD that no action of the turn backs never reaches the person or the stored reply. The nudge path already replaces an unbacked claim with trueLine, and that covers it once claimOf catches it.
3. transcript.ts replyInHistory: remove HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD from the reply's own prose. Then only actionLines carry the marker, and a past forged line cannot pose as a change.
4. CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES and conversation-agent.md: add "Never write 'The app did:' yourself; the app adds it under a reply that changed something". Bump the prompt version and the word-for-word test.
5. Add cases to the claimOf test list in conversation-memory.test.ts.

verdict.notes:

finding.title: The chat model asks for a task change in prose; the person's 'yes' is answered 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Make "Write the prices page prices.html" high priority? That is a change to the task's priority.' comes with no buttons. Typing 'yes' gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' The phone-number edit got the same prose question. On the default chat model, the person cannot make a change said in their own words.
finding.expected: The model calls the change's command; its prompt says 'call the command anyway; the runtime reads it back with Yes and No'. A question the app asks can be answered.
finding.evidence: model-calls #3, #4 claude-haiku-5-5: toolCalls [] with the prose questions; the 'yes' turn made no model call; /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/30-c28-14-ownwords-reply.png
finding.repro: Assisted project; chat 'Most customers only want to know what a repair costs, so the prices page matters more to us than the contact page. Please make it high priority.', then 'yes'.
finding.suspected_cause: No guard catches a yes/no question about a change made without a tool call; the 'yes' parser only knows pending cards.

verdict.root_cause:
The model chose not to call the command, but two parts of the app made that likely and then let it through.

(1) The history teaches the prose read-back. replyInHistory (transcript.ts:354-366) renders a reply that was the runtime's read-back as plain assistant text. It has no mark that a command produced it with Yes and No buttons, even though the stored row has pendingId and readback. The next "yes" turn then shows as "The app did: …". So call #4's history (model-calls.jsonl line 4, claude-haiku-5-5 at effort low) held this pattern twice: the assistant writes 'Make these 2 changes to the tasks of Bike shop? …', the user says "yes", and the app makes the change. No tool call shows anywhere in the history. Haiku copied the pattern almost word for word: 'Make "Write the prices page prices.html" high priority? That is a change to the task's priority.' with toolCalls []. Call #5 did the same for the phone number. This contradicts the prompt's rules: rule 2, 'Read back is the runtime's … do not repeat the read-back', and CHAT_TASK_RULES at agent.ts:669, 'For changes the person names themselves, call each change's tool'. It is the same mechanism that l3-chat-claims fixed for "changed" lines: the history showed the app's act as the model's own prose, and the model copied it one turn later with no tool. Running historyMessages at 4cf11fd on the stored turns gives exactly that output.

(2) No guard catches it. The claim guard (agent.ts:2045-2060, falseClaim → claimOf at claims.ts:139) only matches first-person claims ("I've asked for confirmation", "I've set …"; ASKED claims.ts:69 and CHANGED claims.ts:108). claimOf returns null for both prose questions. It also returns null for call #6's 'The app did: Updated the outcome …', which no command backed. So no nudge ran, and the question went out with no card.

(3) The "yes" turn did what it was designed to do. At agent.ts:1214-1219, a yes with no card is never sent to the model and gets YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (design §3.9). That rule assumes the chat never asks a yes/no question without a card, and (1) and (2) break that assumption.

The finding's suspected cause (no guard; the yes parser only knows cards) is right but incomplete. The history rendering is the app-side cause of the model's choice.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:354 (replyInHistory: a read-back reply's text sent as bare assistant prose); packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:139 (claimOf, ASKED :69 / CHANGED :108 match only first-person claims); packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2045 (falseClaim, so no nudge); agent.ts:1214 (yes with nothing waiting returns 'Yes to what?', by design)
verdict.fix_sketch:
(a) History: in replyInHistory, render a reply with readback/pendingId as the app's own line, not as the model's words. For example: 'The app asked, with Yes and No: <readback>' (a HISTORY_ASK_LEAD next to HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD). Build it from the stored row only, so the cached prefix stays the same bytes. Add one sentence to conversation-agent.md (version bump) and to the Settings and task rules: 'An earlier reply's "The app asked …" is the runtime's read-back of a command you called; never write a read-back yourself: call the command.'

(b) Guard: give claimOf an "asked" claim for a reply that reads a change back as a question in a turn where no command ran. That means a sentence ending in '?' that opens with a change verb (Make/Change/Update/Set/Add/Drop/Pause/Cancel/Move/Rename/Raise/Lower, plus the German forms) and names a quoted task or a field, or that says 'That is a change to'. Leave clarifying questions alone ('Which task do you mean?'). Also add a "changed" claim for a reply that itself starts with HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD ('The app did:'). The existing claimNudge already says 'call its command now; the runtime reads a change that needs a yes back with Yes and No'. If the claim still stands after the nudge, the reply becomes NOTHING_CHANGED_REPLY, so the person never gets a question that has no buttons. The 'Yes to what?' rule stays as it is.

Checked at 4cf11fd without editing. I ran historyMessages (transcript.ts) and claimOf (claims.ts) under node on the stored turns: the history shows the read-back as plain assistant text, and claimOf returns null for both prose questions and for 'The app did: Updated …'. finding.title: A small task pauses before its review with three quarters of its budget left, so a clean run ends 'Ended: 1 paused' and asks for CHF 0.08 more
finding.what_the_person_sees: The task row says 'Paused at its budget · CHF 0.02 of CHF 0.08 budget'. The Inbox says '"Write README.md listing the files and how to open the site" paused at its budget of CHF 0.08 / The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget. / Continue (CHF 0.08 more)'. Details say 'paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.08 has no room for it.'
finding.expected: A task that costs a quarter of its accepted budget finishes, review included. The plan said about CHF 0.41 for 4 tasks and the session spent CHF 0.15. 'Paused at its budget' is not said when the budget is mostly unspent.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st4/steps/c30-screens.json, 09-c30-session-details.png, 12-c30-inbox.png; README coder calls #21-#24 cost USD 0.0198 and no critic call followed; earlier light reviews cost USD 0.026-0.033
finding.repro: bench-live, the Lindenhof brief (/tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/scripts/c30-create.cjs), Approve and start; watch the 4th task (estimate CHF 0.08).
finding.suspected_cause: Since C4b a task's budget counts its reviews, but the plan sets the budget to the work estimate, and the review room check reserves the critic's worst case, which the CHF 0.06 left never covers.

verdict.root_cause: The README task's own budget was USD 0.10 (CHF 0.08). The intake model chose it (its reply has "budgetUsdMicro": 100000) and the plan wrote it without any check (project-plan.ts:574). The coder's work cost 19,754 µUSD (Run row; model calls 22-25), which left 80,246 µUSD. Before the review starts, runner.ts:4856-4873 compares what is left with price.floorUsdMicro. That floor is the price of the review's output cap alone (critic.ts:469): REVIEW_TOKENS_PER_CALL = 8192 (critic.ts:134) at USD 10/MTok on Sonnet 5.5 = 81,920 µUSD. Since 80,246 < 81,920, the review was refused before any call. The state confirms this: there is no critic Run row for the task, and the critic.review_paused event has source task_budget. The task went to needs_human with a card: Continue (CHF 0.08 more), needs_usd_micro 74,868. The hooks precheck would have refused the first call anyway (input plus 8192 output > left). The work run kept no room for the review because R+W is more than half of the USD 0.10 budget (executor.ts:760-762), which is the documented 'it should get done anyway' branch. Real light reviews in this same session cost 26,414, 30,987 and 32,479 µUSD, with at most 835 output tokens per call. So the admission rule makes every budgeted task with budget minus work under USD 0.082 (on Sonnet) impossible to review, even when the review would cost a third of what is left. The app also lets such budgets through without a word. The intake prompt shows 'budgetUsdMicro': int? with no guidance (intake.ts:2025). The plan card's 'about CHF 0.08' is the estimate capped at the budget (withinTaskBudget), so it hides the gap. The 'may leave too little for its review' warning (C4b-left-5) exists only in the Start dialog (start-check.ts:320-343, StartSessionDialog.tsx:552), not on the intake plan card used by 'Approve and start'. The engine did what the C4b design asked: the BA-3 composed case (task-budget-all.test.ts:498-540) asserts this exact pause at USD 0.075, and LC-C32 lists it as branch (ii). But the outcome the person sees is the defect, and the owner's answer 8 ('it should get a warning') is not met on this path. Correction to the suspected cause: the plan did not set the budget from the work estimate (the model picked USD 0.10 and the estimate was capped to it), and the refusal came from the output-cap floor (USD 0.082), not the worst case W.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:4863 (left < price.floorUsdMicro), with packages/critic/src/critic.ts:134 and :469 (the floor is the price of 8192 output tokens); packages/runtime/src/session/project-plan.ts:574 (the model's budget written unchecked); packages/runtime/src/session/start-check.ts:320-343 (the warning exists only for the Start dialog)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1. Engine (needs a session-lead decision, because C4b's design kept 'the critic's per-call floor' off limits): for a review capped by a task budget, size each call's max_tokens from the room, as effort max already does. That is min(REVIEW_TOKENS_PER_CALL, what fits in left minus the input's price), with a smaller minimum such as 2,048 tokens (live light reviews output 98-835 tokens per call). CriticService.reviewCallUsdMicro (critic.ts:456-471, and maxTokensPerCall at :614) should report that minimum's price as floorUsdMicro, so runner.ts:4863 refuses only when even the minimum cannot fit. 2. Plan: when the plan writes a budget the model proposed (project-plan.ts:574, plan-tasks.ts:154), raise a budget that cannot hold the whole estimate plus W to that sum, or leave it 0 so the session pays. Also give the intake prompt (intake.ts:2025) one line: a task's budget covers its work and its review. 3. Screens: put the same reviewMayWaitLine on the intake plan card's task lines (owner's answer 8: 'it should get a warning'). 4. Words: when the review waits while most of the budget is unspent, the row and the card say the review needs up to CHF x and CHF y is left, instead of only 'Paused at its budget'.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed test in packages/runtime/test/task-budget-all.test.ts, or real-daemon via POST /projects/:id/intake and then the plan card's 'Approve and start'. The intake stand-in proposes one coder task with budgetUsdMicro 100_000 at tier 1. The coder bills about 20,000 µUSD. The critic stand-in bills three calls of about 300 output tokens each (about 30,000 µUSD in all). Expect: a critic Run row exists, the task is done, session.ended has paused 0, /inbox has no task:budget_stop card, and the Tasks row reads about CHF 0.04 'of CHF 0.08 budget'. Today it fails: no critic Run row, the task is needs_human, the log says '"…" paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.08 has no room for it.', and the card says 'Continue (CHF 0.08 more)'. A second case: GET /inbox's intake card for that plan carries 'its budget of CHF 0.08 may leave too little for its review, which then waits for Continue.'. That also fails today. The BA-3 case at task-budget-all.test.ts:498 (USD 0.075 budget, 65,000 left) asserts today's pause and would need re-baselining under fix 1.
verdict.area_hint: d1116-budget-all (C4b); the plan-card warning touches d1109-cred-screens' plan card / intake card words
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st4/home/data/state.sqlite. The README task has budget 100000, est 100000, actual 19754 and one Run row (coder, completed), with no critic row. Its card has change_card continue_usd_micro 100000 and needs_usd_micro 74868. The event critic.review_paused has source task_budget. /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st4/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl has the intake reply with budgetUsdMicro 100000 for write-readme and 150000 for the other three. Critic max_tokens is 8192 on claude-sonnet-5-5 at USD 2/10 per MTok. The plan card (06-c30-01-inbox-plan-card.txt) shows 'about CHF 0.08' and no warning. No leftover names this exactly. Related ones: C4bD-3 (tune REVIEW_EVIDENCE_ALLOWANCE_TOKENS and the tier 1 review start from LC-C32; this finding is the floor from REVIEW_TOKENS_PER_CALL, not the evidence allowance), C4bD-1 (the opposite gap, between the floor and the real first call), C4bL-5 (the size of Continue at tiny budgets). The C4b design's money check had already warned: 'At CHF 0.06 (USD 0.075) the first call's worst case is more than the whole budget ... No screen warns'. That warning was later built for the Start dialog only (f02f441, C4b-left-5). The intake picked USD 0.10-0.15 budgets in other live4 runs too (st4, session/s2). So any small task whose work costs more than about USD 0.07 at a USD 0.15 budget hits the same pause. No bench run was needed: the arithmetic and the saved state settle it.

finding.title: A paid task check runs on a run where nothing is wrong: two harmless critic notes trigger it (confirms L4-selftasks-1)
finding.what_the_person_sees: Details: 'Checked the task list after "Write index.html with heading, welcome and hours": no change (less than CHF 0.01).' The review counts 'the session's own checks less than CHF 0.01'.
finding.expected: Zero task-check calls and no Details line when no report has 'For the task list:'.
finding.evidence: model-call #5 critic notes ('... The exact string is still present.', '... It is harmless.'); #7 task_check claude-sonnet-5-5 USD 0.003224 whose Evidence block is those two notes, reply changes [] flagged []
finding.repro: As LC-C30; read the model-call log for role task_check.
finding.suspected_cause: isCriticNote counts every critic info/note finding as a task-list note the task did not cause.

verdict.root_cause: After every accepted or sent-back review, the runner collects the review's findings with `isCriticNote` as "the critic's notes the task did not cause" (runner.ts:3333-3355, filter at :3342). But `isCriticNote` (task-list-notes.ts:134-136) is `f.severity === "info" || f.description.endsWith(NOT_CAUSED_BY_TASK)`. It is a copy of the executor's L-4 predicate `isReviewNote` (executor.ts:700-702). That predicate decides what the retry brief shows as "for your information only". It was never meant to mean "a problem outside this task". The critic prompt (evals/registry/critic/critic.md:97,119) uses `note` for any low-severity point about the task's own work, and schema.ts maps `note` to `info`. So every review with even one harmless note pushes a `review` TaskListNote. `checkTaskList` (runner.ts:2387) then sees evidence that is not empty and makes the paid planning call. That call produces `session.task_checked` (the Details line) and its cost goes into the session review's "session's own checks" (views.ts:862). The plan (runC-plan.json, d1109-selftasks-run: "a review note the task did not cause ... Why: cost; ... not a paid replan after every task"), ADR 0119 point 3 and runtime.md ("the critic's notes the task did not cause") all limit this evidence to findings the task did not cause. Only the runtime's measured "Tried ..." findings carry that mark (critic.ts:903). The live log confirms it. seq 6 is the critic's submit_review with two findings of severity `note` and no "(not caused by this task)" suffix. seq 8 is the task_check (claude-sonnet-5-5, USD 0.003224), and its Evidence block holds exactly those two lines under 'From the critic's notes on "Write index.html..."'. Its reply was {changes:[], flagged:[]}. The finding's #5/#7 are seq 6/8 in the log. No report had the heading. Severity stays minor: about USD 0.003 a check and at most 3 a session. Side effects: an empty Details line and a figure in the session review. These checks also use up the 3-a-session allowance, so a real 'For the task list:' report later in the session can be pushed to the next session. At Advisor or Assisted, the model could also file a suggestion card from harmless notes.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/task-list-notes.ts:134 (isCriticNote counts severity info); used at packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3342, which triggers the check at runner.ts:2387
verdict.fix_sketch: Split the two meanings. Keep executor.ts `isReviewNote` (info OR not-caused) for the retry brief. In task-list-notes.ts, replace `isCriticNote` with `notCausedByTask(f) = f.description.endsWith(NOT_CAUSED_BY_TASK)`, or give it that body, so only the runtime-measured findings the task did not cause become `review` evidence. The critic's own `note`/`info` findings about the task's files stay on the review and do not trigger a check. If critic notes about the plan are wanted later, add an explicit marker (for example a 'for the task list' field in submit_review) rather than inferring it from severity. Update runtime.md's evidence bullet and the predicate's comment. The injection harness calls reviewNoteLines directly (evals/src/injection-runner.ts:1902), so report-004 is unaffected.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed runtime case in packages/runtime/test/session-task-list.test.ts, using a world with a critic stand-in. At Standard, plan two tasks at risk tier 1, with no 'For the task list:' heading in either report. The critic accepts the first task with two `note` findings ('The viewport meta tag was not requested. It is harmless.' and 'The exact string is still present.'). Assert: zero calls on the taskCheck port, no `session.task_checked` event in the session's log (the Details line), and no 'session's own checks' clause in the session review sentence from views.ts. Counterpart case: a finding 'Tried index.html: error on the page: x is not defined (not caused by this task)' gives exactly one check, and its evidence quotes that line. Today the first case fails with one check call. At the bench boundary: rerun LC-C30 (Lindenhof brief, Approve and start) on bench-live or the stand-in with critic notes. Expect no role task_check in model-calls.jsonl and no 'Checked the task list' line under Details.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-run
verdict.notes: No leftover in leftovers-{L3,C2,C3,C4,C4b-design,C4b,C5,C6}.json names this. C4L-15 is about where the check's line shows (Details or person level), not about why the check runs. The composed task-list tests never compose a critic, so the review-note path (runner.ts:3333-3355) has no test. The finding's "expected" is slightly too broad. Per ADR 0119 point 3, a review finding the task did not cause should still trigger a check even with no report heading. In this run neither note had that mark, so zero checks is the right result here. Evidence files: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st4/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl (seq 6 is the critic's submit_review, seq 8 is the task_check) and /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/steps/LC-C30.json. I verified this from the code and the live log, and did not rerun the bench: the code fully explains it. The separate README pause in the same step is L4-selftasks-20, not this finding.

finding.title: Real problems the planning model puts in 'flagged' never reach the person in chat
finding.what_the_person_sees: Nothing. After prices.html was added, the styles task still links only index.html and contact.html, and no line says so.
finding.expected: What the check noticed but did not change is shown with the read-back or the reply, or it becomes a change.
finding.evidence: model-call #1 flagged ['The styles.css task links only index.html and contact.html; it should also cover prices.html once that page exists.']; #2 flagged [same, plus 'Confirm with the owner that Seestrasse 12, Zurich and 044 123 45 67 are correct']; the chat and the card show neither
finding.repro: As LC-C28 check 2; compare the task_check reply with the chat.
finding.suspected_cause: fixTasksInChat (packages/runtime/src/conversation/task-fix-tool.ts) never reads run.reply.flagged. The rules reserve flagged for instruction-like lines, so the model's other notes are dropped (L4-selftasks-9 is the session path).

verdict.root_cause: The finding is real. The suspected cause is slightly off: fixTasksInChat does read reply.flagged, but only indirectly, and then it drops what it read. It passes run.reply to fenceTaskChanges. There, task-check.ts:758 turns every reply.flagged line into an askFirst entry { reason: 'the agent found a line that reads like an instruction', quote: <the line> }. Evidence lines the scanner flagged get the same treatment at :757. Back in chat, task-fix-tool.ts:214 keeps only the entries without a quote (`fence.askFirst.filter((a) => !a.quote).map((a) => a.reason)`). So every quoted line is thrown away. Nothing else carries it: planFix gets only `askFirst: true` (commands.ts:331-338), the read-back gets only fixAsk(change lines), and the footer (:233) gets only reasons[0]. On a check with no changes, the fence returns askFirst [] (task-check.ts:988), and the reply at :199-203 says only fixNoChangeReply plus the refused changes. The session path does show these lines: fileTaskProposal (task-proposal.ts:176) collects the quotes and proposalBody puts quotes[0] in the card's text. Chat does not, which goes against ADR 0119 point 4 (a flagged line 'is quoted to the person') and point 6 (the card quotes it). The bench evidence matches the code. The two Sonnet replies (model-calls.jsonl #1 and #2) hold the flagged lines. The transcript events of 09:06:26 and 09:09:14 have the read-back text and the footer 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself. Checking the tasks cost ...' and no flagged text. Nothing in human_request or message in state.sqlite holds it either. Part of the trigger is the model's own choice. The rules (task-check.ts:102) reserve flagged for evidence lines that read like instructions, and these two notes are not instructions. The styles note could have been an edit of the styles task. But the schema `{changes, flagged, why}` gives the model nowhere else for 'noticed but not changed', and chat would also drop a real instruction quote. So the app is at fault whatever the model chose.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/task-fix-tool.ts:214 (also :199-203 and :233; packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts:757-759 and :988)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) In fixTasksInChat, collect `quotes = fence.askFirst.map(a => a.quote).filter(Boolean)`. Show them in the reply under the read-back, using the session card's sentence (proposalBody: 'A line of the agent's check reads like an instruction: "...". Nothing changes until you say yes.'). Pass them to planFix too, so the Inbox card's text holds them. At Standard, the read-back then also says why it asks. 2) Keep instruction quotes apart from the model's own notes. Either add a reply field, e.g. `notes: [string]` ('what you noticed and did not change, one sentence each, at most 3'), with a prompt version bump and the rule 'a change the task list needs is a change, not a note'. Or, with no prompt change, run readsLikeInstruction over each reply.flagged line: only the lines that match ask first and are quoted; the others become one line under the reply ('The check also noticed: ...'), cut to design section 5 lengths. 3) When a check makes no change but has quotes or notes, the no-change reply (task-fix-tool.ts:199-203, and fence task-check.ts:988, which drops askFirst when there are no changes) still names them. The session path's version of this is L4-selftasks-9 (task-check.ts checkAtBoundary).
verdict.failing_test_idea: A composed test in packages/runtime/test/chat-fix-tasks.test.ts, using the existing setup (ConversationAgent, CommandLoop, FakeProvider scripting the task-check reply). (a) Assisted (level 1): the reply has one add and flagged ['"Style the page" links only index.html; it should also cover prices.html']. chat('fix the tasks'). Expect the text the person reads (reply or footer) to hold that line, and the Inbox human_request (why or steps) to hold it. Fails today. (b) Standard (level 2), same reply: the reply reads back and says why it asks first, with the quote. Fails today: the read-back has no reason. (c) The reply has no changes and one flagged line: the reply names the line. Fails today: only 'Nothing to change in the tasks of Quote page.'. Then a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts: POST the chat line, read the conversation transcript's text and footer, and assert the quoted line is there.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat (owns task-fix-tool.ts); the no-change fence part (task-check.ts:988) is shared with d1109-selftasks-run, whose session-path twin is L4-selftasks-9
verdict.notes: I checked this by reading the code at 4cf11fd and the evidence the walk kept: st3/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl #1 and #2 (Sonnet), #9 (Haiku, also flagged a 'confirm the address' note), the transcript events in st3/home/data/state.sqlite, and human_request rows. I did not rerun the bench: the code path is deterministic, and the stand-in task-check play only flags STEERING evidence lines. No leftover in L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5 or C6 names it; C4L-15 and C3L-14 are nearby but different. It also drops more than the model's harmless notes. In chat, a scanner-flagged line in the kept notes (an injection attempt) is quoted nowhere either, and takeNotes then removes the notes from the project (task-fix-tool.ts:197). So the person is never told about the attempt, against ADR 0119 point 4, although nothing is applied. That could justify raising this to major alongside L4-selftasks-9. I kept minor because what was observed is two harmless notes going missing. A second consequence: at Standard, any flagged line makes the set read back with no 'Asks you first:' reason, because the only reason it adds is the quoted one that :214 drops.

finding.title: A read-back expires after 10 minutes with no notice; an open page keeps Yes enabled and still counts the change as waiting (C6L-11)
finding.what_the_person_sees: The Inbox card disappears at 10 min with no Update. A reloaded chat shows '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)'. On a page left open, Yes is still enabled, the header says 'Waiting for you: 1 question and 1 change to confirm' and the Inbox badge says 2. Yes answers 'The change I asked about expired before your yes, so nothing was changed. Ask again if you still want it.' The person has to pay for a new check.
finding.expected: Per the owner's C6L-11 answer, the read-back lives as long as its Inbox card is open. Until that is built, the open page drops the Yes and the count at expiry.
finding.evidence: request 01a1e8c9-0e29-72cd-93fc-c958bed2a394 expired 09:24:12.910Z (created 09:14:12.905Z); /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/49-c28-23-after10min-inbox.png, 57-c28-25-keepopen-after-wait-before-yes.png, 58-c28-25-keepopen-after-yes.png; c28-25-keepopen.json yesEnabled true at 09:36:37 after the 09:36:02 expiry
finding.repro: Assisted project, chat 'fix the tasks' with a duplicate; wait 10.5 min, both with the page kept open and after a reload; press Yes.
finding.suspected_cause: PENDING_TTL_MS is 10 min (packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts), and expirePending sends no Update and no live event the chat page reacts to.

verdict.root_cause: Every chat read-back is a pending confirmation with a fixed 10-minute life: PENDING_TTL_MS = 10*60*1000 (packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts:21), and the executor arms that timer for each card (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:579-581). When the timer fires, expirePending (executor.ts:1030-1041) deletes the pending entry and sets the human_request row to 'expired'. It does nothing else. ExecutorOptions has no expiry hook, so compose never hears about it: no rt.events.emit("inbox"), no conversation.changed and no message. The open page's live state depends on exactly those signals. The header count, the Inbox badge and liveProjects.refresh come only from inbox.changed (server.ts:3541-3553, apps/ui/src/store/context.tsx:118-127). The chat re-reads only on conversation.changed, which fires only on a chat turn's start, step or end (server.ts:3596-3602). The Yes/No block is drawn from the server's `waiting` flag at load time (server.ts:2786-2795/2863-2864, apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:621-647). So a page left open keeps an enabled Yes, 'Waiting for you: 1 question and 1 change to confirm' and the badge at 2. After the Yes, the agent replies 'expired before your yes' (conversation/agent.ts:530). The chat POST emits inbox only for a new pending card (server.ts:2667), so the count stays at 2 even after that reply. A reload rebuilds the view from the row (card 'expired' -> '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)'), which is why the reloaded case looks right. Expiry also contradicts design §3.9 ('a card waiting (stays until answered or dismissed)') and §3.2 ('stale data is a bug'). It is also silent: the restart path expireOrphanedCards (packages/runtime/src/loop/answered-cards.ts:160-205) sends a plain warning message, but the timer path tells the person nothing. The evidence matches. In the st3 DB, request 01a1e8c9 was created at 09:14:12.905 and expired at 09:24:12.910. The keep-open request 01a1e8d3 was created at 09:26:05.987 and expired at 09:36:05.989 (the finding says 09:36:02, a small slip). At 09:36:37 c28-25-keepopen.json still shows yesEnabled true, Inbox2 and the header count, and afterYes still shows Inbox2.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:1030 (expirePending: row expired, no notice or event; timer armed at :579-581 from PENDING_TTL_MS, packages/commands/src/confirmation.ts:21); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:3541 (inbox.changed only on rt.events 'inbox') and :3596 (conversation.changed only on chat turns); apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:621 (Yes drawn from the load-time r.waiting)
verdict.fix_sketch: (1) The C6L-11 decision: a fix-the-tasks read-back gets no 10-minute TTL. It lives as long as its Inbox card is open. restorePending already re-arms it after a restart. On Yes, compare the task-list fingerprint taken at the check; if the list has changed, say so and offer the check again rather than apply a stale set. Design §3.9 says the same for every chat read-back: it stays until answered or dismissed, so consider dropping the TTL for all chat-filed cards that are not high risk. (2) For any expiry that remains (timer or sweepPending), add an onExpired(id, row) callback to ExecutorOptions and call it from expirePending once humanRequest.expire succeeds. Compose wires it to: events.emit('inbox', {}), so the badge, the header 'Waiting for you' and Home follow; a conversation.changed for the row's project (a notify on conversation turnsOf(), or a new event), so the open chat re-reads, waiting goes false and Yes disappears; and the same plain Update the restart path sends ('The change you asked for was not made: <what>. The card waited 10 minutes ... Ask again in Chat if you still want it.'). (3) In the chat POST, also emit inbox when the turn met an expired card, so a stale count corrects itself on the next answer.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real-daemon test (packages/runtime/test, compose with a fake clock and the bench stand-in): at Assisted, with a duplicate task the person added, POST the chat 'fix the tasks'. The read-back waits and GET /inbox counts it. Subscribe to GET /events. Advance the clock to 10.5 minutes. Today: no inbox.changed and no conversation.changed frame arrives. Per C6L-11 the stronger assertion is that the card is still waiting (conversation reply.card 'waiting', the Inbox card open) and POST 'yes' applies the drop. Where expiry is kept, assert that an inbox.changed frame arrives with needsYouCount down by 1, plus a conversation.changed for the project, and that a message row says the change was not made. UI test (apps/ui, Conversation and the store with an injected EventSource): with a waiting read-back rendered, deliver inbox.changed{needsYouCount:1} and conversation.changed after the fake daemon expires the card. Expect confirm-yes to be gone, readback-closed to read '(not answered; ask again if you still want it)', the Inbox badge to show 1 and the header to read 'Waiting for you: 1 question'. All of these fail today.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat
verdict.notes: C6L-11 (leftovers-C6.json, 'major, decision') already covers the 10-minute silent lapse and the paid check that is lost. This finding adds the stale open page: Yes stays enabled, the header count and badge stay at 2, and they stay wrong even after the Yes. That part is wider than C6L-11, because every chat read-back that still expires (task edits, settings) has the same missing inbox.changed/conversation.changed. I agree with minor for the stale-page part: the Yes is refused with a clear sentence and nothing wrong is applied. The expiry itself carries C6L-11's major. The owner-decisions file contains no C6L-11 text. The 'owner's answer' the finding cites is the session lead's C6-merge decision recorded in leftovers-C6.json. This was a live-model run (bench-live), but the behaviour is entirely code-driven (timer, no event), not a model choice. I queried a temporary copy of the st3 state DB for the row timestamps, then deleted the copy. I did not run the bench.

finding.title: A change the person named in their own words is booked to the agent, and Changes quotes 'Think it through.' as what was said (C6L-10)
finding.what_the_person_sees: Changes: 'Chat · Bike shop · Alice · Changed "Write the contact page contact.html": what done looks like and the criteria. Said: "Think it through."'. The drawer says 'Changed by the agent: ...'. The chat shows 'Think it through.' as the person's message.
finding.expected: Per the owner's C6-merge answer, a change the person named and confirmed is theirs ('by you'), and 'Said' quotes their words.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/c28-19-ownwords-yes.json
finding.repro: As L4-selftasks-13, then press Think it through and Yes; open Changes and the task drawer.
finding.suspected_cause: Chat tool calls run under the agent actor, and wordsUsed for Think it through is the button's line.

verdict.root_cause:
There are two code causes, both confirmed by the bench run's own state.sqlite. In st3, the change_log row at 09:12:45 has author_agent=Alice (the project's agent), author_human=null and words_used "Think it through.". Alice is the agent row and Robin is the person, so "Alice" on Changes is the agent.
(1) Attribution. Every command the chat model calls runs with the agent as actor: commands.ts:324 sets ctxFor to contextFor(turn, {actor: {kind:"agent"}}). The read-back stores that context (executor.ts:532). When the person types yes, Executor.confirm calls p.perform() with the stored agent context (executor.ts:965). The confirming human (`by`) is used only for the answered record. record() then writes author_agent (executor.ts:758-759), so change-rows.ts:53 gives byAgent=true and ChangesPage.tsx:103 names the agent. task.update picks the drawer reason by ctx.actor.kind and writes "Changed by the agent: ..." (task.ts:1840-1843).
(2) The quoted words. The turn's wordsUsed is always req.text (agent.ts:1118). Pressing Think it through sends the button's own line "Think it through." (Conversation.tsx:310). The agent then works out the question the pass actually answers (accepted.question, the person's previous line, agent.ts:1411-1412), but never puts it back on turn.wordsUsed. The pending card (executor.ts:538, 573) and the change row (executor.ts:748) therefore keep "Think it through.", and Changes shows Said: "Think it through.". ChangesPage.tsx:36-38 itself says a button's words are words nobody said.
Neither part is a model choice. The model made the change on the Think turn, but at the base the same change made on any typed turn would also read "by the agent". The owner's decision, quoted in ADR 0119:128 and decided in the C6-merge note (runC-plan session_lead_decisions), is that a change the person names and confirms is theirs. It was deferred to the fix run after live check 4, so it is not built at 4cf11fd.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324; packages/commands/src/executor.ts:965 (perform with the stored agent ctx) and :758-759; packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:1840-1843; packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1118 and :1411-1412; apps/ui/src/components/Conversation.tsx:310
verdict.fix_sketch: Keep the agent actor when the change is proposed, so the ADR 0030 item 2 limit rule and security-command-actor.test.ts still hold. When a human confirms a read-back the model proposed in a conversation turn, run perform with the confirming human as actor. Do this in Executor.confirm, or with a flag stored in StoredCardContext such as personNamed: true, set by commandToolSpecs and kept over restorePending. This gives author_human = the confirmer, Changes naming the person (byAgent false), and task.ts writing "Changed by you: ...". The flag must not be set for planFix (fix_tasks' check), the session source or Undo, so those stay the agent's. In agent.ts, once `question` is settled (after :1412), set turn.wordsUsed = question whenever the turn re-asks an earlier line (an accepted offer, depth "longer", or a bare "think harder"). Then the card and the change row quote the person's words, not the button's line. Touch ADR 0119 and the commands and conversation maintainer docs.

finding.title: At Assisted the footer gives 'is a task you added or changed yourself' as the reason it asks; Think it through repeats the read-back
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself. Checking the tasks cost CHF 0.01.' sits under a read-back that Assisted asks for anyway. The Think it through reply says '... needs your yes ... Confirm it and it goes through.' above the read-back.
finding.expected: The reason line only where it is the reason (Standard and up). The read-back appears once (design section 5).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/13-c28-10-fix1-reply.png; /tmp/frbench/live4/selftasks/st3/steps/c28-18-think.json
finding.repro: Assisted project with a task you added; chat 'fix the tasks'.
finding.suspected_cause: task-fix-tool.ts builds the footer from fence.askFirst whatever the autonomy level.

verdict.root_cause:
Footer (the main claim, real, caused by the code): in fixTasksInChat the read-back goes out when `turn.recordsRead || !makesFixesAtOnce(level) || askFirst` (task-fix-tool.ts:207). The footer is then built from the fence's ask-first reasons whatever caused the read-back: `reasons` at :211 and `footer: joined(reasons[0] ? `Asks you first: ${reasons[0]}.` : "", footer ?? "")` at :233. The code's own comment at :227-228 says the reason line is for "why it asks at a level that would make the changes at once", but :233 never looks at `level` or `recordsRead`. At Assisted (level 1, makesFixesAtOnce false; the journey set this, see 11-c28-07: "2 (Standard) → 1 (Assisted)") every set is read back anyway. So the line 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself.' (fence reason from task-check.ts:823/862/933) gives a reason that is not why the app asks. It showed on both fix1 and fix2. No test covers the chat footer at Assisted. chat-fix-tasks.test.ts only asserts the footer at Standard with no ask-first.
Think it through (secondary, the model's choice): the model got `{status:"pending", readback,…}` from the command tool (loop/commands.ts:306). Following the prompt rule "When a tool answers 'Needs confirmation', say so in a few words and stop" (evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:84-86), it wrote "...needs your yes: the new number ... Confirm it and it goes through." agent.ts:2206 places the model's text before the card's read-back, which is how the app is designed to work. That prose restates the change because the model chose to write it, against the same rule's "do not repeat the read-back". The prompt's "say so in a few words" makes a line like this likely, but this half is not a code defect.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/task-fix-tool.ts:233 (reasons at :211, read-back condition at :207, intent comment at :227-228); secondary: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2206 with evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:84-86
verdict.fix_sketch: In fixTasksInChat, show the reason only when it is the reason: `const fenceIsWhy = askFirst && makesFixesAtOnce(level) && !turn.recordsRead;` then `footer: joined(fenceIsWhy && reasons[0] ? `Asks you first: ${reasons[0]}.` : "", footer ?? "") || null`. At Advisor/Assisted the footer is then just the cost line ("Checking the tasks cost CHF 0.01."). Decide at the same time whether the run-path suggestion card (session/task-proposal.ts:184, `steps: [...changes, ...reasons.map(Asks you first…)]`) follows the same rule. Its ST-11 real-daemon case (apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:20397/20507/20656) and apps/ui/test/selftasks.test.tsx:32/129 currently pin the line at Assisted, so changing one path and not the other makes the two disagree. Optional, for the Think-it-through half: tighten conversation-agent.md rule 2 to "a change that waits for a yes is read back under your reply: write nothing about it, or at most 'This needs your yes.'", checked by an eval. Do not strip the model's text in code.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, describe "d1109-selftasks-chat, run C" (the person's boundary: POST /chat then GET /projects/:id/conversation as the Chat tab reads it): quotePage(a, 1), add a task through client.createTask as the person that the stand-in's task check drops as a duplicate, then POST /chat "fix the tasks". Assert the turn's read-back is the one composed question and its footer is exactly the cost line ("Checking the tasks cost ..."), with no "Asks you first". Same set at quotePage(a, 2): footer starts 'Asks you first: "<title>" is a task you added or changed yourself.' and the set is read back. Today the level-1 assertion fails. A matching composed case in packages/runtime/test/chat-fix-tasks.test.ts: setup({ level: 1 }) with a person-authored task in the check's drop, expect(r.footer).toBe("Checking the tasks cost less than CHF 0.01.").
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: 13-c28-10-fix1-reply.png/.txt show the read-back with Yes/No and under it 'Asks you first: "Build the contact page in contact.html" is a task you added or changed yourself. Checking the tasks cost CHF 0.01.'. 11-c28-07 confirms the project went Standard to Assisted before the check. fix2 (22-c28-12) shows the same footer. c28-18-think.json shows the Haiku 'Think it through' prose above the read-back. Severity words: the line is true as a fence fact but is not why the app asks at Assisted, and design section 5 rules 1 and 2 (short, what needs you first) argue against it. Not run on the stand-in bench: the code path is direct (no level check between :207 and :233), so I reasoned it out instead of reproducing it. The 'Think it through' half is the model's choice under a prompt that invites a sentence. If it is tracked, it belongs to the chat prompt (d1109-chat-depth / conversation-agent prompt) as a words item, not to this fix.

finding.title: Chat asks for a yes in words with no Yes/No card; the person's 'yes' gets 'Yes to what?'; the reply guard never fires
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'This widens what research may read, so I need your yes first. Shall I set research for Reading rules to any public website again?' with no buttons. A typed 'yes' gets 'Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes.' The rule stays 'only developer.mozilla.org'. Project C did the same twice in a row.
finding.expected: A Yes/No read-back on the first try. If the model answers in text only, the reply should be 'Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.'
finding.evidence: Card on the first try in 1 of 3 fresh projects; the guard line appears 0 times in /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/daemon.log. In the model-call log the first-try calls have toolCalls [] and that text (claude-haiku-5-5). Screenshots: l3b/steps/09-rr1-t3-reply.png, 10-rr1-t3b-reply.png, 25-reading-rules-c-t3-reply.png, 28-reading-rules-c-t3c-reply.png.
finding.repro: New project; in Chat say 'only read developer.mozilla.org for research', then 'research may read any public website again', then 'yes'; repeat on two fresh projects.
finding.suspected_cause: The guard looks for claims that a change was made or a yes was asked. It does not catch a question that asks for the yes itself when no command ran. Sibling of L4-session-2.

verdict.root_cause: The model (claude-haiku-5-5, low effort) answered the widening request in text and called no tool. The model-call log at /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl shows this at seq 3, 14 and 15: toolCalls [], replies "...so I need your yes first. Shall I set research ... again?" and "...it needs your yes first. Should research ... be allowed to read any public website again?". The prompt does tell it to call the command, so the slip starts with the model. But the app has a guard built for exactly this live failure (l3-chat-claims, from L3-run-1, which was the same request), and the guard does not see this phrasing. claimOf (packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:139) only matches past-tense claims about the app: ASKED at claims.ts:69-106 ("I've asked for confirmation", "I'm waiting for your yes", "I'll apply it once you approve"...) and CHANGED at :108-119. A reply that asks for the yes in words matches neither: no "Shall I / Should I / Do you want me to ...?" and no "(I|it) need(s) your yes". So falseClaim (agent.ts:2045-2050) returns null. I ran claimOf with tsx on all three live replies and it returned null each time, while the L3-run-1 sentence returned kind "asked". No nudge was sent: each of those turns has exactly one model call, and "chat reply claimed what no command did" appears 0 times in daemon.log. The person then types "yes", and the app catches it before the model (agent.ts:1214-1220). No card waits and the newest reply is no go_ahead offer (liveOffer, agent.ts:893), so nothingWaitingReply sends YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY (agent.ts:527, 2600). That is the app contradicting the question it showed one line above. The prompt adds to the problem: conversation-agent.md:21 says '"yes" ... refer[s] to' the recent conversation, but a bare "yes" with nothing waiting never reaches the model, so asking in words looks answerable to the model when it is not. Rate: a card on the first try in 1 of 3 projects (project B, seq 10). Project C asked in text twice before a reworded line ("yes, let research read any public website") made the model call settings_set. Sibling: L4-session-2 ("Do you want me to start a session ...?").
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/claims.ts:69 (ASKED patterns; claimOf at :139), with packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:2045 (falseClaim) and agent.ts:1214-1220 (bare yes -> YES_TO_WHAT_REPLY, :527)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) claims.ts: add a third claim kind, "asks", for a reply that asks the person for a yes in words. A sentence that is a question offering to make a change ("Shall I / Should I / Do you want me to / Want me to / Soll ich" followed by a change verb: set, change, widen, allow, start, add, raise...), or a sentence saying "(I|it|this) need(s) your yes|confirmation|approval (first|before)" next to such a question. Keep NEGATION and EARLIER as they are, and leave clarifying questions without a change verb alone ("Which project?"). 2) agent.ts falseClaim: count an "asks" claim as false when !did.asked. claimNudge gets a lead for it: "Your reply asks the person for a yes in words, but no command in this turn read a change back, and a typed yes reaches no one. If the person asked for a change, call its command now; the runtime reads it back with Yes and No. Otherwise answer again without asking for a yes." If the model still only asks after the nudge, trueLine gives NOTHING_CHANGED_REPLY / NOTHING_CHANGED_CARD_WAITS_REPLY as today. 3) A backstop at agent.ts:1214: when the newest reply was such an unbacked question (store a flag on the transcript reply, e.g. reply.askedInWords), a bare "yes" should not get "Yes to what?". Either pass the yes, with the earlier line, to the model (safe: any change still gets its own read-back) or say the true line ("Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more."). 4) conversation-agent.md: add "Never ask for a yes in words (\"Shall I ...?\"); call the command and the runtime asks with Yes and No". Fix line 21 so it no longer implies that a bare yes reaches the model. Bump the prompt version. The same fix covers L4-session-2.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, describe "l3-chat-claims, run L3" (real daemon, POST /chat, scripted FakeProvider), add a case. Script: toolReply settings_set {mode:"only", only:["developer.mozilla.org"]}, textReply "Done.", textReply "This widens what research may read, so I need your yes first. Shall I set research for Reading rules to any public website again?", toolReply settings_set {mode:"any"}, textReply "Needs confirmation.". Steps: say("only read developer.mozilla.org for research"), then say("research may read any public website again"). Expect 3 chat-model calls for that turn (the last message carries the "asks" nudge), widened.pendingConfirmation.readback === READBACK, and client.conversation(project.id).waiting set. Then say("yes"): expect researchReads "Research reads: any public website". Second case: the model repeats the question after the nudge. Expect said.reply === "Nothing changed, and nothing waits for your yes. Say it again to try once more.", no pending card, the rule unchanged. A "yes" right after an unbacked question never gets "Yes to what? Nothing is waiting for your yes." Today the first case fails: 1 model call, the reply is the question, pendingConfirmation is null, and "yes" gets "Yes to what?". Also a unit case in packages/runtime/test/conversation-memory.test.ts: claimOf is non-null for the three live replies (seq 3, 14, 15) and for "Do you want me to start a session on Garden club?", and stays null for "Which project do you mean?".
verdict.area_hint: l3-chat-claims (run L3's claim guard; run C's d1109-chat-guard owns the nearby chat regions of agent.ts)
verdict.notes: Checks made: (a) the UI captures l3b/steps/09, 10, 11 and 12 match the claim word for word; (b) model-call log seq 3 and 14/15 have toolCalls [] with the quoted text, each one model call per turn (no nudge), and the "yes" turn made no model call at all (the app answered it); (c) daemon.log has 0 lines "chat reply claimed what no command did"; (d) I ran claimOf with tsx (/tmp/frbench/v-L4-l3-1/claim.mts) on the live texts and got null for all three, against kind "asked" for the original L3-run-1 sentence. The rule never widened before a yes, so nothing unsafe happened. The harm: the person cannot make the change in one go, and the app contradicts itself ("Shall I ...?" followed by "Yes to what?"). No known leftover names this. C3L-8 is a different case: the app's own depth-offer line "Go ahead?" left without a button after another line. LL-10 is only about the correction lines being English. Same root as L4-session-2 (minor), which should be fixed with it. Severity stays major: this is the main way to change something in words, and the same person-visible failure as L3-run-1 (major) with a different phrasing; first try worked in 1 of 3 fresh projects.

finding.title: Chat replies describe the app's tool calls and copy the 'The app did:' history marker
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'The second call was refused only because the setting already matched.' (B); 'The app did: research for Reading rules C now reads only developer.mozilla.org ...' (C)
finding.expected: A plain confirmation with no internals (section 5 rule 6).
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/reading-rules-b-t2.json (two settings_set calls in one turn), reading-rules-c-t2.json
finding.repro: Turn 2 of L4-l3-1 on fresh projects.
finding.suspected_cause: The history now carries 'The app did: ...', and Haiku copies it. Tool refusals are passed to the model and it repeats them.

verdict.root_cause: C ('The app did: research for Reading rules C now reads ...'): the history did not cause this. The model-call log /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, seq 12-13, shows C's turn had no history at all: messages holds only the person's line and the tool round. The marker came from the system prompt the app sends. That prompt says it twice, in words that read like a format for the reply: conversation-agent.md:21-22 says "A reply that changed something ends with the app's own line 'The app did: …'", and agent.ts:605 (CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES) says "An earlier reply's line 'The app did: …' is what that turn changed". Haiku then wrote the marker into its own reply. Nothing removes it afterwards. The reply text goes to the person as written, and replyInHistory (transcript.ts:353-366) keeps the model's prose next to the app's actionLines. So turn 3's history (seq 14) carries two "The app did:" lines for one change, and the model can no longer tell its own lines from the app's. B ('The second call was refused only because the setting already matched'): Haiku made two settings_set calls in one turn, one without the project and one with "Reading rules B". The first one applied. The second is a no-op: refuseNoChange (settings.ts:1078-1084) throws on it, and the tool layer sends it to the model as an error, content "Refused: … is already only developer.mozilla.org." with isError: true (registry.ts:215-218). The prompt then points the model at refusals: "when it is refused, read why and try again" (agent.ts:600-601) and "unless a tool answered … in this turn" (conversation-agent.md:86-88, agent.ts:603-605). No rule tells the model to keep its calls and tool results out of the reply. The same tool talk shows up elsewhere in the run: seq 16 'no tool has accepted a widening in this turn', seq 10 'the never list cleared'. Narrating its duplicate call is partly the model's own choice. The error-shaped no-op and the tool-centred prompt make it likely.
verdict.where: evals/registry/principals/conversation-agent.md:21-22 and packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:605 (the prompt presents "The app did: …" as how a reply ends); packages/runtime/src/conversation/transcript.ts:353-366 (replyInHistory keeps the model's own "The app did:" in the history); packages/commands/src/registry.ts:215-218 with packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:1078-1084 (a no-op set goes back as an is_error "Refused:")
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Prompt (conversation-agent.md, next version, and CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES): say that only the app writes the "The app did:" line, that it is never part of the model's own reply, and that the model never starts or ends a reply with it. Better still, take the marker out of the assistant content: give the history's changes as a facts block the app owns (for example "# Changed in this conversation"), so there is nothing in the model's own replies to copy. Under "How you answer", add: "Say what is true now for the person; never describe your tool calls, their order or their refusals." 2) Code: before a reply is shown and stored, remove a leading or embedded HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD from the model's text (in agent.ts, where finalText becomes the reply). In replyInHistory, also remove that lead from the prose, so the app's actionLines are the only lines that carry it. This keeps the rule "a reply without one changed nothing" true. 3) A no-op set (ForerunnerError details.unchanged) goes back as a plain tool result, not an error: "Nothing to change: <what> is already <value>." Optionally, when an earlier call in the same turn already made that exact change, the second identical settings_set call gets the same non-error answer, so there is no refusal for the model to talk about.
verdict.failing_test_idea: At the chat boundary (POST /chat on the composed runtime with a scripted model; conversation-memory.test.ts or a real-daemon.test.ts case): (a) On a fresh project's first turn the scripted model calls settings_set web_access only developer.mozilla.org, then answers "The app did: research for X now reads only developer.mozilla.org." Expect the reply text the person gets (ChatReplyView.text, the bubble) to contain no "The app did:". Expect the next turn's history assistant message to contain exactly one "The app did:" line, the app's own change sentence. Both fail today. (b) The scripted model calls settings_set twice in one turn, without and then with project, for the same value. Expect the second tool_result not to be is_error and not to start with "Refused:". This fails today. (c) Live eval, for the record: fresh project, Haiku, "only read developer.mozilla.org for research". The reply must not contain "The app did", "call", "tool" or "refused". It failed in 2 of 3 fresh projects in this run (B and C).
verdict.area_hint: small chat-words fix area. The code comes from run L3's l3-chat-claims (HISTORY_ACTION_LEAD, CHAT_RETRIEVAL_RULES, the prompt lines; runC-plan.json run_L3), and d1109-chat-guard is the closest run C chat area
verdict.notes: The finding's suspected cause is half wrong. The marker was not copied from the history: in project C the turn had no history (model-calls.jsonl seq 12-13, messages length 1), so the system prompt was the only source. The history does repeat it in later turns, though. Seq 14's history shows the model's line and the app's line, both starting "The app did:". Hidden risk, not observed in this run: the claim guard (claims.ts) only catches first-person claims ("I've set…"). A model that writes "The app did: …" on a reply that changed nothing gets past the guard, and that line enters the history looking like the app's own line, which breaks the rule the prompt gives ("a reply without it changed nothing"). Fix 2 closes this. B's duplicate call was the model's choice: two parallel settings_set calls, one with project and one without, both resolving to the active project. The app answered the second as an is_error refusal, and nothing in the prompt says to keep tool mechanics out of the reply. The facts in both replies are true and the Undo row is right, so I agree with severity words. I did not run the stand-in bench: its role-player scripts the chat model and cannot show what Haiku chooses. The code and the recorded requests explain the finding. No leftover names it; LL-10 (English-only correction lines) is a different issue.

finding.title: The questions card quotes a scope-check line, not why the specialist asks
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'The specialist said: "The one commit is 'Workspace before 'Review the launch plan in notes/plan.md''."'
finding.expected: The report's lead reason: 'notes/plan.md does not exist, and I am not allowed to write review.md ...'
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/lr-look.json; l3b/steps/68-lr-inbox-card.png
finding.repro: New task, reviewer, 'Review the launch plan in notes/plan.md' (the file does not exist), outcome review.md; Start; open the Inbox.
finding.suspected_cause: specialistReason picks a sentence from the body of the report.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding's suspected cause names the wrong function. `specialistReason` (request-words.ts:213-220) only removes markdown and a findings tag. The sentence is picked earlier, when the card is filed, and stored on it. In the l3b store, human_request 01a1e8d7-298b… has change_card.context = "The one commit is \"Workspace before 'Review the launch plan in notes/plan.md'\"." with source "critic".

That value comes from `questionsReason(finalReport, questions)` (critic.ts:1076-1079 → person-questions.ts:382-401). It scores each report sentence only by the content words it shares with the first question, plus 1 for an "open" section and 1 for REASON_WORDS (:395). The question "Where is the launch plan? `notes/plan.md` is not in the project. Should it be created, or is it one of the existing `docs/` files?" gives the words {launch, plan, notes/plan.md, project, created, existing, docs}.

The Scope check bullet quotes the workspace commit message, and that message contains the task title, which the question repeats. So it shares launch, plan and notes/plan.md and scores 3. The report's lead sentence, "notes/plan.md does not exist, and I am not allowed to write review.md, so I could not produce the deliverable.", shares only notes/plan.md and scores 1. REASON_WORDS (:328-329) has no "does not exist", "not allowed" or "could not", so it gets no bonus. The blocker finding scores 2 ("missing").

I ran the base's own `reportedQuestions`, `questionsReason` and `specialistReason` (tsx at 4cf11fd) on the live report, word for word from event seq 13 of session 01a1e8d6-eae6…. They return exactly the quoted line, and a per-sentence trace gives the scores above. The model's report is well formed: the reason comes first, then the "Questions for the person:" list the brief asks for. The code chose the wrong sentence.

Live check 3's L3-research-3 had the same repro. That report's best sentence happened to be the blocker line, and l3-small fixed only its tag. Any report that quotes the task title (a commit message, a heading) can win this match again.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/person-questions.ts:382-401 (questionsReason; scoring at :395; REASON_WORDS :328-329; reportSentences :336-371), called from packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:1076-1079; quoted by packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:527-534
verdict.fix_sketch:
Three changes in `questionsReason` and its helpers, with no change to the card's words in request-words.ts:

(1) Do not count words inside a quoted span toward the match: double quotes, and single quotes only where they open after a space or the start and close before a space or punctuation. Apostrophes ("doesn't", "club's") must stay, or the L-12 Home page case breaks. A quoted commit message or task title says what the work is, not why it asks. With this alone the commit line scores 0, but the blocker bullet ("blocker, notes/plan.md: …", comma, so no tag is stripped) would win. So (1) is not enough by itself.

(2) Widen REASON_WORDS with does not exist / doesn't exist / not allowed / could not / couldn't / cannot / can't / not found / no such. Optionally reuse COULD_NOT from daemon/event-lines.ts:124-125.

(3) Give the report's lead sentence +1 when it says the work could not be done, as `couldNotWords` already does for the log line. On ties, keep the first sentence (the strict > at :396).

With (1) to (3), the live report quotes the lead sentence, and the L-12 contact and home cases and L3-research-3's report keep their quotes. Update the docs/maintainers/runtime.md paragraph at :1950-1960, which says where the quote comes from.

Also add a unit case: questionsReason(report, listedQuestions(report)) toBe that lead sentence. The existing L-12 cases (contact_page, home_page) must stay green.

This needs a small fix area for the questions card's reason, the follow-up to run L3's l3-small, which fixed L3-research-3 on the same card. verdict.notes:
