finding.title: New task gives the reviewer an outcome that needs a file it may not write, with no note
finding.what_the_person_sees: No note at New task. The run ends with 'I am not allowed to write review.md' and the review grade is 10.
finding.expected: A note at New task, or a specialist that can write the file.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/lr-run.json; the task-who note was null
finding.repro: Same as L4-l3-3.
finding.suspected_cause: The who-note does not check the outcome's files against what the specialist may write.

verdict.root_cause: ADR 0109 says a reviewer writes no file and its findings are its report. That rule exists only as prompt text: the reviewer's registry entry and the planner's delegation rule in project-manager.md. Nothing in code applies it when the person makes the task. (1) New task's who-note (NewTaskDialog.tsx:369-378) shows only two things: `runsOn` (where it runs on which credential) and `limitation`. The daemon (model-settings-view.ts:189-193) sets `limitation` only to NO_WEB_LIMITATION for specialists that need the web. So picking `reviewer` with the outcome 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md' shows nothing. The dialog already sends the typed words to the daemon (TR-11), but nothing compares them with the reviewer's write rule. (2) The app also builds a criterion the reviewer cannot meet. A task with no criteria gets outcomeCriterion() (verification.ts:65-70): 'The work itself shows this outcome (a file, a page or an output, not only the report): …'. The brief (executor.ts:1126-1128) and the critic (critic.ts:482-484) both use it, for every specialist, the reviewer included. The bench log shows the reviewer got exactly that criterion, while its own prompt says 'You write no file, not even a review file a brief names'. The reviewer did what it was told, and the critic graded against the app's criterion. So this is not the model's choice. One caveat on the evidence: in this run the 'could not do' and the grade of 10 come mostly from notes/plan.md being missing, which the check's repro set up on purpose. The missing write right is the second reason. Even with the plan present, this task could not pass its criterion.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/pages/project/NewTaskDialog.tsx:369-378; packages/runtime/src/daemon/model-settings-view.ts:189-193; packages/runtime/src/loop/verification.ts:65-70 (used at packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1126-1128 and packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:482-484); evals/registry/specialists/reviewer/specialist.md (the 'You write no file' paragraph)
verdict.fix_sketch: Daemon side, on the TR-11 words path of GET /settings/models: when a specialist's registry tools include no write tool (no cc:Write or cc:Edit; today that means the reviewer) and the typed outcome or criteria ask for a file (a path with an extension, or 'write/create … file'), return a note in the daemon's words. For example: 'The reviewer writes no file: its findings are its report, in the task's drawer. To have review.md written, choose the writer or Let the agent choose.' New task and Edit show it as task-who-note, the way the limitation note is shown today, and creating the task is not refused. Brief and critic side (ADR 0109 decision 1): for a specialist whose output is its report, outcomeCriterion should read 'The report shows this outcome: …' instead of '… not only the report'. That way a reviewer task the person makes with no criteria can pass on its findings. Update ADR 0109 (or add a note) and the maintainer docs for New task and verification.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/tasks.test.tsx (the person's boundary): open New task, choose 'reviewer', type the outcome 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md'. Expect task-who-note to say the reviewer writes no file and its findings are its report. With the outcome 'lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md', expect no note. Today the first case fails: task-who-note is null. Add a real-daemon case: GET /settings/models?project=…&outcome=review.md… returns the reviewer's note. Add a runtime executor-brief case: a reviewer task with no criteria gets no 'not only the report' criterion, and the critic's evidence carries the same criterion.
verdict.area_hint: No run C area covers this. It needs a small fix area for ADR 0109 on tasks the person makes (New task and Edit who-note, plus outcomeCriterion). The nearest existing area is l3-small, which owned L3-research-3.
verdict.notes: Evidence checked: lr-run.json and lr-look.json. In the bench database the task's specialist is 'reviewer', its outcome is 'review.md lists the gaps and risks found in notes/plan.md', and it has no criteria. In model-calls.jsonl the reviewer's brief has criterion 1 'The work itself shows this outcome (a file, a page or an output, not only the report): review.md …'. The reviewer's report says 'A review task that must produce review.md should go to a specialist allowed to write files.' The task check flagged the same thing but changed nothing. That is by design: the task was waiting for the person, and the task check's flagged lines are never shown to the person. The design doc §3.5 does not promise a who-note about write rights; ADR 0109 covered only the planner. So this is a gap in what the design covers, not a regression. I did not run the stand-in bench: the null note follows directly from the code, which has only the two note sources. Severity minor: it is cheap (CHF 0.04 here), the reviewer's report is honest about it, and the person was asked. The same thing would happen with a chat-made task or an Edit to reviewer.

finding.title: Just after the project budget is raised, Start says the paused task 'needs your answer', but there is no card
finding.what_the_person_sees: Ten seconds after raising the budget: 'Nothing can run: "Write the club motto in motto.txt" needs your answer.' with Open it, and no card in the Inbox. A minute later the task is Ready.
finding.expected: The task is ready at once, or the dialog says it goes on shortly.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/cm-run2.json; l3b/steps/83-cm-run2-start-dialog.png
finding.repro: Set project budget 0.06; a writer task pauses before its review; raise the budget to 0.50; open Start within 10 s.
finding.suspected_cause: The wake after the raise waits for the scheduler tick.

verdict.root_cause: Raising a limit does not wake the tasks paused at it. The only caller of `wakeBudgetWaits` is the scheduler's `refresh`, which runs before each tick (compose.ts:3963), and the tick comes every 30 s (`tickMs = 30_000`, session/triggers.ts:289). The `budget.set` run for a project only writes the project row (commands/budget.ts:362-368): it calls no wake and no prepare. Credentials are handled differently: `credentialSaved` wakes credential waits at once (compose.ts:4663). Until the next tick, the task stays `needs_human` and its budget_stop card stays open. The Start check's `needsYou` (server.ts:1606-1624) picks up that open card, and `startBlocked` (start-blocked.ts:185-190) then says 'Nothing can run: "X" needs your answer.' with Open it. The test suite expects this delay: budget-pause.test.ts:709 says 'The next tick wakes it' and calls `rt.scheduler.tick()` after the raise. The live state database confirms the timing. Raise applied at 09:32:57.486. Start dialog captured at 09:33:07.8, while the card was still open (the Overview in step 83 shows 'Needs you … paused at the project's budget of CHF 0.06 / Answer'). Tick at 09:33:16.822 withdrew the card (`outcome: went_on`) and set the task to ready. Inbox looked at 09:33:50, after the card was gone. So the delay is real, but the 'no card' part is a timing misreading: the card existed when the dialog named it, and the wait was 19 s, not 'a minute'. A second, smaller point: `needsYou` counts any open card on a `needs_human` task. A budget pause at an outer limit (only option: Cancel task; it 'goes on by itself once you raise that budget') is therefore read as 'needs your answer' even before any raise. The plan's comment meant only a pause that got no further, or a question.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:3963 (wake only in Scheduler refresh; tick 30 s at packages/runtime/src/session/triggers.ts:289); packages/commands/src/commands/budget.ts:362-368 (project budget write, no wake); packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:1606-1624 + daemon/start-blocked.ts:185-190 (sentence from the still-open card)
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) Move the `wakeBudgetWaitsDetailed` call out of the scheduler's refresh into one compose function, `wakeLimitWaits()` (it still calls `caps.forget` and prepares through `prepareWorkPort`). Expose it as a CommandPorts hook (e.g. `limitChanged?(scope, projectId)`). Call it from `budget.set`'s run for the project and month scopes (and from undoing a lowered limit) right after the write. Append `wokenLine(wentOn, prepared.result)` to the outcome sentence: 'Raised the project budget … to CHF 0.50. 1 paused task is ready again: it runs at your next Start.' This also closes C3L-3. Keep the tick call as the fallback for a new month. 2) Optional backstop: the `/projects/:id/start-check` route already awaits `refreshEstimates()`; have it await the same wake for its project first, so any write path that skips the command still gives a correct dialog. 3) Words, separately: do not count an outer-limit budget_stop card (no Continue offered) in `needsYou` as 'needs your answer'. Use the card's own sentence instead ('Nothing can run: "X" paused at the project's budget of CHF 0.06: raise it in Settings.'), with a link to Settings.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts, in the case 'a task paused at the project's budget goes on only once that budget changes': confirm `budget.set` through POST /commands/execute and /confirm, and do NOT call `rt.scheduler.tick()`. Then assert: (a) GET /projects/:id/start-check returns `blocked: null` with `runnable` naming "Members chart" (today: 'Nothing can run: "Members chart" needs your answer.'); (b) GET /inbox shows that task's card `withdrawn` with outcome '"Members chart" is ready again: its limit has room; it runs at your next Start.' (today: still open); (c) the confirm's sentence ends with '1 paused task is ready again: it runs at your next Start.' A UI case in real-daemon.test.ts: open the Start dialog right after the Settings raise; it reads 'This session runs "X"'.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-starts-engine
verdict.notes: No leftover names the delay. C3L-3 (words: Settings' change line after a budget raise does not say what follows) is the next-door symptom; `wokenLine` in budget-card.ts:634 is defined but never called, and the same fix closes it. Parts of the finding that are wrong: 'no card in the Inbox' (the card was open at 09:33:07 and withdrawn at 09:33:16.8; the Inbox was read at 09:33:50) and 'a minute later' (it was 19 s, and is at most 30 s). The suspected cause in the finding is correct. Evidence: the human_request and change_log rows in /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/home/data/state.sqlite (card 01a1e8d9-bde2…, applied_at 09:33:16.822; budget.set change 01a1e8da-370e…, 09:32:57.486) and the step file times of 82, 83 and 84. I did not run the stand-in bench: the code and the live timeline settle it, and the existing test asserts the tick-only wake.

finding.title: The run's start line ignores the project budget
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'This run may spend CHF 1.20: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.96 ...' under a project budget of CHF 0.06.
finding.expected: The line names the limit that actually applies.
finding.evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/cm-run1.json
finding.repro: Same as L4-l3-5, first Start.
finding.suspected_cause: The line uses the specialist's run limit.

verdict.root_cause: The run's start line comes from the run's own cap, and the project's budget and the month's cap are never part of that cap. executor.ts:1044 takes runCapOf(task, defaultSpec.maxBudgetUsdMicro). This task has no budget of its own, so that is the writer's per-run limit: USD 1.50 (evals/registry/specialists/writer-marketing/specialist.md:15), which is CHF 1.20. executor.ts:1071-1081 then takes the smaller of that and the session's work budget (CHF 5.00 x 0.8 = 4.00), so CHF 1.20 stays. runCapSource only knows task_budget, specialist_limit and session. executor.ts:1129 puts this figure into brief.budgetUsdMicro, and :1255 copies it into the run token's budgetUsdMicro. At the first model call, hooks.ts:160-166 calls SessionBudget.precheck(runId, claims.budgetUsdMicro, ...). budget.ts:247-252 fixes the wrap-up line from that cap with wrapUpLineOf: reserve 0.24, line 0.96. Only after that do hooks.ts:167-170 check the outer caps (caps.check: project, month, plan), and they only refuse a call; they never change the line. budget-pause.ts:358 then writes 'This run may spend CHF 1.20: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.96 ... reserve of CHF 0.24' while the project's budget is CHF 0.06. The evidence matches this exactly (cm-run1.json, all in one session): the session started with CHF 5.00, the writer's line said CHF 1.20, and the review then paused at 'the project's budget of CHF 0.06'. The wrong figure is more than a wording problem. The wrap-up line (0.96) sits far above the project's stop (0.06), so under a binding outer limit the run is never told to wrap up. It gets a hard stop instead ('its next step would have gone over'), and the line's promise of a reserve to finish is false. ADR 0112 point 6 says a stop names its real limit; the start line breaks that and points 3/4.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1129 (brief.budgetUsdMicro = min(work.capUsdMicro, sessionLeftUsdMicro), no outer cap; runCapSource at :1081); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:160-166 (the line is fixed from claims.budgetUsdMicro before caps.check at :167); packages/runtime/src/enforcement/budget.ts:247-252; packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:358 (the words)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. In LoopTaskExecutor.execute, beside sessionLeftUsdMicro (executor.ts:1071), read what the outer limits still allow for this run's scope, together with the level that binds (project or month; for plan share, its room). Use the stop line, not the 80% room that callRoomUsdMicro uses: for example a CapsPort.remainingUsdMicro(scope, phase) that returns { usdMicro, level }, or CapChecker.check's remaining and level.
2. Make brief.budgetUsdMicro the smaller of work.capUsdMicro, sessionLeftUsdMicro and that outer remainder. When the outer remainder is the smallest, set runCapSource to 'project' or 'month'. The token, the wrap-up line, the reserve and the stop sentence then all follow from one figure, and the run hears the wrap-up inside the project's budget.
3. Optionally let budgetLineWords name a limit that is not the run's own ('This run may spend CHF 0.06, what is left of the project's budget: ...'), as limitWords already does for stops.
4. Open point for the owner, as with BA-4: whether a run under a binding outer limit should keep room in it for its review. Today the review paused at the project's budget.
5. Update the fake daemon and ADR 0112 point 4/7, plus docs/maintainers/runtime.md.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed, through the runtime the daemon uses (packages/runtime/test/budget-pause.test.ts style, runOne). Setup: a session budget of USD 2-5, a project budget of USD 0.075 (CHF 0.06), and one writer or coder task with no budget of its own. The session log's 'This run may spend' line must name at most CHF 0.06, not the specialist's CHF 1.20 or the session's work budget. The wrap-up line and reserve must lie inside the project's budget. When the stand-in model keeps working, the run must hear the wrap-up (heardWrapUp) and pause as 'paused', not hit a hard stop with a budget_exceeded Run row. Mirror it in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts by reading the session's events through the client, next to the L3-run-10 case. Today the line reads 'This run may spend CHF 1.20: before a step that could take it past CHF 0.96 ...'.
verdict.area_hint: d1116-budget-all (owns the run-cap block in executor.ts: runCapSource, the brief's budget, the room passed to the start line; and budgetLineWords in budget-pause.ts)
verdict.notes: The code explains it without a bench run: the line is computed from caps and the first call's estimate, never from the model, and the live evidence (cm-run1.json) shows the CHF 1.20 line and the project's CHF 0.06 pause in the same session. No known leftover names it: LL-9 is about the Tasks row's 'left' figure and is closed for task budgets; C5L-C3-left-6 is chat's room; C3L-10 is chat's project-budget cap line. The run's figure is the writer's registry limit of USD 1.50 (CHF 1.20) because the session's work budget (CHF 4.00) is larger. The design's own figure for the line (ADR 0112 point 7) is min(own cap, session work budget), and the design never brought the outer limits into it. That is a gap, not an owner decision: point 6 says the stop names the limit that applies, and the start line then contradicts the stop it leads to. The existing tests cover only the run's own sources: budget-pause.test.ts:441, the session work budget at CHF 1.28, and the CHF 0.01 project-budget cases at :663 and :1957, which assert only the stop. Severity minor: a misleading figure, plus a missing graceful wrap-up under an outer limit. No money is lost, because the outer cap still stops the run.

finding.title: Session review words do not match what the session did
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Session review: accepted (grade 100, 0 findings).' beside '0 of 1 planned task done' in three sessions whose only task paused. 'Session review: sent back for changes (grade 85, 1 finding).' on a session whose task was done; the finding is an overrun note.
finding.expected: Words that say what waits, and never 'sent back' for a session.
finding.evidence: cm-run1.json, ph-run.json, rg-run2.json, swiss.json; Reviews › Session checks: '85 / 100 sent back ... over their estimate of CHF 0.07 by 51%, with one task tried twice'
finding.repro: A session whose only task pauses; a session whose task overruns its estimate.
finding.suspected_cause: Verdict 'revise' is mapped to 'sent back' except in the two cases L3-run-8 fixed.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding has two halves, and only the second one holds up.

(1) A session whose only task paused reads "accepted (grade 100, 0 findings)". This is by design, not a defect. Wave 7's R-sessreview (L7S-5) chose this on purpose:
- packages/critic/src/session-review.ts:449-466 (onlyPaused) records no finding for such a session.
- docs/maintainers/critic.md:431-436 says the same.
- budget-pause.test.ts:406-415 and event-lines.test.ts:425-427 assert it.
- Live check 3's own L3-run-8 entry named "Session review: accepted" for the paused case as the wording to copy.
The line also sits only under the session page's Details, below the log line '... paused before its review: ...'.

(2) "Sent back for changes" on a session whose only task was done is real. The session review reuses the task review's verdict words. Two lines of the code produce it:
- sessionChecks makes any medium finding blocking (session-review.ts:586, `isBlocking(findings) ? "revise"`).
- The overrun note is a medium finding (session-review.ts:417-423: "Planned tasks cost ..., over their estimate ... with one task tried twice").

So a done session that overran its estimate by more than 50% gets the verdict "revise", and two places turn that into "sent back":
- The session log: views.ts:876 prints `waits ?? verdictWords(verdict)`, where verdictWords("revise") is "sent back for changes" (event-lines.ts:421-422).
- The Reviews tab: ReviewItem shows verdictLabel(r.verdict) for session checks too (ReviewsTab.tsx:108, plain-words.ts:83-84: "sent back"). Its finding badge also says "to fix" (findingStateWords).

L3-run-8 replaced these words only for two cases (runner.ts:4379-4388, waitsFor answers or decision), and only in the log line. A session verdict sends nothing back: the runner and compose do nothing with "revise".

Reproduced by importing the code at 4cf11fd (/tmp/frbench/l4-l3-7/check.mts). One task done, tried twice, CHF 0.07 against a CHF 0.04 estimate:
- Result: verdict revise, grade 85, one medium finding "Planned tasks cost CHF 0.07, over their estimate of CHF 0.04 by 57%, with one task tried twice".
- describeEvent gives "Session review: sent back for changes (grade 85, 1 finding)."
- The paused-only case gives accept, 100, no findings, 0 of 1 planned done, as designed.

finding.title: A session whose only task the person stopped ends with the result 'CHF 0.01.' and nothing else
finding.what_the_person_sees: The session result is just 'CHF 0.01.'; the end counts show paused 0.
finding.expected: 'Stopped by you: "..." is paused. CHF 0.01.'
finding.evidence: Session 01a1e8fa-461d-74d7-b91c-0323cb1fb78a, summary 'CHF 0.01.' (l3b state.sqlite)
finding.repro: Redo a task, Start, then Stop it from its drawer.
finding.suspected_cause: A person's pause during the run is not counted in the end summary.

verdict.root_cause: When the person stops a running task from its drawer, the task becomes needs_human with reason 'Stopped by you'. recordMove (runner.ts:1477-1531) files it under needsHuman. At the end of the session the runner takes it out of needsYou on purpose (runner.ts:3825-3833, pausedByYou: "Paused by you" is not a decision, design §2). The outcome built at runner.ts:3853 has no other field that carries it: `paused` holds only budget-card pauses (pausedCards, :3838-3846), and `cancelled` (:3893, W15-59) holds only cancels. In result.ts, the RESULT_LINE_BUILDERS have a "cancelled by you" sentence (result.ts:360-377) but nothing for a task the person paused. So sessionResultLines returns only the money line. I confirmed this with tsx against the base: an outcome as the runner builds it gives ["CHF 0.01."], and the same outcome with `cancelled` set gives ['You cancelled "Write the club motto in motto.txt"; nothing else ran.', 'CHF 0.01.']. The stored session matches: summary 'CHF 0.01.'; handoff outcome {done:[], needsYou:[], ...} with moved_while_running by_person true; session.ended counts all 0 (needsHuman 0 and paused 0 are what the code is meant to do, since both lists leave out a person's pause). This is the pause sibling of W15-59, which fixed only the cancel case.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3829 (pausedByYou excluded from needsYouNow) and :3853-3910 (outcome has no field for it); packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:360-377 (only a 'cancelled by you' builder) and :65-68 (LastSessionOutcome has `cancelled` but no paused-by-you list)

Add a line-2 builder "paused by you" next to "cancelled by you": when nothing else happened, it says 'You paused "X"; nothing else ran.' (or 'Stopped by you: "X" is paused until you press Resume.'). Combine it with the cancel sentence when both apply. Add the sentence to NOT_NEWS (result.ts:662) so the Inbox Update and the notification stay quiet (design §5.11, the person's own click). (2) runner.ts: in the outcome, set `pausedByYou: uniq(needsHuman).filter((id) => pausedByYou(id) && movedWhileRunning.some((m) => m.taskId === id && m.byPerson)).map(named)`, only when the list is not empty. (3) session-list.ts sessionGist/countsWords: read it from the outcome, so the Sessions row says '"X" paused by you.' and not 'Nothing finished.'. Optionally count it in session.ended (a pausedByYou count, or in `paused`) with endedCounts in event-lines.ts. While there, fix the sibling at runner.ts:4008-4012: the docs/status.md note counts the person-paused task as needing you. finding.title: The Inbox posts the person's own chat changes as Updates
finding.what_the_person_sees: Updates: 'Set web pages research may read for Reading rules C from only developer.mozilla.org to any public website: ... Undo in Changes', one per change.
finding.expected: Section 5 rule 11: the person's own changes appear in Changes only.
finding.evidence: Inbox at 09:33 on l3b (cm-inbox)
finding.repro: Change the research rule in Chat, then open the Inbox.
finding.suspected_cause: Changes made through chat are posted as Updates.

verdict.root_cause: The code causes this, not the model. When the chat model calls a command tool, CommandLoop.commandToolSpecs builds that call's context with actor = the agent (packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324; the comment at :283 says it is logged as the agent's act). CommandExecutor.post (packages/commands/src/executor.ts:829-842) then decides whether to post an Inbox Update, using two checks. theirOwn is true only when the actor is the human. toldElsewhere is true only when source is 'session' or planFix is set. A change the person asked for in chat runs as actor agent, source chat, no planFix, so both checks are false and the change sentence goes into the Inbox as an 'info' message from the agent (shown as 'Alice'). The Yes path does the same: confirm() runs p.perform() with the stored context (actor agent), so a widening the person confirmed is also posted. The parser path (contextFor's default actor human) does not post, so only the model path, the normal one when a Claude key is set, breaks design §3.8 ('Never echoes of the person's own ... chat commands') and §5 rule 11. Reproduced on the stand-in bench (--provider bench, ports 49097/2697, stopped after). (1) Chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"only","only":["developer.mozilla.org"]}}' acts at once, and GET /inbox then holds 'Set web pages research may read for Reading rules W from any public website to only developer.mozilla.org: ... Undo.' from_agent_id = Alice. (2) Chat settings_set {mode:any} is read back; POST /commands/:id/confirm {answer:yes}; GET /inbox gets a second Update 'Set ... from only developer.mozilla.org to any public website ... Undo.' This matches the live l3b Inbox at 09:33 (six such Updates, one per chat change, across Reading rules, B and C). Leftover C6L-18 already names this. It says 'after a Yes', but the repro shows changes that act at once are echoed too. C6L-10 (chat-confirmed changes attributed to the agent) is the same actor issue.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/executor.ts:829 (theirOwn / toldElsewhere, Inbox post at :836-845); cause: packages/runtime/src/loop/commands.ts:324 (model tool calls run with actor agent)
verdict.fix_sketch: Make the Inbox rule follow whose words the change came from, not the actor that is used for policy. In CommandLoop.commandToolSpecs.ctxFor, keep actor agent (the policy and the limit-always-asks rule need it), but set a code-built context flag, e.g. ctx.onPersonsWords = true (never taken from a request or tool input). Carry it into the stored pending context (restorePending / the stored card), so a Yes after a restart keeps it. In executor.post, treat a change as the person's own when (actor is the human) OR (onPersonsWords && planFix === undefined && source !== 'session') && kind !== 'revert'. Then it stays in Changes and the chat reply, with no Inbox line. Agent-initiated changes (session task check, planFix, timed reverts, other people's shared-project lines) keep their current behaviour; the shared_with fan-out to other people should still run. Change the executor.test.ts:61-73 case 'A change the agent makes by itself is news' so its agent-made change uses a non-conversational source (or no onPersonsWords flag), not source voice. Do it together with C6L-10's attribution fix (a change the person named and confirmed in chat reads 'by you'): it is the same flag.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Real-daemon (or bench journey) test at the person's boundary, on the stand-in model. Create a project. POST /chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"only","only":["developer.mozilla.org"]}}', then expect GET /inbox messages to hold no Update with that sentence, while GET /changes lists it. Then POST /chat 'tool: settings_set {"key":"web_access","value":{"mode":"any"}}', confirm with POST /commands/:id/confirm {answer:"yes"}, and expect GET /inbox to still hold no new message. Control in the same test: a timed revert, or a session-sourced/planFix change, still posts its one Update. Commands-level twin: CommandLoop.tools(turn) execute of settings.set leaves store.message.inbox({humanId}) empty, before and after executor.confirm. All of these fail today (repro gave 1, then 2 Inbox messages).
verdict.area_hint: d1109-selftasks-chat
verdict.notes: Evidence: /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/l3b/steps/84-cm-inbox.txt (six 'Set web pages research may read ...' Updates from Alice) and /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/reading-rules-c-t2.json, -t3d.json (the chat turns that made them; t2 acted at once, t3d after Yes). Bench repro scripts and output: /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-l3-9/scripts/repro.cjs and repro2.cjs; bench verify-L4-l3-9 stopped. finding.title: Status pull request turned on for a Work-together project opens nothing, though Settings said it would
finding.what_the_person_sees: Settings: '... each session's status goes to the repository as one pull request ...'. The session log then says 'Created the project status in docs/status.md, kept in the app.', and no pull request appears.
finding.expected: Settings explains or refuses for a shared project.
finding.evidence: Docs note 'Kept in the app: you work on "Kite flyers" together, so GitHub's copy is left as it is.'; the sandbox had no open pull request after the session.
finding.repro: Work together on the sandbox; turn on Status pull request; run a session.
finding.suspected_cause: D9 keeps the status in the app, but the setting's read-back is generic.

verdict.root_cause:
D9 says a Work-together project writes nothing to the repository, and the status writer follows that rule. Settings does not know the rule, so it offers the switch and promises a pull request that never opens. At 4cf11fd:
(1) packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:968 runs `if (!statusPullRequestOn(project) || isTogether(project)) return this.statusInApp(project, update);`. A together project's status stays in the app "whatever the setting" (the comment at :964-967). The session log line "kept in the app" and the Docs note (repository-words.ts:226 togetherStatusNote) are correct.
(2) packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:315-323 shows the "Status pull request" row with its Change button whenever `onHostRepository(p)` is true. Nothing checks isTogether. The C-57 comment there already hides the row for a linked folder because "the switch would change nothing there". The same reasoning applies to a together project but was never applied. The row's description is also generic: "Each session's status of X as one pull request on GitHub".
(3) packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:405-418: the effect sentence for status_pull_request ignores the project and always says "each session's status goes to the repository as one pull request, docs: project status, which you merge when you like". target() at settings.ts:968-981 gives the effect only the project's name and session cap, never its settings.together. settings.set has no together refusal, so the same false read-back reaches Settings, chat and voice.
Result: the person turns the setting on, the change card promises a PR, and no PR opens. This breaks design section 5 rule 9 ("No promises the code does not keep") and run C's D9 decision ("words that promise only what exists"). The evidence matches the code: 08-kt-new-offer shows Work together on Kite flyers; 11-kt-statuspr-after shows the generic read-back; the status went to app-status/docs/status.md; the sandbox had no open PR.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:315 (row shown for a together project); packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts:414 (generic effect read-back; no together case in target() at :968); behaviour it contradicts: packages/runtime/src/loop/docs.ts:968
verdict.fix_sketch:
Make Settings follow D9 for a together project, at the command so chat and voice get it too.
(a) packages/commands/src/commands/settings.ts: in target() (or a status_pull_request hook), when the project is a together project (isTogether from @forerunner/runtime/sources/repository-words; commands already imports from that module in repo.ts and project-join.ts) and the value is true, refuse in one sentence with nothing written. Suggested wording: `You work on "Kite flyers" together with another Forerunner, so its status stays in the app (Docs, Status); no status pull request is opened.` Use details { key, cause: "together" }. Turning it off still acts.
(b) packages/runtime/src/daemon/settings-view.ts:315: show the row only when `onHostRepository(p) && !isTogether(p)`. The other option is a read-only row that reads "Kept in the app: you work on X together" with no Change button.
(c) Mirror both in apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts (about line 6974).
(d) Note the rule in the maintainer doc for settings/docs and in the user guide's "Working with someone on one repository" section.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Extend the composed two-home case in packages/runtime/test/onerepo-together.test.ts (or add a real-daemon case under 'd1109-onerepo-link, run C' in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts). After home B presses Work together on o/kite, check two things through the HTTP API:
(1) GET /settings on B has no row with key 'project.status_pull_request' and scopeId kiteId, or that row says the status is kept in the app and offers no change.
(2) POST /commands settings.set {key:'status_pull_request', value:true, project:kiteId} answers a refusal naming the together reason, B's change log gains no row, and the project's settings.status_pull_request is unchanged.
Today (1) lists the row with the generic description, and (2) answers a change card with the effect "each session's status goes to the repository as one pull request…". Add a UI test (SettingsPage with the fake daemon's together project) asserting there is no "Status pull request" Change button.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-onerepo-link
verdict.notes: Checked against the code; I did not reproduce it on the stand-in bench, because the code paths settle it. The existing together test (onerepo-together.test.ts:160-185) writes status_pull_request:true straight into the row and checks only the Docs note, so the Settings path was never covered. No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names it. C4L-1 (Work together for a project already here) and C4L-5 (a closing project's fr/status after a join) are different problems. The model played no part: the change card and row come from fixed code. Minor is the right severity: it is a promise the code does not keep, but the session log and the Docs note tell the truth afterwards, and no data is lost and nothing is written to GitHub.

finding.title: Merge pressed ~1 s after a push answers 'Merging #62.', then refuses 4 s later
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Merging #62.' then the row reads '#62 changed after the review ...'. Nothing is merged.
finding.expected: The red line at once.
finding.evidence: g3-pushC-pressC.json: press answer 1032 ms {state: queued}
finding.repro: With the Overview open, push a commit to an accepted PR's branch, then press Merge within ~1 s.
finding.suspected_cause: GitHub's pull list was probably stale ~1 s after the push. A press at normal person speed was not retested.

verdict.root_cause: The press checks for a moved head before it answers, but it compares the reviewed commit only with the head that GitHub's pull-request endpoints report. GitHub updates a pull request's head.sha in the background after a push, so for a moment after the push those endpoints still show the old head. The branch ref itself moves as soon as the push returns. On a pull request whose task builds on nothing gone, the press's only head check is pull-requests.ts:751-760. It reads `listed.find(...).head.sha` from the GET /pulls?state=open it just made (read() -> readView, pull-requests.ts:335). When that head equals reviewed_head_sha it does `continue` at line 757 and never calls headMovedNow. If the listing did have the new head, headMovedNow reads getPullRequest again (merge.ts:2094-2100, `moved = now?.head.sha || head`), which can be just as stale, and then returns null. Either way the press goes on to approveInOrder and answers {state: "queued", "Merging #62."}. The background merge step reads getPullRequest again (merge.ts:363/378). By then GitHub has the new head, so it settles the record head_moved and the row shows the red line. Nowhere does the press read the branch ref (host.getBranchHead, already in the GitHost port). Timeline from the evidence: push 200 at 09:53:01.691Z. The press was clicked straight after it returned (press.cjs clicks right after act()); the ~1 s in the finding is how long the answer took, not the gap. The answer came at about 09:53:02.72. The daemon log has 'merge record ... left_to_you head_moved' at 09:53:04.256Z, and the screenshot taken just after the answer already shows '#62 is not merged yet: the row below says why.' So the refusal came about 1.5 s after the answer, not 4 s. Nothing wrong can merge: the final PUT pins sha (merge.ts:550). The harm is one contradicting answer.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/pull-requests.ts:751-760 (head check on the listing's head.sha, skip at 757); packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:2094-2100 (headMovedNow re-reads getPullRequest, which lags the same way)
verdict.fix_sketch: Judge the press against the branch ref, which the push itself moves at once, not against the pull request's head as GitHub reports it. In ProjectPullRequests.merge (pull-requests.ts:751-760), for each chain task with a reviewed_head_sha, read `host.getBranchHead(ref, listedPr.head.ref)`. Take that head when it differs from the listing's head.sha, and call headMovedNow whenever either one differs from the reviewed commit. In headMovedNow (merge.ts:2094-2100), do not let a getPullRequest head equal to the reviewed commit override a newer head passed in from the branch read. Use the branch head when it is not the reviewed one, so that keepsOwnChange (GitHub's Update branch) and the rebuilt-by-Forerunner case still decide as they do today. This costs one extra GET per chain task per press. Leave the merge step's sha-pinned PUT as it is.
verdict.failing_test_idea: In packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts (chainWorld), plus a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts: give the fake git host a 'pull head lag' option, so a push moves refs/heads/<branch> at once but the pull request's head.sha keeps the old commit until a later read or clock tick. Today syncPullsForBranch in testenv/src/githost/ops.ts:296 updates it in the same step as the push, which is why the existing 'L3-github-3: Merge pressed...' case passes at the base. Run a task to accepted, push a commit to its branch with the lag on, then at once press Merge through POST /projects/:id/pull-requests/:n/merge, as the Overview's Merge does. Expect {state: 'refused', sentence: '#N changed after the review: look at the new commits, ...'}, nothing merged, the record left_to_you/head_moved and one card. At the base it answers {state: 'queued', sentence: 'Merging #N.'} and refuses afterwards.
verdict.area_hint: l3-merge (run L3's merge area, which owned L3-github-3 and the press-time head check; no run C d1109-* area owns merge)
verdict.notes: This does not reproduce on the stand-in bench: FakeGitHost moves a pull request's head in the same step as the push, and the existing L3-github-3 unit case passes at 4cf11fd (run under flock). The code still explains the live result: the press trusts only pull-request heads, which lag a push on real GitHub. Corrections to the finding: the press came milliseconds after the push's 200, not about 1 s after (1032 ms was the answer's latency), and the row turned red about 1.5 s after the answer (log at 09:53:04.256Z; the screenshot just after the answer already shows it), not 4 s. A person who pushes and then comes to the app will rarely be this fast, and nothing can be merged by mistake (the merge PUT pins the sha), so it stays minor: it is a race at machine speed and the cost is one contradicting answer. LL-2 in leftovers-L3.json is a sibling (a check failed or the PR stopped merging cleanly after the last look, and the press still says 'Merging #N.' first). It assumes head moves are already said at once, so it does not name this case.

finding.title: The head-moved card cuts the task title
finding.what_the_person_sees: '"Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to…" changed after the review'
finding.expected: The whole title.
finding.evidence: g3-inbox.json, inboxwatch-*.json
finding.repro: A 55-character title ending in '"Seal Bay"'; push a commit; press Merge.
finding.suspected_cause: q() avoids cutting inside the quotes by cutting before them.

verdict.root_cause: The finding is real, and the code explains it exactly. L3-github-9 added a rule to balancedCut that keeps a title whole when it is at most 15 characters over the limit. That rule only fires when the cut part leaves a quote open (quoted-title.ts:21-22). The task title 'Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to "Seal Bay"' is 55 characters. cutWords(t, 50) (request-words.ts:242-248) cuts at the last space inside the first 49 characters, which is the space just before the opening quote. The kept part 'Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to' has no quotes at all, so the quote count is even. balancedCut returns the cut at line 21 and never reaches the slack rule on line 22. q() (request-words.ts:251), used by leftOpenCardTitle for head_moved (request-words.ts:1303), therefore shows '"Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to…" changed after the review'. The Answered list shows the same card title. The finding's suspected cause is close but a little off: balancedCut does not move the cut before the quote. The plain word cut happens to land there, and balancedCut does not notice that the quoted part was dropped. I reproduced this with the source's balancedCut and a verbatim copy of cutWords (/tmp/frbench/v-L4-l3-12/repro.mts). It is inconsistent with L3-github-9's own intent ('a short overrun keeps the title whole'): 'Link trips page from kite/index.html as "Our trips"' (51 characters) and 'Write kite/ferry.txt about a ferry trip to "Seal Bay"' (53) are both kept whole, but the 55-character 'the ferry trip to "Seal Bay"' version loses its whole quoted name. Whether the title is kept whole depends only on where the word cut lands.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/quoted-title.ts:21 (balancedCut returns early when the kept part has no quotes, even though the title has quoted words after the cut); called through q() at packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:251 from leftOpenCardTitle at request-words.ts:1303
verdict.fix_sketch: In balancedCut, check for a dropped quoted part before the early return. If the full title has a quote of its own that the cut removed or left open (t.slice(kept.length).includes('"'), or kept has an odd number of quotes) and t.length <= max + slack, return t whole. Otherwise keep today's behaviour: cut before the open quote, or drop the marks when the title starts with its quote. Callers that pass slack 0 (notifications, the 'will be stuck' consequences) do not change. Card titles are computed when the card is read (leftOpenCardTitle via request-words and state-ports.ts:298), so cards already open read correctly after the fix. Extend the L3-github-9 test in packages/runtime/test/l3-merge.test.ts with the ferry title and the 53-character variant.
verdict.failing_test_idea: At the boundary the person uses: in dependent-branches-merge.test.ts, following the existing L3-github-3 case (Merge pressed after a commit is pushed on the fake host), name the task 'Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to "Seal Bay"', press Merge, and read GET /requests. Expect the head-moved card's title to be '"Write kite/ferry.txt about the ferry trip to "Seal Bay"" changed after the review'. It fails today with '…trip to…". A unit test beside it: leftOpenCardTitle({status:"head_moved"}, that title) gives the whole title. A 70-character title with a quote should still cut before its quote.
verdict.area_hint: l3-merge (run L3's area that wrote quoted-title.ts for L3-github-9; small words fix in packages/runtime/src/daemon/quoted-title.ts)
verdict.notes: Evidence matches: g3-inbox.json and both inboxwatch-*.json show the cut title, both in the card heading and in the Answered list. The same card's 'Task:' line and the Updates line show the whole title, so the person can still read it one line up. That is why I agree with severity 'words', not minor. No leftover in leftovers-{L3,C2,C3,C4,C4b-design,C4b,C5,C6}.json names this, and the owner decisions of 2026-11-09 say nothing about cutting titles. finding.title: The rebuild card's Merge after a merge on GitHub says 'Merged #59.'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Done: Merged #59.' / Answered 'Merged #59.'
finding.expected: '#59 was merged on GitHub already.'
finding.evidence: g2-step5-card-merge.json; daemon log 09:54:54 'merge record ... merged', then 'pull request merged on the host'
finding.repro: Merge the PR on GitHub, then press the card's Merge at once.
finding.suspected_cause: The answer treats the record's 'merged' state as the app's own merge.

verdict.root_cause:
The press's own merge step was the first part of Forerunner to see the merge GitHub had made, about 3 s earlier, before any watcher poll. Two parts of the code then treat it as Forerunner's own merge:
- At packages/runtime/src/session/pr-answers.ts:320, applyRebuildMerge's mergedAlready() check comes back null. The record is not 'merged' yet, so the press goes to approveInOrder/mergeApproved.
- In packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts, mergeChecked (:362-369) sees pr.merged and returns status 'closed' with alreadyMerged=true. ReviewedPrMerge.finish (:1818-1846) then folds that into a normal merge. The record goes to 'merged' with last_outcome 'merged', not 'merged_on_host', and method null. The returned MergeOutcome is status:'merged' with no already-merged flag; only the task reason says 'already merged on the host'.

pr-answers.ts:328-329 maps last.status==='merged' to merge_result 'merged'. request-words.ts:1352-1353 shows that as 'Merged #59.', and the Inbox shows it as 'Done: Merged #59.'. ADR 0111 point 3 says this press must read '#42 was merged on GitHub already.'.

The live log matches this path. At 09:54:54.169 the press's merge step logged 'merge record … merged', then '[compose] pull request merged' with method:null (method is null only on the alreadyMerged branch). The watcher's 'pull request merged on the host' came 0.5 s later.

I reproduced it on the stand-in: a copy of the L3-github-2 test, run under flock with merge on the fake GitHub first, then syncPrAnswers, and no poll in between. It answers 'Merged #2.' and the record reads merged/last_outcome merged/method null. The existing test passes only because it runs m.poll() before syncPrAnswers, so the watcher reads the merge first.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/loop/merge.ts:1818 (finish folds alreadyMerged into status 'merged', last_outcome 'merged'); packages/runtime/src/session/pr-answers.ts:328 (status 'merged' -> merge_result 'merged'); packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:1352 ('Merged #N.')
verdict.fix_sketch: In ReviewedPrMerge.finish (merge.ts:1818), when a.alreadyMerged is set and a.status is not 'merged', write last_outcome 'merged_on_host'. dependent-branches.mergedOnHost already writes that value. Also carry the fact on the outcome: add MergeOutcome.alreadyMerged (ports.ts:581), or set its sentence to '#N was merged on GitHub already.'. Then in applyRebuildMerge (pr-answers.ts:327-333), call mergedAlready(store, task) before mapping status 'merged' to 'merged', or look at last.alreadyMerged first. A merge found already made then reads '#N was merged on GitHub already.', and only Forerunner's own merge reads 'Merged #N.'. Separately, think about making mergedOnHost's early return (dependent-branches.ts:211) re-read the record after mergeMethodOf. In the live log, merge.merged was heard twice for #59 because the watcher read the record before finish moved it.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add to packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts, next to the existing L3-github-2 test at :2794: chainWorld level 2; run A, then B, which depends on A; close A; poll, so the rebuild card is open. Answer the card's Merge, then m.github.mergePullRequest(REPO, prB) with NO m.poll(), then syncPrAnswers({ …, merge: m.merge }). Expect answeredLine(m, row.id) to be `#${prB} was merged on GitHub already.` and the merge record's last_outcome to be 'merged_on_host'. Today it reads 'Merged #2.' and the record has last_outcome 'merged' (reproduced at 4cf11fd). At the UI boundary, a real-daemon case can check that the Inbox Answered line, and the 'Done:' line, of a rebuild card pressed right after a merge on GitHub do not read 'Merged #N.'.
verdict.area_hint: l3-merge (run L3's merge area, which built L3-github-2 in pr-answers.ts, merge.ts and dependent-branches.ts); no run C d1109 area owns this code, so a small fix area such as live4-merge-words
verdict.notes:
The claim holds, and the suspected cause is almost right. The card does not read the record's 'merged' state. It reads the press's own merge outcome, whose status is 'merged', and the merge step writes the record as its own merge (last_outcome 'merged'). So even mergedAlready() would say '#59 was merged already.' instead of '… on GitHub already.'.

No known leftover names this. LL-1 to LL-6 in leftovers-L3.json cover nearby merge cases: a close on GitHub, a failed check after the last look, B merged on GitHub while it still holds A. The owner decisions of 2026-11-09 say nothing on this wording.

Side observation, not part of this finding: two parts each moved the record to merged, the watcher's pullRequestState/mergedOnHost and the press's finish, so '[compose] pull request merged' was logged twice for #59. The record ended with method 'merge' and last_outcome 'merged_on_host' from the watcher's later write.

The scratch repro is /tmp/frbench/v-L4-l3-13/repro.test.ts with vitest.config.mjs. Nothing was changed in the worktree; the scratch node_modules symlinks are removed.

finding.title: Card items are still cut mid-phrase with '…'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Left to do: '... plus a short introduction. Put…'. A failed card reads '... (the git status check below shows… "Write kite/club-day.txt ..." waits on it.'
finding.expected: No cut inside an item.
finding.evidence: l3b/steps/117-rg-card.png; g1-inbox.json
finding.repro: A writer task 'Write a 3,000-word guide to the club in guide.md' with Budget 0.15.
finding.suspected_cause: Items are clipped at a fixed length.

verdict.root_cause:
The two cuts have different causes in the code, and both reproduce.

(1) Budget card, "Left to do". parseHandoff caps every item at 200 characters with `cut` (budget-pause.ts:146 and :207, MAX_ITEM_CHARS=200 at :57). `cut` breaks inside a word. The live state shows this: card.left[0] in l3b's state.sqlite is exactly 200 characters and ends in "... plus a short introduction. Put cl…". The display step, cardItem (request-words.ts:227-238, called from pausedWorkLists :985), sees the stored "…", drops the broken word and keeps the ellipsis, so the person reads "Put…". cardItem also cuts at 220 with cutWords, so a long item never shows whole. The comment on budget-card.ts:170-176 and runtime.md:2453 say "each item whole", but the 200-character bound on the parsed handoff is still there. The wrap-up words (loop.ts:109, budget-pause.ts:53) never ask the model to keep items short, so a long item from the model is expected, not a model fault. The same cut item also goes into the continuation brief (task-context.ts:163, quote(t, 200)), so the next run loses the end of its own next step.

(2) Failed-task card, "It reported: ...". emptyChangeSummary (pr-executor.ts:612-624) takes the report's first sentence and cuts it at a word past 160 characters. Its sentence split, /(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=["'(\p{Lu}])/u, does not split after a full stop followed by a closing quote: in `Sundays." I rewrote` the character before the space is `"`. So the "first sentence" runs on to "...(the git status check below shows whether anything actually changed)." That is over 160 characters, so it is cut to "(the git status check below shows…", which also leaves a parenthesis open. With a correct split the first sentence is 'Summary: kite/club.txt already existed with one line, "The kite club meets on Sundays."' (about 85 characters), which fits whole.

Reproduced with tsx on the 4cf11fd source (/tmp/frbench/v-L4-l3-14/repro/repro.ts): parseHandoff and then requestWords give exactly "... plus a short introduction. Put…", and emptyChangeSummary on the run's real report (l3a run 01a1e8e3-234b-…) gives exactly "...(the git status check below shows…".
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-pause.ts:146,207 (cut at MAX_ITEM_CHARS=200, :57); packages/runtime/src/daemon/request-words.ts:227-238 (cardItem keeps the stored '…', cuts at 220), :985; packages/capabilities/src/githost/pr-executor.ts:615-622 (emptyChangeSummary: sentence split misses a closing quote after the stop; 160-character cut)
verdict.fix_sketch:
(a) parseHandoff should keep each item whole up to a generous limit (for example 1000 characters, the same order as the note's 600). If an item is still too long, end it at its last whole sentence, never inside a word. Keep the whole item in the handoff, so the continuation brief (task-context.ts:163, raise quote 200 to match) gets it too.
(b) cardItem for "Left to do" items should show the item whole when it is up to about 400 characters. Above that, end at the last whole sentence that fits, using the same sentence rule as firstSentences, and add "…" only when a single first sentence is itself too long. Cards stored before the fix still go through the existing drop-the-broken-word path.
(c) In emptyChangeSummary, let the split accept a closing quote or bracket after the stop: (?<=[.!?]["'”’)\]]?)\s+(?=["'(\p{Lu}]). When the line must still be cut, cut at a clause and close any open parenthesis, or use balancedCut as titles do, so the card never shows "(… shows…". Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md (the budget card words) and the capabilities doc to match.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
Real-daemon, next to apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts:9328 (the budget pause case). A stand-in run hears the wrap-up and ends its report with "Left to do:\n1. Check the unread docs files for club facts. Then write `guide.md` in sections, each about 500 words: History, Meetings, Rules, Tournaments, Membership and Etiquette, plus a short introduction. Put club-specific facts in clearly marked placeholders.\n2. Run `wc -w guide.md` ...". The test asserts that GET /requests' card lists[1].items[0] contains no "…" and ends with "placeholders." (the item whole, without markdown), and that the continuation brief quotes the same whole item.

For the failed card, a second case: a coder run that changes no file and whose report starts with '**Summary**: `kite/club.txt` already existed with one line, "The kite club meets on Sundays." I rewrote it with the same content (the `git status` check below shows whether anything actually changed). ...'. The card body must equal 'What failed: The run changed no file. It reported: Summary: kite/club.txt already existed with one line, "The kite club meets on Sundays."' with no "…" and no unclosed "(". Both cases fail at 4cf11fd.
verdict.area_hint: small words fix area (card cuts): budget card lists are d1109-oversize-pause's code (budget-pause.ts parseHandoff, request-words.ts cardItem/pausedWorkLists); the failed card's quote is pr-executor.ts emptyChangeSummary (w15-words lineage)
verdict.notes:
The finding's suspected cause, "items clipped at a fixed length", is right for both cards, but the two cards have separate cuts. On the budget card, the 200-character cut happens when the handoff is stored, before any display. The display then turns "Put cl…" into "Put…". On the failed card, a sentence-split bug makes the 160-character cut hit the second sentence; with a correct split nothing would be cut. A cut at a word with "…" is otherwise a designed pattern for quoted reports (design section 5 rule 1: card body ≤ 2 sentences), so the fix for the failed card is the split and the open parenthesis, not "never cut". The "Left to do" list is promised whole (RequestListWords: "each whole"; runtime.md:2453), so there "no cut inside an item" is the right expectation.

No leftover in L3/C2/C3/C4/C4b-design/C4b/C5/C6 names this. CL-11 is about recall answers cut at 160 characters, which is unrelated.

Evidence checked: l3b/steps/117-rg-card.png and .txt; l3b state.sqlite human_request 01a1e8f6-d22f-73ea-8e11-24708c48723e (left[0].length == 200, ends "Put cl…"); l3a state.sqlite human_request 01a1e8e3-48b7-759a-b5c0-ff8a3d4375b9 and run 01a1e8e3-234b-7224-a206-7a69033c3fa1 (the full report).

Also noticed, out of scope: the failed card keeps the report's "Summary:" label ("It reported: Summary: ...").

Copies of the state databases and the repro are in /tmp/frbench/v-L4-l3-14/. No bench or server was started.

finding.title: A step cut off at max_tokens is paid for and lost, with no line in the log
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'read README.md', then 'Told the writer to wrap up: it spent CHF 0.06 ...'; the card says 'No files created or changed.' CHF 0.08 spent, nothing written, no reason given.
finding.expected: A line saying the step was cut, and the writer told to write in parts.
finding.evidence: Model-call log seq 33: max_tokens 6308, stopReason max_tokens, USD 0.065244, no tool call
finding.repro: Same as L4-l3-14.
finding.suspected_cause: The budget caps max_tokens, and a one-call write of a long file is truncated.

verdict.root_cause:
The evidence checks out (l3b/home/bench/model-calls.jsonl, run 01a1e8f5-d110, the second seq 33 in the file): max_tokens 6308, stop max_tokens, 6308 output tokens, USD 0.065244, no text and no tool call. The session's own events (state.sqlite, session 01a1e8f5-d08b) go from 'read README.md' (seq 11) straight to 'Told the writer to wrap up' (seq 12). The code explains each part.

(1) The cap comes from the budget, as designed (W15-13). A file-writing run's call may use only the money below the run's wrap-up line (loop.ts:640-659: room = line - spent - searches, then fitMaxTokens). Line CHF 0.06 minus USD 0.0075 already spent gives 6308 tokens, and that one reply used all of the money below the line.

(2) The cut reply had nothing it could keep, so the loop asks again (loop.ts:910-947). The retry's cap cannot be raised, because no money is left below the line. loop.ts:647-649 checks `!wrapUpSent` before beforeModelCall decides on the wrap-up, so the reserve never pays for the retry and seq 34 gets the 4096 floor. The same request carries both the cut note and 'Wrap up now'. Because the reply showed no blocks, `where` is 'before it said anything' (loop.ts:920). That picks 'Answer again, more briefly.' (loop.ts:1335-1336), not the 'one file per call, short enough to fit' wording. Two different causes look the same here, and the log cannot tell them apart: hidden thinking (call-log.ts:302-330 does not record thinking_delta), or a write_file whose tool_use_end never came (collectStream drops it, types.ts:457).

(3) No log line. The loop reports the cut only as a bare `warning` RunEvent (loop.ts:943-946). The executor's onEvent (executor.ts:1442-1520) turns budget_line, web_search*, wrap_up_sent, model_call_end and tool events into steps, but has no branch for `warning`. compose.ts:3624 ignores it too. The person sees no line, and the CHF 0.05 call shows up only as spend (runner.ts:2728). The budget pause card is built from the handoff alone ('No files created or changed'), so it never gives the reason. The only mention is in the model's own report ('My previous attempt hit the output limit and produced nothing'), which the card does not show. This breaks design §3.7 and §4.14 ('Each model and tool call ... emits one step line').

Paying for a cut reply and not using it is by design (U-085: 'Every call is billed, the cut ones included'). The model's choice to spend 6308 tokens in one reply is its own. But the missing line and the wrong-variant note are app behaviour, so this is not the model alone.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1442-1520 (onEvent has no branch for the loop's cut-off warning); packages/runtime/src/agent/loop.ts:937-947 (cut reported only as a bare `warning`), :1331-1338 (cutOffNote 'Answer again, more briefly'), :640-659 (cap = money below the line)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. loop.ts, cut branch (:910-948): emit a typed RunEvent such as `reply_cut` {maxOut, where, kept, costUsdMicro, specialist} instead of the bare warning. The current warning also claims 'asking again with up to 25232', a cap the next call never asked, so fix that too.
2. executor.ts onEvent: map `reply_cut` to a step note in person words, for example: 'The writer's reply was cut off at its length limit and could not be used (CHF 0.05); it was asked to send less in one reply.' Keep it to one log line (§5.1).
3. cutOffNote: in a file-writing run, 'before it said anything' should get the 'one file per call, short enough to fit' wording, with the limit in words. A hidden thinking block and an unclosed write_file both reach this branch.
4. budget-card / handoff: when the run's last cut kept nothing, add one clause to the card ('its last reply was cut off at its length limit, so nothing was written').
5. For the owner or ADR 0112 (a design question, not a must): when the retry after a cut lands in the same request as the wrap-up, let the reserve pay the retry's raised cap. The `!wrapUpSent` check at :647-649 runs before the wrap-up decision. Or say the per-reply output limit in a file-writing brief. Note that the writer's write_file only overwrites a whole file, so 'write one file in parts' is not really possible with today's tools.
6. testenv call-log.ts: record the thinking length (and any started but unfinished tool call), so a cut reply's content can be read in evidence.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
A composed real-daemon test with the Messages API stand-in (or a scripted provider through runner and executor). A writer task with budget CHF 0.15 and write_file offered. Call 1: list_dir. Call 2: stop_reason max_tokens with no blocks and output_tokens equal to the call's max_tokens. Call 3: a report with 'Where I stopped:' and 'Left to do:'. Assert three things:
(a) GET /sessions/:id/events (the Session page log) has a task.step line between 'looked at the folder' and the wrap-up line that says the reply was cut off at its length limit and could not be used, with its CHF. This fails today: no such event.
(b) The request after the cut tells a file-writing run 'one file per call, short enough to fit', not 'Answer again, more briefly'. This fails today.
(c) The budget pause card or the result names the cut.
To walk it on the bench, the stand-in needs a way to play a max_tokens reply first: role-player.ts:440-446 never returns max_tokens, so it cannot reproduce on the bench today.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-oversize-pause (a large task does as much as it can and pauses cleanly), or a small runtime fix area: agent/loop.ts cut-off event and note, plus session/executor.ts step line
verdict.notes:
I checked the evidence against l3b's model-call log and state.sqlite (bench-live, real model, pass 2). The cut call's cap of 6308 tokens matches the money below the wrap-up line: USD 0.065244 actual, against roughly USD 0.067 of room. After seq 33 the run had spent CHF 0.06 of its CHF 0.13, so the wrap-up came at once. The run ended at CHF 0.068 of 0.13, so about half the reserve was never used.

The app did tell the model about the cut, in the seq 34 request: 'Your last reply was cut off at the output limit (6308 tokens) before it said anything, and nothing of it was used. Answer again, more briefly.' That came together with the wrap-up text. So the 'writer told' half of the expected outcome partly happens. What is missing is the person-facing line, and the wording for a file-writing run.

I could not reproduce this on the stand-in: neither the role-player nor the Messages API stand-in can produce a max_tokens stop. No bench, tests or edits were run; this verdict comes from reading the code and the evidence.

No leftover in L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5 or C6 names this. C5L-L3-left-14 is about booking a Stop-now cut call on the right billing source, which is a different issue.

finding.title: 'paused at its budget of CHF 0.15' when only CHF 0.08 was spent and only the review waits
finding.what_the_person_sees: The card title, notification and result all read '... paused at its budget of CHF 0.15'. The body says 'The work is done; its review waits for room in the budget.'
finding.expected: A title that says the review is waiting for budget room.
finding.evidence: ph-run.json, ph-inbox.json
finding.repro: A researcher task with Budget 0.15 that finishes at about CHF 0.08.
finding.suspected_cause: The review-room pause reuses the at-budget title.

verdict.root_cause:
When the critic's review does not fit the task's own budget, the pause reuses the generic at-limit title. runner.ts:3189-3198 builds the review-pause BudgetStop with `stoppedBy: "budget"` hard-coded and calls `budgetStopTitle(now, stop, rate)` (runner.ts:3199). budgetStopTitle (budget-card.ts:125-158) has only two families of title: "paused before … ran out" (stoppedBy wrap_up) and "paused at …". It has no form for "the work is done and only its review waits", so it returns `"X" paused at its budget of ${cap}` (budget-card.ts:148). That one string becomes:
- the task's reason (runner.ts:3204),
- the card's `why` and `title` (budget-card.ts:261, 270),
- the notification title, cut to '"Search MDN…" paused at its budget of CHF 0.15'.

The session result and the session page row go the same way on purpose. runner.ts:3876 sets `before` only when `stopped_by === "wrap_up" && review_waits !== true`, so result.ts:603 `pausedSentences` writes `paused at its budget of CHF 0.15: continue or cancel it in the Inbox.`, and task-words.ts:409 `budgetPauseLabelOf` falls back to "Paused at its budget". Only three places got a review-waits wording: the card body (request-words.ts:996-997), the drawer/row detail (task-words.ts:430) and the log line `reviewPausedWords` (budget-pause.ts:282-293, '… paused before its review: its own budget of CHF 0.15 has no room for it.'). So the headline says the budget was reached while the body, the log and the CHF 0.08 figure say the work finished with CHF 0.07 left.

The base pins this behaviour. task-budget-all.test.ts:527 asserts the reason '"Write the footer" paused at its budget of CHF 0.06.', and :534 asserts the same text as the card title, with only CHF 0.01 spent. I ran that test at 4cf11fd under the lock and it passes. Live check 3's L3-research-2 found the same mismatch ('paused at its budget of CHF 0.15' beside 'it spent CHF 0.09'). Its fix covered only the wrap-up stop and left the review-room pause out.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/budget-card.ts:148 (budgetStopTitle has no review-waits form); packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3189-3199 (review-pause stop with stoppedBy "budget" then budgetStopTitle); packages/runtime/src/session/runner.ts:3876 + packages/runtime/src/session/result.ts:603 (session result 'paused at …'); packages/runtime/src/daemon/task-words.ts:409-421 (row label)
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Give budgetStopTitle a review-waits form, either as a `reviewWaits` argument or as a stop with `stoppedBy: "review"`. It names the limit the way reviewPausedWords does, one wording per source, for example:
   - task_budget: '"X" is done; its review waits for room in its budget'
   - session: '… in this session's budget'
   - project: '… in the project's budget'
   - month: '… under this month's cap'
   - plan: '… in the share of your Claude subscription'
   It must keep the 60-character notification title once the task title is cut.
2. At runner.ts:3199, pass the review-waits form so the task reason, the card's why/title and the notification all use it.
3. Carry `review: true` into PausedTask at runner.ts:3862-3880, from card.review_waits. pausedSentences then writes '"X" is done; its review waits for room in its budget of CHF 0.15: continue or cancel it in the Inbox.' (or goesOnByItself at the outer limits).
4. Give budgetPauseLabelOf a label for card.review_waits === true, such as 'Review waits for room in its budget', so the Tasks row and the session page row match the card.
5. Update the fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-tasks.ts) and the maintainer doc for budget-card in the same commit.

finding.title: Costs calls the session's task checks 'planning'
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'planning 3 runs CHF 0.01' / 'Planning and chat 3 runs' in a project that never planned.
finding.expected: 'The session's own checks', as Details calls them.
finding.evidence: Club motto Costs (l3b steps *cm-costs*)
finding.repro: Run sessions on a folder project, then open More › Costs.
finding.suspected_cause: Task-check calls are booked under planning.

verdict.root_cause: The Costs view labels the session's task-check runs (Run.specialist "task-check", ADR 0119) as "planning". The label was added deliberately in b7a1acf ("the Performance view counts the check as planning"): costFacts() puts TASK_CHECK_RUN_SPECIALIST in the same branch as INTAKE_RUN_SPECIALIST, so both read "planning" (views.ts:1479-1480). The task check's Run and ledger rows have no task_id (ADR 0119, 2026-11-16 amendment), so on By task they fall into the "(none)" bucket, which costView always calls "Planning and chat" (views.ts:1266). The evidence matches this exactly. A copy of the l3b state.sqlite shows that Club motto (01a1e8d8-…) has only writer-marketing (5), critic (5) and task-check (3) runs, and no intake and no chat. Its 3 task-less ledger rows are runs 01a1e8dc-aaf9, 01a1e8dd-4851 and 01a1e8dd-da2e, all specialist "task-check", prompt task-check@1.1.0. Their 6668+2462+1604 USD micro make the "planning 3 runs CHF 0.01" and "Planning and chat 3 runs CHF 0.01" rows in step 96-cm-costs. Other places name the same spend differently. The session review says "the session's own checks CHF 0.01" (session-review.ts:778; views.ts:862; step 121), and the session log says 'Checked the task list after …'. The owner's own reading (owner-decisions D5 item 4) lists "planning" and "the task check" as separate things. So "planning", in a project that never had a plan, breaks design §5 rules 6 (plain words) and 4 (true now).
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1479 (bySpecialist label: INTAKE_RUN_SPECIALIST || TASK_CHECK_RUN_SPECIALIST -> "planning"); also views.ts:1266 (By task "(none)" -> "Planning and chat") and views.ts:1452 (comment "the task check is planning too")
verdict.fix_sketch: 1) costFacts (views.ts:1474-1481): label "intake" only as "planning". Give "task-check" its own words, the ones the session already uses: "checking the task list", matching the log line 'Checked the task list after …', or "the session's own checks", matching the session review. Choose one and use it in both places. Avoid "the project's own checks": that means the kept-work lint and test checks (ADR 0104/OP-2). Keep notWork() as it is, so there is still no Accepted figure for the check. The Performance view can keep counting the check as the planning mode internally. 2) By task "(none)" row (views.ts:1266): costFacts already reads every entry's run. Collect which kinds make up the task-less spend: the intake gives planning, a ledger row with no run or chat gives chat, a task-check gives the checks. Name only the kinds that are there: Club motto would read "Checking the task list", and a project with all three would read "Planning, chat and checking the task list". The alternative is one By task row per kind. 3) Update the comment at :1451-1452 and the ladder.ts:194-198 doc comment. Docs: the Costs section in docs/maintainers/billing.md or runtime.md, and a dated note under ADR 0119 point 9 ("What the person reads"). Fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fixtures.ts / fake-daemon) uses the same label.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts: on a folder project made with createTask, with no intake and no chat, run a session whose writer report carries a "For the task list:" line, so the stand-in runs one task check. A case in the selftasks block can reuse the quotePage helper and checkRuns() to assert one task-check run. Then call client.costs({ projectId }) and assert three things. costs.bySpecialist.map(s => s.label) does not contain "planning" and does contain the chosen words, e.g. "checking the task list". costs.byTask.map(b => b.label) does not contain "Planning and chat" and does contain "Checking the task list". A control project whose only no-task spend is its intake still reads "planning". It fails today: the labels are "planning" and "Planning and chat". Add a CostsTab render test in apps/ui with that view, and a packages/runtime/test/views.test.ts unit case: a Run row with specialist "task-check" and a ledger row with task_id null, then costView(store, { projectId }).
