finding.title: Read-backs for same-titled tasks drop '(the older one)'; the resume read-back states the result before Yes
finding.what_the_person_sees: 'Pause "Write the guide"? ...'; 'Resume "Write the guide"? It is ready again. It runs at your next Start.'
finding.expected: Say which task, and describe the outcome in the future tense before Yes.
finding.evidence: gc-p.json, gc-r.json
finding.repro: Two tasks named 'Write the guide'; pause and resume the older one from chat.
finding.suspected_cause: The read-back uses the title only.

verdict.root_cause:
The finding is half right.

Part 1 is real. A move's read-back and its after-Yes line name the task by its title only, so when two tasks share a title the person cannot tell which one Yes will change. `findTask` (task.ts:243-288) uses the person's word to pick the right task at :261-263, but it returns a bare TaskRow and the word is lost. After that, `moveCard` (task.ts:1627-1649) builds `ask: moveAsk(task, ...)` and `sentence: moveSentence(task, ...)`. Both build their text from `const t = quote(task.title)` (moveAsk :509, moveSentence :572), which gives 'Pause "Write the guide"? No session runs it until you press Resume.' (:537), 'Resume "Write the guide"? It is ready again.' (:542), 'Paused "Write the guide": ...' (:580) and '"Write the guide" is ready again.' (:586). `task.transition`'s card (:1280-1301) has the same gap. The evidence confirms the app's own deterministic text: gc-p.json and gc-r.json show "calls": [] and usd 0, so no model call was made, and the person's "(the older one)" appears in neither the read-back nor the line after Yes. The user guide (docs/user-guide.md:322-325) says two same-titled tasks "are named apart in Chat by what tells them apart", and design §5 rule 3 asks for names that identify. Run L3's l3-small fix fixed which task the word picks (L3-run-6). Its own check_in_the_app step expected the read-back 'Resume "Write the guide"? …', so this gap was left untouched, not brought back by a later change.

Part 2 is not a defect. The Resume read-back's 'It is ready again. It runs at your next Start.' follows the design. Its first sentence is the design's own consequence line for Resume (core-experience.md:147: "It is ready again; the next session can run it."). The second comes from withPreview (task.ts:1681-1695), which drops 'Ready: ' from previewWork's line. The design writes every consequence line in the present tense to say what Yes does ('No session runs it until you press Resume.', 'Drops it.', §5 Move dialog). A future tense would be a change to the design, not a bug fix.
verdict.where: packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts:509 (moveAsk quotes the title only), :572 (moveSentence the same), :1647 (moveCard's ask), :262 (findTask drops the word that picked the task); design core-experience.md:147 for the Resume consequence line
verdict.fix_sketch:
1. Add a helper in task.ts, say `taskLabel(ctx, task)`. It returns quote(title) when no other task of the project has the same `sameTitle()`. Otherwise it returns quote(title) plus the tag that tells this task apart: "#17" when each task in the group has its own pull request, else the age tag in brackets, "(the older one)". Use the age tag, not the state tag: it is the only kind that stays the same from read-back to after-Yes line to Undo, since a state tag changes when the move does ("the ready one" becomes "the paused one"). Simpler still: reuse the person's own word when it picked the task.
2. Pass the label into moveAsk and moveSentence as an optional `name` that replaces `t`. Do this from moveCard, from task.transition's plan and run, and from the move's undoSentence.
3. A task with a unique title keeps 'Pause "X"? …' exactly.
4. Leave the Resume consequence line as designed. Change it to "It will be ready again" only if the owner rewords core-experience.md:147.
5. Update docs/maintainers/commands.md, in the "Tasks of one title" entry.
verdict.failing_test_idea:
In packages/runtime/test/conversation-memory.test.ts, the chat boundary through w.chat with no model, next to the l3-small L3-run-6 case:
- Add two "Write the guide" tasks one minute apart.
- `pause Write the guide (the older one)`: expect pendingConfirmation.readback toBe 'Pause "Write the guide" (the older one)? No session runs it until you press Resume.'
- Answer "yes": the reply contains 'Paused "Write the guide" (the older one): no session runs it until you press Resume.'
- `resume Write the guide (the older one)`: the readback starts with 'Resume "Write the guide" (the older one)?'
- Add a control: a task with a unique title still reads back 'Pause "Write the notes"? …'.

Today the read-back is 'Pause "Write the guide"? …', so the test fails. A matching case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts through the chat route would cover the screen.
verdict.area_hint: Not a run C area. It is a small words fix in packages/commands/src/commands/task.ts (move read-backs and sentences), following run L3's l3-small same-title work (W15-37 / L3-run-6). d1109-starts-engine owns only the appended 'It runs at your next Start.' preview, which is correct.
verdict.notes: Judged from the code at 4cf11fd and the live evidence; I did not run the stand-in bench. The text is the app's own deterministic text (calls [], usd 0 in /tmp/frbench/live4/l3/evidence/gc-p.json and gc-r.json), and the right task was picked: the header reads "Ready: 1 task waits for your Start" after the pause, and run L3's review checked the task ids. No leftovers file (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) names this, and the owner decisions of 2026-11-09 say nothing about read-back tense. I agree with the 'words' severity for part 1: Yes still changes the right task, but the person cannot check that before pressing it. The same title-only naming appears in assertFrom's '"Write the guide" is paused, not cancelled or done.' (gc-redo.json, task.ts:1621) and in the undo sentences. The fix should cover those too.

finding.title: Chat says 'Answered with your Claude subscription' under a reply that says it could not answer
finding.what_the_person_sees: In chat, with the API key at its limit, preset 'API key first, then subscription', and a subscription that Anthropic does not accept, the reply reads: 'I could not answer (model call failed).' Under it: [Think it through] 'Thinks longer on this model: about 30 seconds, at most CHF 0.03.' and the footer 'Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 11:57.'
finding.expected: No 'Answered with ...' note when nothing answered. The note appears once, under the first answer the subscription really gives. A failed answer says why and what to do (design section 5), and no paid 'Think it through' is offered on the credential that just failed.
finding.evidence: c26.json: chatProxyReqs shows 4 POST /v1/messages?beta=true with the subscription token, all 401; chatApiReqs is [] (no call on the key); chatFooters is ['Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 11:57.']. Daemon log at 10:20:21.758Z: 'ERROR [agent-loop] run failed {error: "model call failed"}'. Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/12-c26-chat-question.png.
finding.repro: On a bench like c26: the key is resting (restingUntil set), the preset is key_then_subscription, and the subscription is one Anthropic refuses (the bench's token). Ask any chat question.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts around l.1378-1390 builds switchNote before the model call, from the hold check (credHold.answersOn), and marks the stop as noted. Around l.2306 it is used as the footer whatever the call's outcome. The 'noted' mark then also keeps the note off the first real answer.

verdict.root_cause: The CE-9 note comes from the hold check made before the model call, and the outcome of the call never gates it. At agent.ts:1378-1387, credentialHold() reports not held with answersOn=subscription because the key is resting. switchNote is built from that prediction. At :1388-1391 the stop goes into conv.notedStops at once, before any model call. At :2296-2307 the footer is `(stopped ? … : deep ? … : null) ?? switchNote ?? fixFooter`, and nothing there checks result.outcome. So when the call fails, the note "Answered with your Claude subscription: …" still sits under "I could not answer (model call failed).". The stop is already marked as noted, so the first answer the subscription really gives in this conversation gets no note. Separately, the Think it through closer at :2274-2292 needs only `result && longerFigures && !heldAfter && results.length===0`. It never checks result.outcome === "completed", so a failed call still gets the paid offer. A second cause explains why the reply says "model call failed" and not a refusal or hold reply. Agent SDK 0.3.304 throws "Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 …" from the iterator. claude-code.ts:195-204 catches it as provider_error and never runs isClaudeCodeRefusal on it. RoutedProvider therefore never marks the subscription refused, the loop throws provider_error "model call failed" (loop.ts:842), and agent.ts:2226-2239 never re-checks the hold, because provider_error is not in CREDENTIAL_HOLD_CODES.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/conversation/agent.ts:1380 (switchNote built and noted at :1388-1391 before the call); agent.ts:2306 (footer uses switchNote whatever the outcome); agent.ts:2274 (closer offered under a failed call); contributing: packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:200 (thrown 401 result text mapped to provider_error)
verdict.fix_sketch: In agent.ts, keep switchNote as a candidate before the call, but do not add the stop to conv.notedStops there. After the run, use the note as the footer only if a model answer was really given: result?.outcome === "completed" (or deep.result completed), !stopped and !heldAfter. Only then add stopNoted to notedStops. A better version takes the credential from the call's own billing (message_end billing.sourceId and kind, or the ledger row) and not from the pre-call prediction, so a switch inside the call is named correctly. Add `result.outcome === "completed"` to the closer condition at :2274, so no Think it through appears under a failure. For the reply itself, the catch in claude-code.ts:195 should run isClaudeCodeRefusal(null, errorMessage(e)) and give provider_auth. Do the same in the sdk.ts catch at about :606 for task runs. RoutedProvider then marks the subscription refused, files the one card and tries the next source. Chat then gets the hold or refusal reply through CREDENTIAL_HOLD_CODES and not "I could not answer (model call failed)." The general wording of chat failures is C3L-7.
verdict.failing_test_idea: A composed-runtime test through POST /chat, set up like packages/runtime/test/billing-order.test.ts (fetchImpl Messages API stand-in plus the sdkQuery Claude Code stand-in). Set credential_policy to key_then_subscription. The API answers 400 "You have reached your specified API usage limits. You will regain access on 2026-10-31 at 11:00 UTC." Turn 1: the key rests and Claude Code answers. Then the sdkQuery stand-in throws Error("Claude Code returned an error result: Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid."). Turn 2 must have no footer matching /^Answered with/, and its chat.reply event must have no closer. Then Claude Code answers again (a new token is saved). Turn 3's footer must be "Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 12:00." Today turn 2 gives "I could not answer (model call failed)." with that footer and a closer {estimateUsdMicro 16780, atMost 37500, 30 s}, and turn 3's footer is null. I reproduced exactly this with a throwaway test at /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-13/switch-note.test.ts, output in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-13/out.txt. Add a sibling case for subscription_then_key with a resting subscription and the API failing with a 500: the note must not appear under the failure and must appear on the next answer on the key, because that is the answer the person pays per use for.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (CE-9 chat note); the Think it through closer under a failure is d1109-chat-depth's
verdict.notes: The bench evidence matches: c26.json has chatFooters = ['Answered with your Claude subscription: your API key is at its limit until 11:57.'], chatButtons = ['Think it through'], chatApiReqs = [] and 4 subscription POSTs with 401. It also reproduces on the code at 4cf11fd in a composed runtime. The throwaway test in /tmp/frbench/verify-L4-creds-13 sits outside the checkout and nothing in the checkout was edited. It ran under the heavy.lock and printed: STEP2 "I could not answer (model call failed)." with the footer and the closer; STEP3 "From Claude Code." with footer null. Severity: major rather than words. The page contradicts itself, a paid offer appears under a failure, and the note is used up. In the subscription_then_key direction, a failed call would hide the note from the first answer that is charged per use to the API key, which goes against CE-9's "once per stop per conversation" and the owner's 7b. No leftover names the footer issue. C3L-7 (leftovers-C3) covers only the general 'I could not answer (<error>)' wording. The contributing cause is that claude-code.ts and sdk.ts do not classify the SDK's thrown 'Claude Code returned an error result: … API Error: 401' as provider_auth. That is also why c26's subscription was never marked refused (timeline subRefused null; the run outcome was 'error'). It may be reported as its own creds finding, so check before merging fixes.

finding.title: Start dialog says nothing about the API key's limit under 'API key first, then subscription'
finding.what_the_person_sees: Before the stop the dialog reads 'This session runs "Write notes/moss.md" (about CHF 0.07).' and 'If your API key runs out, the work goes on with your subscription.' While the key rests until 11:57 it reads only 'This session runs "Write notes/lichen.md" (about CHF 0.07).', with no line about the credential at all. Settings meanwhile says 'Your API key is at its limit until 11:57; your subscription does the work meanwhile.'
finding.expected: The dialog names the stop and says where the session runs, as it does in the other direction ('Your subscription is at its limit until 15:40, so this runs on your API key ...'). For example: 'Your API key is at its limit until 11:57, so this runs on your subscription.'
finding.evidence: c26.json dialog1 and dialog2; screenshots 04-c26-start-dialog-before.png and 11-c26-start-dialog-while-the-key-rests.png in /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/.
finding.repro: Choose preset key_then_subscription and let the key meet its limit (bench-api --api-key limited, FORERUNNER_BENCH_API_LIMIT_FORM=400). Open Start on a project with a ready task.
finding.suspected_cause: In packages/runtime/src/daemon/credential-start.ts, serves() starts with 'if (first.kind !== "subscription") return false'. Under whenStopped 'next' with the key as first choice the line is therefore null; only the subscription-to-key direction has a run-out line.

verdict.root_cause: startCredential() has only one test for whether the other credential can serve, `serves()`, and it was written for one direction ("The other credential (the API key, after the subscription) serves now"). Its first statement is `if (first.kind !== "subscription") return false;`. Under key_then_subscription (whenStopped 'next'), firstChoiceStop() returns the resting API key with a stopKey. The early `ifRunsOutLine` return at l.98-99 is therefore skipped, and the 'next' branch at l.133-140 returns `line: (await serves()) ? startRunOutLine(...) : null`, which is null. The dialog loses the line it had before the stop and gets no stopped line in its place. The wording function already handles both directions: startRunOutLine('api_key', ...) at credential-policy-view.ts:336 produces "Your API key is at its limit until 11:57, so this runs on your subscription (about CHF 0.07).", but nothing calls it for the key-first case. CS-3's decision says "with the first choice stopped: under next the run-out line" and does not name a direction. Its acceptance and the real-daemon case (real-daemon.test.ts about l.22215-22240) only test subscription_then_key with the subscription resting, so the gap was never caught. The evidence fits this exactly: dialog1 shows the ifRunsOutLine, the key's limits hold restingUntil 10:57Z, subRefused is null (Settings: subscription "Works now"), lichen is Ready (runsWork true), there is no grant, and dialog2 shows only the plan sentence.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/daemon/credential-start.ts:124 (serves() starts with `if (first.kind !== "subscription") return false`), used by the whenStopped 'next' branch at credential-start.ts:133-140
verdict.fix_sketch: In credential-start.ts, split the check into two. (1) For the 'next' branch, add `nextServes()`. It looks at the other credential of first.kind: for an api_key first choice, the enabled subscription source, which must be in policy.rule.kinds; it must have no currentStopOf, and it needs no month-cap check because the subscription has no per-use cost. For a subscription first choice, it keeps today's checks (the key has no stop and the month has room). The 'next' branch then returns startRunOutLine(first.kind, stop, about, opts), which already gives "Your API key is at its limit until 11:57, so this runs on your subscription (about CHF 0.07)." (2) Keep today's subscription-only serves() for the ask/wait 'Use API key' buttons: those buttons only make sense when the subscription is the stopped first choice, and key_only must never offer them. If neither credential can serve under 'next', the start is blocked and start-blocked.ts gives the reason, so returning null there is fine. Sibling to fix in the same commit: planCardLine (credential-policy-view.ts:415) ends with "(costs money)" after whichever credential is the other one. Under key_then_subscription with the key resting, the plan card would read "...: your subscription does the work meanwhile (costs money).", which is false. Add the money clause only when the other credential is the API key. Update the fake daemon's start-check mirror if it builds this line.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Add a real-daemon case in apps/ui/test/real-daemon.test.ts, in the 'd1109-cred-screens, run C' describe, next to the CS-3 case at about l.22215. Run composeCs() with both credentials saved, add one Ready task, then setPolicyCs(client, 'key_then_subscription'). Rest the API key source until resetAt, the key-side twin of restSubscription (billing_source.limits.restingUntil). Then `const out = await client.startCheck(project.id)`. Expect out.blocked to be null, out.credential.line to match /^Your API key is at its limit until 11:40, so this runs on your subscription \((about CHF \d+\.\d\d|less than CHF 0\.01)\)\.$/, and out.credential.runOut to be null. This fails today because line is null. Optionally press Start and check that the run row's billing source is the subscription, so the sentence matches what the engine does. Add a unit case in packages/runtime/test/credential-policy-view.test.ts for startRunOutLine('api_key', {reason:'limit', until}) with the exact string. Add a planCardLine case asserting that the key-first 'next' wording has no "(costs money)".
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-screens (CS-3 Start dialog line; CS-4 plan card sibling)
verdict.notes: No known leftover names this. C6L-3, C6L-4 and C6L-8 are other Start-dialog and credential wording items, all in the subscription-first direction. I did not rerun the bench: the c26 run already took place on the stand-in bench (bench-api with --api-key limited and FORERUNNER_BENCH_API_LIMIT_FORM=400), and the code path explains the result. Each branch before l.133 is ruled out by the evidence: first is non-null with a stopKey (key restingUntil 10:57Z), there is no grant, lichen is Ready, and Stop all is off. That leaves serves() returning false at l.124. The evidence also shows the subscription stand-in failing with a 401 (the bench token is not a real sign-in), but the app had recorded no refusal (subRefused null, Settings "Works now"), so the app's own view says the subscription serves and the line should appear. Severity is minor, not major: no money is spent unexpectedly (the session goes to the subscription, which has no per-use cost), and Settings and the session log name the stop. But at the moment it matters, the dialog drops even its earlier if-it-runs-out line. Sibling to check: planCardLine at credential-policy-view.ts:415 says "(costs money)" after the subscription under key-first 'next'. I saw this in the code only, not in this evidence. finding.title: The session page shows two clocks: the computer's beside the person's zone
finding.what_the_person_sees: The header reads 'Moss notes · session at 10:19' and the log times read '10:19'. Beside them: 'Your subscription took over at 11:19 (your API key's limit)' and 'your API key is at its limit until 11:57'. The Sessions list row reads '10:19 · under a minute'.
finding.expected: One clock per screen: the person's zone, which the daemon's sentences already use.
finding.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/06-c26-session-page.png. The config timezone is Europe/Zurich; the bench browser runs in UTC.
finding.repro: Set the person's zone in setup to a zone other than the computer's (or travel). Open a session page that has a credential switch.
finding.suspected_cause: The desktop UI formats times in the browser's zone (only apps/ui/src/mobile/time.ts passes timeZone), while the daemon's sentences use human.timezone. The mismatch shows only when the two zones differ.

verdict.root_cause: The UI and the daemon write times in different zones. Every desktop time helper in apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts calls toLocaleTimeString/toLocaleDateString("en-GB", HH_MM) and never passes a timeZone, so it uses the browser's zone: formatTime :49-54, formatClock :23-30 (its "today" test at :28 is also the browser's day), formatDateTime :11-16, formatDate and formatDayMonth :33-46. The file's own header (:2-4) and formatClock's comment (:18-21) say they match "the daemon's own sentences ... clockTime". They do not. The daemon's clockTime (packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:203-228) formats with timeZone = human.timezone, and the session result line uses it (packages/runtime/src/daemon/server.ts:2099-2100, credential-policy-view.ts:441 resultSwitchLine), as do the log line "your API key is at its limit until 11:57" and every other "until/at HH:MM" sentence. On the session page, the title (apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx:70-75 startedAtWords -> formatTime, title built at :379) and each log row (:691 formatTime(e.at)) are in the browser's zone. The daemon's sentences on the same page are in the person's zone. The Sessions row (apps/ui/src/pages/project/SessionsTab.tsx:31 formatClock) and FilesTab.tsx:20-22 use the browser's zone too. The evidence matches exactly. The c26 config has timezone Europe/Zurich (home/config/config.json:5). The bench ran at 10:16-10:25 UTC and the browser was in UTC. So one instant (10:19Z) reads "session at 10:19" and "10:19" in the log, but "took over at 11:19" (UTC+1) beside them, and the reset "until 11:57" is 10:57Z. I reproduced it: under TZ=UTC, toLocaleTimeString of 2026-11-17T10:19:30Z gives 10:19, and Intl with Europe/Zurich gives 11:19. The run was on the stand-in (provider bench-api, live false), so it reproduces without the real model. The UI can already read the person's zone from GET /me (server.ts:850-856, timezone), but lib/time.ts never uses it. The mobile helpers take a zone, but the store passes deviceTimezone() (apps/ui/src/mobile/store.tsx:373), so the phone has the same gap.
verdict.where: apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts:49 (formatTime, and :23 formatClock, :11 formatDateTime: no timeZone); apps/ui/src/pages/SessionPage.tsx:74 and :691; apps/ui/src/pages/project/SessionsTab.tsx:31; against packages/runtime/src/session/credential-wait.ts:203 (clockTime in human.timezone)
verdict.fix_sketch: Make the person's zone the one display zone in the UI. (1) Load /me.timezone once into a small zone holder or React context. Refresh it after the setup or Settings save of the time zone. Fall back to the browser's zone only until /me has answered. (2) Give every helper in apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts a zone: add timeZone: zone to HH_MM and to the date options. In formatClock, compare the calendar day in that zone (Intl parts in the zone, not toDateString). Keep the en-GB 24-hour form. (3) Route FilesTab.tsx:20-22 through formatClock instead of its own toLocaleTimeString. (4) Mobile: seed env.timezone from /me.timezone instead of deviceTimezone() (store.tsx:373). Then parseWhen's "until 15:00" and describeUntil agree with the daemon too. (5) The fake daemon (apps/ui/test/fake-daemon.ts:8427 has timezone "UTC") should use the same zone as /me in its resultSwitchLine opts, so the fake and the real daemon agree. Optional: when the browser's zone differs from the person's, name the zone once in Settings ("Times are shown in Europe/Zurich"). Daemon sentences stay as they are; ADR-backed daemon wording already uses human.timezone.
verdict.failing_test_idea: apps/ui/test/credential-switch.test.tsx (or a new session-zone.test.tsx). Run the process with TZ=UTC (process.env.TZ set before the first Date use, or vi.stubEnv in a separate worker). Give the fake daemon /me timezone "Europe/Zurich" and a session started at 2026-11-17T10:19:00Z with a credential switch at the same instant. Its result line comes from resultSwitchLine with opts.timezone "Europe/Zurich", so it reads "took over at 11:19". Render SessionPage. The test expects getByTestId("session-header") to contain "session at 11:19", the first event-row time to read "11:19", and the switch line's "11:19". Today the header and rows read 10:19. Add a sibling assertion on SessionsTab: sessionRowLine starts "11:19 · under a minute". Add a unit case in a lib/time test: formatClock("2026-11-17T23:30:00Z", now = 2026-11-17T12:00Z, zone "Europe/Zurich") reads "18 Nov, 00:30", not "23:30". At the real boundary: the bench walk c26 with a UTC browser and a Europe/Zurich config shows one clock on the session page.
verdict.area_hint: small fix area: ui-person-zone (apps/ui/src/lib/time.ts plus the /me zone holder; touches SessionPage, SessionsTab, FilesTab, mobile store). No run C area owns UI-side times. The nearest owners are d1109-sessions (session title, Sessions row) and d1109-cred-screens (the switch lines that expose the mismatch).
verdict.notes: No leftover names it. C5's item about compose capturing human.timezone at compose time is a different issue: the daemon side, a zone changed without a restart. The run C plan deliberately moved daemon sentences and chat facts to the person's zone (D3-6, recall windowOf, credential waits "in the person's time zone"), but it never changed the UI's own clocks, so the mismatch is a gap the plan left, not a decision. Scope is narrower than "any person": SetupPage prefills the person's zone from the browser (SetupPage.tsx:27, :323), so on a normal install the two zones match. It shows when the person picks another zone, travels with the laptop, or set up through the CLI without --timezone (schema default "UTC", packages/state/src/schema.ts:132; daemon falls back to "UTC"). The CLI case hits everyone outside UTC. Minor is right: no wrong action follows, but one screen shows two clocks an hour apart for the same instant, and the "until 11:57" reset reads as later than it is next to the log's times. Evidence files: /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/06-c26-session-page.png and .txt, 14-c26-end-projects-*.txt:32 (Sessions row "10:19 · under a minute"), 10-c26-settings-rows.txt:48 and 12-c26-chat-question.txt:32 (daemon "until 11:57"), /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/home/config/config.json:5 (Europe/Zurich), bench.json startedAt 10:16:17Z.

finding.title: Task runs on the subscription ignore the configured Anthropic API address
finding.what_the_person_sees: With an API address set in setup (config.json anthropicApiBase, for example a company gateway), chat on the subscription and every call on the API key go through it. A task run on the subscription goes straight to api.anthropic.com.
finding.expected: Every call goes to the configured address, task runs on the subscription included.
finding.evidence: In c26 the proxy at anthropicApiBase logged 0 requests during the task run (10:19:35-10:19:38) and 4 during the chat turn (10:20:19). The run's 401 reads 'OAuth access token is invalid', which is the real API's wording; the proxy answers 'Invalid bearer token'. The same happened in c22: its run (09:00:57-09:01:03) has no proxy entry, and the proxy's subscription entries come only from chat at 09:01:41 (/tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c22-proxy/requests.jsonl).
finding.repro: Run fr setup --anthropic-api http://127.0.0.1:<port> with a logging proxy at that port and a subscription saved. Start a task that runs on the subscription and read the proxy log.
finding.suspected_cause: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts reads req.baseURL (l.523), but no caller ever sets it. compose.ts passes config.anthropicApiBase only to ClaudeCodeProvider (chat) and the Messages adapter (l.1869, l.1882).

verdict.root_cause: The configured `anthropicApiBase` never reaches the Agent SDK driver that runs a task on the subscription. `SdkAgentDriver.run` only sets `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` from `req.baseURL` (sdk.ts:62, :523), and no caller sets that field. The executor's one SDK call (executor.ts:1549-1580) passes token, credential, model, prompt, cwd, tools and similar fields, plus `env` only when Headroom's `sessionContext.sdkEnv` is set. It never passes a baseURL. `SdkExecutorDeps` (executor.ts:363-378) has no base field. compose.ts builds the driver (2119-2125) and the executor's `sdk` deps (2602-2608) without `config.anthropicApiBase`. compose.ts passes the address only to the per-call providers: `ClaudeCodeProvider` (1869), which serves chat, planning and reviews on the subscription, and `AnthropicMessagesProvider` (1882), which serves the key. That is why chat on the subscription went through the gateway and the subscription task run did not. The evidence agrees with the code. In c26 (config.json anthropicApiBase http://127.0.0.1:49048) the daemon picked the subscription with driver "sdk" at 10:19:34.986. The run failed at 10:19:38.841 with Claude Code's "401 OAuth access token is invalid", which is the real API's wording; the proxy would have answered "Invalid bearer token" locally (proxy.mjs:136). The proxy log has only the 4 chat requests at 10:20:19-20. c22 shows the same pattern: the SDK run failed at 09:01:04 with no proxy entry, and the chat entries came at 09:01:41. A side effect: the bench's fake subscription token was sent to the real api.anthropic.com. It is fake, so nothing leaked, but a real token would also skip a company gateway.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/session/executor.ts:1549 (sdk.driver.run without baseURL); packages/runtime/src/daemon/compose.ts:2119 and :2602 (SDK driver and sdk deps built without config.anthropicApiBase); packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:523 (the only consumer of req.baseURL)
verdict.fix_sketch: In compose.ts, give the SDK path the same base URL that ClaudeCodeProvider gets, with the same rule as claude-code.ts:239: set ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL only when the address is not the default https://api.anthropic.com. The simplest place is `SdkDriverDeps` (sdk.ts:125): add `baseURL?: string` and set it at compose.ts:2119 from `config?.anthropicApiBase`. Then sdk.ts:523 uses `req.baseURL ?? this.deps.baseURL`, so every SDK run gets it, task runs and any later SDK caller included. Alternatively, add `baseURL` to `SdkExecutorDeps` (compose.ts:2602) and pass it at executor.ts:1549. Keep the current order: Headroom's `req.env` is spread after it and still wins while Headroom is on. Update docs/maintainers/runtime.md (SDK driver env) and the setup docs to say the API address covers subscription task runs too.
verdict.failing_test_idea: Composed daemon test (compose with the `sdkQuery` seam capturing `options.env`). Use a config with anthropicApiBase "http://gw.test", a subscription saved in the vault and the policy set to the subscription. Approve and start a one-task plan so the task runs on the "sdk" driver. Assert that the captured query's env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is "http://gw.test", the same as the chat turn's ClaudeCodeProvider env in the same daemon. Add a second case with the default https://api.anthropic.com and assert ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL is absent. This fails today: the SDK run's env has no ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Optional bench check: the creds journey's c26 setup (logging proxy at anthropicApiBase) shows proxy entries with benchSubscription:true during the task run, not only during chat.
verdict.area_hint: d1109-cred-engine (provider and credential wiring in compose.ts); small enough to be its own fix area (compose.ts + sdk.ts/executor.ts)
verdict.notes: I did not run the bench: the code explains the finding, and the c22 and c26 logs (daemon.log and the proxy's requests.jsonl) match it. One caveat on the finding's wording, "every call on the API key go through it". In c26 the key's loop run also left no proxy entry, because start-c26.sh uses --provider bench-api: the bench's stand-in answers the key's Messages calls before they reach the proxy. That is a bench artefact. The code shows the key path does pass baseURL (compose.ts:1882), and in c22 the proxy logged the key's /v1/models calls. None of the leftovers files (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) or the owner's decisions mention the API base or ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL. Minor is the right severity: it matters only to a person who set a gateway address and runs tasks on the subscription. Where api.anthropic.com is blocked, every subscription task run would fail; the 401 would then read as a refused sign-in.

finding.title: Costs lists a model named '<synthetic>'
finding.what_the_person_sees: After a failed run on the subscription, the project's Costs page lists under By model: '<synthetic> · 1 · — · — · CHF 0.00'.
finding.expected: No internal marker shown as a model name. Book the run under the model it asked for, or show no row for a run that never reached a model.
finding.evidence: Screenshot /tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/steps/13-c26-end-projects-01a1e904-c8db-71ca-be07-d8530e9.png. The cost_ledger row has kind subscription, model '<synthetic>', USD 0.
finding.repro: Any run on the subscription that Claude Code ends with an error. Here it was a refused sign-in; Claude Code also sends a synthetic message when the plan's limit is reached.
finding.suspected_cause: The SDK driver books the usage of Claude Code's synthetic error message under that message's model field, '<synthetic>'.

verdict.root_cause: When an API call fails (a refused sign-in, or the plan's limit), Claude Code makes up an assistant message itself. That message carries `error` (for example "authentication_failed"), `model: "<synthetic>"` (Claude Code's own constant, present in the bundled binary of @anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk 0.3.304) and an all-zero `usage` object. The SDK driver's assistant branch books any message that has a `usage` object (packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:424-432). R-modelusage takes the model from the message: `const model = typeof m?.model === "string" && m.model ? m.model : req.model`, so the model is "<synthetic>". The driver also adds one to numTurns. book() then calls hooks.afterModelCall with that model (sdk.ts:353-366), and afterModelCall writes a cost_ledger row with `model: opts.model ?? ctx.model` (packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:271). The price lookup for "<synthetic>" fails and falls back to the run model's price, so the cost is 0 and no money is wrong. The daemon's Costs view groups the ledger by its model column and uses the raw key as the label (packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1196-1205). The run facts know no run on "<synthetic>", so Runs shows the entry count of 1 and Accepted shows — (views.ts:1271-1280). The Costs tab then prints "<synthetic> · 1 · — · — · CHF 0.00". The evidence DB (/tmp/frbench/live4/creds/c26/home/data/state.sqlite) holds exactly that row: kind subscription, model '<synthetic>', all token counts 0, the anthropic-sdk run that failed with "401 OAuth access token is invalid". That run's own model is claude-sonnet-5-5. The Claude Code provider (packages/runtime/src/provider/claude-code.ts:166-169) skips the error message with `continue`, so only the SDK driver books it. The unit tests missed it because the fake error message in sdk-driver.test.ts:342-346 has no `model` and no `usage`, unlike the real shape. This breaks design §5 rules 3 and 6: an internal marker is shown as a name.
verdict.where: packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts:424-432 (the model taken from the synthetic message and booked); ledger write at packages/runtime/src/enforcement/hooks.ts:271; shown via packages/runtime/src/daemon/views.ts:1196-1205 and :1271-1280
verdict.fix_sketch: In SdkAgentDriver.handle's assistant branch, treat Claude Code's synthetic error message as "no model call". When `msg.error` is a string, or `m.model === "<synthetic>"` (one named constant, for example CLAUDE_CODE_SYNTHETIC_MODEL), do not book, do not add to numTurns and do not run the beforeModelCall estimate. Still record sdkError as now. If such a message ever has usage above zero, book it under req.model, never under the marker. To be safe, resultTotals/resultShares should also map a "<synthetic>" key in modelUsage to the run model. Optionally, as defence for rows already in the ledger: the daemon's Costs view (and services/state-api/src/views.ts byModel) could leave out a model bucket whose key is "<synthetic>" and whose usd and tokens are all 0, or fold it into the run's model. Update the fake error messages in sdk-driver.test.ts (rate_limit) and in cred-world/subscription-path to Claude Code's real shape (id, model "<synthetic>", zero usage). Note it in docs/maintainers/runtime.md next to R-modelusage.
verdict.failing_test_idea: This test fails today. In a composed or real-daemon test on the subscription path (the cred-world or subscription-path harness, with the SDK driver and a fake query), the fake query emits init, then `{type:"assistant", error:"authentication_failed", message:{id:<uuid>, model:"<synthetic>", content:[{type:"text", text:"Failed to authenticate. API Error: 401 OAuth access token is invalid"}], usage:{input_tokens:0, output_tokens:0, cache_read_input_tokens:0, cache_creation_input_tokens:0}}}`, then `{type:"result", subtype:"success", is_error:true, result:"Failed to authenticate. ..."}`. After the session ends, GET /projects/:id/costs must give a byModel with no entry whose key or label is "<synthetic>" (and no label starting with "<"), and no cost_ledger row may have model "<synthetic>". Today it lists `{label:"<synthetic>", runs:1, cost CHF 0.00}`. Do the same with error "rate_limit" (the plan's limit). A unit case in sdk-driver.test.ts checks that hooks.afterModelCall is never called with model "<synthetic>" and that the result's steps is 0.
verdict.area_hint: small fix area: SDK driver booking (R-modelusage follow-up in packages/runtime/src/agent/sdk.ts). No run C area owns sdk.ts. The symptom is on the Costs tab (d1109-cred-screens/d1116-budget-all screens), but the fix belongs in the driver.
verdict.notes: Confirmed from the evidence, not inferred. bench.json shows provider bench-api with live false, so the real Claude Code binary ran against the stand-in, and this is the stand-in bench's own reproduction. The steps text (13-c26-end-...txt) shows "By model: <synthetic> 1 — — CHF 0.00". c26.json's ledger shows the single row with model '<synthetic>' and zero tokens, while the run row says claude-sonnet-5-5 / anthropic-sdk / outcome error. The API-key run before it (usage_limit) booked no row. The money is right (CHF 0.00) and Costs sits behind More, so I agree with 'words'. Side effects of the same line: the synthetic message counts as a step (numTurns), and each failed subscription run adds one zero row under the marker, so "Runs" in By model counts a model that never ran. None of the leftovers files (L3, C2, C3, C4, C4b-design, C4b, C5, C6) mention synthetic, By model or SDK booking. The cloud runner's state-api byModel (services/state-api/src/views.ts:462) labels buckets by raw key the same way, so it would show the same row wherever the SDK driver books there. No unit test or bench was run: the real-run DB row plus the code path are conclusive, and the task was read-only.
